row.title: A builder was handed a slice whose fix shipped three days earlier and came back saying there was nothing left to do

content.description: Seen 2026-09-11. A worker pulled the top pick off the dispatch head and found the defect already repaired on main. The merge that repaired it had been recorded against the row as landed:pr-16021@a91c0ef221, yet every acceptance checkbox on the row still read met:false and the status still read in_progress, so the head kept offering it as fresh work and the worker slot was burned for nothing. Nothing reconciles the shipped marker with the checkboxes: they are written by two different verbs and neither verb reads the other. Two ways out, either closes it: make the dispatch head skip a row carrying a shipped marker unless some checkbox is genuinely outstanding and is not merge-shaped, or make the verb that writes the shipped marker also tick the merge-shaped checkboxes so the halves cannot drift apart. Count how many rows in the dispatch head carry a shipped marker today before choosing between them.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The population is counted first: how many rows in the dispatch head carry a shipped marker while a checkbox still reads met:false, quoted with the date of the read.
MERGE-GATED (the lead closes this): merged with the required gates green and the sha recorded.

corpus.title: bp task ready still lists rows whose work has LANDED — two landed:pr-N labelled rows sat at P1 in the ready head for days

content.description: Measured 2026-09-03 by lead-studio-3r during wave-3 triage: task-fe4648fa743ab0a6 (landed:pr-15515@9d38bff985, zero criteria) and pe-w2-bl-media-delete-where-used (landed:pr-15557@0ab5818f1d, 3 criteria, none stamped) were both in the P1 ready head although their PRs had merged days earlier; both closed only because a lead re-verified the PR by hand. The landing verb (bp task landed) records the artefact but the row stays open and claimable, so every lead that triages it pays a full T1 (gh pr view + git grep) to learn what the label already says. Two honest shapes: (a) bp task ready renders a LANDED marker (label + sha) on such rows and sorts them behind un-landed rows of the same priority, or (b) a landing with --pr on a zero-criteria row, once the PR is MERGED (CI can tell), auto-closes done with the PR+sha as close_reason — a merge-shaped criterion already exists for that. Whichever is chosen, a landed row must never look identical to fresh work in the ready head.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: bp task ready (human and -o json) marks a row carrying a landed:pr-N@sha label or a content.landed entry with a visible LANDED field (pr + sha), and orders landed rows after un-landed rows of the same priority; a test pins the ordering and the field.

A zero-criteria kind:task row whose landed PR is MERGED on main is closable by CI or by bp task landed --pr N without a holder claim, closing done with close_reason naming PR+sha; a test proves an OPEN PR does not close it.
PR merged to main (lead closes on merge).

corpus.title: Ready queue admits rows already labelled landed:pr-NNNNN@sha — a landed row with met:false criteria is dispatched as fresh work and burns a builder slot

content.description: Observed 2026-09-05 ~12:00Z by lead-search-3: task-01c6c2c9b9726409 (media search offset ceiling) sat in bp task ready with labels landed-on-main + landed:pr-15560@86c304c279 (merged 2026-09-02T22:33Z, an ancestor of main) while every criterion read met:false and status in_progress. A lead triaged, claimed and dispatched a headless builder on it; the builder came back with 'already fixed'. The label and the criteria disagreed and nothing reconciled them. Two fixes, either closes it: (a) the ready-queue filter (api/lib/barkpark/tasks queue readiness) excludes rows carrying a landed:pr-* label unless a criterion still reads met:false AND is not merge-shaped; (b) bp task landed (the verb that writes the label) also flips the merge-shaped criteria met:true so the halves cannot drift. Ledger lane owns (a), cli lane owns (b) — file the cli half as a child. Count the current population first: rows in ready carrying landed:pr-* is the denominator.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: the population is counted and quoted: rows currently in bp task ready that carry a landed:pr-* label, with their met counts

RULED 2026-09-05 (main), after the sizing: NO readiness filter ships. Instead, `labels` rides the bp task ready card so a lead can SEE a landed:pr-* label before dispatching, and the source fix is the cli child task-4dca6c8453fb1f7c (bp task landed reconciling the criteria it contradicts). THE SIZING that decided it: applying "exclude a landed:pr-* row unless a non-merge-shaped criterion is still unmet" to the measured 21 excludes only 2 (sp-cf-verify at 0 unmet of 3, and task-6d80c6cc7d97b1d1 at 1 of 7); the other 19 — including all nine zero-met rows — carry genuinely unmet, non-merge-shaped criteria and are rows with work left, not falsely-ready rows. BOTH FILTER SHAPES WERE REJECTED WITH REASONS. (i) A SQL predicate in ready_query would duplicate two Elixir regexes (Criteria.merge_gated?'s marker and Landed.landing_worded?) into the query queue.ex documents as planner-fragile, where they drift silently the next time either is widened — a second copy of a predicate, for 2 rows. (ii) An Elixir post-filter would reuse the exact predicates with zero drift but breaks queue.ex's own stated law that every readiness axis lives in the base WHERE "so ready/1 and the atomic claim can never disagree": bp task ready would hide a row bp task claim still hands you, which is a worse defect than the one being cured. Also ruled: empty-unmet counts as excluded (so sp-cf-verify needs no separate row), and NO container exemption is needed — all three umbrella rows (8, 26 and 0 children) carry non-merge-shaped unmet criteria, so the criteria predicate already keeps them. MET WHEN: labels ride the ready card (merged, additive, pruned so a label-less card is byte-identical) AND the cli child is filed.
task-01c6c2c9b9726409 and the counted population are re-read after the merge and no longer appear in ready

corpus.title: bp task stamp once returned success while the criterion stayed unmet

content.description:
Observed once, unreproduced, filed honestly rather than dropped. During a stamp of
pds-w13-charter-lands (not the crown), `bp task stamp` returned a rev with no error, but a
subsequent `bp task get` showed the criterion still met:false. Re-issuing the identical stamp at the
meanwhile-bumped epoch flipped it correctly.

HYPOTHESIS: a lost-update race between a preceding `bp task pulse` and a stamp issued at the same
epoch. Not confirmed.

MITIGATION ALREADY IN PLACE: scripts/pds-crown-stamp.sh's stamp subcommand re-reads the published
ledger after every write and exits 2 if the read-back disagrees, so the sanctioned tool is already
defensive against this class even though the underlying CLI behaviour is unfixed. Anyone stamping
by hand must do the same read-back.

This is a bp CLI / server concern, outside the PDS surface fence. Filed here because PDS is where it
was observed and PDS is what it would damage.

If reproduced: the lost update is fixed and proven by mutation — evidence: the failing case before and passing after

corpus.title: Two concurrent bp task stamps on one row can lose an update: the criteria array is read-modify-written with no per-criterion CAS

content.description: SPUN OUT of task-22bc2e2578ef1222, whose stated mechanism (evidence text containing %{ being mangled or dropped) was REFUTED BY RUN on 2026-09-02: a scratch row stored the %{ sequence byte-identically, and a criterion-text mismatch refused loudly rather than silently no-opping. What survives is the criterion's own second hypothesis, a rev race with the next write. bp task stamp updates content.acceptance_criteria by reading the array, replacing one element and writing the WHOLE array back. Two stamps that overlap on different indices of the same row can therefore lose one another: the later writer's array was read before the earlier writer's element landed. That matches the observed shape on task-bb83570ba0f6f9f2 -- claim epoch 13, released_by lead-reconcile-2, i.e. many re-claims and re-stamps by more than one actor -- and it matches the sibling row pds-bl-stamp-silent-noop. This campaign runs roughly thirty agents against one ledger, and a lead stamping several criteria in a loop is the ordinary case, so the window is not exotic. The stamp path is api/lib/barkpark/tasks/stamp.ex; the epoch fence guards the CLAIM, not the criteria array, so a same-worker loop at one valid epoch is entirely unfenced against itself.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: REPRODUCED OR REFUTED BY RUN: two stamps against the same row at the same held epoch, on DIFFERENT criterion indices, issued concurrently; then read the PUBLISHED row and state whether both landed. Paste both commands, both read-back lines and the published acceptance_criteria array. A single-threaded loop does not discharge this - the two writes must actually overlap.

If reproduced: the criteria write is made safe against a lost update - name which mechanism ships (per-criterion patch, a rev CAS on the stamp write, or a row-level lock) and why the others were rejected. If refuted: the row closes with the run output and the concurrency window that IS closed is named from the code.

A regression test pins the chosen behaviour and is MUTATION-PROVED: disarm the fix, show the test reds, restore. AMENDED 2026-09-05 by lead-ledger-3, on the lead's ruling, from an original that additionally required the test to CONSTRUCT THE OVERLAP rather than assert the guard in isolation. That form is not satisfiable by any correct implementation under the Ecto SQL sandbox, so it was a defective criterion rather than an outstanding obligation. Both ownership modes fail it for opposite reasons: {:shared, pid} serialises every process onto ONE checked-out connection, so a second stamper QUEUES behind the first instead of racing it and the test would pass with the advisory lock deleted -- a vacuous green; :manual gives each process its OWN transaction, so the task row inserted by setup is invisible to the second stamper and the race cannot even be set up. The amended ask is what is actually provable in-suite: a SQL-shape oracle on the statements the stamp emits, mutation-proved, PLUS the out-of-suite concurrency run that supplies the overlap. The residual -- an in-suite two-connection overlap test, which needs a harness outside the sandbox -- is filed as its own row and is NOT discharged here.
MERGE-GATED (the lead closes this): the PR is merged to main with the required gates green on its head, and the merge sha is recorded.

corpus.title: Fix deploy_runner_test.exs:581 flake — hermetic cd so main is reliably green

content.description:
ANCHOR SLICE, Felix Pristine Wave 11 (epic task-96a908af98698118, Paper felix-pristine-wave-2026-07-16). This flake reds `main` under the full parallel api/ Elixir suite and forces admin-merges on every .ex PR. Make it reliably green.

MECHANISM (verify-fleet SETTLED — the original env-leak brief was REFUTED, do NOT chase it): the test `test/barkpark/sites/deploy_runner_test.exs:581` ("the default node engine script is deploy/site-deploy-node.sh (argv, not env)") does `put_cfg(enabled: true)` then triggers a node rollback for slug rt-default. `command_for(:rollback, :node)` (deploy_runner.ex:358) returns the UNCHANGED shipped default `{"bash", ["deploy/site-deploy-node.sh", "--rollback"]}` (deploy_runner.ex:78), and `run_cd` (deploy_runner.ex:374) = `Path.dirname(File.cwd!())` = repo root, where the REAL script exists. On Linux CI (flock present) the real script runs, logs `[site-deploy-node ...] no live route for 'rt-default' (not_supported)`, and NEVER echoes its own path — so `assert Enum.any?(status.log, &String.contains?(&1, "deploy/site-deploy-node.sh"))` (line 593) is STRUCTURALLY UNSATISFIABLE. It is order/seed-INDEPENDENT (two CI seeds 584655/706849 gave identical output). macOS passed by ACCIDENT (no flock → bash's `flock: command not found` error is prefixed with the script path). `config()` is read LIVE from Application env every call (deploy_runner.ex:134) and never enters GenServer state — so `delete_env`/reset-singleton fixes NOTHING and is forbidden churn.

FIX (HERMETIC, test-file-only, ~14-line diff): give line-581's config a scriptless cwd — `put_cfg(enabled: true, cd: scriptless_tmp)` where `scriptless_tmp` is a fresh `File.mkdir_p!`'d tmp dir that does NOT contain `deploy/site-deploy-node.sh` (clean up in on_exit). `run_cd` honors `config[:cd]` first, so bash runs from there, cannot resolve the relative `deploy/site-deploy-node.sh`, and prints `bash: deploy/site-deploy-node.sh: No such file or directory` (path present) DETERMINISTICALLY on EVERY host — the real script never runs. Keep the shipped @default command UNTOUCHED (the test's whole point is to prove the SHIPPED default names the node script — argv, not env). Do NOT weaken the assertion; ADD a negative assert that the log does NOT contain `not_supported` / `no live route`, proving the real script did not execute. Add a one-line comment tying `cd:` to why it is load-bearing (a future drop of the :cd override silently reverts to non-hermetic). This also restores the file's own moduledoc contract (lines 5-6: "Stub commands only, never the real deploy/site-deploy.sh").

SIBLINGS ARE OUT OF SCOPE (verify-fleet proved benign): do NOT touch self_update/runner_test.exs or provisioner_test.exs — every one of their behavior tests overrides the exact key it asserts on, so there is no default-reliance a leaked prior could green-wash. Improvement-only forbids hardening clean files.

BUILD DISCIPLINE: worktree off origin/main, isolated `MIX_TEST_PARTITION` (never drop shared barkpark_test), `CC=/usr/bin/clang`, opus. Commit to your worktree branch only; steward pushes + PRs. DISJOINT from concurrent cloud-build W6/W7 — touch ONLY api/test/barkpark/sites/deploy_runner_test.exs.

RED-BEFORE / GREEN-AFTER on macOS (no flock): simulate Linux by putting a fake `flock` on PATH that exits 0: `FB=$(mktemp -d); printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > "$FB/flock"; chmod +x "$FB/flock"`; then `PATH="$FB:$PATH" mix test ...` reds on origin/main and greens with the fix (also run plain, no fake flock, to prove macOS still 36/0).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: RED-BEFORE reproduced deterministically: on origin/main, running `test/barkpark/sites/deploy_runner_test.exs:581` under a Linux-equivalent fake `flock` on PATH (a script exiting 0) fails at line 593 with the real-script log `no live route for 'rt-default' (not_supported)` and no `deploy/site-deploy-node.sh` string in the log.

Hermetic fix applied test-file-only: line-581 uses `put_cfg(enabled: true, cd: <scriptless tmp>)`, the shipped @default_node_rollback_command is UNCHANGED, the log-contains-`deploy/site-deploy-node.sh` assertion is preserved, and a NEW negative assert proves the log does NOT contain `not_supported`/`no live route`. `git diff --stat` shows only deploy_runner_test.exs changed.

GREEN-AFTER host-independent: with the fix, `CC=/usr/bin/clang MIX_TEST_PARTITION=<slice> mix test test/barkpark/sites/deploy_runner_test.exs` is 36 tests / 0 failures BOTH under the fake-flock PATH (Linux-equiv) AND plain (macOS, no flock).

No collateral / siblings untouched: `mix test test/barkpark/sites/deploy_runner_test.exs test/barkpark/sites/provisioner_test.exs test/barkpark/self_update/runner_test.exs` all green; the diff touches no lib/ source and no sibling test.
MERGE GATE (lead closes): PR merged to origin/main and the full parallel api/ Elixir CI suite runs green on the merge commit — this flake no longer forces an admin override.

corpus.title: W6.2 · Instance rollback API — POST /v1/admin/rollback with sync preflight + async Port run

content.description:
Self-update W6 (charter .claude/workflows/bp-self-update-w5-charter.md W6 D15; the W6 Contract section is BINDING — W6-S3 builds the CP relay against these exact shapes in parallel).

Add POST /v1/admin/rollback to the instance API, sibling of the existing self-update trigger: same /v1/admin scope, same [:api, :require_admin] pipeline (api/lib/barkpark_web/router.ex:1537-1541), same BARKPARK_SELF_UPDATE_APPLY feature gate (503 feature_not_configured when off).

CONTROLLER (extend api/lib/barkpark_web/controllers/self_update_controller.ex with a rollback/2 action — keep the update family in one controller): (1) enabled? check → 503 {error:{code:"feature_not_configured"}}; (2) run the preflight SYNCHRONOUSLY: System.cmd("bash", ["deploy/instance-deploy.sh", "--rollback-preflight"], cd: <repo root — same cwd derivation the Runner uses: parent of the BEAM cwd>) and map exit codes per the W6 contract: 21→409 {error:{code:"no_previous_slot"}}, 22→409 {error:{code:"not_supported"}}, 23→409 {error:{code:"already_running"}}; (3) exit 0 → parse TARGET_SHA=<40-hex> from stdout, then trigger the ASYNC run and answer 202 {status:"started", target_sha: sha}. Make the preflight command injectable (app env / opts) exactly like the Runner's command is, so tests fake it with a stub script — never run the real deploy script in tests.

RUNNER (api/lib/barkpark/self_update/runner.ex): add a rollback trigger that opens the same OS Port machinery running 'bash deploy/instance-deploy.sh --rollback', SHARING the single-flight run state with self-update (one run slot for both verbs — a rollback during an update returns :already_running and vice versa). Reuse the bounded 500-line log; GET /v1/admin/self-update status should show the run (include a mode: "rollback"|"update" field in the status payload — additive, tolerant consumers).

Async failure semantics: the script exits 24 (unhealthy_fail_closed) — that surfaces via the status/log endpoint, NOT the 202. Do not fake a sync success/failure for the flip itself.

Schema-stays-forward copy (D19): any human-facing message quotes the law — rollback is app-level only, schema stays forward.

TESTS: extend api/test/barkpark_web/controllers/self_update_controller_test.exs (and runner tests under api/test/barkpark/self_update/ if needed) with the existing stub-command idioms: 202 happy (parses TARGET_SHA, spawns run), each 409 mapping, 503 when disabled, single-flight collision (rollback during running update → 409 already_running).

GATE (dry-run green at Decide, 20/0): cd api && CC=clang mix test test/barkpark_web/controllers/self_update_controller_test.exs test/barkpark/self_update/checker_test.exs — run YOUR new tests plus these. .ex change → PR WAITS for the Elixir Test CI gate before merge. Worktree from origin/main after git fetch; claim first; PR body carries 'Task: isu-w6-instance-rollback-api'.

Sync preflight mapping proven by tests: exit 21/22/23 -> 409 no_previous_slot/not_supported/already_running; exit 0 -> 202 {status:started, target_sha} with sha parsed from TARGET_SHA=
Async run shares single-flight with self-update (collision test both directions) and reuses the Port+log plumbing; status payload carries mode
cd api && CC=clang mix test test/barkpark_web/controllers/self_update_controller_test.exs test/barkpark/self_update/checker_test.exs green including new tests

corpus.title: Audit the 7 remaining async:true Cloud test modules that swap node-global Application env

content.description:
Discovered while fixing gr-p5-cloud-flake (commit 05b222825). The proven flake was ONE async:true module globally swapping :site_box_relay. Seven other async:true modules under cloud/test also call Application.put_env on node-global keys, each of which is a latent version of the same race the moment a second async module starts reading that key: billing_reconcile_isolation_test.exs (Billing), cloudflare_test.exs (Cloudflare), github_test.exs (GitHub), oauth_test.exs (OAuth), vercel_test.exs (Vercel), web/router_test.exs (:platform_admin_emails), web/usage_route_test.exs (:usage_fanout_budget_ms). Today each key is read only by its own module (two of them carry comments showing the author reasoned about exactly this), so none is a live red — do NOT churn them blindly. The work is: for each, decide whether the seam can be passed per-call/per-process (the owner-keyed fake pattern in test/support/sites_fake_box_relay.ex) instead of through app env, and where it can, do it; where it genuinely cannot, add the key to @shared_seam_keys in cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/async_global_seam_guard_test.exs only if a second reader appears. SECOND, UNRESOLVED ITEM: the p5 survey reported cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/cloudflare_standalone_degrade_test.exs as a co-failing file. It did NOT reproduce in ~15 full-suite runs after the :site_box_relay fix (8 consecutive random-seed runs all 2107/0), and it is async:false so it cannot run concurrently with the async offenders. Best current read: it was collateral of the relay-stall timeouts. If it ever reds again, capture the seed AND the full failure output before assuming this task explains it.

--- PREMISE REFUTED (Honest-Gates epic, Decide 2026-07-20) ---
This task's premise — "today each key is read only by its own module, so none is a live red" — was ALREADY FALSE AT FILING TIME for TWO keys, not one.
OAuth: router_oauth_test.exs (async:true) reads the swapped config INDIRECTLY through the router (router.ex:909 OAuth.enabled?/1), which is why a direct grep for co-readers finds nothing. Reproduced deterministically.
Cloudflare: site_cf_deploy_test.exs was added 2026-07-15, FOUR DAYS BEFORE this task was filed, and drives the live deploy path through Cloudflare.client() with no process scoping; a two-Task probe showed a read during the swap window resolves Real and returns {:error, :http_client_not_configured}, breaking its assert conn.status == 201.
Also: the census is 8 swappers in cloud/test, not 7 — registry/cloudflare_credential_test.exs was missed.
Billing IS safe, and safe by construction rather than by luck: FailingRegistry delegates to the real Registry for any process lacking :billing_reconcile_isolation_fail_id in its own dictionary. Vercel is safe by VALUE (its swap always sets the safe default). :platform_admin_emails is safe by IDENTITY (the allowlist is the test's own random email). :usage_fanout_budget_ms is safe only because its population is one file, and its in-file defence reasons about TIMING rather than scope — the weakest of the five.
SUPERSEDED BY hg-w1-async-seam-ban-and-scanner, which bans the shape rather than auditing keys.

corpus.title: The Astro flagship stops shipping 577 KB to a viewport it has already hidden — asserted at 390px, with a desktop-positive control

content.description:
D79. OBSERVED IN A REAL BROWSER, not inferred. At a true 390x844 mobile emulation the deployed Astro flagship issues 11 requests including bp-graph.js (140,221 B) and graph.json (436,769 B) = 576,990 B, while matchMedia('(min-width: 768px)') is FALSE and getComputedStyle('#bp-graph-slot').display is literally 'none'. slotChildren is 1: the React portal mounted GraphPane into a hidden element and GraphPane's mount effect appended the script tag.

CAUSE. index.astro:49 hides the slot in CSS ONLY (`class="hidden min-w-0 flex-1 md:block"`), and FinderIsland.tsx's useGraphSlot resolves it by document.getElementById alone with NO matchMedia anywhere in the hook, so :348 portals GraphPane whenever the element exists. GraphPane.tsx:51-60 loadRendererScript then appends <script src=base+'bp-graph.js'> to document.head.

THE FIX IS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN IN THE OTHER EDITION. templates/search-starter/components/desktop-only.tsx:38-44 documents this exact defect in code: 'CSS display:none does NOT stop that script from downloading and executing, but never mounting it does.' It gates on useSyncExternalStore(matchMedia) with getServerSnapshot()=false so the subtree is absent from initial HTML. Apply the same MECHANISM to the Astro island — gate the PORTAL on a media query, not the CSS. Do not import from templates/search-starter (different tree); write the small hook in the astro tree OUTSIDE src/finder/ (src/finder/ is BYTE-LOCKED by scripts/check-astro-finder-drift.sh and must not gain files).

THE BEAT. Add a sixth PHONE beat to tooling/search-smoke/journey-smoke.mjs — do NOT build a new harness. It is already raw CDP against --headless=new with zero npm deps, Network.enable is already sent at :284, and its --self-test already boots healthy/rotten/dead-socket fixtures and asserts the exact expected reds, so the mutation proof is native. Assertion: at a 390x844 device-metrics emulation, after load and settle, ZERO Network.requestWillBeSent URLs match /bp-graph\.js|graph\.json/.

MANDATORY PAIRING — WITHOUT THIS THE BEAT IS A FALSE SEAL. Nobody has measured the Astro graph at >=768px. A PHONE beat alone can ship GREEN over a graph that is dead at every width, which is exactly the failure class this epic keeps correcting. The beat MUST be paired with a desktop-positive assertion: at >=768px the same page DOES request bp-graph.js and the graph renders. The control is proven non-vacuous on the Next edition (390 -> zero matching requests; 1440x900 -> GET bp-graph.js [304], mdMatch true), so the pair is known to be able to fail in both directions.

HONEST LIMIT to state in the harness header: 390 comes from CDP Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride, not a real window (chrome-devtools resize_page floors at 500px). That is the same mechanism a CI beat uses, so it is the right fidelity — but it is emulation, not a phone.

STAY OUT OF: src/finder/** (byte-locked), GraphPane.tsx and graph-normalize.ts (stw11-provenance-line owns those), and .github/** (D85b).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The Astro graph portal is gated on a media query rather than CSS alone, in a file OUTSIDE src/finder/, so the renderer script is never mounted below the md breakpoint

A DESKTOP-POSITIVE assertion is paired with it: at >=768px the same page DOES request the renderer and the graph mounts, so the phone beat cannot pass over a graph that is dead at every width

corpus.title: A muted team stops permanently spending its trial-expiry warning on a notice that was never sent

content.description:
Charter D600 binds this slice; read it on origin/main before you start.

THE DEFECT, measured by RUNNING on a freshly dropped/created/migrated test DB, not by reading.
`TrialExpiryWorker.maybe_notice/5` calls `claim_notice/3` — an
`UPDATE teams SET trial_notice_3d_sent_at = now WHERE id = $1 AND trial_notice_3d_sent_at IS NULL` —
and only THEN calls `notify/3`. The stamp only matches NULL, so it can never re-fire: it is the
warning's entire budget and it is spent BEFORE anything is proven sent. `perform/1` returns
`{:ok, run(...)}` unconditionally and `dispatch_event/3` is `@spec ... :: :ok` with a blanket rescue,
so Oban's `max_attempts: 3` never fires either.

TWO ARMS, AND ONLY ONE IS YOURS. The CRASH arm is already half-fixed and you must not re-litigate it:
`dispatch_event/3`'s rescue writes a `suppressed` Delivery row and the console renders it as a
first-class "Withheld" badge with its own filter chip (`app.js:3390/3408/3648`). Any framing of "the
crash leaves no trace" is refuted at build time.

THE MUTE ARM IS YOURS, and it is the surfaceless one. `should_send?/2`'s `alerts_enabled: false`
clause short-circuits BEFORE the rescue can run, so nothing raises and NO withhold row is written.
Proven: a globally muted team burns BOTH stamps in one run — `stamp_1d` and `stamp_3d` set by the
same call, because the T-1 arm claims the 3-day stamp too — `delivery_rows_total = 0` at any status
including suppressed, and un-muting one minute later recovers nothing
(`run2_after_unmute = %{noticed_3d: 0, noticed_1d: 0}`). Neither `trial_notice_3d_sent_at` nor
`trial_notice_1d_sent_at` has ANY reader anywhere in `cloud/lib` or `app.js` outside the worker's own
claim, so no surface — member, admin or operator — can ever show a consumed-but-unsent warning. A
team that mutes alerts on Monday and un-mutes on Wednesday has already spent both trial warnings and
the destructive teardown proceeds on schedule.

WHAT THIS BREAKS THAT IS SUPPOSED TO BREAK. `@always_send ~w(test trial_expiring)a` exists precisely
because "a trial-ending heads-up is important enough to bypass the per-event opt-in toggle". The
stamp burn defeats that ruling from underneath.

THE FIX — entirely inside `cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/workers/trial_expiry_worker.ex`. Do NOT touch
`notifications.ex`; do NOT widen `dispatch_event/3`'s return type (that is a public-contract change
the lead has not ordered, and every producer currently ignores the return). Instead: before claiming
ANY stamp, read the team's `EmailSettings` and, when the team cannot receive the alert at all
(`alerts_enabled: false`), claim nothing and count nothing — the budget survives the mute and the
next hourly run after an un-mute delivers the warning. Prefer the existing public accessor over a
new one; if none exists, read the settings row directly rather than adding a seam to Notifications.
Also stop the T-1 arm from claiming the 3-day stamp on a run that sends nothing: the supersede is
only legitimate when a 1-day notice actually went out.

THE TEST YOU MUST REWRITE, and it is the reason this slice is not routine.
`cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/workers/trial_expiry_worker_test.exs` currently PINS the defect as
intended behaviour, with a comment reading "The worker still CLAIMS the notice (the stamp is the
idempotency key, not a delivery receipt) — what must not happen is a delivery", followed by
`assert {:ok, %{noticed_3d: 1}} = perform_job(...)` and `assert notice_count(team.id) == 0`. You are
reversing a documented prior decision. Rewrite that test and its comment to the new contract, and say
so PLAINLY in the PR body — do not silently delete an inconvenient assert.

OUT OF SCOPE, filed separately, do not build here: the teardown emits no event of its own (there is
no `trial_expired` event anywhere in the vocabulary) and the console's unconditional
"We'll remind you 3 days and 1 day before the trial ends." copy — that copy row is
`cch-w50-s5`, already open.

HIGH-FLIP-RISK (E2): the key judgment is BEHAVIOURAL EQUIVALENCE for the un-muted path — that adding
a settings read before the claim does not change idempotency, ordering, or the happy path under
concurrent hourly runs. An independent re-derivation of that judgment is owed before merge.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `maybe_notice/5` reads the team's notification settings BEFORE any `claim_notice/3` call and claims NOTHING when the team cannot receive the alert (`alerts_enabled: false`). Evidence: the diff, plus a test asserting both `trial_notice_3d_sent_at` and `trial_notice_1d_sent_at` are still nil after a run against a muted team inside the T-3 window.

The T-1 arm no longer claims the 3-day stamp on a run that sends nothing — the supersede fires only when a 1-day notice actually went out. Evidence: a test showing a muted team inside the T-1 window leaves BOTH stamps nil (today it burns both in one call).

RECOVERY IS PROVEN: a team muted during the T-3 window, then un-muted, receives the warning on the next run. Evidence: a test running the worker muted (0 notices, 0 stamps), un-muting, running again, and asserting `noticed_3d: 1` plus exactly one Delivery row.
THE HAPPY PATH IS UNCHANGED: an un-muted team still claims once, delivers once, and a second run is a no-op. Evidence: the pre-existing un-muted assertions still pass unmodified.

The test that PINNED the defect as intended behaviour is rewritten, not deleted around: the comment 'the stamp is the idempotency key, not a delivery receipt' and its `assert {:ok, %{noticed_3d: 1}}` are replaced by the new contract. Evidence: the diff hunk.

The PR body states in its own paragraph that this slice REVERSES a documented prior decision recorded in that test's comment, and why the prior reading was wrong (the stamp is a one-shot budget with no reader and no second chance).

No file outside `cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/workers/trial_expiry_worker.ex` and its test is modified — in particular `notifications.ex` is untouched and `dispatch_event/3`'s `:ok` return type is unchanged. Evidence: `git diff --name-only origin/main`.
The worker suite is green. Evidence: `cd cloud && CC=clang mix test test/barkpark_cloud/workers/trial_expiry_worker_test.exs` output pasted, with the test count named.

corpus.title: PUT blob answers with bytes RECEIVED, never bytes stored — Blobstore.put_bytes returns a bare :ok

content.description:
HIGH-FLIP-RISK: the obvious cheap fix is a PROVEN FAKE GREEN. An independent second reviewer is owed before merge.

FIRST, CORRECT THE FILED WORDING. put_bytes is NOT "a bare :ok on an exit code" — S3 gates on HTTP 2xx and Local on File.write's syscall (charter PDS-D310). Writing "reports success on an exit code" is refutable in one grep and must not appear in the PR. The honest claim is RECEIVED vs STORED with NO POST-CONDITION READ.

THE TRAP, PROVEN BY RUNNING AGAINST A BLACK-HOLE BUCKET (200 on PUT, stores nothing):
- `File.stat(Media.file_path(rel))` returns {:ok, %File.Stat{size: 11}} — it PASSES with the exact expected byte count — because S3.put_file warm-caches the SOURCE bytes to that exact path.
- WORSE, the obvious defensive move is a SECOND fake green: S3.ensure_local/1 short-circuits on File.regular? and returned {:ok, path} with ZERO bucket requests. "Read it back through the abstraction" is also fooled.
- The bucket is provably empty: drop the cache copy and ensure_local = {:error, :not_found}.
So the read-back MUST bypass the warm cache. Do not put it in Media.put_blob (which lives above the backend seam, in the same module as Media.file_path — exactly where a builder reaches for File.stat).

THE HONEST SHAPE: a NEW per-backend Blobstore callback (today's behaviour has exactly five — put_file/put_bytes/delete/ensure_local/serve_strategy — there is no stat/head, so this is an add, not a reuse). Local -> File.stat on the real store. S3 -> a presigned HEAD that BYPASSES the warm cache. Presign.url/4 takes the method as a plain string and puts it as line 1 of the canonical request, so HEAD needs NO new signing code; proven against a stub bucket to return 200 + content-length for a stored key and 404 for a never-written key.
ETAG IS THE CHEAP TIER, NOT THE HONEST ONE. The PUT response's ETag is DISCARDED today (request/3 matches only on status). When present it equals the md5 hex and can verify client-side with no extra round trip; when absent Req yields []. It is absent under SSE-KMS and multipart and is provider-dependent, so the receipt CANNOT be designed assuming it. Shape: {:ok, %{received: n, stored: n | :unverified, verified_by: :etag | :head | :stat, unverified_reason: <named>}} — degrade to a NAMED :unverified, NEVER silently reuse the received count. Note for the record: an ETag is response-backed (class A2), strictly weaker than a HEAD post-condition read.

THE CONTRACT CHANGE HAS THREE EXACT-:ok GATES AND THEY MUST LAND IN ONE COMMIT: S3.put_file's `with :ok <- put_bytes(...)` (a receipt falls through VERBATIM and SKIPS warm_cache), Media.upload/3's `:ok <- Blobstore.put_file(...)` (its else-list has NO catch-all, so a receipt RAISES WithClauseError -> a bare 500, violating the module's own moduledoc), and Media.put_blob's case (CaseClauseError). Both raises were reproduced.
COVERAGE HOLE YOU MUST CLOSE: only ONE test file in the repo sets backend: :s3 and it NEVER calls Media.upload/3 — all 47 Media.upload sites run under :local. So the media.ex x S3 path that RAISES has ZERO coverage. Add an s3-backed Media.upload/3 test in this PR or the gate is vacuous.

RECEIPT WORDING: keep `bytes` meaning RECEIVED (the CLI compares against it today — do not repurpose the key) and ADD a distinct stored claim. A read-back that DISAGREES is a named non-2xx, not a 200 with a discrepancy field.
ADJACENT, FIX OR FILE: the PUT-blob receipt's `written` field carries a PATH STRING, not a byte count, sitting next to a field named `bytes` — an invitation to exactly the misreading this epic exists to kill.
COST: a HEAD per blob doubles round trips on bundle import (the crown proof moved 34 blobs). State the cost rather than discovering it in the crown rehearsal.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A NEW per-backend read-back callback exists; the S3 implementation is a presigned HEAD that BYPASSES the warm cache — proven by a test in which the bucket is empty but the warm-cache file exists, and the read-back FAILS (a File.stat-based check would pass, and that is demonstrated as the trap)
The receipt distinguishes RECEIVED from STORED and degrades to a NAMED :unverified with a reason when neither ETag nor HEAD is available — it never silently reuses the received count
All three exact-:ok call sites (S3.put_file, Media.upload/3, Media.put_blob) are updated in the same commit; a test proves Media.upload/3 no longer raises WithClauseError on the new return shape
An s3-backed Media.upload/3 test exists — the path that raises had ZERO coverage before this PR, and the PR states that
The PR does NOT claim put_bytes 'reported success on an exit code' (it is a write-ACK: S3 on HTTP 2xx, Local on File.write); the claim made is RECEIVED-vs-STORED with no post-condition read
Gate green: cd api && CC=clang mix test test/barkpark/media/blobstore_local_test.exs test/barkpark/media/blobstore_s3_test.exs

corpus.title: bp task landed marks a row landed but leaves its criteria met:false — the label and the criteria disagree and nothing reconciles them

content.description: CHILD of task-14eac58b39fd3692, split per main's routing: the ledger lane owns the readiness-filter half, the cli lane owns this one. THE SHAPE. bp task landed writes a landed:pr-NNNNN@sha label (plus landed-on-main) onto a row whose acceptance_criteria are untouched. Nothing then reconciles the two, so a row can say 'this shipped in PR 15560, an ancestor of main' in its labels while every criterion still reads met:false. A lead reading the criteria dispatches it as fresh work; a builder returns 'already fixed'. That is the burn this family of rows is about. MEASURED 2026-09-05T13:1xZ by lead-ledger-3 against guerrilla: 21 of 1,658 rows in bp task ready carry a landed:pr-* label, and NINE of them are at ZERO criteria met — the shape most likely to be mistaken for untouched work: task-076719e53a42102d (0/4, pr-15403), task-0a48c7b64d5ab0f1 (0/2, pr-15732), task-10fe06277f2858e4 (0/3, pr-15717), task-5e88e691e0d6e31d (0/6, pr-15613), task-75afc025fa0ad872 (0/3, pr-14963), task-d2f355bf53765120 (0/4, pr-15621), task-dd37cc248363e633 (0/3, pr-15465), task-e428b30fb9b2d4c7 (0/3, pr-15909), task-f56d553a70a4bba8 (0/5, pr-15505). WHY THIS HALF IS NOT THE SAME AS THE FILTER HALF: a readiness filter hides the row from the queue but leaves the ledger still asserting two contradictory things about it, so every later reader — a census, a rollup, a human — inherits the contradiction. The label is a claim about the world; the criteria are the evidence for it. Only the verb that writes the first is in a position to settle the second. ONE CONSTRAINT FROM THE SIBLING WORK, so this does not overreach: a merge-gated criterion is the LEAD's to stamp at close, and PR #15602 established that a met-flip after close rewrites the verdict the close sealed. So whatever this verb flips, it must not flip a merge_gate criterion on the builder's authority, and it must not touch a row already terminal.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A DECISION IS RECORDED before code on what bp task landed should do to criteria: flip only the merge-shaped ones, flip nothing and instead REFUSE to label a row whose criteria contradict the label, or write the landed fact into a field the readiness query already reads. State the rejected options and why. A verb that leaves two fields contradicting each other is the defect, so doing nothing is not one of the options.

WHATEVER SHIPS IS PROVEN BY TEST, red-without and green-with, on a row constructed in the measured shape (a landed:pr-* label with met:false criteria). MUTATION-PROVED: disarm it and the test reds again.

THE MERGE-GATE FENCE HOLDS: a criterion carrying merge_gate:true is NOT flipped by this verb, and a terminal (done/cancelled) row is not touched at all. Both asserted directly, because a met-flip after close rewrites the verdict the close sealed (PR #15602).

THE NINE MEASURED ROWS ARE RECONCILED or explicitly triaged one by one — each either has its criteria settled, or is recorded as genuinely unfinished despite the label with the reason. A fix that leaves the measured population untouched has cured the mechanism and not the damage.

corpus.title: bp task ready and bp task get return different row shapes, and the difference manufactures a confident zero

content.description:
`bp task ready` and `bp task get` return DIFFERENT row shapes for the same task, and the difference is silent in the direction that manufactures a confident zero.

MEASURED by lead-cloud-c5, 2026-09-07, against guerrilla, 1502 ready rows over two pages.

THREE CONCRETE DIVERGENCES.

1. `lifecycle_status` IS PRESENT ONLY ON NON-READY ROWS. Of 1502 rows, 21 carried it (all `blocked`) and 1481 OMITTED IT ENTIRELY. So the natural filter — keep the rows whose `lifecycle_status == "open"` — returns EXACTLY ZERO, and zero from a 1502-row list is indistinguishable from a lane with no work. A lead applying it would report "lane dry" and stand down with 1481 rows in front of it. Absence means ready; presence means NOT ready. That inversion is nowhere in `docs/setup/TASK-SYSTEM.md`.

2. THE READY ROW IS FLAT AND ITS `content` IS EMPTY. `bp task ready` emits `doc_id`, `priority`, `title`, `claim`, `child_count`, `criteria_met`, `criteria_total`, `labels`, `parent_id`, `updated_at` at the TOP level, with no `content` object. `bp task get` nests the same facts under `doc.content` and names the id differently. A reader written against `get` (looking for `id` and `content.priority`) prints `None` for every field of every row while the titles come back correctly — which reads as missing DATA rather than a wrong KEY.

3. THE ENVELOPE KEY DIFFERS BY VERB. `bp task ready` returns `{"docs": [...]}`; `bp doc ls tag --all` returns `{"documents": [...]}`. A pager keyed on the wrong one writes zero rows and exits 0.

WHY THIS IS THE EXPENSIVE CLASS. All three are the failure mode where the command SUCCEEDS, the value is CORRECT for the question the field actually answers, and no error is raised — so no positive control catches them, and the output is a tidy number a lead will act on. Compare `docs/setup/TASK-SYSTEM.md:58`, which DOES warn that `bp task get` nests criteria under `doc.content.acceptance_criteria` and that "a reader walking the top level sees an empty row". That warning exists because someone already paid for it once. The same sentence is owed for the ready-list shape, and it is missing.

RELATED, SAME FAMILY, ALSO UNDOCUMENTED: the acceptance-criterion text lives under the key `criterion`, not `text`. A reader using `text` prints N criteria with empty strings — which looks exactly like a row filed with no criteria, the very thing a triaging lead is scanning for.

NOT A SERVER BUG. The shapes are defensible individually; the defect is that the CONTRACT is unwritten, so every reader re-derives it by being wrong first. The fix is documentation plus one machine-checkable example, not an API change — changing the wire shape now would break every existing reader.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: docs/setup/TASK-SYSTEM.md states, in the ready/ls section, that `lifecycle_status` is OMITTED on ready rows and present only when the row is NOT ready, and says explicitly that filtering for =='open' returns zero. Evidence: the committed sentence.

The same doc records that `bp task ready` rows are FLAT (doc_id/priority at top level, no `content` object) while `bp task get` nests under `doc.content`, and that acceptance-criterion text is keyed `criterion`, not `text`. Evidence: the committed text naming both key sets.

A machine-checkable example ships with it so the contract cannot rot silently: a script or test that reads a real ready page and ASSERTS both arms in one run — a ready row has no `lifecycle_status` AND a blocked row has one — and REFUSES loudly (distinct CANNOT READ line, non-zero exit) on an empty or unparseable page, so a failed read is never byte-identical to a pass.

corpus.title: Ledger has no back-link from a discharging PR to the OTHER rows it satisfies — five silent sibling discharges in one day

content.description:
SYSTEM DEFECT, measured FIVE times on 2026-09-06 across four lanes: a criterion on row A was silently DISCHARGED by a PR opened under row B's trailer, and row A never learned. Instances: (1) clk-bl-idempotency-preview-token-sweeps-have-no-caller's Idempotency half landed in ea4fc7bc5 / #16070 under a SIBLING trailer; (2) arpss-w10-bl-member-only-predicate-drift-pairs C2 was already true on main, satisfied by a sibling PR that even cites it; (3) studio's c7 was discharged by task-f559f7c508527010, done since 2026-08-22; (4) task-432c858369909088 was substantially discharged by #16521 (a security PR under a different trailer); (5) pds-w40-bl-item-share-silent-noop's error-path half was discharged by arpss-item-share-revoke-unscoped-revoke. In every case a lead re-triaged, or a builder was dispatched, to re-derive a finished thing.

ROOT: the ledger has NO back-link from "the PR that discharged a criterion" to "the OTHER rows whose criteria that PR also satisfies". The only link is the one Task: trailer on the PR, which credits exactly one row. A row keeps advertising work that no longer exists; `bp task ready` and `bp task get` show met=false with no hint that origin/main already holds the fix. The failure direction is the expensive one: a stale UNMET reads as work, and costs a full re-derivation to refute (measured: a lead grepping `def` for a `defp` symbol concluded "already fixed" — the SAME class from the other side).

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT (properties, not mechanism — the builder reads the ledger code): a merged PR that names more than one row (trailer PLUS body citations, `Task:` plus `Also-satisfies:` / `Refs:` lines, or a `bp task link <pr> <row> --criterion N` verb) leaves a durable, readable mark on EVERY named row — visible in `bp task get` and `bp task show` beside the affected criterion, as "possibly discharged by PR #N (sha) under row X; verify against origin/main" — WITHOUT stamping met=true (a triage verdict may route, not close; only the row's holder decides). And the lead brief's own recipe ("before dispatching, re-verify the criteria against origin/main") stops being a memorised discipline and becomes a field a reader can see.

SCOPE GUARD: this is the ledger/task system (api/lib/barkpark/tasks + the bp CLI's task verbs). It is filed by lead-security because security hit it, but it belongs to whichever lane holds api/lib/barkpark/tasks and internal/cli. Do not solve it with a doc line in the brief — that is what has been failing.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A merged PR that cites a second row (by a documented body/trailer form or a bp verb — the builder picks and documents ONE form) leaves a readable mark on that second row, visible in `bp task get <id>` beside the criterion it names, carrying the PR number, merge sha and the primary row id. Evidence: a real row on the prod ledger showing the mark, and the command that produced it.

content.description: REQUEST from gates-w16 (task-2e16f1390ffc064f, PR #14993 push-to-main landing workflow), measured live on guerrilla 2026-09-02 with a read,write token and no claim: (1) POST /v1/tasks/:id/stamp is unusable from CI — check_holder then check_fencing refuse 409 not_holder, and holder_override exists only on close; (2) POST /v1/data/mutate patch on a task resolves its base through the DRAFT spelling (Content.Mutations.get_patch_base/4 -> DraftId.draft_id) — measured on task-71762fd1bf152e49: mutate with the task API's rev -> 412 (actual = the draft's rev); with the draft's rev -> 200 results[0].id = drafts.task-…; a fresh GET /v1/tasks/<id> unchanged. Any CI or agent that patches a task through mutate gets a 200 and writes nothing anyone reads — pr-task-gate.yml's hotfix-override createIfNotExists may be landing invisible override records the same way (unverified); (3) stage's note clobbers disposition_reason; (4) labels work and are what shipped. Requested: POST /v1/tasks/:doc_id/landed {commit, pr, note, criterion|null}, write-tier token, NO claim, NO epoch; unions commit/pr/note into content.landed the way Tasks.Close.merge_landed/2 unions prs/files/capability_slugs; when criterion is given AND that criterion's own text is merge-shaped (/pr\s+merged|merged\s+to\s+main|merged\s+into\s+main/i or Criteria.merge_gated?) AND it is not already met, sets met=true with note as evidence; refuses any other index and never overwrites an already-met criterion; emits task.landed with the caller token id. corpus.title: Merge-gated acceptance criteria don't carry merge_gate:true — the automation that would stamp them can never fire

content.description:
THE TRAP, FOUND ON THE CROWN ITSELF. `api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex:344` `autostamp_merge_gate` auto-flips criteria carrying `merge_gate: true` when the close supplies a non-empty `landed`. `pds-w1-crown-proof`'s criterion 10 reads "PR merged to main (LEAD closes this criterion on merge)" and its keys are exactly `['criterion','evidence','met']` — no `merge_gate` field at all. So it will NEVER auto-stamp. A wave that assumes the merge closes it waits forever on an automation that cannot fire, and the task sits at 10/11 looking mysteriously stuck (PDS-D140).

THIS IS SYSTEMIC, NOT ONE TASK. Every wave in this repo files a criterion worded "PR merged to main (LEAD closes this criterion on merge)". Audit how many carry the flag. The likely answer is approximately none, which means the feature exists and has never been used.

TWO HONEST SHAPES, PICK ONE AND SAY WHY: (a) make the authoring path set `merge_gate: true` whenever the criterion text matches the merge-gate convention, so the flag follows the wording; or (b) drop the wording convention and require the flag explicitly, failing the authoring gate when a criterion says "PR merged" without it. (b) is stricter and less magical; (a) is kinder to existing tasks. Do NOT do both halves half-way — a convention that is sometimes load-bearing is worse than either.

Whichever way it goes, the outcome must be that a lead who merges a PR and closes with `landed` sees the merge criterion flip, or gets told plainly that they must stamp it by hand.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An audit reports how many existing tasks carry a merge-gate-worded criterion WITHOUT merge_gate:true. Evidence: the count and the query that produced it.

One of the two shapes is chosen, implemented, and its rationale recorded — the convention is either wired to the wording or replaced by an explicit required flag, never left half-wired. Evidence: the decision paragraph plus the diff.
A test proves a lead close with a non-empty `landed` actually flips the merge criterion under the shipped rule. Evidence: the test name plus green output.
TASK-SYSTEM.md documents the shipped rule so future task authors get it right by default. Evidence: the doc diff.
PR merged to main (LEAD closes this criterion on merge).

corpus.title: An open p0 row with a vacant (released) claim is refused by claim as not_ready - readiness predicate disagrees with the row, control row of identical shape claims fine

content.description:
MEASURED 2026-08-23 ~16:35-16:50Z against guerrilla. task-ed7ae8110c7c8b41 (tenancy import-membership-grant, priority 0, lifecycle open, _draft false, blocked_by/depends_on/twin_of/engagement/disposition ALL null, assignee null, claim RELEASED cleanly: worker=null, released_at=2026-08-20T17:32:26Z, released_by=worker-import-grant, epoch 5, NO expired_at key) is UNCLAIMABLE:

  bp task claim task-ed7ae8110c7c8b41 go-tree-triage        -> rc=6 not_ready (reproduced twice, 10 min apart)
  bp task claim task-ed7ae8110c7c8b41 worker-import-grant   -> rc=6 not_ready (the released worker cannot re-enter either)
  bp task ready --limit 500 (priority order)                -> row ABSENT, despite priority 0 (cap caveat: exactly 500 rows returned, but a p0 row should sort into any top-500)

CONTROL that isolates the shape: task-039938a48b952aeb carries the SAME claim shape (worker null + released_at, no expired_at) and claims+releases fine (rc=0, epoch 4->bump). So the released-claim shape is NOT the blocker; something row-specific excludes task-ed7ae8110c7c8b41 from the readiness predicate, and the not_ready hint ("someone else holds it") is FALSE for this row - nobody holds it.

Board-wide census from a 500-row open snapshot: 25 open rows carry released-only claims, 50 carry expired-only; both shapes have members that claim fine, so the fourth-shape hypothesis (released blocks) is REFUTED - filed here so the next agent does not re-derive it.

WHY IT MATTERS: this row is 6/7 with its PR (#12837) MERGED - it is exactly the built-work-waiting-on-one-proof class the board prioritizes, and the ONLY remaining criterion (live E2E bp cloud workspace import --with-blobs) cannot even be attempted honestly because stamp is holder-only and claim refuses. The readiness bug thus silently withholds the cheapest real win on the board AND blocks recording the honest miss. Sibling shapes already filed: task-f07ead0c1f8025bb (open+held claim deadlock), pds-w43-bl-stale-claim-third-shape (worker+closed_at). This is a DISTINCT shape: open + VACANT claim + not_ready.

Server-side predicate lives in api/ (Barkpark.Tasks readiness/claim path) - out of the Go-tree lane, filed for the api owners.

SECOND INDEPENDENT SIGHTING, same day, DIFFERENT claim shape - recorded by the lead.

I hit not_ready on cch-w41-bl-the-remaining-five-local-authority-copies-consume-the-server-fact while unblocking PR #13154. That row was NOT vacant-claim: it was in a MIXED state - lifecycle_status "open" while claim.worker still named "cloud-lane-agent", epoch 1, ts 2026-08-23T07:51:24Z. The pr-task-gate diagnosed it precisely and refused rather than falling open, saying: "that mixed state does not come from the claim/close engine (a reap nulls the worker)."

WHAT SEPARATES THE TWO CASES, and it is the useful part:
- claiming as a DIFFERENT worker ("lead") -> not_ready, the same refusal this row reports;
- claiming as the ORIGINAL named holder ("cloud-lane-agent") -> rc=0, lifecycle flipped to in_progress at epoch 2, and the PR gate then passed on re-fire.

So at least one not_ready is produced by a stale-but-present claim.worker rather than by readiness, and the CLI's own hint ("if YOU hold it, re-claim with your own worker id to renew") is the working escape - but only if you can work out who "you" is, which nothing in the refusal tells you. The refusal names neither the holder nor the reason, so the caller cannot distinguish "someone holds it" from "it is not ready" from "you are the wrong worker".

TWO CONCRETE ASKS FOR THE PREDICATE OWNER, beyond the root cause:
1. Make not_ready SAY which arm refused - held-by-<worker> vs not-ready vs wrong-worker. Three different remedies currently share one word.
2. Explain how a mixed state (open + non-null claim.worker) is reachable at all. The gate asserts the engine cannot produce it, so either a partial write does, or that assertion is wrong. This matters beyond claiming: 50 of today's 463 closes were found half-written in the sibling way (lifecycle terminal, disposition unset), which suggests the write path can land one field without the other more generally.

Also of record: the pr-task-gate warns that RELEASING such a claim afterwards is unrecoverable - release merges released_at into the surviving claim and never touches expired_at (apply_release_update/2), so released_at >= expired_at trips an ordering clause at pr-task-gate.sh:462 that no re-fire can clear, only a fresh claim. I therefore left the claim held. Anyone triaging this bug should not "tidy up" by releasing.


ROOT CAUSE FOUND, 2026-08-23. THIS IS NOT A WRITE-PATH DEFECT. A full-corpus audit (7,051 rows, every lifecycle status paged) found ZERO write-path defects, and named the actual cause:

**`bp task stage` is a THIRD WRITER, and it is not bound by the claim/close engine's invariants.** Its own help states the write set NEVER includes `content.claim`, deliberately - "the false-done reopen recipe DEPENDS on reopening a done task; it legitimately re-enters the ready backlog via stage, KEEPING its claim." Its legal edges include done→open, cancelled→open, blocked→open AND in_progress→open. So staging any of those to `open` moves `lifecycle_status` while leaving `claim.worker`, `closed_by`, `closed_at` and `close_reason` exactly where they were.

EVIDENCE, NOT INFERENCE: of the 9 corpus rows in this exact shape, **7 carry stage's OWN durable fields** (`disposition` / `disposition_reason` / `disposition_rerun`). This row is that shape.

SO THE DEFECT IS IN THE READER, NOT THE WRITER. `pr-task-gate.sh` asserts "that mixed state does not come from the claim/close engine (a reap nulls the worker)". That assertion is **TRUE AND INCOMPLETE** - it is scoped to claim/close, and `stage` is simply not covered by it. The gate then refuses a legitimately-staged row as corrupt. That is what cost this row hours of a blocked merge, and it is why the remedy that worked was re-claiming under the ORIGINAL holder rather than any repair.

CORPUS CONTEXT so nobody re-opens this as a data-integrity scare: three invariants hold with ZERO violations across all 7,051 rows - `released_at >= expired_at` (the gate's permanent-refusal ordering is real, documented, and currently UNREALIZED), `claim.worker` set with no `claim.epoch` (the fencing pair is never half-written), and `in_progress` with `claim.worker` null. A separate 89-row shape traces to ONE batch on 2026-07-23 and has not recurred since.

REMAINING ASK ON THIS ROW is unchanged and still worth doing: make `not_ready` SAY which arm refused - held-by-<worker> vs not-ready vs wrong-worker. Three different remedies currently share one word, and the caller cannot tell them apart.

corpus.title: Does bp task stamp print its success receipt from the returned document or from the request it sent? The server side is already pinned; the CLI side is not

content.description:
SPUN OUT of task-70e6ba4aaf0480b3, which was cancelled after triage rather than closed on a root cause nobody found.

THE OBSERVATION, measured 2026-09-02 by lead-silent on the live ledger: two bp task stamp --met calls each printed "the store holds it - criterion index N: met=true evidence NNN bytes". A bp task get seconds later, and again minutes later, showed BOTH criteria met=false with evidence of ZERO bytes. The writes never landed. It surfaced only because the following close refused with "acceptance criteria 2, 3 are not met on the task AS STORED".

WHAT TRIAGE ESTABLISHED, so this row starts from a narrower place:

1. The SERVER cannot produce that receipt over a missing write. api/test/barkpark/tasks/receipt_honesty_test.exs asserts, for stamp specifically, that the rendered receipt equals the rendered STORED row on every key, naming the divergent keys on failure. If the transaction did not commit, no {:ok, doc} is returned at all.

2. A met stamp with ZERO-BYTE evidence cannot be created through the verb: build_update/4's met clause requires a non-empty binary and otherwise refuses evidence_required. So the reported symptom is a write that NEVER LANDED, not a write that landed empty. That rules out the reading most people take from the title.

So the remaining question is entirely on the CLI side, which is why this row is filed into the cli lane rather than the ledger's: does the Go CLI render "the store holds it" from the DOCUMENT the server returned, or from the request it sent? If from the request, the line is a restatement of intent wearing the costume of a receipt, and every worker in this campaign reads it as confirmation.

THE OPERATIONAL RULE UNTIL THIS IS ANSWERED, which is worth keeping even after: a stamp receipt is not evidence. Re-read the row and confirm met plus evidence length before closing.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Establish by reading the code which source the "the store holds it" line is rendered from: the document in the server's response body, or the request the CLI sent. Quote the function and the field it reads. This is a finding either way and discharges even if the answer is that it already reads the response.

If it renders from the request: it renders from the returned document instead, and prints a refusal naming the criterion index when the returned document does not carry the met flag and non-empty evidence it just claimed. Mutation-proved with a seam returning a document whose criterion did not change.

A test pins whichever behaviour ships and fails when the read-back is removed. If the answer to criterion 1 is that it already reads the response, the test pins THAT, because the guarantee is currently carried by nothing.
MERGE-GATED (the lead closes this): the PR is merged to main with the required gates green on its head, and the merge sha is recorded.

corpus.title: POST /v1/tasks/:id/landed silently drops the files field the schema accepts, and the merge-shaped criterion flip has no server-side overlap check - the client-side half shipped in #17345, the server half is the tasks/landed.ex owner's

content.description: Measured 2026-09-10 by gates-w3r4 while building task-c3c9922e7d8e3815 (PR #17345 b2e2b80ce): content.landed accepts a files key (api/lib/barkpark/tasks/internal.ex:603 @landed_keys) but Barkpark.Tasks.Landed.record/2 builds its write from digest(commit, pr, note), so a files field in the POST body is silently dropped and returns 2xx - the changed paths reach the ledger only inside the note string, which no reader can query. And the --criterion flip (merge-shaped criteria, bp task landed --criterion N) is permitted server-side whenever the wording is merge-shaped, with no check that the landing's paths overlap anything the row names; #17345 withholds the OFFER client-side but a direct caller can still flip. Invariant wanted, not mechanism: (a) a files list posted to /landed is stored on the landing and read back verbatim (bounded: list, or count + top-level dirs past 40), never dropped without a refusal; (b) a --criterion flip whose landing carries files that overlap none of the paths/areas the row's title, description or criteria name is refused with a reason naming the row, the PR and the paths compared, and a flip with overlap still succeeds (positive control). Filed by lead-gates-r4; routed to the api tasks owner (not the gates fence).

Both arms are tests in api/test and both are mutation-proven (drop the overlap check -> the refusal arm reds, the control stays green)

corpus.title: Auto-stamp the merge-gate criterion at close so no wave hand-patches the ledger

content.description: Kill the recurring ledger toil at the tool: the final LEAD-CLOSED merge-gate criterion is left met=false at builder-close time (Mode B, intentional — builders can't know a PR is merged) and every wave a reviewer hand-patches it. Auto-stamp it at close. SEAM (verify-proven): bp task stamp CANNOT touch a done task ({:not_in_progress,"done"} -> 409, the ledger is sealed by close), so the ONLY working seam is close.ex apply_close_update. DESIGN (conservative, verify-mandated): identify the merge-gate criterion by an EXPLICIT '"'"'merge_gate'"'"': true marker on the criterion entry (author-set) — NOT a text/last-entry/index heuristic (proven unreliable: only 14/34 Felix children carry '"'"'MERGE GATE'"'"' as the last-entry substring). In apply_close_update, when new_status is terminal (done) AND a non-empty landed map is present (the LEAD merge close — a builder pre-merge close carries no landed, so Mode A is NOT recreated) AND the marked criterion is still met=false AND the caller'"'"'s criteria payload did not already touch that index, inject a synthetic {index, met:true, evidence} into the criteria list so it rides the SAME merge_criteria + rev-CAS write. Composed evidence = worker_id + claim.epoch + landed.prs/commit + ts_iso. Pure server-side, derived from data already flowing -> ZERO OpenAPI drift, no bp CLI change (close-route survey: landed/criteria already ride the generic passthrough, never surface in the OpenAPI requestBody). Branch from ORIGIN/main; isolated worktree; CC=/usr/bin/clang. Mode-A hardening is a SEPARATE backlog task (task-felix-stamp-index-guard) — do NOT scope it here.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An explicit merge_gate:true marker on an acceptance_criteria entry is what close.ex uses to identify the merge-gate criterion — NO text/last-entry/index heuristic anywhere in the path.

apply_close_update auto-stamps the marked criterion met=true with composed evidence (worker + claim.epoch + landed PR/commit + ts) ONLY when new_status is terminal AND a non-empty landed map is present AND the criterion is still met=false AND the caller criteria payload did not already touch that index.

FAIL-BEFORE: a done-close with landed leaves the merge_gate criterion met=false without the fix; WITH the fix it flips to met=true carrying the composed evidence string. The fail-before/after pair is green under CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test test/barkpark/tasks/close_test.exs.

CONSERVATIVE negatives: a builder pre-merge close (no landed) and a criterion WITHOUT the marker are NOT auto-stamped (negative test green); no OpenAPI drift (git diff docs/openapi.json empty — server-side only, no new args).
MERGE GATE (lead-closed): PR merged to origin/main with a green Elixir gate.

corpus.title: Merged PRs with a Task: trailer leave their row open — the merge stamps nothing and the builder's release strands the seal

content.description: MECHANISM, measured by lead-reconcile on 2026-09-01 across the P1 ready backlog: a PR lands on origin/main with 'Task: <id>' in its squash body, every criterion the PR proves is verifiable from the tree, and the row stays lifecycle open with assignee = the builder's worker name (L3-csp-floor, cloud-gh-secret, fix-flat-default-scope, ...) and NO live claim. Nothing in the merge path writes to the ledger: scripts/bp-merge.sh / gh pr merge squash the branch, the Task: trailer is read by the PR-task gate only as a presence check, and the builder — told to 'report, not close' — releases or lets the claim lapse. The seal is owed to a lead who never arrives, so the next lane spends a worker re-triaging a finished row. THREE OF 27 EXAMPLES (all closed by lead-reconcile from the tree today): task-b68092d5bac508e0 <- PR #14368 (1249e81bc2, Task trailer, merged 2026-09-01, row open with assignee lead9-cloud, epoch 8, no claim); task-9009e2e4f0e5b5b6 <- PR #14362 (fc0900fbb2, merged 2026-08-31, assignee L3-web-listen-perspective); task-076ca42e29836029 <- PR #14458 (3b34f91fcd, merged 2026-09-01, assignee cloud-domain-guard). Of the first 18 rows with a Task-trailer PR on main, 14 were in this state; 27 rows were sealed by hand this session and 9 more were part-stamped. WHAT A FIX LOOKS LIKE (decide, do not assume): either the merge path stamps a 'merged as <sha>' fact onto the row (a ledger write keyed on the Task: trailer, holder_override on the record), or the lead brief makes 'seal on merge' a required step with a check that lists open rows whose Task: trailer is on origin/main. This row asks for the mechanism decision plus the listing instrument; it does not ask anyone to close rows by hand.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An instrument exists (script or bp verb) that lists open task rows whose id appears in a Task: trailer of a commit on origin/main, and it reproduces at least the three example rows above when run against the ledger state of 2026-09-01T20:00Z (or a documented equivalent fixture).

A recorded decision names which side owns the seal after merge — the merge script writing a merged-as fact to the row, or the lead brief requiring the close with the instrument as its checklist — with the reason the other side was not chosen.

Whichever side is chosen ships: either scripts/bp-merge.sh (or the PR-task gate) writes the merge fact to the row on a squash merge, mutation-proven by a merge whose row does not carry it turning the check red; or LEAD-BRIEF/TASK-SYSTEM.md carries the seal-on-merge step and the instrument, and a lane run shows zero open Task-trailer rows at its end.

corpus.title: A zero-criteria row gets criteria BEFORE it is claimed — the missing check is at CLAIM time, not close time

content.description: REPLACES zero-criteria-is-a-legal-bypass-of-the-close-gate, cancelled 2026-09-02 because the close-time gate it asked for already shipped: check_close_artifact/5 (api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex:681) refuses a done close of a zero-criteria task row whose reason names no PR+sha and pastes no run, 409 close_reason_needs_artifact, with ten assertions in api/test/barkpark/tasks/close_artifact_test.exs. So the close door is shut. THE FINDING THAT SURVIVES IS A DIFFERENT KIND. A row with zero acceptance criteria is one whose done state can be attested ONLY by artifact and never by criterion. That is a legitimate shape for a decision or a goal, and a bad shape for work: the artifact says something landed, it cannot say what the row was FOR. Main measured roughly 172 open rows in that state. Catching it at close is too late by construction — by then the work is done and the only honest options are an artifact reason or a cancel, so the criteria that would have defined success are written, if at all, after the fact by whoever is trying to get the row shut. THE CHECK BELONGS AT CLAIM TIME. A builder claiming a criteria-less work row should be told, at the moment it costs nothing, that this row states no acceptance criteria and asked to add them first — the point in the lifecycle where the criteria still shape the work rather than describe it. That is a different door from the close gate and does not weaken it. OPEN QUESTIONS THIS ROW MUST DECIDE, not assume: whether the claim is REFUSED or merely WARNED (about thirty agents drive this verb daily and a new refusal is a new way to be blocked, so the bar for refusing is high); which kinds are exempt, reusing close_artifact_exempt?/1's vocabulary rather than inventing a second list (non-task kinds, decision/goal label segments, rows with children); and whether an existing warn-only instrument already covers this and was ignored — Plugins.Tasks.warn_if_create_zero/1 is a Logger.warning whose only reader is the server journal, and close.ex's own comment records that it fired on 9 of 11 rows and changed nothing, which is the strongest argument in the file against shipping another warning.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: THE POPULATION IS DERIVED, NOT ESTIMATED: a run over the live ledger counts OPEN rows with kind:task, zero acceptance_criteria, and none of close_artifact_exempt?/1's exemptions (non-task kind, decision/goal label segment, has children). State the number and the denominator, and record the command so anyone can re-run it. Main's ~172 is the figure to check, not to inherit.

A DECISION IS RECORDED BEFORE ANY CODE on whether a claim of such a row is REFUSED or WARNED, with the reasoning and the rejected option. It must engage with the evidence already in close.ex that a Logger-only warning (Plugins.Tasks.warn_if_create_zero/1) fired on 9 of 11 rows and changed nothing — if the answer is a warning, say what makes THIS one reach a human when that one did not.

THE EXEMPTIONS ARE SHARED, NOT REINVENTED: whatever ships reuses close_artifact_exempt?/1's vocabulary rather than declaring a second list, so the two doors cannot drift into disagreeing about what a container is. Evidence: the call site.

PROVEN BY TEST IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: a claim of a criteria-less work row hits the new behaviour, and a claim of each exempt shape (decision label, goal with children, non-task kind) does NOT. MUTATION-PROVED: disarm the check, show the test reds, restore. A check that also fires on the exempt shapes has replaced the rule rather than implemented it.

THE EXISTING DOORS ARE UNTOUCHED: check_close_artifact/5 still refuses what it refused, and its ten assertions in close_artifact_test.exs stay green. A claim-time check that buys itself room by loosening the close gate trades one hole for another.

corpus.title: bp doc publish on a claimed task silently drops the claim and reopens the row; close-after-stamps 409s until a re-claim

content.description:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 ~09:30Z by lead-security-6 on guerrilla, while writing acceptance criteria onto a row it held.

THE SEQUENCE
  1. bp task claim task-49b5c183f10ad0fc lead-security --yes      -> lifecycle in_progress, claim.worker lead-security, epoch 1
  2. bp doc patch task task-49b5c183f10ad0fc --set 'acceptance_criteria:=[...]' --yes   (draft written, rev f2677c9d)
  3. bp doc publish task task-49b5c183f10ad0fc --yes               (rev 33f0a390)
  4. bp task get task-49b5c183f10ad0fc  -> lifecycle OPEN, claim None, epoch None. The criteria landed; the CLAIM WAS GONE.

Nothing errored. The row silently fell back into `bp task ready` while its lead believed it held; only a read-back before dispatch caught it (re-claimed as epoch 1 again). The same shape hit the CLOSE path later: `bp task close` refused 409 doc_changed_since_claim three times in a row (era-scim-conformance-polish) because stamps between claim and close moved the rev, and the refusal's own hint (--set observed_rev=<rev>) then answered "close genuinely ABSENT … re-claim" — the close only landed after a re-claim for a fresh epoch. Two writers of the same document (the doc door and the task door) disagree about what a publish means for a claim.

WHY IT MATTERS: the lead brief's own recipe for a zero-criteria row is "write criteria, then dispatch" — patch + publish is the ONLY documented way to write criteria onto a published task. If publish drops the claim, every lead following the brief loses the claim exactly between writing the spec and dispatching the builder; a peer's `bp task next` can take the row in that window, and the lead's later stamp fails not_holder an hour later. A claim is the one thing the ledger promises to keep.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH (a builder reads the code, not this paragraph): whether `bp doc publish` on a type:task copies the draft's content wholesale over the published row (so `content.claim` and `lifecycle_status` are overwritten by the draft that was forked BEFORE the claim), or whether the patch itself forks a draft from a stale published rev. Either way the invariant is the same: publishing a doc patch that does not name claim/lifecycle fields must not change them.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A test reproduces the sequence claim -> doc patch (a field other than claim/lifecycle_status) -> doc publish on a type:task and asserts the published row still carries lifecycle_status in_progress and the same claim.worker and claim.epoch; the test REDS on today's main.

The fix names the mechanism (draft forked before the claim overwrote the live claim on publish, or whatever the code shows) in the PR body and in a comment at the write site, and the same protection covers every field the task door owns (claim, lifecycle_status, close_reason, closed_by) — enumerated from the task write path, not from this row.

The close-after-stamps path is covered: a claim -> stamp -> stamp -> close sequence by the same worker closes without a 409 doc_changed_since_claim, or the 409's hint text leads to a close that actually lands on the first retry (proven by a run pasting the refusal and the successful close).
