corpus.title: bp task landed cannot send a files manifest — the Go client has no --files flag to reach the server field

content.description:
Carried from lead-cli-r5's worker reports and re-filed here so it stops living in a scratchpad. `bp task landed` is the verb that records a merge against a row. The server side (api/lib/barkpark/plugins/tasks.ex) can carry a files manifest for the landing, but the Go client exposes no `--files` flag, so no caller can populate it. The consequence is that a landing records the sha and not WHAT it changed, which is exactly the information a later reader needs to decide whether a row's criteria are actually covered by the merge.

Related and already known: `bp task landed` flips merge-SHAPED criteria by WORDING, takes no claim/worker/epoch, and `"merge_gate": false` on a criterion is the one-field veto. Whoever adds --files should read that behaviour first, because a files manifest arriving alongside a wording-triggered autostamp is a second implicit input to the same decision.

FENCE: internal/cli (the flag + the request) and api/lib/barkpark/plugins/tasks.ex (the field, if it is not already there). Verify the server field EXISTS before building the client half — do not assume it from this description.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The server-side field is confirmed to exist (or added): a landing can carry a files manifest. Evidence: the field read back off a real landing, not the schema.
bp task landed accepts a --files manifest and the manifest arrives on the row. Evidence: the command run against a live row and the row read back showing the files.
The path can LOSE: with the flag wiring removed, a test reds naming the missing manifest. Evidence: the failing run and the passing run.

corpus.title: Two rows filed today duplicated defects that closed today — the filing path does not read the ledger before it writes

content.description:
MEASURED 2026-09-05 while hand-reading 45 ledger rows for routing. TWO of them duplicated work that closed the SAME DAY, and in both cases neither lead saw the other's row.

CASE 1. task-259bada0f2e65815 (filed 2026-09-03 by lead-studio-3r: two landed:pr-N rows sat at P1 in the ready head for days) and task-14eac58b39fd3692 (filed 2026-09-05, measured 21 of 1,658 ready rows carrying a landed label, nine at zero criteria met). Same mechanism, same consequence, two days apart, two leads.

CASE 2. pds-bl-stamp-silent-noop (a stamp returned success while the criterion stayed unmet; hypothesis: a lost update between a pulse and a stamp at one epoch) and task-bf3adebfec5833df (filed 2026-09-05 with the mechanism read off stamp.ex: the criteria array is read-modify-written and the epoch fence guards the CLAIM, not the array). Roughly a month apart.

THIS IS NOT A CRITICISM OF EITHER FILER. Both rows are good rows, honestly measured, and one of them was mine. The point is structural: if a row can be filed hours after its own defect is closed, the FILING PATH IS NOT READING THE LEDGER BEFORE IT WRITES.

WHAT MAKES IT MORE THAN AN ANNOYANCE. A duplicate is not only wasted filing — it is wasted BUILDING. Each of these could have sent a builder at a defect already fixed, and one of them nearly did: task-4dca6c8453fb1f7c was filed as the live remainder of case 1 only because a lead happened to hold both rows at once. The dedup wall exists and DID fire on a row I filed today at 0.3056 similarity, which is how a third duplicate was avoided — so the machinery is present and the question is why it does not reach these.

CANDIDATE MECHANISMS, none confirmed, and the row should determine which rather than assume: (a) the dedup wall scores on title/description similarity and these pairs describe the same DEFECT in different vocabulary ("landed:pr-N rows in the ready head" vs "rows already labelled landed"), so a shape-keyed defect escapes a name-keyed check; (b) the wall runs at create time only, so a row filed BEFORE the fix lands is never re-checked against later closes; (c) leads do not search the ledger before filing because the query verb is slow or the vocabulary is unguessable — bp task ls --match walks all pages and a full listing is ~30s over 8k rows, which is a real disincentive measured in cchi-bl-task-get-needs-a-server-side-prefix-lookup.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: THE POPULATION IS MEASURED, NOT INFERRED FROM TWO CASES: sweep closed rows and open rows for pairs describing the same defect, and state how many duplicate pairs exist and what the median gap is between the two filings. Two cases are an anecdote; the row needs a rate. State the denominator and the matching method, and say plainly what the method CANNOT catch.

THE ESCAPE MECHANISM IS DETERMINED, not guessed: for the two known pairs (task-259bada0f2e65815 / task-14eac58b39fd3692 and pds-bl-stamp-silent-noop / task-bf3adebfec5833df), run the dedup wall against each pair and quote the similarity it scores. If it scores them BELOW the threshold, the defect is that a shape-keyed duplicate escapes a name-keyed check and the remedy is not a threshold tweak. If it never ran, say why.

THE COST OF SEARCHING FIRST IS MEASURED: time the search a lead would actually run before filing. If it is slow enough to be a disincentive, that is a finding about the read path and links to cchi-bl-task-get-needs-a-server-side-prefix-lookup rather than about lead discipline.

WHATEVER SHIPS IS PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL: plant a row that duplicates an existing one in DIFFERENT vocabulary, show the check catches it, remove the duplicate, show it passes. A check that has never seen a real duplicate pair is a sentence with an exit code.

corpus.title: --merge-gated is an honour system that leaves no trace, and wave 56's own decide phase hit it

content.description:
AMENDMENT 2026-09-07 (lead-gates-3, on the orchestrator's ruling). NARROWED, NOT DISSOLVED — one of the three claims has gone stale under the row. Re-verified by content on origin/main, not by re-reading the filing.

CLAIM (c) IS STALE. The row says `--merge-gated` is "STRIPPED before dispatch, so the server never learns an override happened", citing `internal/cli/tasks_stamp_cmd.go:298`. On origin/main that code is at :539 and it is now CONDITIONAL:

    case "--merge-gated":
        sa.mergeGated = true
        if !mergeGatedDeclared {
            continue // legacy server: undeclared flag, never forwarded.
        }

So the flag is stripped ONLY against a legacy server that does not declare it. WHEN THE SERVER DECLARES `--merge-gated`, IT IS FORWARDED. `parseStampArgs` takes `mergeGatedDeclared bool` (:526) and the comment at :520 says so outright: "`mergeGatedDeclared` says whether the SERVER declares --merge-gated." The file header at :40 records the transition in the past tense — "It used to be a CLI-only flag guarding a…" — and :564 names the live guard as `Barkpark.Tasks.Criteria.merge_gated?/1` ON THE SERVER, with `merge_gated_criterion` a real server refusal code the CLI now handles (:87, :140).

CLAIMS (a) AND (b) ARE NOT REFUTED AND STILL NEED A SERVER-SIDE CHECK. That the flag now reaches the server says nothing about whether the server AUTHENTICATES the caller as entitled to override, or AUTHORIZES the override against anything. Forwarding a boolean is not checking it. Whoever takes this row should re-derive (a) and (b) against `Criteria.merge_gated?/1` and its callers rather than against the CLI, which is no longer where the decision lives.

WHY THIS AMENDMENT EXISTS RATHER THAN A CLOSE. The finding is real and the row should stay open. But its central sentence would send a builder at CLI code that no longer behaves the way the sentence describes, and the line number is 241 lines off — so the builder either concludes the row is wrong and drops it, or "fixes" a stripping behaviour that is already conditional. Both outcomes are worse than the row simply being narrowed here.

A NOTE ON THE LINE NUMBER, so nobody mistakes it for the defect: :298 -> :539 is LINE DRIFT, and line drift never refutes a premise. What refutes claim (c) is the `if !mergeGatedDeclared` branch, which is a behaviour change, not a move.

--- ORIGINAL TEXT BELOW ---

`internal/cli/tasks_stamp_cmd.go:298`: `case "--merge-gated": sa.mergeGated = true; continue // CLI-only: never forwarded to the server.`

The flag is a bare local boolean. It is (a) not authenticated, (b) not authorized, and (c) STRIPPED before dispatch, so the server never learns an override happened. The refusal text at :59 is an honour system in its own words: "Pass --merge-gated to override only if you are the lead closing the gate." One flag, any builder.

THE HALF THAT MATTERS MOST IS THE MISSING RECORD, not the missing check. Because the token is stripped, a lead-authorized stamp and a builder's override are BYTE-IDENTICAL in the store. Even a post-hoc audit cannot separate them. Any fix that only adds an authority check leaves this unsolved - the override must be RECORDED (forwarded as a server-side field, or written into the evidence string) before authority is worth checking.

LIVE ENCOUNTER, wave 56 decide: four wave-55 rows had every non-merge criterion met and their PRs merged with four green contexts, and bp CORRECTLY refused the stamp with `merge_gated_criterion`. Wave 56 DECLINED the override precisely because it leaves no audit trail - so four provable rows stayed open. The guard works; the escape hatch beside it does not.

SECONDARY, filed twice already and still unfixed on main: `isMergeGatedText` (tasks_stamp_cmd.go ~:330) is `strings.Contains(u,"MERGE-GATED") || strings.Contains(u,"MERGE GATED")` over the WHOLE criterion text, so the tripwire fires on any criterion that merely MENTIONS merge-gating. A guard that over-fires trains people to reach for the override that has no authority check - the two defects compound, and fixing the override alone makes the false-positive MORE painful. Fix both or neither.

FENCE WARNING (deploy-reliability D391, measured LIVE): `internal/cli/**` trips ZERO required gates, so a guard shipped here CANNOT LOSE IN CI. Any fix must land its proof somewhere a required context runs, or declare the path in a gate, or the fix is a sentence with an exit code.

=====================================================================================================
WAVE 57 AMENDMENT (2026-08-09) — charter D679. MEASURED LEDGER-WIDE; TWO CRITERIA ADDED.
=====================================================================================================
REALIZED, NOT THEORETICAL — AND THE REALIZED HALF IS THE RECORD, NOT THE AUTHORITY. Walking both epics by doc_id
(the trap: parent_id holds the SLUG, not the UUID in `id`; walking by `id` returns a family of 2 and a silent zero,
which is a BROKEN QUERY, not an answer): family 994, sanity total 453 criteria carrying the MERGE-GATED marker,
215 met — and ALL 215 sit on non-live rows; ZERO live rows carry a met merge-gated criterion.

THE SHARPEST FACT: **the server's merge-gate autostamp seam has NEVER FIRED ANYWHERE ON THE LEDGER.** Zero of 994
family tasks carry the STRUCTURAL `merge_gate: true` field the autostamp keys on; ledger-wide there are 16 such
criteria at met=true (all on pds-*/felix-*/cd-* rows) and NOT ONE carries `compose_merge_gate_evidence/4`'s signature.
The phrase "auto: lead-closed on merge" appears exactly ONCE in the entire 55MB roster — as PROSE inside the task that
BUILT the seam. close.ex:688 and the GitHub reconcile_merge_gate/3 bridge are dead code in production terms: every
merge-gate met-flip that has ever happened was hand-authored.

THE MITIGATION IS REAL AND SHOULD SHAPE THE FIX, NOT EXCUSE IT: 168 of the 215 name both a PR number and a merge sha,
46 name a sha only, 1 a PR only, and only THREE name neither — and the one substantive claim among those three checks
out on main. The CONVENTION held; the MECHANISM never did. So the argument is not that a builder COULD lie; it is that
this epic's 215-row done-record is UNAUDITABLE BY CONSTRUCTION. An authority check without a record buys nothing the
convention is not already delivering; a RECORD makes 215 rows auditable going forward. Criterion 0 already asks for
exactly that and is the right ask.

THE MISMATCH THAT EXPLAINS THE SIX STUCK ROWS: the CLI tripwire keys on the WORD in the criterion text, while the
server's honest autostamp keys on a structured `merge_gate: true` field. The stuck rows carry the TEXT convention and
not the field — which is why they need a hand-stamp at all.

THE SHAPE TO COPY IS ONE MODULE OVER: close.ex already ships holder_override / criteria_override as plain close-body
params (:82-83), composed by compose_override_record/3 (:469) and written as content.close_override on the SAME
rev-CAS write as the lifecycle flip (:566, merge_override_record/2 :630-637) — "an overridden close and its confession
land together or not at all", and params.ex:697-703 states the doctrine verbatim as an HONESTY gate, not authorization.
Genuine lead-vs-builder authority needs a role model that does not exist on tokens at all; honesty-gate parity with
close is the right ceiling for this row.

NOT CUT AS A WAVE-57 SLICE: api/lib/barkpark/tasks/** and internal/cli/** are both out of this epic's fence and need a
fresh numbered ADD; wave 56's six stuck rows are already filed at priority 0 under
cch-w56-bl-six-free-closes-await-a-lead-attestation.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An override is RECORDED: a stamp or close that used --merge-gated is distinguishable from one that did not, by reading the stored task alone. Evidence: two stored rows, one overridden one not, showing the difference.

NOT BUILDABLE AS WRITTEN — AND THE PRECISION MATTERS, BECAUSE THE BLANKET FORM OF THIS SENTENCE IS WRONG. A check keyed on the ASSERTED WORKER NAME is VACUOUS and always will be. A check keyed on the AUTHENTICATING TOKEN is a different question: the token is already threaded and stored (`tasks_controller.ex` passes `caller_token_id(conn)`, and the receipt records `authenticated_token_id`), so the plumbing exists — what is missing is anything to COMPARE it against. Amended 2026-09-08 on main's correction, which flagged the original headline as over-broad; the body below already drew this distinction but buried it, and a reader who stopped at the headline learned the over-broad thing. This criterion asks the override to "check authority against something the server can verify." There is nothing to check against TODAY. `worker_id` is a client-supplied body param — `close.ex`'s own header says the honesty gates are "HONESTY GATES, NOT AUTHORIZATION" and anyone who can call the verb can name any worker, so a check keyed on it is vacuous. `authenticated_token_id` IS unforgeable by the body and is a real audit anchor, but `Barkpark.Auth.ApiToken` carries only `permissions` and `kind` — there is no lead/reviewer/closer role anywhere in the schema to compare against, and it is `nil` for internal callers, so gating on it would fail open or break the webhook path. Recording it is the correct use; gating on it is not available today. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT BUILDABLE, so this is a deferral and not a dismissal: a role or scope on `api_token` (e.g. a `close:merge_gate` permission), plus binding the claim to the authenticating token id at claim time, so the close could assert "the same credential that claimed is the one sealing." That is a schema change and an auth-model decision, not a slice of this row. WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD is the honesty half: the override now leaves a signed receipt naming the asserted worker, the authenticated token id, the criterion and that nothing was verified — so the act is attributable and auditable even though it is not authorised. The same wall stopped cch-w65's actor axis, and both rows now say so in the same words.

THE TRIPWIRE ALREADY KEYS ON THE FLAG, MEASURED, SO THE ORIGINAL PREMISE IS SPENT. On the live server 2026-09-07, a criterion whose prose discusses merge-gating and carries an explicit `merge_gate: false` stamped cleanly at exit 0 with a plain `--met`, and the refusal on a real gate names its own detector: "DETECTOR: the merge_gate FLAG … this row is a DECLARED gate, so the refusal is NOT a prose false positive." So there is no over-firing to narrow where the flag is present. THE RESIDUAL, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT ROW'S SUBJECT: where a criterion carries no `merge_gate` key at all, the wide prose fallback still fires on wording alone. That undeclared population is owned by `bl-merge-gate-flag-backfill-two-directions` (deferred for this campaign: its criterion 2 is ~46 writes into other lanes' live rows). THIS CRITERION IS DISCHARGED BY MEASUREMENT PLUS THAT BOUNDARY — the detector needs no change; the population needs a backfill. Evidence of the boundary being real rather than asserted: this row's own eight criteria carried NO `merge_gate` key until 2026-09-08, when the holder declared them all false — a row describing the undeclared-criterion defect was itself an instance of it.
The proof runs where a required context can see it, or the PR body states which required gate now dispatches on internal/cli/** for this file. Evidence: the gate run or the declaration.

`bp task close --set 'criteria:=[…]'` is subject to the SAME merge-gate marker check as `bp task stamp`, or the stamp tripwire is decoration — the close path flips the identical met bit in one atomic write with no marker check today. Evidence: a mutation on a throwaway task showing the close path refused (or recorded) where it previously flipped silently.

The four wave-55 rows carrying the broken `close with --merge-gated` prescription (`cch-w55-s2` / `s3` / `s4` / `s5`, notes at `task.pulse` 190968 / 190969 / 190970 / 190971, all 2026-08-08T15:50:36Z) are ANNOTATED ON THE ROW'S OWN DESCRIPTION — the only durable surface writable on a terminal row — stating that the prescription is broken twice over: `bp task close` has no `--merge-gated` flag, AND the re-claim it opens with is refused on a terminal row (`not_ready`, "only [open, blocked] is claimable"), so the sequence cannot begin.

THE CLAIM NOTE ITSELF IS NOT TO BE CORRECTED AND NOT TO BE REACHED BY REOPENING THE ROW. A now-note cannot be written to a terminal row's claim (`not_in_progress:cancelled`, "Nothing was written: no now-line, no epoch bump"), and reopening four sealed histories to repair a note is a remedy costing more than the harm.

THE SURFACE CHANGED; THE TRIPWIRE DID NOT. This criterion still fails if any of the four carries an uncorrected broken prescription — that is the test of its own boundary, and rewording it to reach a DIFFERENT REMEDY remains forbidden. A prohibition without a test for its own boundary gets applied by vibe.

SUPERSEDED WORDING, PRESERVED: "corrected IN THE CLAIM NOTE, never by rewording the criterion" — recorded as MISSED at epoch 29 before this re-cut, on the writability evidence below. This criterion did not become payable because the work changed; it became payable because the mandated surface was proved dead and a durable one was named.

EVIDENCE: the annotation text on each of the four (verified against stored text, byte deltas recorded), plus the writability test on disposable probe row `task-64a240372c57ecc0` — precondition asserted (`cancelled` before the question), positive control (a now-note written to a LIVE claim, read back verbatim), negative control (impossible token absent).

CARRIED from duplicate cch-bl-merge-gated-override-cannot-tell-a-lead-from-a-builder: the CURRENT hole is demonstrated by run first — a stamp refused with merge_gated_criterion, then the identical command plus --merge-gated succeeding against a criterion whose carrier PR is NOT merged; both outputs quoted.

CARRIED from cch-bl-merge-gated-override-cannot-tell-a-lead-from-a-builder: a legitimate lead close on a genuinely merged, fully-green carrier still succeeds — the fix does not strand real arrears sweeps.

content.description:
ROUND 1. NO CODE DEPENDENCIES. This is Standing Law 0's residue obligation, not housekeeping: a wave may not end with more live rows than it began, and eight rows are carrying merged work as open debt.

THE EIGHT, each with its carrier PR MERGED and its merge sha an ancestor of origin/main, and all four required contexts green on the PR HEAD (read on HEADs with --paginate, never on merge commits):
  1. cch-w54-s2-suspension-closes-the-three-mint-and-reveal-paths - in_progress 8/9, #10848, merge 4a26d181b. Claim was LIVE at epoch 5.
  2. cch-w54-s6-decommission-sweeps-dns-by-value-not-by-name - in_progress 8/9, #10851, merge 981ee6f51. Claim was LIVE at epoch 5.
  3. cch-w54-s7-the-ledger-arrears-pays-twenty-five-rows - open 8/10, #10852, merge 9b8e75f55.
  4. cch-w54-s8-the-guard-suite-refuses-an-absent-object-database - open 7/8, #10853, merge 5d07f73e8.
  5. cch-w49-bl-required-checks-drift-calls-its-own-job-blocking - open at 2/2, ZERO unmet criteria. Rode #10728 (merge 7907b78e9). Pure bookkeeping debt nobody scheduled.
  6. cch-w51-bl-two-factor-and-identity-changes-leave-no-audit-trail - open at 4/4, ZERO unmet criteria. Rode #10727 (merge 8af8c2adf). NOTE its claim note cites commit 71a288c49, which is NOT an ancestor of origin/main (a stale pre-rebase sha) - stamp with 8af8c2adf / head 017170cd0, never 71a288c49.

SPARED, NOT CLOSED - and this is the part a careless sweep gets wrong:
  7. cch-w53-s4-sign-out-everywhere-ends-the-live-stream - open 10/11, #10849 merged.
  8. cch-w53-s6-oauth-exchange-stops-skipping-two-factor - open 10/11, #10850 merged.
Their criterion 11 is NOT a bare merge gate. Each reads "HIGH-FLIP-RISK - warrants a genuinely INDEPENDENT second reviewer" on a named judgment (session-revocation scope for s4, refusal shape for s6). Closing them on the merge sha alone would stamp a criterion whose actual condition was never met - the exact false-done class this epic exists to prevent. Record them in the receipt as SPARED with the reason, and leave them open for the lead.

THREE MECHANICAL CONSTRAINTS. Get these wrong and the sweep silently does nothing.
  (a) CAPTURE `claim.now` BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANYTHING. A re-claim WIPES that field. Read and record all eight notes first; they are the only surviving record of what each builder said it did.
  (b) SIX OF THE EIGHT CARRY A LAPSED CLAIM (`claim.worker` is null with `claim.previous_worker` preserved). Closing on the PRINTED worker/epoch FAILS THE CAS SILENTLY. The recipe is already filed at `cch-w47-bl-four-merged-round-1-rows-all-need-a-re-claim-not-just-one`: re-claim on `claim.previous_worker`, READ THE NEW EPOCH BACK from the re-claim response (epochs bump on re-claim - any epoch quoted in this brief is PRE-re-claim and must NOT be passed to close), then close, with re-claim and close as ADJACENT calls because leases lapse on a ~15-minute timer. Rows 1 and 2 read as LIVE claims and may close directly on their own worker; a 409 there means the lease lapsed between the read and the write and is EXPECTED - fall back to the same recipe.
  (c) `cch-w54-s7`'s criterion 8 (live <= 340) is ARITHMETICALLY UNREACHABLE: it was set against a 365 baseline (365-25) while the true pre-sweep baseline was 382, so the floor available to a 25-row sweep was 357. Close that row with criterion 8 stamped as an honest MISS (`--miss --note`), never flipped. Its own receipt already records this, and the shape fix is filed as `cch-bl-live-count-criteria-must-be-deltas-not-absolute-floors`.

RE-DERIVE THE CENSUS YOURSELF AT FIRST CLAIM AND AGAIN AT THE END. Concurrent sessions file continuously, so any number in this brief is stale the moment it is written. At the time of writing the roster read 363 live of 725 published (open 362 / in_progress 2 / considering 1; done 317, cancelled 45). Quote the seal predicate's own denominator: published children only, `drafts.*` excluded.

THE RECEIPT. Write ONE file, `tooling/grip/ledger/cch-w55-arrears-2026-08-08.md`, carrying: the eight captured `claim.now` notes verbatim; per row the carrier PR, its merge sha, the ancestor check, the four required contexts on the HEAD, and the exact close command used; the two SPARED rows with their reason; and the before/after census with the command that derives it. Touch nothing else under `tooling/grip/`.

DO NOT close any row whose carrier you did not verify merged, and do not close on the N-1 heuristic alone - seven of thirty rows in a prior sweep were genuinely stranded work, not bookkeeping.

--- DO NOT FOLLOW THIS ROW'S CLAIM NOTE (annotated 2026-09-08 by lead-ledger-c5) ---

THIS ROW'S CLAIM NOTE PRESCRIBES A COMMAND THAT CANNOT WORK. The note is recorded at task.pulse id=190971, 2026-08-08T15:50:36Z, recoverable from mutation_events (walk from id 0 with --payload; a bare --limit returns the OLDEST events and will not find it). Its closing sentence reads:

    "LEAD CLOSES: re-claim, then close with --merge-gated."

IT IS BROKEN TWICE OVER, both measured 2026-09-08:

 1. `bp task close` HAS NO `--merge-gated` FLAG. The close-path overrides are criteria_override, holder_override, ack_override and close_reason_override. The flag exists on `bp task stamp`, not on close.
 2. THE RE-CLAIM IT OPENS WITH IS REFUSED ON THIS ROW. A terminal row is not claimable: `bp task claim` returns rc=6 not_ready — "lifecycle_status is \"done\"; only [\"open\", \"blocked\"] is claimable." So the sequence cannot even begin.

DO NOT FOLLOW IT. Nothing about this row needs the override; the instruction was written on 2026-08-08 by a worker escalating a merge-gated criterion to its lead, and the escalation was correct — only the command it named was wrong.

WHY THE NOTE ITSELF WAS NOT CORRECTED, WHICH A READER SHOULD NOT MISTAKE FOR THE JOB BEING DONE. cch-w56-bl-merge-gated-override-has-no-authority-check-and-no-record criterion 5 requires these notes be corrected IN THE CLAIM NOTE and forbids rewording the criterion to reach a different remedy. A now-note CANNOT be written to a terminal row's claim: `bp task pulse` returns rc=6 not_in_progress, and the server says "Nothing was written: no now-line, no epoch bump." Verified on a disposable probe row created, claimed and closed for the purpose, with the precondition asserted and both controls firing.

SO c5 IS RECORDED AS A MISS AND REMAINS UNPAID. This annotation does not discharge it. It protects the next reader of THIS row while the criterion's mandated surface stays dead; main refused reopening these four rows to reach it, on the grounds that a remedy costing four reopened histories is out of proportion to the defect. The re-cut of c5's remedy is routed to main and is not this lane's to write.

corpus.title: `bp --set <unknown-key>=…` exits 0 and stores nothing — an operator who put their justification on the record did not

content.description:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 while free-closing pds-w25-round-terminal. THE EXACT INVOCATION:

  bp task close pds-w25-round-terminal bare-rows-w27 1 cancelled "<reason>" \
      --set criteria_override="<why the 8 criteria are not stamped>" --yes

IT RETURNED EXIT 0 (rev d2c8d578c8b1ec3b6c99e4c29821fc68) AND THE VALUE IS NOWHERE ON THE DOCUMENT. A published-perspective read back shows the full stored key set, and `criteria_override` is absent from it:
  _createdAt, _draft, _id, _publishedId, _rev, _type, _updatedAt, acceptance_criteria, assignee, claim,
  close_reason, description, disposition, disposition_owner, disposition_reason, disposition_rerun,
  github, kind, lifecycle_status, main_tag, parent_id, priority, tags, title, wave_paper
`[k for k in doc if 'override' in k.lower()]` returns []. The key does not exist on the schema at all.

WHY IT WAS UNNEEDED HERE, WHICH IS THE POINT RATHER THAN THE EXCUSE: the close targeted lifecycle `cancelled`, and a cancelled close does NOT gate on unmet acceptance criteria. Only a `done` close does. THE CONTRAST IS FROM THE SAME SESSION, ONE HOUR EARLIER: closing pds-bl-hzresdone-registry-row-vacuous `done` at 0/4 was REFUSED with 'acceptance criteria 0, 1, 2, 3 (0-BASED) are not met on the task AS STORED, and criteria flipped in this very close command do not count — that would be the closer grading its own homework. Stamp them as you prove them, or close over them on the record: --set criteria_override="<why it is done anyway>"'. So the CLI itself advertises the flag, and there is a real path where it is load-bearing.

THE DEFECT IS THAT THE OPERATOR CANNOT DISTINGUISH 'NOT NEEDED' FROM 'SILENTLY DROPPED'. Both look like exit 0. I only learned which had happened by reading the document back and enumerating its keys. The case where a caller most needs that justification durable is a close over unmet criteria — which is exactly the moment they are least likely to re-read, because the close 'succeeded'. EXIT 0 REPORTS THAT THE CALL SUCCEEDED, NEVER THAT THE WRITE LANDED: the same disease as a receipt built on the transport rather than on the stored row, which is the defect class this whole epic exists to remove.

PROPOSED FIX — REJECT AN UNKNOWN `--set` KEY RATHER THAN SWALLOW IT. The defect is the silent acceptance of an unrecognised key, NOT the missing criteria_override feature; whether that field should exist is a separate question this row does not decide. A `--set` naming a key the target schema does not carry should exit non-zero and name the key, the way a mistyped flag already does. Note the blast radius before building: `--set` is the generic typed-field door used across many verbs, so the check belongs where the key set is known, and any legitimate write-only/request-scoped key (observed_rev and observed_rail_rev are the ones already documented on close) must be allowlisted rather than newly refused.

RECOVERY TAKEN AT THE TIME, so the finding is not merely theoretical: the rationale was folded into pds-w25-round-terminal's disposition_reason, which IS durable, and reads back at 1651 B.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A `--set` naming a key the target document's schema does not carry exits NON-ZERO and names the offending key, instead of exiting 0 and discarding the value. Demonstrated with the verbatim before/after of the recorded invocation (`--set criteria_override=…` on a `bp task close`).

Request-scoped keys that are legitimately not stored on the document are ALLOWLISTED and keep working — observed_rev and observed_rail_rev at minimum, each named in the allowlist with the reason it is not a document field. A test pins that they do not regress to a refusal.

The blast radius is measured before the change, not estimated: every verb accepting `--set` is enumerated from source and the count quoted, and any call site that relies on writing an unschema'd key today is named or shown not to exist.

A regression test drives the real dispatch with an unknown `--set` key and asserts the non-zero exit plus the key in the message; it is mutation-proven by reverting the guard and showing the test reds.

Whether `criteria_override` should be a stored field is answered EXPLICITLY — either it is added to the task schema and persisted on close, or the CLI's own refusal text stops advertising it. The two must not disagree, which they do today.

corpus.title: a wrong field path in bp task get answers CONFIDENTLY: content.claim reads as unclaimed and content.criteria as no-criteria, both silent, both unsafe

content.description:
Hit 2026-09-06 by lead-studio-10 in the first ten minutes of a shift, on a live claimed row. The wrong read returned a value that was indistinguishable from the dangerous answer, and nothing warned.

WHAT HAPPENED: relaunching after a lead death, my standing order was "do NOT blanket re-claim; re-claim only what claim-health shows lapsed". I read a held row with `bp task get <id> -o json` and a parser walking `doc.content.claim`. It returned null. That reads exactly like a lapsed claim on a row whose pulse loop had died — the precise condition I was told to remediate by re-claiming. The claim was in fact HEALTHY at epoch 2, held by my own worker id, lease extended on an open PR. A re-claim would have bumped the epoch under a live pulse loop and could have stolen a peer's row had the id differed.

THE MECHANISM, measured on `bp task get <any task> -o json`:

  duplicated at BOTH doc.* and doc.content.*   assignee, kind, lifecycle_status, parent_id, priority
  ONLY at doc.* (top level)                    claim, criteria_progress, rev, status, title, doc_id, labels, ... (21 fields)
  ONLY at doc.content.*                        acceptance_criteria, description, tags, main_tag, github

The two fields a reader checks FIRST — `lifecycle_status` and `priority` — are duplicated, so both paths work and the reader learns "task fields live under content". That lesson is then wrong for exactly the two most dangerous fields in the document:

  * `content.claim` is absent -> reads as UNCLAIMED -> invites a claim steal.
  * `content.criteria` is absent, and the criteria are at `content.acceptance_criteria` keyed `criterion` (NOT `text`) -> reads as A ROW WITH NO CRITERIA -> invites a criteria-free close or a stamp against a criterion whose text the writer never actually read.

Both failures are SILENT and both fail in the unsafe direction. A missing key in JSON is not an error in any of the languages agents write these parsers in.

CONTRIBUTING: `bp task get --help` documents only `usage: barkpark task get <doc_id>` and its one argument. It does not mention `-o json`, does not describe the envelope, and offers no accessor. Every reader is therefore obliged to hand-roll a path walk against an undocumented shape, and the shape actively teaches the wrong lesson.

RELATED, same family, already broadcast this campaign: "a count is only as good as the filter you can name" (ready carries claimed, blocked and drafts.* rows), and "a stamp receipt is not evidence" (read the row back). This row is the READ-side sibling of both: the write side has been hardened repeatedly while the read side still lets a wrong path answer confidently.

NOT PROPOSING A MECHANISM. The invariant is that a wrong or stale field path must not be able to return a well-formed answer that is indistinguishable from a true one, on the two fields whose misreading causes a claim steal or a false close.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Reading a task claim or its acceptance criteria through a plausible-but-wrong path cannot return a well-formed answer indistinguishable from a true one. Demonstrated by a check that a stranger can run: the two specific wrong reads recorded here (content.claim, content.criteria) each produce a distinguishable outcome rather than a value that reads as unclaimed / criteria-free.

bp task get --help states how to get machine-readable output and where the claim and the acceptance criteria live in it, including that criteria entries are keyed `criterion`. Verified by running the help and reading it back, not by inspecting the source.
The guard proves it can see: a positive control shows the check FAILS if the safe behaviour is removed, so it cannot rot into a vacuous pass.

corpus.title: Close the 39 cleanly-closable one-short epic rows, and stop the sweep being ordered a fourth time

content.description:
CHARTER D225. This is a LEAD act, not a builder slice — merge-gated criteria are the lead's by contract, and 43 of the 54 rows refuse a close under any fresh worker name.

THE SET IS 54, NOT 38 (D204 superseded). 232 dr-* rows, 218 open, 54 exactly one criterion short. corpus.title: Fourteen done PDS tasks stop under-reporting themselves — the merge criterion is stamped with the sha that proves it

content.description:
LEDGER-ONLY SLICE — you touch no repo files. corpus.title: The ready-queue ORDER BY has no index, so ?limit=1 still pays for the whole claimable set — closing it needs a cast index that can make a task unwritable

content.description: DECIDE, do not build blind: `GET /v1/tasks/ready` still pays a full ordered pass over the workspace's claimable task rows whatever `?limit=` says, because ORDER BY is `(content->>'priority')::int ASC NULLS LAST, inserted_at, id` and no index serves it. PR #14813 removed the whole-corpus term (two MATERIALIZED CTEs + a 1.3M-row anti-join; 49k-task corpus 895-1051ms -> 92-115ms) but deliberately did NOT close the limit gradient. THE ONLY THING THAT CLOSES IT is an index on ((content->>'priority')::int) — e.g. (workspace_id, ((content->>'priority')::int), inserted_at, id) WHERE type='task' — which lets Postgres walk in ORDER BY order and stop at the LIMIT. THE COST OF THAT INDEX, which is why it was not taken unasked: an index expression is evaluated on WRITE. A `type:task` document whose content.priority is not an integer becomes UNWRITABLE — the INSERT/UPDATE errors, not the read. Tasks.Validation.check_optional_priority/2 enforces "integer 0..4 when set" on the task write path, but the generic content door (POST /v1/data/mutate and the Studio writer) does not run Tasks.Validation, so the invariant is enforced at ONE of at least two doors. Today a bad priority is already a 500 on the READ (the ORDER BY casts it), so the invariant is de facto required — this change moves the failure from read to write, which is worse in blast radius and better in honesty. WANTED, in this order: (1) measure whether any type:task row in prod has a non-integer/absent-but-present priority (`SELECT count(*) FROM documents WHERE type='task' AND content ? 'priority' AND content->>'priority' !~ '^-?[0-9]+$'`) — a non-zero answer settles it NO on its own; (2) rule: is priority-is-an-integer a repo invariant we are willing to enforce at the storage layer, or is the read-side cast the bug and a guarded expression (CASE WHEN ... ~ '^-?[0-9]+$' THEN ...::int END, applied to BOTH the ORDER BY and the index) the right shape? Note the guarded form CHANGES SEMANTICS on malformed data — 500 becomes "sorted last" — so it needs the same before/after set-equality proof PR #14813 carried. DO NOT ship the naive index without (1) and (2).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: THE PROD COUNT IS IN THE ROW: the number of type:task documents whose content.priority is present and not an integer is measured against prod and quoted here. A non-zero count settles the naive index as NO on its own.

A RULING IS RECORDED EITHER WAY: either priority-is-an-integer becomes a storage-layer invariant and the index ships, or the guarded-cast shape is chosen and the ORDER BY changes with it — with the same before/after set-equality proof PR #14813 carried, since the guarded form turns a 500 on malformed data into sorted-last.
IF AN INDEX SHIPS, limit=1 COSTS MATERIALLY LESS THAN limit=40, measured, not read off the diff.

corpus.title: 24 open rows carry their own merge-keyed close condition; four of the conditions landed up to 14 days ago

content.description:
## THE SWEEP HAS A FALSE-POSITIVE RATE OF 2 IN 4, AND BOTH MISSES SHARE ONE CAUSE

**Verified: of the four "confirmed" rows above, only TWO were real. The rule needs one more clause.**

> **MATCH THE ROW'S OWN CLOSE INSTRUCTION — never any PR number or sha appearing anywhere in its prose.**

**CLOSED, genuinely rotting (2):**
- `cch-w36-bl-confirm-brake-billing-sentence` — closed 4/4. Fix on main, landed `5b7f1fd126` (#9851). Mutation-proved: reverting the call-site guard produces exactly ONE failure, naming the row's own defect; restoring gives 1135/0.
- `pds-w35-declared-register-basis-drift` — closed 2/2, both criteria mutation-proved, both specified corrections landed.

**FALSE POSITIVES (2), and neither was ever this sweep's to claim:**

**`cch-w65-bl-the-merge-gate-autostamp-has-no-lead-check` has NO close condition at all.** The string the sweep matched — *"landed PR #11435 (26b8614259)"* — is **QUOTED FABRICATED EVIDENCE that the row exists to complain about**: the sentence a server auto-wrote when a scratch worker paid a merge gate citing a different epic's PR it never touched. #11435 did merge, which is *exactly why it was available to be cited falsely*, and *exactly why a sha-ancestry join confirms a condition that was never this row's*.

**The row predicted this in its own last paragraph:** *"Any future audit grepping for that phrase as a fabrication signal must exclude them."* **The sweep ran that grep and was misled by it.** The row is open, unbuilt, out of fence (charter D70 rules `close.ex` out by name), all four criteria genuinely unmet.

**`pe-w7-epic-seal`'s condition belongs to a SIBLING.** The matched sentence is *"pe-w6-bp-paper-new closes on #11934's merge (lead)"* — this row's instruction **about another row**, inside its disposition list. #11934 merged and `pe-w6-bp-paper-new` is already `done` 5/5, so nothing is rotting there either. This row's own work is undone: its epic is open at 2/3, and the row is explicit that on a rubric fail you *"stamp NOTHING, leave the epic open."*

## The two prose categories that reliably carry OTHER entities' merge conditions

1. **A row ABOUT fabricated close evidence** — which by necessity contains text engineered to look like a real close condition.
2. **An epic seal row** — which NAMES its children's conditions in its disposition list.

Both dispositions are now recorded on the rows themselves so a future audit does not re-flag them.

**The deeper point:** a sha-ancestry join is a strong instrument and it confirmed two conditions that were never asserted by the rows it matched. **Strength of evidence does not compensate for matching the wrong claim** — the join was correct about the world and wrong about whose claim it was testing.

---

**24 open rows carry their own close condition keyed to a merge — and for at least four of them the merge landed days or weeks ago and nobody closed the row.** The instruction existing is not enough, because the merge happens in a PR and the row lives on the board; nothing joins the two.

## The four confirmed, by direct check

| row | its own instruction | the condition |
|---|---|---|
| `cch-w36-bl-confirm-brake-billing-sente…` | *"CLOSES THIS ROW WHEN PR #9851 MERGES"* | **#9851 MERGED 2026-08-06** — 14 days |
| `cch-w65-bl-the-merge-gate-autostamp-ha…` | *"closed on merge by w65verify — landed PR #11435 (commit 26b8614259)"* | **#11435 MERGED 2026-08-09**, and `26b8614259` **is an ancestor of main** — 11 days |
| `pe-w7-epic-seal` | *"closes on #11934's merge (lead)"* | **#11934 MERGED 2026-08-17** |
| `pds-w35-declared-register-basis-drift` | *"the lead closes this row when the register slice merges"* | register merged as `47ed5f2188`, **is an ancestor of main** |

**The remaining 20 name a condition that is not a bare PR number** — a sibling row's merge, a slice, "the surviving row" — and need the same join done per row.

## The query is cheap, which is the point

```
rows where lifecycle_status == "open"
  AND description matches /clos\w+ (this )?(row|task)? ?(on|when)\b/ near /merge|land|ship|register|slice/
  JOIN against: gh pr view <n> --json mergedAt
             or git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main
```

That found 24 candidates over 7,354 rows in one pass, and confirmed four in three commands. **This should run on every board sweep, and ideally on every merge.**

## Why it rots, stated precisely

A predicted-close row is *more* likely to rot than an ordinary one, not less. The author has discharged their obligation by writing the condition down, so nobody feels responsible for it afterwards — and the event that satisfies it happens somewhere the row is not. **A close condition with no watcher is a note, not a mechanism.**

## A THIRD SHAPE, worse because it is invisible to this query

A row whose fix landed **inside the very PR whose review filed it.** `task-c637c1e05c6afbda` was filed by the independent review of PR #6537; the reviewer found the defect, it was **fixed in flight before merge**, and the row was never closed. Not "fixed later by someone else" — *fixed before it ever needed staffing, by the same PR that filed it.*

**A review that files findings and then fixes them in the same PR must close its own rows in that PR.** Otherwise it manufactures backlog that looks live for a month and reads as real unbuilt work to every audit that follows. Of 12 rows surveyed on 2026-08-20, **four described defects that no longer existed**, and this was one of the mechanisms.

## Do NOT bulk-close on the condition alone

A satisfied close condition means the row is a **candidate**, never that it is done. Each still needs its criteria checked — the same day this was filed, a row whose close condition was satisfied was correctly left OPEN because one criterion depended on a selftest that exits 1. **Verify per row, close per row**, and where a premise turns out to have expired, close as already-landed citing the commit and open no empty PR.

## RE-RUN UNDER THE CORRECTED RULE (2026-08-20) — 0 of 30 remaining rows have a satisfied condition

Re-swept all 2,955 open rows, extracting each row's OWN close sentence before any git join.

  35 rows carry a close-shaped sentence
   5 excluded by clause 3 (carrier shapes)
  30 remaining, of which 2 were already adjudicated and closed
   3 carry a resolvable PR/sha in their OWN sentence — NONE merged
   0 CONDITIONS SATISFIED

**27 of the 30 name a condition that is not a bare ref** — "when the surviving row merges", "when the rig slice merges", "close on merge evidence (6, lead closes)". These need a per-row join and cannot be bulk-checked. That is the honest shape of the remaining backlog: the cheap half of this sweep is DONE, and what is left is judgement.

### A THIRD CARRIER SHAPE, same family as the first two

**A SUPERSEDES row names the SUPERSEDED sibling's close condition.** `pds-w43-liveview-residual-32-fold` ends "SUPERSEDES (lead closes on merge): pds-w42-liveview-residual-32-plugin-session", and `pds-w43-judgment-coverage-ladder` ends "SUPERSEDES (lead closes on merge): pds-w40-judgment-coverage-ladder". In both, the close belongs to the row NAMED, not the row carrying the sentence — and the condition is that THIS row merges. Both w43 rows are still open, so pds-w42 (0/3) and pds-w40 (0/14) are STILL-OPEN, not candidates.

So the exclusion list is now three: a row ABOUT fabricated close evidence, an epic-seal row, and a SUPERSEDES row. All three carry another entity's condition **by necessity of what they are**, which is why prose matching keeps finding them.

### ONE GENUINE ROT FOUND AND ADJUDICATED

`dr-bl-w8-refusal-class-reads-the-code` — its own condition "Close this row when dr-w14-s3 merges" is SATISFIED (dr-w14-s3 landed 709ced114d / #10352). Criteria 0-2 stamped and MUTATION-PROVEN in a throwaway tree; criterion 3 is the lead's and is UNPAYABLE AS WRITTEN — there is no PR for this row and there should not be, because the work landed in #10300 and #10352. Already-landed disposition: lead closes citing both commits, opens no PR. Left open at 3/4, claim released.

### METHOD NOTE

`bp doc query task --filter '_id^=…'` and `--filter '_id*=…'` return ZERO rows silently — `_id` is not filterable. A prefix hunt for a truncated slug must go through `title*=` or `bp search`, or it reports "not found" for rows that exist.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The row list is RE-DERIVED at execution time, not taken from this row's description — a named row list goes stale within days, and this row already records a 2-in-4 false-positive rate on its own earlier sweep. The derivation query and its output are pasted.

The refined matching rule is applied and stated: a row is matched on ITS OWN close instruction, never on any PR number or sha appearing elsewhere in its prose. The rule is written into the evidence so a later reader can re-run the sweep identically.
For every row proposed for closure, the merge is verified against the PR record using `.merged` (never `.merge_commit_sha`), and the verification output is pasted per row.
Each close carries a close_reason naming the specific merge that discharged that row's own stated condition — and the evidence confirms no row was closed on a sibling's merge.
Rows that match the wording but FAIL verification are reported with the reason rather than silently dropped, so the sweep's false-positive rate is measured again rather than assumed to be fixed.

corpus.title: bp task close … cancelled with a BLANK reason lands with no close_reason and rc=0 — the only record a cancel leaves is the one field it lets you omit

content.description:
HIT BY lead-cli 2026-09-06 ~05:27Z, twice in one minute, on real rows. A scripting fault made `$(cat reason.txt)` expand to the empty string; `env -u BARKPARK_TOKEN bp task close task-e1920c0a8cd3013b lead-cli 1 cancelled "" --yes` returned rc=0 and printed `✓ the store holds it — lifecycle_status=cancelled  criteria 0/3 met`. Read back: lifecycle cancelled, close_reason ABSENT, closed_by lead-cli. Same on task-a43083b022e04950. The only repair afterwards was an append-only `bp task stamp --miss --note` on criterion 0, which is not where anyone looks for a cancel reason.

WHY THIS IS A HOLE AND NOT A PREFERENCE. `cancelled` is exempt BY NAME from every close-time gate — the criteria gate (check_criteria_proven), the close artifact gate (check_close_artifact, PDS-D291) — precisely because "abandoning the work is what cancelling MEANS" and the ruling on task-ce0c0ffff6edde23 offers "cancel with the reason" as the honest exit. So for a cancel the reason is the ENTIRE record. Yet api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex (the "Dossier close rationale" block, ~:1068-1073) treats a blank reason as "do not overwrite an existing value" and writes nothing, and the manifest declares `reason` `required: false` on task.close (internal/cli/tasks_close_pulse_execute_test.go:47 fixture mirrors it). A done close with zero criteria is refused on prose alone; a cancel with NO prose at all sails through. That is the absent-vs-zero collapse this codebase refuses everywhere else, on the one status whose reason nothing else backs.

BLAST RADIUS, measured before filing: none of the other close-time gates touch cancelled, so a refusal here changes exactly one path — a cancel that carries no reason. A cancel that carries any non-blank reason is unaffected. Re-closing an already-cancelled row (idempotent replay) must stay as it is.

FIX SHAPE (the invariant, not the mechanism): a close to `cancelled` (and, if the builder finds the same shape, `blocked`) whose reason is blank/absent is REFUSED server-side in Tasks.Close, with a message that names the fix ("a cancel is exempt from every other close gate, so its reason is its only record — pass one"). Server-side so bp, MCP task_close, Studio and raw HTTP are all covered. The bp render should show the refusal verbatim. Do NOT add a default reason ("cancelled") — a manufactured sentence is worse than a refusal.

WHAT THE WRONG FIX WOULD DESTROY: refusing blank reasons on `done` too would break lead seal closes that carry their record in the landed digest and criteria evidence; scope the refusal to the statuses that are exempt from the other gates.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Server-side: Tasks.close to `cancelled` with a blank or absent reason is REFUSED with an error whose message names the fix; a cancel with a non-blank reason still lands; a `done` close with a blank reason is NOT newly refused (it is governed by the criteria and artifact gates). A test per arm.

Reproduced through bp against a throwaway row before the fix (paste the rc=0 + `the store holds it` line + the read-back showing close_reason absent), cancelled afterwards with a reason naming this row; and shown REFUSED through bp after the fix with the refusal text pasted.
Mutation-proved: removing the refusal reds ONLY the refusal test; the permit arms stay green with the refusal on and off.
MERGE-GATED (the lead closes this): PR merged to refs/remotes/origin/main with the four required contexts green on its head; merge sha recorded.

corpus.title: `bp task stamp --merge-gated` exists but is absent from the capabilities manifest

content.description:
FOUND WHILE CLOSING MERGE-GATED CRITERIA (cch-w19-s5, 2026-08-01). `bp capabilities -o json` lists task stamp's flags as [criterion, criterion-text, met, evidence, miss, note] and `bp task stamp --help` prints the same six. But stamping a criterion whose text carries the MERGE-GATED marker is refused 409 merge_gated_criterion with 'Pass --merge-gated to override only if you are the lead closing the gate.' - a flag that works and is discoverable ONLY from the refusal message.
WHY IT MATTERS: an agent reading the manifest (the sanctioned way to learn this CLI) cannot know the escape hatch exists, and an agent reading the refusal has no way to check it is real short of trying it. This wave needed it five times.
A SECOND, SHARPER EDGE, MEASURED: the marker check is TEXTUAL, so it fires on criteria that merely MENTION the phrase. cch-w19-s5's own criterion 5 - 'cch-w14-bl... are stamped on their merge-gated criteria with #8818...' - is not itself merge-gated, yet its plain stamp was refused and needed the override. A guard that cannot tell a gate from a sentence ABOUT a gate teaches agents to pass the override reflexively, which is the opposite of what it is for.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `bp capabilities -o json` lists --merge-gated under task stamp's flags, and `bp task stamp --help` prints it with a one-line description naming who may use it. Both outputs quoted.

The merge-gated marker check is shown to be textual and its false-positive rate is stated: a criterion that merely mentions 'merge-gated' in prose is either exempted, or the refusal message says out loud that the match is on the TEXT and may be a mention. Whichever is chosen, it is proven by stamping a mention-only criterion and quoting the result.

corpus.title: Set merge_gate:true at create time when the marker OPENS the criterion — 427 declarations are stranded, and 74 lookalikes must stay unflagged

content.description:
PART 3 of the task-d1654bf0d20d5009 ruling, filed separately because it changes the WRITE path for every future task row, which is a different blast radius from the read-side receipt that shipped in PR #16252.

THE STRAND. A criterion worded as a merge gate but carrying no merge_gate flag is refused to the builder by stamp.ex's prose arm AND skipped by close.ex's autostamp, which keys on the flag. PR #16252 made the second half VISIBLE — the reconcile receipt now names those criteria instead of silently returning :no_marker — but it deliberately did not stamp them, because close's autostamp is a PERMIT and a prose-wide permit fabricates dones.

This row closes the strand at its source instead: set merge_gate: true at CREATE time when the criterion is genuinely a gate declaration, so the flag and the prose never disagree from the row's first moment.

THE NARROWING THAT MAKES IT SAFE, and the measurement behind it. Across 14,699 criteria on the live ledger, 501 are worded as merge gates with no flag. Splitting them on WHERE the marker sits:

  427  the marker OPENS the criterion (within the first ~12 characters) — genuine gate declarations
   74  the marker is buried later in the prose — criteria ABOUT gating, not gates

The 74 are the ones that must not get a flag. Examples, verbatim: "The four lead-gated rows are adjudicated `open` — NOT closed, each with a reason naming the specific outstanding [MERGE-GATED] lead act." and "Every machine-checkable merge gate is verified with `gh pr view <n> --json statusCheckRollup` and `.mergeCommit.oid` ancestry, then stamped and closed on the CURRENT claim." Flagging either would make it auto-stampable on merge, which is the fabricated done PR #16252 exists to refuse.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS VALIDATED AGAINST THE ROWS THAT ALREADY GET IT RIGHT, not invented: of 618 criteria carrying BOTH the flag and the wording, 612 open with the marker. Position is what separates a declaration from a mention, and the correctly-flagged population agrees.

ALREADY HALF-BUILT, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT FOR DOING IT: the create path ALREADY detects this shape and emits a soft warning — "acceptance_criteria [N] open with the MERGE-GATED marker but carry no merge_gate: true — the close-time autostamp keys on the FLAG, not the wording, so a lead merge will not flip them. Add merge_gate: true to each gate entry (soft warning, save proceeds)". The detection exists and is trusted enough to warn; this row is about whether it should also ACT, and under what narrowing.

NOT A BACKFILL. Whether the existing 427 get flagged is a separate question with a separate blast radius, and it should not ride in on this.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The create path sets merge_gate:true ONLY when the merge-gate marker OPENS the criterion, and leaves a buried marker alone. The threshold is stated and justified against the measured population, not chosen by feel.

A test walks BOTH columns from the live ledger: declarations that must get the flag, and the buried-marker criteria that must NOT — including the two verbatim examples that assert the opposite of what a flag would make them mean. It reds when the narrowing is dropped.
An author who explicitly writes merge_gate:false is never overridden, and an author who writes merge_gate:true is left alone. Declared intent always beats the detector.

The existing soft warning is reconciled: it either stops firing for the case now handled automatically, or its text is updated so it no longer tells authors to do something the server just did. A warning that survives its own fix trains people to ignore warnings.
MERGE-GATED (the lead closes this): the PR is merged to main with the required gates green on its head, and the merge sha is recorded.

corpus.title: bp task landed --criterion flips criteria a merge CANNOT discharge: merge_gate:true means 'the lead closes it', not 'a merge closes it' — PROVEN, a claim-free CI-reachable fabricated done

content.description:
PROVEN 2026-09-06 by lead-deploy-10, against a disposable scratch row created for the purpose (task-a12d63d3107a77b2, since cancelled) so no real row was touched.

THE HOLE: `bp task landed --criterion N` flips an acceptance criterion to met=true. It holds NO claim, NO worker_id and NO epoch — it is, by its own help text, "the verb CI can actually call". Its only permit conditions are that the criterion is MERGE-SHAPED (carries "merge_gate": true, or its wording says MERGE-GATED / MERGE GATE / PR merged / merged to main) and is not already met. The --note becomes the criterion's evidence, unverified.

THE PROBLEM IS THAT `merge_gate: true` DOES NOT MEAN "A MERGE DISCHARGES THIS". In practice leads set that flag to mean "the LEAD closes this, not the builder" — and they set it on criteria that demand far more than a merge. A real, live example is task-6d80c6cc7d97b1d1 criterion 6 (S9, studio), which carries merge_gate: true and whose text reads: "MERGE-GATED -- THE LEAD CLOSES THIS, AND ONLY ON THE DEMO. An editor completes the full round trip -- open, edit rich text, set alt text, preview, publish -- in a NON-DEFAULT workspace, WITHOUT touching the API, with the run shown. That is the demo Gyldendal could not run." A merge cannot satisfy that criterion. The permit predicate cannot tell the two apart, because one boolean is carrying two different meanings.

THE PROOF, on the scratch row, not on a real one: a single criterion with merge_gate: true and text saying "A merge cannot satisfy this; only a demonstrated run can." Before: met=false, evidence empty. Command: bp task landed <row> --criterion 0 --pr 99999 --note "PROBE: a landing notice claiming a live demo happened. It did not." After, read back from the store rather than from the receipt: criteria_met=1/1, c0.met=true, and c0.evidence is that exact sentence. No claim was held at any point.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE FLIPPED FLAG: the criteria gate refuses a `done` close over unmet criteria. Once the last unmet criterion is flipped this way the row reads fully met, so that gate has nothing left to refuse. bp's own help for this verb anticipates the shape - "a false positive would be a SILENT fabricated done" - and the predicate it chose is exactly the one that produces false positives, because merge_gate is overloaded. This is the CI-reachable, claim-free version of the defect class this campaign has been chasing all week: stamped evidence that describes work nobody did.

NOT A THEORY ABOUT INTENT: the verb is a good idea and the union/no-clobber semantics are careful. The defect is the predicate, not the verb.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A criterion that a MERGE cannot discharge is not flippable by a landing notice. The permit distinguishes 'the lead closes this rather than the builder' from 'a merge discharges this', instead of reading one overloaded boolean for both. State which signal now carries which meaning.

Proved on a disposable row, both directions: a criterion whose text demands a live/demonstrated run is REFUSED by bp task landed --criterion with a message naming why, AND a genuinely merge-discharged criterion is still PERMITTED. A permit that refuses everything is not a fix.

The already-flipped rows are found and reported: sweep live rows for criteria met=true whose evidence came from a landing notice while their text demands a demo, a live read, or an operator action. Name the count and the method; a zero must come with a positive control proving the sweep can see a known instance.

task-6d80c6cc7d97b1d1 criterion 6 is confirmed still met=false, or its evidence is corrected — it is the live example this row was found from, and it must not be left flipped by the mechanism being fixed.
