corpus.title: A cancelled or blocked close can RAISE a declared merge gate to met — the honesty-gate exemptions are correct for requiring criteria and wrong for writing them

content.description:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 by lead-ledger-c5 on the live server, on disposable rows. Filed as its own row on main's ruling, split out of cch-w56 because it is a DIFFERENT defect from "--merge-gated mints no receipt" and burying it there would lose it.

THE PRINCIPLE THAT DECIDES THE FIX, stated first because everything below follows from it: A CANCEL MAY ABANDON ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. IT MAY NEVER ASSERT THEM.

THE MECHANISM. Every honesty gate on the close path EXEMPTS cancelled (and blocked) BY NAME. That is correct for the REQUIRING half — abandoning acceptance criteria is what cancelling means. It is wrong for the WRITING half, because the same command that abandons the row can also flip a declared gate to met on its way out, and the exemption removes the only thing that was stopping it. THE EXEMPTIONS ARE NOT THE BUG; APPLYING THEM TO A WRITE IS.

DEMONSTRATED, THREE RUNS, EACH ON ITS OWN DISPOSABLE ROW CARRYING ONE `merge_gate: true` CRITERION AND NO CARRIER PR:
 1. `bp task close … done --set 'criteria:=[{index:0,met:true,…}]'` -> EXIT 5, REFUSED. But NOT by a marker check: the refusal is the D289 criteria gate, verbatim "acceptance criteria 0 are not met on the task AS STORED, and criteria flipped in this very close command do not count — that would be the closer grading its own homework." On the done path the bit is protected BY ACCIDENT, by something counting unmet criteria, not by anything that knows the criterion is a gate.
 2. `bp task close … cancelled --set 'criteria:=[…]'` -> EXIT 0. Read back: met=true, merge_gate=true, lifecycle cancelled, and NO override or autostamp trace of any kind. Row task-64774d99b1ebd6b5.
 3. `bp task close … blocked --set 'criteria:=[…]'` -> EXIT 0. Identical result: met=true, merge_gate=true, lifecycle blocked, no trace. Row task-da353d0802b19ad7. SO IT IS TWO LIFECYCLES, NOT ONE, AND THE FIX IS ONE PREDICATE COVERING BOTH RATHER THAN TWO PATCHES.

CONTRAST THAT MAKES IT A DEFECT RATHER THAN A DESIGN: on the SAME declared gate with the SAME absent carrier PR, `bp task stamp --met` REFUSES at exit 5 and names its own detector ("DETECTOR: the merge_gate FLAG … no wording change will lift it"), while `bp task close cancelled --set criteria:=` flips the IDENTICAL BIT at exit 0 and says nothing. One door is guarded and loud, the other is unguarded and silent, and they write the same field.

A THIRD DOOR, FOUND INDEPENDENTLY BY ANOTHER LANE AND CORROBORATING THIS ONE: task-a12d63d3107a77b2 is lead-deploy-10's scratch probe from 2026-09-06, whose close reason records that `bp task landed --criterion 0` — a verb that takes NO CLAIM AND NO EPOCH, and which CI can call — ALSO flipped a merge_gate:true criterion. Two lanes reached the same class from different directions a day apart. Whoever fixes this should decide whether the predicate belongs on the close path alone or wherever a met bit is raised.

SEVERITY, BOUNDED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED. A sweep of 200 cancelled rows found exactly FOUR carrying a met merge-gate, and ALL FOUR ARE DELIBERATE PROBES — three of mine from tonight and lead-deploy-10's from 2026-09-06. ZERO ORGANIC INSTANCES. So this is a live mechanism with no known victim, and the row should be read that way: the door is open, nobody has walked through it by accident yet. Do not let the mechanism's elegance set the priority.

WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH: whether any consumer READS a met merge-gate on a terminal row and acts on it. criteria_met/criteria_total are computed in tasks.ex, expectations.ex, internal.ex, query.ex, the tasks controller and params.ex, and I did not trace which of those, if any, would treat a cancelled row's met gate as a proof. If none does, the consequence is confined to a misleading read; if one does, the severity rises. That trace is cheap and belongs with the fix.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A close with lifecycle cancelled or blocked REFUSES any `criteria:=` entry that RAISES `met` from false to true, with a NAMED error. Lowering met, clearing evidence and editing criterion text all remain allowed on those lifecycles — the refusal is scoped to raising, because a cancel may abandon acceptance criteria and may never assert them.

The existing exemptions are left INTACT: a cancelled close still bypasses the D289 criteria gate, the holder gate, the acknowledgement gate and the close-artifact gate exactly as before. Evidence: a cancelled close over UNMET criteria still succeeds after the fix. A patch that makes cancelling harder in any other way is the wrong fix and must be rejected.

NEGATIVE ARM, required, and it must cover BOTH lifecycles measured here: a test drives the raise through a cancelled close AND through a blocked close, shows both REFUSED after the fix, and shows both previously succeeding — quote all four runs. A fix proven on cancelled alone leaves the blocked door open, and they are the same code path.

The `bp task landed --criterion` door is RULED ON rather than silently left: state whether the same predicate covers it (it takes no claim and no epoch, and CI can call it), or why it is deliberately out of scope. Cite task-a12d63d3107a77b2, lead-deploy-10's independent probe, which is the evidence it exists.

The blast radius is MEASURED before the fix ships and the number is quoted: how many non-probe rows carry a met merge-gate on a terminal lifecycle, over a stated denominator. Measured 2026-09-08 at ZERO organic instances in 200 cancelled rows (all four hits were deliberate probes) — re-measure at your own sha rather than inheriting that, and say whether any consumer READS such a bit, which I did not establish.

corpus.title: 55 live criteria are worded as merge gates but carry no flag — and 36 of them are NOT gates, so a one-directional backfill would lock innocent rows

content.description:
THE TWO READERS (re-derived from source, 2026-08-24).

  * api/lib/barkpark/tasks/criteria.ex:107 `merge_gated?/1` — the STAMP REFUSAL. Reads the structural `merge_gate` key FIRST, and falls back to PROSE (`~r/MERGE[-\s]GATED|MERGE[-\s]GATE\b/i`, criteria.ex:124) when the key is absent. WIDE, deliberately (moduledoc measured-refutes narrowing twice).
  * api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex:815 `merge_gate_synthetics/3` — the CLOSE AUTOSTAMP, shared by `autostamp_merge_gate/6` (lead close) and `reconcile_merge_gate/3` (merge webhook). Reads `Map.get(entry, "merge_gate") == true` ONLY. STRICTLY structural, no text heuristic, by explicit comment (close.ex:719-721).

THE GAP. A criterion that is WORDED but UNFLAGGED is refused to the builder by the wide arm and NOT autostamped for the lead by the strict arm, so close.ex:479 `check_criteria_proven/4` returns `{:criteria_unmet, [i]}`. The row closes only on a LOUD override (`--merge-gated` stamp, or a criteria_override reason minting a `close_override` record). This is NOT the recorded premise 'the reader is narrow, widen nothing, backfill the flag' — the STAMP reader was already widened on 2026-08-22. Only the AUTOSTAMP reader is strict, and it must stay strict.

MEASURED (7072 task docs, 31680 criteria, 2026-08-24). Rows carrying the flag: 794. Rows the wide predicate gates: 2181. The recorded census figures 669/7 are stale in BOTH directions. Live rows (open/in_progress/blocked): 720 gated, 698 already flagged, 28 prose-only — a mass flag backfill landed 2026-08-23 (759 of the 794 flagged rows were updated that day). The residue is 55 prose-only criteria across 46 rows once `considering` is included.

THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE REMEDY. Hand-checked all 55: only 19 are genuine merge gates. 36 merely MENTION merge-gating — a 65% false-positive rate on the backfill candidate set, versus the 3.51% criteria.ex measures corpus-wide. The residue is enriched in meta-rows whose SUBJECT is the merge-gate machinery. Backfilling `merge_gate:true` across the worded set would permanently make 36 innocent criteria lead-only, and `met` has no un-stamp. The correct write is TWO-DIRECTIONAL: `true` for the 19, and the documented `merge_gate:false` exemption (criteria.ex:78-81) for the 36.

SHARPEST INSTANCE. Six jf-w1-* rows were CORRECTED on 2026-08-20 to replace the merge gate with 'verifiably present on main, NOT a merge notification' — but the correction quotes the original wording verbatim, so the prose arm still fires and the builder still cannot stamp. The correction re-armed the tripwire it was undoing. Four of them are in the structurally-stuck set below.

STRUCTURALLY STUCK: 7 non-terminal rows whose ONLY unmet criteria are prose-only gates (not the recorded 23) — dr-w19-bl-merge-gated-paperwork-is-unsatisfiable, jf-w1-engine-narrow-dark-fixes, jf-w1-media-cors-upstream, jf-w1-og-four-routes, jf-w1-width-tokens-gate-rig, mob-w3-rich-tail, tgw11-bl-screen-classifysafety-global-option-launder. Two need `true`, five need `false`. A one-directional backfill unsticks two and lies about five.

SCRIPT (reviewed, dry-run clean, all 55 text guards validated against live `bp doc get` reads): /Volumes/SATECHI/dev-caches/tmp/claude-code/claude-501/-Volumes-SATECHI-github-barkpark/ba5f66f9-9370-4639-ae79-5f38bb0e7fe1/scratchpad/merge-gate-flag/backfill-merge-gate-flag.py — DRY_RUN by default (BACKFILL_APPLY=1 to write), per-criterion text-prefix guard so a slid index ABORTS rather than flagging the wrong row, ifRevisionID CAS, publish, and a read-back assertion. It writes ONLY the `merge_gate` key; it never writes `met`, never claims, never closes.

OUT OF SCOPE, filed as observation: 219 flagged criteria carry no marker wording at all (14 on 2026-08-22) — machine-gated but invisible to a human reading the board.

--- 2026-09-08, lead-ledger-c5: THE POPULATION KEEPS REPRODUCING ITSELF ON THE ROWS WRITTEN ABOUT IT ---

APPENDED, NOT AMENDED: nothing above is changed, and criterion 1's demand that the 55/19/36 classification be RE-DERIVED at execution time rather than inherited stands untouched. This is one more argument for the row, measured on rows filed the same night, and it should be read as evidence for the premise rather than as a new count of the population.

FOUR ROWS IN ONE NIGHT CARRIED NO `merge_gate` DECLARATION ON ANY CRITERION UNTIL I SET THEM. Every one of them is itself a row ABOUT ledger-shape defects — three of them about merge-gating specifically:

  * task-8ca0bd7a8ed50f14 — "a cancelled or blocked close can RAISE a declared merge gate to met". Five criteria, `merge_gate` ABSENT on all five, declared false before any stamp.
  * task-f828cc60a70ef79b — "a stale draft twin freezes a claimed row's acceptance criteria". Four criteria, ABSENT on all four.
  * task-d10d9eb47f2cc5e4 — "a new close refusal exits 2 instead of 5". Filed WITH the flag declared, because by then I had learned to.
  * task-21f8a5c522ad8710 — "one comment map rotted twice". Same.

The first two are the demonstration and the last two are the control: the flag is ABSENT by default and present only when an author remembers, which is exactly the asymmetry this row exists to fix. A default that depends on the author having read a backlog row is not a default.

WHY THAT IS THE STRONGEST FORM OF THIS ARGUMENT. A census says "55 criteria are worded as gates and carry no flag" and invites the reply "how many of those matter?". This says something a census cannot: the rows being written to DOCUMENT the defect are themselves instances of it, filed by someone who had just finished measuring it. If the population reproduces on the rows most likely to be authored carefully, it reproduces everywhere.

AND IT COST SOMETHING REAL, TWICE, WHICH IS THE PART THAT ARGUES FOR THE FIX RATHER THAN FOR A SWEEP. On task-f828cc60a70ef79b the undeclared criteria met the PROSE fallback in `Criteria.merge_gated?/1` — their wording discusses merge-gating — so a plain `--met` was REFUSED on criteria that were never gates. The escape that presents itself at that moment is `--merge-gated`, which would have FALSELY DECLARED them gates and been recorded as an override. The honest fix was structural: declare `merge_gate: false` on every entry, texts asserted byte-identical, and stamp normally. A wide prose fallback plus an absent flag does not merely mis-classify; it steers the blocked author toward the one action that makes the ledger less true, and it does so at the exact moment they are stuck.

NOT A CLAIM ABOUT THE 55. I did not re-run the census and I am not adjusting any number in this row. Four rows, named, from one night.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The two readers are named in the fix with file:line and the asymmetry stated: criteria.ex `merge_gated?/1` is flag-OR-prose (wide, stays wide) and close.ex `merge_gate_synthetics/3` is flag-only (strict, stays strict). Evidence quotes both call sites from the tree at fix time, not from this description.

The 55-criterion classification is re-derived at execution time, not inherited: the census query is re-run, its row count reported against the 55/46 recorded here, and any criterion that has since been flagged, stamped met, reworded, or whose row closed is dropped with the drop named. A named row list goes stale in minutes.

Each of the 19 genuine gates carries `merge_gate:true` and each of the 36 mentions carries `merge_gate:false`, verified by READ-BACK per row (not by the script's own exit code). Evidence: the post-run census showing zero prose-only criteria remaining on non-terminal rows.

MUTATION PROOF that the fix does what it claims, both directions, on two rows chosen from the list: a `true` row is shown to be autostamped by a lead merge-close (or, if no merge is available, `merge_gate_synthetics/3` is shown selecting it), and a `false` row is shown to accept a plain builder stamp where it previously returned `merge_gated_criterion`. Both runs pasted.

The six jf-w1-* corrected criteria are addressed as a CLASS with the mechanism written down — quoting a retired gate's wording verbatim re-arms the prose arm — and the authoring guidance records how to quote a retired gate without re-arming it (the `merge_gate:false` exemption, or not quoting the marker).
No criterion was stamped `met` by this work. Evidence: a diff of the met-set over the affected rows before and after, showing it unchanged.

corpus.title: Tasks.Close autostamp keys on the merge_gate FLAG only, so a MERGE-GATED-worded but unflagged criterion is invisible to the lead's merge autostamp while stamp.ex refuses the builder on its prose

content.description:
MEASURED on origin/main (read via git show origin/main:api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex).

Two halves of the same rule disagree about what a merge gate IS:

- api/lib/barkpark/tasks/stamp.ex:274 refuses a builder --met via Criteria.merge_gated?/1, which is flag-OR-PROSE (criteria.ex:107) — a criterion whose TEXT says MERGE-GATED is treated as a gate even with no merge_gate key.
- api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex:246 (reconcile_locked/4) and close.ex:1152 (merge_gate_synthetics/3, the seam autostamp_merge_gate/6 feeds) both filter on Map.get(entry, "merge_gate") == true — the FLAG alone. Criteria.merge_gated?/1 is never called from close.ex (grep: zero hits).

Consequence: a criterion worded as a merge gate but carrying no merge_gate key is (a) refused to the builder by the prose arm, and (b) skipped by the lead close-time autostamp and by the merge-webhook reconcile, because neither can see it. It is stampable only by a lead explicitly passing --merge-gated on that index — the automatic paths that exist precisely to close gates on merge never touch it. That shape is what bp task create files by default (the server emits a soft merge_gate_unflagged warning; it does not set the flag).

NOT fixed by PR #15440 (merge sha 54e2763fdd116965c57cbe2d189a77960afd6551), which was CLI-only (5 files under internal/cli) and made the CLI print the server advisory and name the detector on refusal. The server-side asymmetry is untouched.

Remedy to rule on: either route close.ex two filters through Criteria.merge_gated?/1 (symmetric with stamp), or have the create path set merge_gate:true rather than only warn. Picking one is the task; both halves must agree.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The asymmetry between stamp.ex and close.ex is RULED ON and the reasoning lives in close.ex, not only in a PR body: a wide predicate is safe gating a REFUSAL and dangerous gating a PERMIT, close's autostamp is a permit, and symmetry with stamp is therefore not a goal. The comment names the measured population and at least one self-refuting example.

Criteria that READ as merge gates but carry no flag are NAMED in the reconcile receipt and nothing is stamped for them. The receipt lists the criterion indices rather than counting them, and the tag rides through to the webhook response.

MUTATION-PROVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: silencing the new receipt reds the naming tests, and applying the remedy the row asked for — routing BOTH close.ex filters through the prose predicate — is shown to FLIP a criterion that merely discusses merge gating. Paste the before/after tuples.

No existing consumer breaks: the reconcile receipt's other tags still mean what they meant, an explicit merge_gate:false still vetoes the wording, and any existing test whose expectation changes has its substantive assertions preserved with the reason recorded. Paste the suite counts.
MERGE-GATED (the lead closes this): the PR is merged to main with the required gates green on its head, and the merge sha is recorded.

corpus.title: Zero acceptance criteria is a LEGAL BYPASS of the close honesty gate, not just an audit blind spot — 27 open rows, 143 already spent it

content.description:
A row with an EMPTY `acceptance_criteria` list is not merely under-specified — it is a LEGAL BYPASS of the close honesty gate, and it is invisible to every audit that computes met/total, because 0-of-0 is vacuously complete.

## The mechanism, read from source rather than inferred

`api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex`:
- `:458` — `defp check_criteria_payload(_doc, []), do: :ok`
- `:479` — `check_criteria_proven(doc, "done", landed, override_reason)` calls `unmet_after_autostamp/2`; on a doc with no criteria that returns `[]`, which matches the `[] -> {:ok, nil}` head.

So a `done` close over ZERO criteria passes the PDS-D289 gate with **no evidence required and no `criteria_override` on the record**. Every other route to `done` either carries stamped evidence or carries a loud override. This one carries neither, and leaves no trace that it was taken.

## The measured distribution (2026-08-24), correcting the ~160 estimate

The prior census estimated ~160 open rows in this blind spot. **Measured: 27.** The estimate is wrong for `open` by ~6x. The closest real number is 143 — the count of rows that already reached `done` with zero criteria — so the estimate most likely counted the DONE population, or the whole non-open population (198).

OPEN rows by criteria count (2264 total):

| criteria | rows |
|---|---|
| 0 | 27 |
| 1-3 | 1296 |
| 4-7 | 841 |
| 8+ | 100 |

Zero-criteria across EVERY status: open 27 · done 143 · cancelled 44 · considering 11 · blocked 0 · in_progress 0 = **225 rows**. The `done` 143 are the ones that already spent the bypass.

Every number is one `bp doc query task --filter lifecycle_status=<s> --fields acceptance_criteria` sweep away; the `acceptance_criteria` KEY is absent (not an empty list) on all 27 open rows, confirmed by `bp task get`.

## The 27 open rows classify into five measured classes

1. **Epic root with live children (10)** — criteria arguably delegated downward, but the root itself can be sealed with no proof. `ci-gate-script-integrity-audit` (64 children, 46 open), `api-controller-plug-correctness-audit` (54/24), `task-57451a6ce0a0505e` (189/37).
2. **Epic root NEVER decomposed — zero children (3)** — declared and left standing as ready work with neither a definition nor any work beneath it. `api-auth-accounts-correctness-audit`, `api-plugins-correctness-audit`, `task-04d698cfab17e94f`.
3. **Work already on origin/main, row still open (9)** — the sharpest class, because the row is done in fact and no audit can see it. Each proved by `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main`: `spd-bl-doc-checkbox-is-an-unfocusable-span` (a730cecebf), `jpf-runtime-image-pruning` (88803ac018), `task-5f55dace30cbba8d` (546ec86d5c), `task-9b96d39e0fa3d9e5` (405f8440c4), `task-a4d515e25e2b524d` (4c69d47478), `task-2419c4c5a1081696` (c29efb4f3a), `task-dae18f8eed626f51` (15160047c7), plus `task-802f054c2f455956` (519b9dade9) and `task-04d698cfab17e94f` (142f01142c) where the landed commit is PARTIAL against the row's stated scope.
4. **Substantive leaf task, nothing landed (4)** — `task-ee29f6b43e0a7b88` (cancel 147 shards: a DESTRUCTIVE bulk write with no definition of done), `task-bc3bee400498557f`, `task-01d21110a7ea835f`, and the two all-children-done roots `task-e9e8867d672b9acf` (15/15) and `akbr-feedback-2026-08-epic` (9/9).
5. **Genuinely trivial (1)** — `task-70ff0e0e4c62f95a`, a deliberate SCRATCH probe row.

## One filer accounts for a whole cohort

**Every one of the 6 rows filed by `guards-tree-w34` has zero criteria** — and 3 of them are already `done`, each having closed through the vacuous gate. Among the 198 non-open zero-criteria rows the top closers are `lead-loop` (20) and `cch-w61-s3-roster-pass` (19). This is a FILER-side and CLOSER-side pattern, not random decay: the remedy belongs at the write path, not in a wider reader.

## Drafted criteria — proposal, not applied

3-6 independently checkable criteria were drafted for each of the top 15 ranked rows. Nothing was written into bp: authoring criteria onto another agent's row is a real change and belongs to the row's holder or the lead.

Ranked top 15 (by impact = substantive work whose doneness is currently unobservable):
1 `ci-gate-script-integrity-audit` · 2 `api-controller-plug-correctness-audit` · 3 `task-57451a6ce0a0505e` · 4 `api-auth-accounts-correctness-audit` · 5 `api-plugins-correctness-audit` · 6 `cloud-control-plane-correctness-audit` · 7 `task-495cc9a9af43472c` · 8 `task-21cd02088dd2f762` · 9 `task-ee29f6b43e0a7b88` · 10 `task-bc3bee400498557f` · 11 `task-01d21110a7ea835f` · 12 `task-802f054c2f455956` · 13 `task-04d698cfab17e94f` · 14 `api-content-render-correctness-audit` · 15 `go-client-correctness-audit`.

Draft file (SESSION-SCOPED, copy it before the scratchpad is reclaimed):
`/Volumes/SATECHI/dev-caches/tmp/claude-code/claude-501/-Volumes-SATECHI-github-barkpark/ba5f66f9-9370-4639-ae79-5f38bb0e7fe1/scratchpad/zero-criteria/drafted-criteria-top15.md`

## The load-bearing remedy is at the write path

Widening the audit readers is the WRONG fix — a reader cannot invent a proof obligation that was never authored. Two candidate remedies, both at the chokepoint:
- Make a `done` close over a ZERO-length criteria list require the same loud `criteria_override` a close over unmet criteria already requires. Today it is the only silent route to `done`.
- Refuse to publish a `type:task` in `open` with no `acceptance_criteria` — the same wall that already rejects an unregistered tag.

---

# ADDENDUM — the erasure hypothesis is REFUTED, and the bypass is now proved on a live instance

A lead observed `paper-editor-bundle-stale-and-escape-stoppropagation` appearing to LOSE its four criteria across a stamp-and-close. Tested three ways; the data was never lost.

## 1. The named row never lost anything

`bp doc history` returns 24 revisions. Every one was fetched with `bp doc revision` and its `acceptance_criteria` counted:

`4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4` — 16 revisions at met=0 (2026-07-20 to 07-23), then 21:54 and 21:59 on 08-23 at met=0/in_progress, then 22:24:52 at **met=4**/in_progress (the stamp), then 22:25:50 at **met=4**/done (the close). Its live state today is 4 criteria, 4 met, done.

## 2. The erasure does not happen at scale either

24 done zero-criteria rows sampled across every burst date (07-24, 07-31, 08-06, 08-09, 08-17, 08-18, 08-20, 08-23), 246 revisions read in total. **24 of 24 were BORN EMPTY** — zero criteria at revision 1 and at every revision after. Not one row lost criteria. Rows whose revision reads failed were retried until they resolved rather than being scored as born-empty on a miss.

## 3. What the lead almost certainly read instead

`bp task get` returns the criteria ONLY at `doc.content.acceptance_criteria`. At the top level, `doc.acceptance_criteria` is `nil` on every task — including one with 4 stamped criteria. A reader keyed on the top level sees nothing and reads it as an empty list. Confirmed on the very row in question.

Worse for auditing: `criteria_progress` is present as `{met, total}` when criteria exist and is **ABSENT ENTIRELY** — not `{met: 0, total: 0}` — when they do not. Whether an audit treats that absence as 0/0 or as "skip" decides whether these rows read as fully proven or vanish. Both readings are wrong in the same direction.

## 4. The bypass, proved two-armed on the LOCAL instance (localhost:4000, never production)

Same verb, same worker, same instance, minutes apart. The ONLY difference is whether the list is empty:

| arm | criteria | close done, no override | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | **0** | `bp task close … zc-probe 1` | **ACCEPTED** — lifecycle done, `criteria_override` nil, `close_reason` empty |
| B | 2, both unmet | identical command | **REFUSED** — `criteria_unmet:0,1` |

Arm B's refusal text: "acceptance criteria 0, 1 (0-BASED) are not met on the task AS STORED … that would be the closer grading its own homework." Arm A got no such sentence because there was nothing to count. A third control (3 criteria, stamped 3/3, then closed) came back 3 criteria / 3 met / `criteria_progress {met:3,total:3}` — stamp-then-close preserves the list exactly. All three probe rows were deleted afterwards.

## 5. Rate over time, with a denominator

Raw counts are confounded by throughput, so the rate is what matters. Across 4187 done rows:

| window | done | zero-criteria | rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-07-20 .. 07-23 | 655 | **0** | 0.00% |
| 2026-07-24 onward | 3532 | 144 | 4.08% |
| overall | 4187 | 144 | 3.44% |

The phenomenon has a START DATE — 2026-07-24 — not a gradual onset. After that it is EPISODIC, not monotonic: bursts on 07-24 (39.1% of 23), 08-06 (20.8% of 48), 08-18 (20.7% of 116) and 08-20 (21.3% of 136), separated by days at or near zero. Today's rate (08-23) is 4.3% of 442 — at baseline, not elevated. Days with fewer than 5 closes (08-11 at 100% of 1, 08-14 at 66.7% of 3) are noise and should not be read as trend.

**30 of the 144 (21%) are epic-cycle `*-wave-N-log` rows** — bookkeeping artifacts that never carried criteria by design and should be excluded before any remedy targets the rest. 86 are opaque `task-<hex>` ids; 28 are named slugs.

## What this changes

The defect is authoring and closing, NOT data loss. No write path erases criteria. The remedy stays where it was — refuse a `done` close over an EMPTY list the same way an unmet list is already refused — and gains a second, cheaper leg: make `criteria_progress` return `{met: 0, total: 0}` on a zero-criteria row instead of omitting the key, so every existing audit reader sees the row at all.

---

# ADDENDUM 2 — the gate is REAL and it is only a Logger line. Read from source, not from the log.

`api/lib/barkpark/plugins/tasks.ex`, `warn_if_create_zero/1` at :264-274, reached from `eval_criteria(:absent, prev)` and `eval_criteria([], prev)` at :245-246, wired as a `before_save` lifecycle hook at :119.

```elixir
defp warn_if_create_zero(nil) do
  Logger.warning("task quality gate: a new task is being saved with zero acceptance_criteria — …")
  :ok
end

defp warn_if_create_zero(_prev), do: :ok
```

It returns `:ok` on every path. It cannot halt — the halting arms of the same gate (`{:halt, …}` for an empty title and for malformed criteria) are right beside it, so the permissiveness is deliberate, and the moduledoc at :97-100 says so by name: *"zero acceptance_criteria on a fresh task → SOFT WARN … Never a hard stop — quick authoring and the fresh-install invariant stay smooth."*

**A second hole the log line does not reveal:** the warn fires ONLY when `prev == nil`, i.e. on a fresh create. `warn_if_create_zero(_prev), do: :ok` means a write that takes an EXISTING task from N criteria down to zero passes in complete silence — no warning at any level. Nothing in my revision walk shows a row that actually took that path, so this is an unexercised hole, not an active one.

## The asymmetry that matters more than the halt question

Fifty lines below, the sibling nag `warn_unflagged_merge_gates/1` (:311-327) emits its message TWICE:

```elixir
Logger.warning("task quality gate: " <> message)
Barkpark.Content.Warnings.put("merge_gate_unflagged", message, "warning")
```

and the comment above it explains exactly why the second call exists:

> *"the Logger line alone let 669 unflagged rows accumulate in silence — its only reader was the server journal, which no task author ever sees. Warnings.put rides the mutate SUCCESS envelope (`warnings: [...]`), which the bp CLI prints to stderr (emitWarnings) and Studio folds into its save flash — so the author is told at the moment of authoring."*

**The zero-criteria arm calls `Logger.warning` and nothing else.** It is the same defect, in the same function, that the repo already diagnosed and fixed on the sibling arm — and the diagnosis is written directly above the fix. No task author has ever seen this warning.

## Numbers for the owner — what a hard requirement would have cost

**A create-time halt would block a mainstream authoring flow.** Two independent random samples of done rows that TODAY carry criteria were walked back to revision 1:

| sample | n | born with zero criteria, gained them later |
|---|---|---|
| seed 11 | 25 | 5 (20.0%) |
| seed 29 | 45 | 11 (24.4%) |
| combined | 70 | **16 (22.9%)**, 95% CI ≈ 14–34% |

Create-then-fill is not an edge case: roughly one in four well-formed rows was created empty. A hard gate would have refused on the order of 900 creates that went on to become perfectly good tasks.

**What would break in the suite:** `api/test/barkpark/plugins/tasks_quality_gate_test.exs:89` — describe block *"zero acceptance_criteria on a fresh task → soft warn, still saves"*, two tests, both asserting `{:ok, doc}` and a persisted document. A halt reds both. They are a SPEC, not an oversight.

## Severity is lower than the raw count suggests — and the reason reframes the remedy

Of 153 done zero-criteria rows (measured 2026-08-23 ~22:55; the count grew from 144 to 153 during this lane, so treat it as a moving number):

| bucket | rows |
|---|---|
| epic-cycle `*-log` bookkeeping (never owed criteria) | 30 |
| carries a SUBSTANTIVE `close_reason` (≥120 chars) | 115 |
| thin `close_reason` (<120 chars) | 25 |
| **no criteria, no close_reason, not a log row** | **12** |

Eight of those 12 are `akbr-*` Aker Brygge design-feedback children — visual fixes whose evidence is screenshots in a Paper, exactly the kind of proof that does not fit a criteria list.

**So the ledger is not full of unprovable claims.** 115 of 153 left real prose evidence at close. The defect is that the evidence is UNSTRUCTURED — invisible to every automated completeness check — not that it is missing. That is a machine-readability problem, and it points at a different remedy than a halt.

## Two mechanisms were proposed; one is proved and one is refuted

- **PROVED:** creation-time permissiveness. The gate exists, it only logs, and its log never reaches an author.
- **REFUTED:** erasure on close. See Addendum 1 — 24 revisions of the named row all carry 4 criteria, and 24 of 24 sampled done zero-criteria rows were born empty across 246 revisions. No row has been shown to lose criteria.

## CROSS-REFERENCE (2026-09-06): task-c652c3ba8129c607 — the OTHER door on the same gate, NOT folded into this one

`task-c652c3ba8129c607` ("The criteria gate discounts flips in the close it is gating") is a SEPARATE bypass of the SAME criteria honesty gate, filed and fixed independently of this row. It is recorded here so neither fix can be credited for both.

- **This row's door:** a task carrying ZERO acceptance criteria — `check_criteria_proven/5` has nothing to measure and answers `{:ok, nil}` vacuously. REFUTED on main and cancelled 2026-09-02 (see the close_reason above): `check_close_artifact/5` already stands in that gap.
- **The other door:** a task carrying criteria that are all `met: true` at read time, closed with `--set 'criteria:=[{"index":N,"met":false}]'`. The gate measured only the PRE-write snapshot, so the closing write lowered the lock AFTER the gate had already passed. Reproduced verbatim on prod probe row `task-8e3942fa840b8bf3` (2026-09-06): close rc=0, `lifecycle_status: "done"`, criterion stored `met: false`, and NO `close_override` key on the raw read-back — one advisory warning and nothing else.

**Why they are not merged.** The two doors close by DIFFERENT mechanisms and neither fix reaches the other: this one is shut at the artifact gate (a zero-criteria row must name a PR+sha or paste a run), that one is shut by making `check_criteria_proven/5` measure the UNION of the pre-write and post-merge unmet sets so a close that ENDS with an unmet criterion needs `criteria_override` regardless of which direction the write moved it. Folding them would let one fix take credit for both while the other silently survives — which is exactly what a shared gate name invites and what this pair of rows exists to prevent.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The OPEN distribution is re-derivable: a stated bp query returns 2264 open rows partitioned 27 (zero) / 1296 (1-3) / 841 (4-7) / 100 (8+), and a re-run at read time either reproduces those four numbers or the reader states the measured drift with the new numbers. The ~160 prior estimate is explicitly corrected, not silently replaced.

The zero-criteria population is stated for EVERY lifecycle status, not only open — open 27, done 143, cancelled 44, considering 11, blocked 0, in_progress 0, total 225 — each re-derivable by one `bp doc query task --filter lifecycle_status=<s> --fields acceptance_criteria` sweep, and the six per-status numbers sum to the stated total.

The bypass is proved from source, not asserted: `api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex` is quoted at the two heads that make it real (`check_criteria_payload(_doc, [])` -> `:ok` at ~:458, and `check_criteria_proven/4` returning `{:ok, nil}` when `unmet_after_autostamp/2` yields `[]` at ~:479), showing that a `done` close over zero criteria requires neither evidence nor a `criteria_override` on the record.

Each of the 27 open zero-criteria rows is assigned to exactly one of the five measured classes (live-children root / never-decomposed root / work-already-landed / substantive-leaf-unlanded / trivial), the class counts sum to 27, and every row id appears exactly once across the classes.

Every row claimed to have work already on main names a sha proved an ancestor of origin/main by `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main`, and rows whose landed commit is PARTIAL against the row's stated scope (task-802f054c2f455956, task-04d698cfab17e94f) are marked partial rather than counted as done.

The drafted-criteria artifact exists and carries 3-6 independently checkable criteria for each of the 15 ranked rows, every criterion naming an artifact a reader can re-derive (a command, a file:line, a bp query, or a sha) rather than resting on a closer's assertion; nothing from it has been written onto any of the 15 rows without their holder's or the lead's decision.

The erasure hypothesis is settled with revision evidence, not inference: for a stated sample of done zero-criteria rows, every revision from `bp doc history` is fetched via `bp doc revision` and its criteria length recorded, and the verdict born-empty vs lost-criteria is given per row. A row whose revision read FAILED is retried until it resolves and is never scored born-empty on a miss.

The bypass is demonstrated two-armed on a NON-production instance: an identical `bp task close` is ACCEPTED on a row with zero criteria and REFUSED with `criteria_unmet` on a row with unmet criteria, both outputs pasted, and every probe row created for the demonstration is deleted afterwards (proved by a read-back returning not_found).

The rate of zero-criteria closes is reported per day WITH its denominator (zero closes over total done closes), so a burst in raw count is distinguishable from a burst in throughput; the report names the first date the rate leaves zero and states explicitly which low-volume days are noise rather than trend.

The reader-side confound is documented: `bp task get` exposes criteria only at `doc.content.acceptance_criteria` (top-level `doc.acceptance_criteria` is nil even on a fully stamped row), and `criteria_progress` is ABSENT rather than `{met:0,total:0}` when there are no criteria — each shown with an actual response from a named row.

Benign sub-populations are separated before any remedy targets the set: the count of epic-cycle `*-wave-N-log` bookkeeping rows within the zero-criteria population is stated with its share, so a fix is not aimed at rows that never owed criteria.

The creation-time gate is characterised FROM SOURCE, not from a log line: `warn_if_create_zero/1` in api/lib/barkpark/plugins/tasks.ex is quoted showing it returns `:ok` on every path, its call sites in `eval_criteria/2` are named, and the moduledoc sentence declaring the soft-warn intent is cited with its line numbers.

The silent-update hole is stated separately from the create hole: `warn_if_create_zero(_prev), do: :ok` means a write taking an existing task from N criteria to zero emits NO warning at any level, and the report says whether any row is known to have taken that path rather than implying one has.

The author-visibility asymmetry is documented with both call sites side by side: the merge-gate nag calls `Logger.warning` AND `Barkpark.Content.Warnings.put/3`, the zero-criteria arm calls only `Logger.warning`, and the in-repo comment explaining why the second call was added (669 rows accumulated in silence) is quoted.

The cost of a hard requirement is measured, not estimated: at least TWO independent random samples of rows that today carry criteria are walked back to their first revision, the born-empty fraction is reported per sample and combined with an interval, and the sample sizes are stated so a reader can judge the precision.

What a halt would break is named concretely: the test file, line, and describe block that pin soft-warn-and-save are cited, with the count of tests that would red, and they are characterised as a spec rather than an oversight.

Severity is reported with the evidence-bearing buckets separated: of the done zero-criteria population, the counts carrying a substantive close_reason, a thin one, none at all, and the count that are epic-cycle log rows are each stated, so the number of genuinely evidence-free rows is distinguishable from the raw total. The measurement time is given because the population is moving.

content.description:
MEASURED 2026-07-31 (PDS-D433). THE POPULATION IS FOUR, NOT FIVE: pds-w29-taskboard-envelope-fence is already done 8/8 (closed by loop-lead, epoch 8), so "five merged-but-open rows" double-counts it.

THE FOUR, all with their PR on main: pds-w29-pay-lb 12/14 (#8644 -> 9a1811da4), pds-w29-registry-postcondition-invariant 9/10 (#8645 -> f84f4ac93), pds-w30-live-proof-runner 9/10 (#8647 -> 1cef6eed3), pds-w30-board-envelope-poison-parity 5/6 (#8648 -> 8b2018bc0). All four claims are EXPIRED (worker null), so they are lapsed leases, not locks.

THREE CRITERIA ARE STAMPABLE: pay-lb c10, live-proof-runner c10, and board-parity c6 - whose two companion clauses are independently satisfied (pds-bl-board-tui-reader-honesty is done 4/4 with its amended criteria 2 and 3 stamped against #8648, and pds-w29-taskboard-envelope-fence c8 is satisfied because that row is 8/8).

TWO MUST NOT BE STAMPED, and stamping them to tidy is the failure this epic exists to kill.
 - pds-w29-pay-lb c13 is VIOLATED BY MERGED CODE. Its text forbids editing internal/cli/hetzner_net_cmd_test.go (PDS-D414) and `git show --stat 9a1811da4` lists that file at 13 insertions. Separately it demands a stateful single-resource GET per kind for five kinds and the shipped file has three (/load_balancers/7, /floating_ips/11, /primary_ips/9); the other two deviate by DECLARED design at hetzner_lb_cmd_test.go:365-368. That is ONE defect plus ONE criterion-vs-design conflict to ADJUDICATE - amend the criterion with its reason, or file the D414 breach as its own row. Leaving it silently unmet at 12/14 is the third and worst option.
 - pds-w29-registry-postcondition-invariant c9 is HALF satisfied: merge yes, but both required closures (pds-w27-bl-support-run-registry-rows-vacuous 0/6 and pds-bl-hzresdone-registry-row-vacuous 0/4) are open with substantive unpaid criteria. Stamping it would launder up to ten.

ALSO: 31 PDS children are lifecycle done with met < total, FIFTEEN of them at 0/N (pds-bl-export-no-serialization 0/3, pds-bl-close-holder-and-criteria-gate 0/5, pds-bl-autostamp-elixir-guard 0/4 and twelve more), and pds-bl-ndjson-accept-server-branch is done with NO acceptance_criteria key at all. Fifteen rows at 0/N is not a stamping accident.

REFUTED PREMISE, do not inherit it: there are NOT two non-expiring epoch-8 loop-lead claims in the PDS family. There is exactly ONE open claim with expired_at null (pds-bl-repull-into-populated-target-500, epoch 3, worker null); the epoch-8 detail came from a CLOSE record. The 105-of-4498 null-expiry claims repo-wide are a ledger-wide property filed separately.

--- 2026-09-08, lead-ledger-c5: CRITERION 3 RE-ANCHORED TO A PREDICATE; THE 638 SPLIT OUT ---

RE-MEASURED BEFORE CLAIMING, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON THIS WAS CAUGHT. Criterion 3 named "the 31 false-done rows" and "the 15 at 0/N". At 2026-09-08 the real figures on the whole published ledger are 638 and 369, over a denominator of 5,432 criteria-carrying done rows = 11.7%. The count excludes 386 done rows carrying ZERO acceptance criteria, which are D291's population and a different class; that exclusion is why 5,818 becomes 5,432, and it is stated here so a later reader does not "fix" it back.

"31" IS NOT CALLED WRONG. It is called UNSTATED: the row gives no window, so a taker inherits it as a property of the ledger rather than as a measurement of a slice. A FILED ROW IS A MEASUREMENT WITH A TIMESTAMP. Main refused the option of inventing a window now — that would be guessing which slice the author meant and writing the guess into a criterion, which is the same defect one generation later.

THE SPLIT, per main's ruling (options 2 and 3 together, not either-or):
 * THIS ROW keeps the DOOR. Criterion 3 is now a predicate that refuses or flags a done seal over unmet criteria, motivated by the rate.
 * THE 638 are a SWEEP, filed as their own row WITH A STATED SAMPLING METHOD — deliberately not "triage all 638". A verdict on a sample with a declared method beats a confident verdict on an arbitrary slice, which is what the old wording invited.

THE RE-DERIVATION COMMAND, which pays criterion 4 outright:

    bp doc query task --filter lifecycle_status=done \
      --fields acceptance_criteria,lifecycle_status --all -o json

then count rows whose acceptance_criteria is a NON-EMPTY list and where any entry has met != true. Repeat with lifecycle_status=cancelled and =blocked for the abandon lifecycles.

**`--all` IS LOAD-BEARING AND ITS ABSENCE IS SILENT.** `--limit` caps at 1000 with no warning against a population of 5,818, so a paged read reports roughly a fifth of the ledger and looks entirely fine. That is a lying instrument with a tidy output, and it is exactly how a "31" survives long enough to be inherited.

THE SIBLING ROW IS task-8728d9197113b45e — "638 done rows carry unmet acceptance criteria — 11.7% of the ledger, and it is one habit with 369 instances rather than 638 mistakes". It carries the arrears as a SAMPLED sweep with a declared method, and its first criterion requires the sampling method to be written down BEFORE any row is opened. A taker who turns it back into a 638-row hand triage has undone this split.

=== THE MOTIVATION FOR THE PREDICATE, MOVED HERE 2026-09-08 FROM THE SWEEP ROW THAT WAS RULED DOWN ===

*** CORRECTED 2026-09-08 — THE SENTENCE BELOW OVERCLAIMS AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT FIXED IT CAME AFTER IT WAS WRITTEN ***

THE SENTENCE "ONE IN NINE CRITERIA-CARRYING DONE ROWS DOES NOT CARRY THE EVIDENCE IT CLAIMS" IS WRONG. It was written by main (team-lead) and transcribed here by lead-ledger-c5; it is corrected by measurement rather than by argument, and named so the record shows an orchestrator's framing dissolved by a count rather than a lane quietly restating its own row.

THE ACCURATE SENTENCE: ONE IN NINE WAS CLOSED OVER UNMET CRITERIA, AND 94% OF THOSE SAID SO ON THE RECORD AT THE TIME.

638 OF 5,452 CRITERIA-CARRYING `done` ROWS CARRY AN UNMET CRITERION — 11.7%, and that figure survives. But 598 of the 638 carry `close_override.criteria`, the DESIGNED escape, each naming an actor, the unmet rows and a reason. THEY ARE NOT A GATE FAILURE; THEY ARE THE GATE WORKING EXACTLY AS SPECIFIED. `Close.check_criteria_proven/5` (D289) already refuses a `done` close over unmet criteria, and this lane proved it in PR #16891's own suite.

638 ROWS WITH UNMET CRITERIA AND 638 ROWS THAT ESCAPED A GATE ARE DIFFERENT CLAIMS, AND ONLY MEASURING `close_override` DISTINGUISHES THEM. The predicate this row once demanded would have shipped a DUPLICATE of a gate that already exists.

(Denominator note unchanged and still correct: 5,838 published `done` rows, 386 carrying ZERO acceptance criteria EXCLUDED as D291's population; the 5,838 -> 5,452 gap IS that exclusion and is not an error to fix back.)

SUPERSEDED SENTENCE, PRESERVED: ONE IN NINE CRITERIA-CARRYING DONE ROWS DOES NOT CARRY THE EVIDENCE IT CLAIMS. 638 of 5,432 = 11.7%.

The figure travels with its scope so it cannot be re-derived wrong: 5,818 published rows are `done`; 386 of those carry ZERO acceptance criteria and are EXCLUDED because they are D291's population, a different class. THE 5,818 -> 5,432 GAP IS THAT EXCLUSION AND IS NOT AN ERROR TO FIX BACK. Of the 638: 369 are at 0/N with nothing stamped at all, 230 are exactly one criterion short, 39 are partial. Measured 2026-09-08; re-derive with `bp doc query task --filter lifecycle_status=done --fields acceptance_criteria,lifecycle_status --all -o json` rather than inheriting it — `--limit` caps at 1000 SILENTLY against 5,818 and a paged read prints a tidy, confident, wrong answer.

THE ARREARS WERE FILED AS A SAMPLED SWEEP (task-8728d9197113b45e) AND MAIN RULED THAT ROW DOWN, on the answer below. The number is here instead because a figure that justifies closing a door is wasted inside a closed row nobody opens. The sweep row keeps its pre-registered sampling method and adjudication rule as a reusable method for the next sweep that does run.

WHY THE SWEEP DIED AND THE DOOR DID NOT. Traced to the predicate rather than inferred from call sites: `DependencySatisfaction.satisfied?/1` is the gate every dependent passes through, and it is `done?(content) and has_provenance?(content)` where `done?` reads `lifecycle_status == "done"`. Neither half touches `acceptance_criteria`. The ready-query SQL opens `?->>'lifecycle_status' = 'done'`. Every consumer of `Criteria.progress/1` — board badges, the wire envelope, task_resolver.ex, data_viz.ex — RENDERS a count and none gates.

IT IS NOT THAT NOTHING ACTS ON A FALSE-DONE ROW. PLENTY DOES. IT IS THAT NOTHING ACTS ON ITS CRITERIA. The lifecycle does all the work and the lifecycle is `done` either way, so a false-done row unblocks its dependents exactly as a correctly-closed one does. The 638 are indistinguishable from correct rows to every machine and distinguishable only to a reader. A TRUTHFULNESS DEFECT, NOT A CORRECTNESS ONE — which is precisely why the remedy is a DOOR and not a cleanup: nothing downstream will ever notice the 638, and nothing downstream will ever stop the 639th either.

=== AND THE STRUCTURAL FACT THAT TRACE ESTABLISHED, WHICH IS BIGGER THAN THIS ROW ===

THE WHOLE ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA APPARATUS IS ADVISORY. Nothing in the dependency graph, nothing in the ready query, and no consumer anywhere reads a criterion to DECIDE anything. Every gate this campaign has built on criteria — the merge gate included — is a convention enforced by READERS, not by the system.

THAT IS NOT AN ARGUMENT TO WEAKEN IT. It is the reason the WORDING of criteria has mattered so much: when the only enforcement is what a human or an agent believes on reading a row, the text IS the mechanism. It also explains the shape of nearly every defect found in this campaign — they were defects of what a reader would BELIEVE, not of what the code would DO. A criterion that misleads is not a documentation problem here; it is the failure mode.


RE-DERIVED 2026-09-10 (lead-cli-r3, from cli-r3-w18's read-only pull). `bp doc query task --id_prefix pds-w30- --fields doc_id,lifecycle_status,acceptance_criteria --all` returns FOUR rows in total, three of them done (pds-w30-board-envelope-poison-parity 6/6, pds-w30-hcloud-context-rung-dead-on-macos 3/3, pds-w30-live-proof-runner 10/10); the only open one is pds-w30-anonymous-read-preflight-audit at 0/3, which is unstarted rather than merged-but-open. The "four" of the title is discharged to ONE, and pds-bl-w47-stale-claim-third-shape-rescoped's "only 2 open rows carry a pds-w30-* slug" is also stale by one. THIS DOES NOT TOUCH CRITERION 3: its FIVE is a different population — board-wide false-done rows closed after the D289 gate went live — re-verified live 2026-09-10 with all five still done with unmet criteria and close_override null. The two numbers were never in conflict; the title was measuring the population the row has since stopped being about.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The three stampable criteria are stamped with evidence naming their merge sha, and the four rows' lifecycle is moved to done where every criterion is then met.

pds-w29-pay-lb c13 is ADJUDICATED in writing: either the criterion is amended with the reason the +13 lines in hetzner_net_cmd_test.go were a genuine dependency and the class-A2 create path legitimately supersedes two of the five GET fixtures, or the PDS-D414 breach is filed as its own row. It is NOT stamped and NOT left silently unmet.
pds-w29-registry-postcondition-invariant c9 stays UNMET with an honest note naming its two open blockers and their 0/6 and 0/4 states - or those blockers are genuinely closed first with evidence.

RE-CUT AGAIN 2026-09-08 (SECOND RE-CUT, SAME DAY) — THE POPULATION IS FIVE. The TEN of the first re-cut carried an explicit MEASUREMENT CAVEAT: its dates were `_updatedAt`, a PROXY for the close, and it instructed the next reader to re-derive each real close from mutation_events before treating any row as a leak. THAT CAVEAT HAS NOW BEEN DISCHARGED, AND IT FIRED ON EXACTLY THE CASE IT WAS WRITTEN FOR.

Re-derived from `task.closed` events (674 pages, id-ASC to the end; negative control 0 hits on an impossible id, positive control found a close made the same night). All ten rows have a real close event. FIVE OF THEM MOVED — and they moved EARLIER, not later:

  pds-w22-close-holder-criteria-honesty   row said 2026-08-21 -> REAL 2026-07-28T00:36:33Z
  pds-w22-deploy-stamp-and-harness        row said 2026-08-21 -> REAL 2026-07-28T00:36:43Z
  pds-w22-status-commit-read-path         row said 2026-08-21 -> REAL 2026-07-28T00:36:55Z
  pds-w22-receipt-and-sidecar-honesty     row said 2026-08-21 -> REAL 2026-07-28T00:37:05Z
  pds-w22-manifest-and-counts-honesty     row said 2026-08-21 -> REAL 2026-07-28T00:37:38Z

2026-07-28 IS THE PIVOT DAY ITSELF, so a date-granularity test cannot settle them and the question becomes a clock question: WHEN DID D289 ACTUALLY START RUNNING? Pinned from the surviving deploy record:

  448749cf1 merged                                    2026-07-28T00:35:31Z
  `Deploy (production)` run 30317756494 started       2026-07-28T00:35:34Z
  job `instance` (GUERRILLA_HOST) started             2026-07-28T00:35:57Z
  job `instance` SUCCESS - deploy AND smoke test      2026-07-28T00:43:38Z
  deployment id 5632142355 `success` status           2026-07-28T00:43:39Z

The `instance` job is the ledger box and that is not inferred from the job's name: its smoke test at that sha is a literal `curl` of https://guerrilla.barkpark.cloud/api/schemas asserting 200, so SUCCESS means guerrilla answered on the new build. (`control-plane` was skipped that run.) THE LAST OF THE FIVE CLOSED 6m01s BEFORE THE GATE WAS LIVE, and before the deploy's remote step had even begun. They are PRE-GATE IN EFFECT and they leave the population.

WHY THE RECORD EXISTS WHEN THE RUN LISTING SAYS IT DOES NOT: Actions run retention has expired for July - `gh run list -w "Deploy (production)" -L 400` reaches back only to 2026-09-04 - but the deployments API is on a different clock and pages back to 2026-07-13. The run and its jobs are then reachable BY ID from the deployment status's log_url though they appear in no listing. A LISTING'S FLOOR IS NOT THE API'S FLOOR, and a lane that had checked only `gh run list` would have concluded, wrongly and confidently, that no July record survives.

THE LIVE LEAK IS THESE FIVE, and each is a distinct closing session:

  2026-08-19T23:53:40Z  4/8  cch-w58-s2-a-refusal-is-not-a-started-run
  2026-08-24T16:51:48Z  0/1  task-085400fe55735eb7
  2026-08-24T21:52:35Z  6/7  task-2b7cbaf8265f6b4e
  2026-09-02T17:47:06Z  0/1  task-dc8084c57af3b5a7
  2026-09-05T01:05:36Z  2/3  task-2bde38694b4539b2

THIS IS NOT A SOFTER FINDING THAN THE TEN, AND THE ROW SHOULD NOT BE READ AS ONE. The first re-cut's consolation was that five of the ten were ONE closing session, so the ten were 'really six events'. THE CLUSTER IS PRECISELY WHAT WAS REMOVED. What remains is five separate sessions, five distinct id prefixes, spread thin across 17 days with the most recent on 2026-09-05 - a continuing trickle rather than one bad night, which is the worse shape of the two even though it is the smaller number.

ONE BOUND STATED SO IT IS NOT OVER-TRUSTED: 00:43:39Z is when the deploy SUCCEEDED. instance-deploy.sh restarts the service partway through that 7m41s window, so the true cutover lies somewhere in 00:35:57Z-00:43:38Z and CANNOT be narrowed further - the step-level log died with the run's log retention. It does not matter here only because the ENTIRE window is later than 00:37:38Z. Had any of the five closed at 00:40Z it would be marked UNRESOLVED rather than resolved to the convenient side.

A gate is warranted only if a live path is found; if all five resolve to writes that bypassed the task verbs entirely, the remedy is a different door and this criterion says so rather than demanding a gate anyway.

corpus.title: The ready queue serves brief cards carrying a `claim` that no ready FIXTURE can construct: seeding a worker-bearing claim removes the row from the page, yet live serves nine such cards

content.description:
MEASURED 2026-09-07 by lead-ledger-c5 and its builder while shipping PR #16798 (task-69ba050120c2c021). Recorded because it was found in passing and NOT chased - it may be correct behaviour I do not understand, and I would rather file the discrepancy than let it evaporate.

THE OBSERVATION. The `/v1/tasks/ready?view=brief` card renders a `claim` block. On a live `bp task ready --limit 50` the `claim` key measures 936 B across the page and appears on NINE of fifty cards. In the in-repo fixture, seeding nine worker-bearing claims dropped the rendered page from 50 cards to 41 - the rows left the ready queue outright. The fixture's own claim residues are deliberately WORKER-LESS for exactly that reason, and the card census printed by the tripwire confirms they render nothing at all: `claim` is absent from every one of the 50 fixture cards.

SO THE LIVE PAGE CARRIES A CLAIM SHAPE THE FIXTURE CANNOT REPRODUCE. Two readings, and I am not asserting either:
 (a) the ready predicate admits rows whose claim has lapsed but still names a worker, and the fixture's local queue does not reproduce that state; or
 (b) the exclusion predicate differs from what the fixture assumes, in which case the fixture's premise - that a worker-bearing claim is never ready - is wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. 936 B of the live page is a key the byte guard measures as ZERO, on top of the density gap that row already declared. It is also the shape a stale-claim sweep would key on. And a `claim` object can be lapsed RESIDUE, so filtering on claim PRESENCE is already known to be wrong - this row is about which of those the ready endpoint actually serves.

WHAT I DID NOT DO. I did not read the ready-queue predicate, did not check whether the nine live claims carry expired_at, and did not test whether a lapsed worker-bearing claim survives the queue locally. Nobody has re-derived this; it is one measurement, taken in passing, by two parties who agreed. Treat it as UNCONFIRMED, not established: I am claiming I saw a discrepancy, which is weaker than claiming there is a defect.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The live/fixture divergence is SETTLED by reading the ready-queue predicate itself, not by inference from card counts: state whether a row whose claim names a worker can be ready, and under exactly what condition (lapsed, expired_at set, released). Quote the predicate.

The nine live claim-bearing ready cards are characterised against that predicate - for each, say which condition admits it. If they are admitted legitimately, the FIXTURE's assumption is what is wrong and must be corrected; if they are not, the predicate is. Name which of the two it is; do not close this row without picking one.

NEGATIVE ARM: whichever side is corrected, a test reproduces the LIVE claim shape on a ready page and mutation-proves it in both directions. A fixture that renders zero `claim` keys while production renders nine cannot detect any regression in that block, which is the same vacuous-guard class as task-69ba050120c2c021 - so a fix that leaves the fixture rendering zero claims does NOT satisfy this.

corpus.title: The ready queue and the claim door read task dependencies from DIFFERENT sources — content.dependencies vs task_edges

content.description:
FOUND 2026-09-06 while building cch-w3-task-birth-attribution, and found only because a mutation FAILED to bite.

TWO DOORS ANSWER "what are this task's dependencies" FROM TWO DIFFERENT SOURCES:

  Tasks.Queue.ready/1   reads content.dependencies — a JSON array on the row itself
                        (queue.ex, the NOT EXISTS over jsonb_array_elements_text(content->'dependencies'))
  Tasks.Claim           reads task_edges — via Edges.dependencies(doc.id, kind: :blocks)
                        (claim.ex check_deps_satisfied/1)
  Tasks.Close           also reads task_edges, same Edges.dependencies call
                        (close.ex all_blockers_done?/1, the cascade-unblock)

So the ready queue and the claim door do not consult the same set. A dependency recorded in content.dependencies but with no matching blocks EDGE is INVISIBLE to the claim door; one recorded as an edge with nothing in content.dependencies is invisible to the ready queue.

HOW IT SURFACED, which is the only reason anyone noticed: a test fixture set content.dependencies and asserted the claim door refused. It did not refuse — because that door reads edges, and the fixture had created none. The test was passing against a dependency the door could not see. A mutation reverting the claim-side predicate then reddened nothing, which is what sent me looking.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT SYMMETRIC. The ready queue is what hands work out, and the claim door is what lets a worker take it. A row whose dependency exists only as an edge is offered as READY by the queue while the claim door refuses it — the worker sees a row it cannot take, with no explanation. A row whose dependency exists only in content.dependencies is withheld by the queue while the claim door would have allowed it — work that never surfaces.

WHAT THIS ROW MUST ESTABLISH, in order:
  1. WHICH SOURCE IS AUTHORITATIVE. Both are written by something; neither is documented as the truth. Until that is decided, every fix is a guess about which door is wrong.
  2. WHETHER THEY DISAGREE TODAY, measured over the live corpus rather than assumed. The dependency feature is tiny — 4 rows carry content.dependencies and 7 rows are named as a dependency across 8,580 — so the measurement is cheap. A count of zero is worth recording as a FLOOR ("no live divergence today"), never as a dismissal: the feature is small enough that zero is what you would expect even if the two sources were wired to different writers entirely.
  3. WHAT HAPPENS TO A ROW WHOSE DEPENDENCY EXISTS IN ONE AND NOT THE OTHER — named, per direction, with the observable symptom a human would report.

NOT THIS ROW'S QUESTION, deliberately: whether the dependency feature earns its complexity at 4 rows in 8,580. That is a real question and folding it in would let the divergence be closed by deleting the feature rather than by understanding it.

A POSSIBLE FOURTH COPY, found 2026-09-06 while fixing the fallout from cch-w3-task-birth-attribution.

`api/test/barkpark/tasks/claimable_statuses_test.exs` contains a test whose own name is "unsatisfied content.dependencies excludes the candidate (RAW-SQL CTE COPY)". A test that describes itself as holding a copy of production SQL is a fourth place this predicate lives, alongside queue.ex, claim.ex and close.ex.

IT PASSES TODAY. When the dependency predicate was narrowed to require close provenance, that test failed — and it was fixed by giving its FIXTURE provenance, not by editing any SQL inside it. So either its copy is thin enough not to include the satisfaction clause, or it delegates to the real query. I did not chase it down, because the row it belonged to was already open and the fix did not need the answer.

WHY IT BELONGS HERE ANYWAY. "It passes today" is exactly how a copy earns its place until it silently disagrees. A test carrying its own duplicate of production SQL is the same drift shape this row is about, one level further out: not two doors reading different sources, but a test asserting against a predicate that is not the one production runs. When it diverges it will not fail loudly — it will keep passing while the thing it claims to pin has moved.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH: whether that test's SQL is a genuine copy of the ready CTE or a thin fixture query; if a copy, whether it still matches production today; and whether it should be replaced by a call into the real query so it cannot drift. Same question as the queue-vs-edges divergence, asked of a test instead of a door.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The AUTHORITATIVE source is decided and recorded — content.dependencies or task_edges — with the writers of each named from the code, and the reasoning for the choice. A fix that makes both doors read the same source without first deciding which is right is a coin flip dressed as a repair.

DIVERGENCE MEASURED on the live corpus: for every row, does its content.dependencies set equal its blocks-edge set? State the count of disagreeing rows per direction, and if the count is zero say so as a floor with the population size, not as an all-clear.

Both directions of the failure are named with their observable symptom: a dependency visible only to the queue, and one visible only to the claim door. A test constructs each and pins what the fleet actually sees.
The chosen fix is MUTATION-PROVED at BOTH doors, and the mutation is asserted to have applied. A change that makes one door agree while the other silently keeps its own source is the defect restated.
MERGE-GATED (the lead closes this): the PR is merged to main with the required gates green on its head, and the merge sha is recorded.
