corpus.title: The task ledger stops double-counting draft twins, without deleting the tasks that legitimately live at drafts.<id>

content.description:
THE DEFECT IS ONE MISSING PREDICATE, IN FIVE READ PATHS, AND THE OBVIOUS FIX IS THE WRONG ONE.

WHAT IS BROKEN. child_tasks/2 (api/lib/barkpark_web/controllers/tasks_controller.ex:395-408) is the ONLY producer of `bp task get <epic>`'s children + child_count (child_count = length(children) at :380). Its whole pipeline is: from(d in Document, where: d.type == "task", order_by: ...) |> maybe_filter_workspace |> maybe_filter_project |> maybe_filter_parent_id |> Repo.all(). There is NO draft or twin predicate. And maybe_filter_parent_id (api/lib/barkpark/tasks/query.ex:76-86) makes it WORSE rather than neutral: it regexp-strips ^drafts\. from BOTH sides, so a draft twin whose parent_id is drafts.<epic> is GUARANTEED to match the published epic's doc_id. A task existing as both t1 and drafts.t1 therefore contributes TWO rows and +2 to child_count.

THE SAME HOLE IS IN FOUR MORE PLACES. The /v1/tasks index base (tasks_controller.ex:271-276) has no doc_id predicate either. Barkpark.Tasks.Query contains NO exclusion anywhere in its 814 lines - every drafts. occurrence is a STRIP (:68, :81, strip_drafts/1 at :719) - so Query.docs_for_query/2 (:190-198, the PortableDoc task-block live-plan fetcher) and Query.agg_docs/2 (:420-427, the data-viz aggregate fetcher) are holed identically. FIXING ONLY THE FIRST TWO CREATES A NEW INCONSISTENCY: papers would double-count while the API does not. Fix all four or scope and document the exclusion explicitly.

THREE IN-REPO PREDICATES EXIST AND THEY ARE NOT EQUIVALENT. Choosing wrong silently UNDERCOUNTS:
 (A) api/lib/barkpark/tasks/queue.ex:146-173 - TWIN COLLAPSE, published-wins, scope-matched SQL NOT EXISTS. Its moduledoc (:16-19) states the law: "a drafts.<id> shadow row is suppressed while its published twin exists in scope, so a twinned task yields exactly ONE ready/claimable row (published-wins)". The o.doc_id != parent_as(:doc).doc_id guard (:159) is what stops a published row suppressing itself. THIS IS THE CORRECT LAW.
 (B) api/lib/barkpark/tasks/board.ex:210-219 - the same law by a different mechanism (group_by published_id, then canonical_twin = Enum.find(twins, hd(twins), & &1.status == "published")). Note the hd(twins) default: a drafts-only task SURVIVES.
 (C) api/lib/barkpark/studio_chat.ex:1807 - a BLANKET `where: not like(d.doc_id, "drafts.%")`. Correct THERE (its comment at :1802-1803 says why: the claim lives on the published row) and WRONG HERE. It would delete from every epic's count every mutate-created task that lives at drafts.<id> with NO published twin - a population api/lib/barkpark/tasks/claim.ex:128-139 exists precisely to claim ("tasks created via mutate land as drafts.<id>", exact-first then drafts.-fallback resolution). SHIPPING (C) WOULD TRADE A DOCUMENTED OVER-COUNT FOR AN UNDOCUMENTED UNDER-COUNT. Do not.

BUILD. Put ONE shared collapse_twins/1 helper in Barkpark.Tasks.Query - its own moduledoc (:2-18) already declares it "ONE owner for the task index/filter fragments ... so the filter semantics can't drift", and putting a fourth fork anywhere else contradicts the module that already claims the job. Apply it at child_tasks/2, the /v1/tasks index base, docs_for_query/2 and agg_docs/2.

MECHANICAL PRECONDITION - IT WILL NOT COMPILE WITHOUT THIS. queue.ex's form uses parent_as(:doc), which requires the outer query to bind `as: :doc`. Neither child_tasks' base (:400) nor the index base (:271-276) binds it today. Either add `as: :doc` to both, or write the helper as a correlated subquery that does not depend on the named binding.

WHY THIS ALSO ANSWERS THE OPEN INDEX QUESTION. Under twin collapse (rather than a drafts filter) a drafts-only row has no DISTINCT same-scope published twin, so the NOT EXISTS is vacuously true and the row SURVIVES in both the children read and the index. The two surfaces therefore stay consistent, and claim.ex's population is preserved by construction. Divergence between `bp task get <epic>` and `bp task ls --parent <epic>` would manufacture exactly the disease this wave exists to cure - one number meaning two things.

DISCLOSE THE PAGINATION CONSEQUENCE. The index's limit/offset live in the BASE (:274-275), so adding a WHERE shifts which rows land on which page and moves `bp task ls --all` totals. Say so in the PR body. Consider a diagnostic opt-out (e.g. ?twins=raw) so a human can still SEE shadow rows after this lands - the next debugging session will want it.

A GREEN SUITE HERE PROVES NOTHING BY DEFAULT. api/test/barkpark_web/controllers/tasks_controller_test.exs documents its total as 8 tests (ready/claim/close/edges/auth) and NONE concerns drafts or twins, so it will pass before AND after. You must add both new tests yourself.

STATE THE DELTA. Paste before/after child_count for task-fb4fb869490b4213 from a real bp run. It moves DOWNWARD or not at all (the predicate can only remove rows). Today the epic carries 319 children / 172 live, of which exactly ONE live row is a drafts.* shadow (drafts.dr-w26-hg-gyldendal-operator-packet-corrected, unpaired and unpublishable per dr-w27-bl-gyldendal-packet-409s-on-the-dedup-wall) and six cancelled ones. So the expected movement on THIS epic is ZERO for the live count - which is itself the point: an unpaired drafts-only row must NOT be deleted. A count that drops by one here means you shipped predicate (C).

HIGH-FLIP-RISK: REACHABILITY. The judgment is whether twin collapse preserves the drafts-only population. This wave rules YES by construction, and the non-vacuity test below is what makes that judgment able to lose. An independent re-derivation is owed before merge.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A single collapse_twins/1 helper lives in Barkpark.Tasks.Query and is applied at child_tasks/2, the /v1/tasks index base, docs_for_query/2 and agg_docs/2 - not copy-pasted into four places.
The predicate is TWIN COLLAPSE (published-wins, scope-matched NOT EXISTS with the self-exclusion guard), NOT the blanket `not like(d.doc_id, "drafts.%")` form from studio_chat.ex:1807.
NEW TEST 1: a twinned pair (t1 and drafts.t1 in the same scope, both children of the epic) is counted ONCE in child_count.

NEW TEST 2 (NON-VACUITY, the one that makes the ruling able to lose): a drafts-only child with NO published twin is STILL counted. Swapping the helper for the blanket drafts exclusion must RED this test - paste that red.
The index and the children read return the SAME cardinality for the same set, demonstrated by a paired query in the test.
`as: :doc` is bound on both bases (or a binding-free correlated subquery is used) and the app compiles - a parent_as(:doc) lifted verbatim will not.

Before/after child_count for task-fb4fb869490b4213 is pasted from a real bp run, with the direction of movement explained. On this epic the LIVE count should not drop; a drop of one means the blanket predicate shipped.
The pagination consequence (limit/offset sit in the base, so page boundaries and `bp task ls --all` totals move) is stated in the PR body.
Gate green and pasted: cd api && CC=/usr/bin/clang MIX_ENV=test mix test test/barkpark_web/controllers/tasks_controller_test.exs
MERGE-GATED (the LEAD closes this): merged to main.

corpus.title: bp task stamp silently REVERTS an earlier criterion — a second stamp at the same epoch persists a stale criteria array (lost update)

content.description: Measured 2026-09-02 by core-w6 while closing task-1f369f877ae7a774. Criterion index 1 was stamped and the CLI read back the confirmation 'the store holds it - met=true'. After stamping indices 2 and 3 at the SAME claim epoch, index 1 read back met:false with 0 bytes of evidence. The per-stamp read-back had been TRUE when printed; a later stamp wrote back a criteria array captured before it, and the earlier met flag was lost. bp task close then correctly refused the done close with 409 criteria_unmet naming index 1, which is the only reason this was caught at all. This is a silent data-integrity defect in the ledger's criterion write path, not a CLI display bug: a lead who stamps several criteria in one claim and trusts the per-stamp receipt will close over criteria the store no longer holds, or will be blocked by a 409 naming a criterion they can see they already proved. The per-stamp read-back is NOT sufficient evidence that a stamp survived.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A test proves the lost update: stamp criterion A met, then stamp criterion B at the SAME epoch, then re-read the whole acceptance_criteria array and assert A is STILL met=true with its evidence intact. The test is RED against the current write path and GREEN after the fix.

The criterion write is made read-modify-write safe on the server: a stamp updates only its own index rather than persisting a criteria array the caller read before an earlier stamp landed. Name the mechanism in the module doc (per-index patch, or a rev/epoch CAS that refuses a stale array instead of silently overwriting it).
A stamp that would clobber another criterion is REFUSED with a named code rather than accepted, and the refusal has its own test that is RED when the guard is removed.

corpus.title: The CHILDLESS half of the umbrella trap is still live: a P0 GOAL row whose children hang off another root renders as an ordinary leaf, and both obvious vocabulary signals are already REFUTED

content.description:
FILED 2026-09-07 by lead-ledger-c4 after shipping PR #16762 (merge sha 84fc4d124f, task-52f4f3aff99c64d5), which closed HALF of this problem and says so in its own moduledoc.

WHAT #16762 FIXED. `bp task ready` brief cards now carry a `dispatch` key derived from the PARENT EDGE: `delegated` when at least one child is non-terminal, `undecided` when children exist and all are terminal (the rule REFUSES to judge), absent for a leaf. Measured on a live 1,000-row page: 15 delegated, 6 undecided, 979 untouched leaves. Re-derived independently by the lead with a different definition of a live child - both derivations agree.

WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX, AND THIS ROW IS THAT. Recall against a hand-labelled page is 11 of 16. A seal row whose children hang off a DIFFERENT root carries child_count 0 and renders as an ordinary leaf, so the parent edge is structurally blind to it. FIVE CONFIRMED MISSES on the same page, and the first one is the whole point: task-08b05ad1e792a850 'GOAL: drive the mobile epic to the seal' AT PRIORITY 0 - the exact trap task-52f4f3aff99c64d5 was filed for - plus task-b55fafd148bb2578 (Agent flight recorder, epic), survey-once-build-forever-epic, legendary-quality-takeover-final-review and ecd-bl-second-env-launch-proof.

TWO DEAD ENDS, ALREADY MEASURED. Do not re-derive these.
(1) The clause 'the LEAD closes this' is NOT a seal signal - it is merge-gate BOILERPLATE appearing as the final criterion on roughly a third of ordinary buildable rows (verbatim: 'PR merged to main (LEAD closes this criterion, pasting the merge SHA)'). A detector keyed on it inverts the failure it is meant to fix.
(2) A bare case-insensitive `seal` over criterion text matches 23 of 1,000 rows and MOST are ordinary buildable slices about the seal PREDICATE SCRIPT - tooling/grip/seal.mjs, seal-predicate.mjs, scripts/seal-run.sh. THE VOCABULARY READS A TOOL'S FILENAME, NOT A ROW'S SHAPE. This is worse than (1) because its false positives look topical rather than boilerplate, so a reader spot-checking two hits would accept it.

THE CANDIDATE SIGNAL, MEASURED BUT DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED. The discriminating property is the INBOUND edge rather than the outbound one: a criterion that requires ANOTHER task id to be CLOSED. Measured 8 hits across 988 rows carrying criteria, of which about 3 are genuine (pe-w7-epic-seal, task-08b05ad1e792a850, task-a9467ebf92ded337). Better than vocabulary and NOT shippable as-is: the ready card does not carry criteria text, so this needs either that text on the card or a server-side pass. The #16762 builder recorded this scope limit in writing rather than smuggling it in, which is why this row exists.

ALSO CORRECTED HERE, because it nearly killed the buildable half: an orchestrator broadcast held that all five predicted umbrellas carry child_count == 0 and that this REFUTES the child_count premise. True of those five; FALSE of the specimen the original row names - task-fb4fb869490b4213 renders in `bp task ready` carrying child_count 359. There are TWO POPULATIONS, and 'insufficient alone' is a different claim from 'refuted'.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A ready row whose remaining work is a SEAL, but which carries child_count 0, is mechanically distinguishable in `bp task ready` output. Demonstrate on task-08b05ad1e792a850 specifically - the PRIORITY 0 miss - by quoting its rendered line beside a genuine leaf's from the same listing.

The signal is STRUCTURAL and its error rate is MEASURED against a hand-labelled corpus, reported as precision AND recall with the labelled set named. Neither of the two refuted vocabulary signals may be used: the clause 'the LEAD closes this' (merge-gate boilerplate on ~32% of ordinary rows) and a bare `seal` token (23 of 1,000 hits, most of them rows ABOUT the seal predicate script). If you reach for a vocabulary term anyway, you must first show it beats the inbound-edge signal on the same corpus.

NEGATIVE ARM, required, and it must be measured on the SAME page as the positive arm: ordinary leaves are not reclassified, the reclassified count is strictly less than the page size, and the rows the rule DECLINES TO JUDGE are named rather than silently defaulted to dispatchable. State the false-positive rate PER BUCKET if the rule emits more than one class - an aggregate rate does not hold inside its buckets, and the highest-confidence bucket has been the least accurate one before.

The relationship to PR #16762 is stated in the code, not only here: whatever ships says which population it covers and which it does not, so the next reader cannot mistake half the fix for the whole one. #16762's Dispatchability moduledoc already names its own five false negatives; match that standard or better.

corpus.title: bp task ready hands out epic UMBRELLAS as P0 work: a 359-child seal row is indistinguishable from a dispatchable defect, and its own criterion 0 forbids quoting the headline its title advertises

content.description:
FOUND 2026-09-07 by lead-deploy-12 while triaging its own lane, and it cost a full triage read on the single most attention-grabbing row in the queue.

THE STATE: task-fb4fb869490b4213 ("Guerrilla deployments fail 69% of the time and nothing says so") is returned by `bp task ready` as PRIORITY 0. It is not work. It is a 359-CHILD EPIC UMBRELLA whose last criterion reads verbatim: "SEAL - THE LEAD CLOSES THIS. Every child is done, cancelled WITH A REASON, or re-parented out, with the count RE-MEASURED at seal time."

WHY IT IS READY: its claim EXPIRED at 2026-09-06T01:27:00Z and the lease sweeper left claim.worker = null. A lapsed umbrella is indistinguishable, in the ready listing, from a lapsed leaf defect. Nothing in the listed fields says "this is a seal, not a slice".

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN ONE WASTED READ: the row's own criterion 0 is already MET and says its headline is STALE. A child (task-a02741ad13bbf010) re-derived the failure rate on 2026-08-09 with a relabelling-immune measure and found failed/(failed+live) collapsing 90.89 (07-30) -> 83.42 (08-05) -> 60.47 (08-06) -> 3.14 (08-07) -> 1.21 (08-09). Criterion 0 then states, in its own text, that NO criterion, plan or build in this epic may quote 69% as current. So a lead who claims this P0 in good faith, reads the title and description, and dispatches a builder, sends that builder to repair a 69% failure rate the row itself forbids quoting. The most eye-catching row in the backlog is a trap that only opens if you read to the seventh criterion.

THIS IS THE GHOST CLASS'S STRUCTURAL COUSIN. A ghost is a row whose premise died. This is a row whose premise is fine and whose AUDIENCE is wrong: it is addressed to a lead at seal time, and the queue hands it to whoever is looking for work. The existing verdict set (fixed elsewhere / foreclosed / superseded / never reproducible / contaminated / unblocked / instance-stale-class-live) has no shape for it, because nothing about the row is stale - it is correctly open, correctly P0, and correctly not dispatchable.

THE CHEAP ANSWER THAT MUST NOT SATISFY THIS ROW: telling leads in a doc or a brief to "check child_count before dispatching a P0". Every lane already has more doctrine than it can hold, this specific instruction would be the Nth line of it, and the failure mode is a tired lead at 4 a.m. reading a title and a priority. The burden must move off the reader and into the instrument.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `bp task ready` MECHANICALLY distinguishes an umbrella-seal row from a dispatchable slice, in its own output, without the reader opening the row. A doc line, a lane convention, a brief paragraph, or an instruction to leads DOES NOT SATISFY THIS CRITERION - it is the cheap answer this row exists to refuse, and it leaves the burden on the reader who is already tired. Demonstrate by running the shipped command against task-fb4fb869490b4213 and against a known leaf row in the same listing, and quoting both rendered lines side by side so the difference is visible in the output itself.

The rule is DERIVED FROM ROW STRUCTURE, never from a typed list of known umbrella ids and never from title vocabulary. A vocabulary match finds only the phrasings someone already imagined - one sweep in this campaign keyed on vocabulary and missed two of three instances. Name the structural signal used (for example: a positive child_count with open children, or a criterion the row marks as the lead's seal) and prove it DISCRIMINATES by running it over a full `bp task ready` page and reporting how many rows it reclassifies, with at least ONE reclassified row that is NOT task-fb4fb869490b4213. A rule that fires only on the example that prompted it has not been shown to work.

NEGATIVE ARM, required: an ordinary leaf row is NOT reclassified. Take a row with zero children that is genuinely dispatchable, show it renders unchanged, and show the count of reclassified rows is strictly less than the page size. A classifier that flags everything is as useless as one that flags nothing, and both look like success from the reclassified row's side. Also state which rows the rule declines to judge and why, rather than silently defaulting them to dispatchable.

corpus.title: bp task close enforces only the epoch — any worker can close any claim, and unmet criteria never gate it

content.description:
FOUND WHILE REOPENING THE FALSELY-CLOSED CROWN (PDS-D138). `api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex:157-161` `check_fencing/2` matches solely on `%{"claim" => %{"epoch" => row_epoch}} when row_epoch == observed_epoch`. It does NOT compare the worker id. That is how `oc-lead` closed a claim held by `epic-builder-the-climb-...`: any worker string can close any claim whose epoch it knows. And close never reads `acceptance_criteria` as a precondition, so a task with unmet criteria closes clean (TASK-SYSTEM.md:88 "Unmet criteria warn, never gate").

CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED NOT HYPOTHESISED: `pds-w1-crown-proof` was closed at 2026-07-20T04:13:22Z with criteria 6 and 10 `met:false`, seven seconds after #4722 merged, while the builder's own now-line on that same claim read "Task stays OPEN per D122 — rung 6 unmet." PDS-D122 has ZERO mechanical enforcement. The epic's own closing rule was violated by the epic's own lead because nothing could stop it.

WHAT TO DECIDE, NOT JUST BUILD. Two separable changes and they have different risk: (a) fence on HOLDER IDENTITY as well as epoch — low risk, obviously right, but note the legitimate lead-closes-on-merge flow must keep working, so it likely needs an explicit override rather than a hard refusal; (b) refuse a `done` close while criteria are unmet unless an explicit force flag is passed — higher blast radius, because "unmet criteria warn, never gate" is currently documented behaviour that other flows may rely on. Survey the callers before changing (b); a doc-and-behaviour change together needs its own note in TASK-SYSTEM.md.

NOT PDS'S LANE. This is the tasks plugin, not api/tenancy + internal/cli + scripts/. Concurrent sessions have held uncommitted edits in `api/lib/barkpark/tasks/*.ex` — check `git status` on any shared checkout and work in your own worktree.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A close attempted by a worker that does not hold the claim is REFUSED (or requires an explicit documented override), with a test that fails on the pre-fix code. Evidence: the test name plus pre-fix red and post-fix green output.
The lead-closes-on-merge flow still works — the legitimate path is proven by a test, not assumed. Evidence: the test name plus green output.
A decision is recorded (in the PR body or TASK-SYSTEM.md) on whether unmet criteria now gate a done close, with the callers surveyed either way. Evidence: the survey list plus the recorded decision.
TASK-SYSTEM.md matches the shipped behaviour — no doc line survives that the code contradicts. Evidence: the doc diff.
PR merged to main (LEAD closes this criterion on merge).

corpus.title: A retrieval limit mistaken for a population — three bp read surfaces silently return a subset (or ZERO) and nothing marks the answer as truncated

content.description:
CLASS, not an instance. Three variants measured on 2026-09-01, one class: a caller asks for the population, receives a bounded subset, and NOTHING in the response says so. Every downstream count is then computed over an unknown fraction and is internally consistent.

VARIANT 1 — bp task ready --limit is silently capped at 1000. --limit 2000 and 5000 both return exactly 1000 rows, no truncation marker. Read as a horizon it hid 1543 rows: the ready queue is 2543 deep (walked with --limit 1000 --offset N until an empty page), and only the top 400 had ever been triaged. Six lanes were staffed off a 16 percent sample for a full session. --offset exists and works; nobody had used it.

VARIANT 2 — bp search recall is partial and unflagged. "bp search query PPCC sealed shard" returned 72 distinct ppcc-build-task-* ids while direct id-space enumeration (001..160, bp task get per id) found 160 present with no gaps: 45 percent recall. A lifecycle tally computed from the search result read 42 done / 30 open — confident, internally consistent, over less than half the set. Enumerate a known id space; a miss is then a real absence, not a recall gap.

VARIANT 3 — bp doc query paper --limit above ~200 returns ZERO rows, silently, at exit 0. Measured: --limit 50 -> 50, 100 -> 100, 200 -> 200, 500 -> 0, 1000 -> 0. Not an error, not a truncation marker: an EMPTY result. Worst variant: a partial answer invites a sanity check, an empty one invites the conclusion that there is nothing there. Sizing the Paper corpus with --limit 1000 yields "0 papers"; paging at 100 with --offset returns 1050. This nearly mis-sized a migration campaign the same day.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS. Each surface should honor the requested limit, refuse it loudly (an error naming the max), or mark truncation in the envelope (a total field, a truncated flag, or a next-offset cursor). Variant 3 additionally needs the over-limit request to ERROR rather than empty-succeed — returning zero for asking too politely is fail-open in the reporting direction. RED-before test per surface: request limit > max, assert the response errors or carries a truncation marker, and assert a naive count from the response cannot silently be smaller than the true population (fixture-scoped ids; the fleet shares one test database).

DISTINCT FROM task-406343e4f378cbdf (bp task ready --all INTERMITTENTLY omits a row): that is a non-deterministic race where an identical run over unchanged data returns 0 then 1. This is the opposite — a DETERMINISTIC, reproducible ceiling returning the same truncated result every time with no marker. Same surface, different mechanism. Also distinct from the web/lib, astro-search and hundesteder application-code truncation rows: those are Sanity client .limit() calls in shipped app code; this is the bp CLI's own read verbs.

Found by the L6-DOCS fleet while triaging the never-read tail of the ready queue.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: EACH OF THE THREE VARIANTS GETS A TRUNCATION MARKER OR A NAMED DISPOSITION. Variant 1 (bp task ready --limit silently capped at 1000 — 2000 and 5000 both return exactly 1000), variant 2 (bp search partial recall — 72 of 160 ppcc ids, 45%), and the third variant this row names are each either made to SAY they are truncated, or recorded with the reason they cannot be. A subset that does not announce itself is the whole defect.

THE MARKER IS MACHINE-READABLE, NOT PROSE ON STDERR. A caller parsing -o json can tell a complete answer from a bounded one (a `truncated` boolean, a `next_cursor`, or a total alongside the page) — a warning line before the JSON is exactly what a scripted reader misses.

THE MEASUREMENT IS REPRODUCED ON TODAY'S HEAD BEFORE THE FIX. The caps and recall figures are from 2026-09-01; the row re-runs them and records the current numbers, since the ready queue depth and the search corpus both move.

THE COST IS RECORDED SO THE CLASS IS NOT RE-FILED AS A NIT. The row keeps the measured consequence — six lanes staffed off a 16% sample for a full session, and a lifecycle tally (42 done / 30 open) that was confident, internally consistent, and computed over less than half the set.
MERGE-GATED (the lead closes this): PR merged to refs/remotes/origin/main with the four required contexts green; merge sha recorded.

corpus.title: A done-close over ZERO criteria is silent, while a close over UNMET criteria costs a reason

content.description:
`bp task close <id> done` treats "this row has NO acceptance criteria" as identical to "every criterion is proven". One clause, verified on origin/main at api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex:450:

    defp check_criteria_proven(%Document{} = doc, "done", landed, override_reason) do
      case unmet_after_autostamp(doc, landed) do
        [] ->
          {:ok, nil}

`merge_gate_criteria_list/1` returns `[]` when the `acceptance_criteria` key is ABSENT, so the empty-list arm is reached by two completely different worlds. A done-close over UNMET criteria is refused unless the closer writes an `override_reason` — a real cost, paid in a sentence. A done-close over NO criteria sails through with no reason, no refusal, and NO RECORD THAT NOTHING WAS CHECKED.

THIS IS THE SAME ABSENT-VS-ZERO COLLAPSE THIS CODEBASE REFUSES EVERYWHERE ELSE, and the surrounding comments prove the file already knows the distinction matters: the block immediately above deducts merge-gate criteria BY NAME rather than by falling through, and the next clause is headed "Exempt BY NAME - not by falling through a catch-all." The zero-criteria case is the one place the file does fall through.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, not hypothetical. Census of the whole ledger, 7,407 task documents, `bp task ls --all`, rows read from the `docs` key explicitly (no `or []` chain), filter control run on the exact flag combination used (`lifecycle_status=zzzz-impossible` -> 0, so the clause is not being dropped):

  criteria-less AND lifecycle_status=open    224
  criteria-less AND ALREADY done             134   <- the realized hazard
     ...closed under a real claim            132
     ...carrying a close_reason              112
     ...with a MERGED Task:-trailer PR        52

Those 134 rows can never be audited by anyone. There is no ratio to read, no criterion to re-derive, and nothing in the close that says so. A row with 3 criteria closed over 1 unmet leaves a written reason; a row with 0 criteria closed over nothing leaves silence, and silence reads as completeness.

`acceptance_criteria` is NEVER an empty list in this ledger - 6,984 rows carry a non-empty list and 423 have no key at all. So "no ratio" always means KEY ABSENT, and the fix has a clean discriminator to key on.

THE OPEN 224 ARE THE UNREALIZED HALF, and their shape says this is authoring drift rather than policy: 181 of 224 carry a full Purpose brief - someone wrote the entire case and stopped before the criteria - and 81 of the 208 leaf rows sit under a parent whose OTHER children are >=80% criteria-carrying. Same filer, same wave, criteria written for the neighbours and skipped here. Only 2 rows sit in a family where criteria are the exception. Roughly 78% unfinished authoring against 22% deliberate (13 containers, 26 probe/scratch rows, 10 notes/rulings).

SCOPE
1. Split the `[]` case at close.ex:450. A `done` close on a row whose `acceptance_criteria` key is ABSENT must take the same override path an unmet close takes - or be refused outright. Closing an unverifiable row should cost a written sentence instead of nothing.
2. Exempt the legitimately criteria-less kinds BY NAME, not by silence - containers/goals whose children carry the criteria, probe/scratch rows, and notes/rulings. The file's own convention is to exempt by name and it says so in a comment; follow it.
3. Do NOT run a backfill campaign over the 224. The 163 never-started rows are benign, and the fix is what stops them becoming the next 134.

ACCEPTANCE - both directions, each arm mutation-proven independently.
  * A `done` close on a criteria-less row WITHOUT an override reason is REFUSED, and the refusal names the absent key rather than reporting a generic criteria failure. Evidence: the refusal output.
  * The SAME close WITH an override reason succeeds and the reason is persisted and readable afterwards. A guard that refuses everything is indistinguishable from one that refuses correctly unless the permit arm is proven too.
  * A close on an exempt kind still succeeds with no reason.
  * A close on a row that HAS criteria, all met, still succeeds - the existing legitimate `[]` path must not regress. This is the arm most likely to break, because it shares the clause being split.
Disabling the new guard must red ONLY the refusal test. If any permit test goes green-to-red or stays green when the guard is off, the tests are not testing the guard.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A `done` close on a criteria-less row WITHOUT an override reason is REFUSED, and the refusal names the absent key rather than reporting a generic criteria failure. Evidence: the refusal output.
The SAME close WITH an override reason succeeds and the reason is persisted and readable afterwards — the permit arm proven, not just the refusal.
A close on an exempt kind still succeeds with no reason.
A close on a row that HAS criteria, all met, still succeeds — the existing legitimate [] path must not regress; this arm shares the clause being split.
Disabling the new guard reds ONLY the refusal test. If any permit test goes green-to-red or stays green when the guard is off, the tests are not testing the guard.

corpus.title: Nothing runs landed-open-report.sh — the landing back-link has a reader and still no consumer

content.description:
scripts/landed-open-report.sh (shipped in #16616, merged 920276260) reads the ledger for rows carrying the landed-on-main label that are still open or in_progress -- work that merged and was never stamped or closed. At the time of the change: 8,718 rows walked, 439 carry the label, 41 live. Filter named: content.labels contains landed-on-main AND lifecycle_status in {open, in_progress}.

NOTHING RUNS IT. It is a script a lead must remember to invoke, which is the same shape as the gap it was built to close -- a facility nobody consumes.

WHY IT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED IN #16616, and why this is its own row rather than a follow-up commit: the workflow needs a ledger READ TOKEN that the builder could not exercise or prove in CI, and an unproven scheduled job is precisely how this repo grows a permanently-red workflow that everyone learns to ignore. Shipping the schedule on an unproven credential would have traded a script nobody runs for a workflow nobody trusts. The token has to be proved FIRST.

Two further constraints inherited from the reader's own design, which the schedule must not undo. (1) The report FLAGS its two measured false-positive classes rather than filtering them -- [PARENT] rows (epic/goal, or child_count > 0; a PR naming a parent is a CONTRIBUTION, not a discharge, and one row was named by 34 PRs) and [GATE?] rows (an unmet criterion with human-gate wording). A scheduled consumer must keep those flags visible; a clean-looking list is the failure mode. (2) The reader REFUSES on an empty read -- a malformed input prints CANNOT READ and exits 2, and --min-population guards the honestly-empty case -- so the schedule must treat a refusal as a red, never as "nothing to do".

Recall is low by design (439 of ~2,618 PR-backed rows), so this does not replace the merged-PR trailer sweep; both are needed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A ledger read token usable from CI is PROVED before any schedule is wired: a workflow run (or a dispatch) shows scripts/landed-open-report.sh completing against the LIVE ledger and printing a non-zero population, with the run id quoted. A 401/403 must be loud and must fail the job, never a silent empty list.

The scheduled job treats a FAILED READ as a red: with the token deliberately unset or invalid, the job FAILS and its log carries the reader's own CANNOT READ line. Proven by a real run or a dispatch, not by reading the YAML.

The output preserves the [PARENT] and [GATE?] flags, so a reader cannot mistake a contribution or a human-gate row for a discharged one. Shown by quoting an actual run's output containing at least one flagged row, or by stating that zero were flagged in that run and why.
The job publishes NO new required context and its venue is justified in one sentence in the workflow file: a report about ledger state, not about a PR diff, does not belong on every PR push.
MERGE-GATED (the lead closes this): PR merged to origin/main with the four required contexts green; merge sha recorded.

corpus.title: Close-path gate inventory: three honesty gates, none discharges another - proven by firing each, plus a shipped fenced_off hint that names causes which did not happen

content.description:
THE CLOSE-PATH GATE INVENTORY, verified by MAKING EACH GATE FIRE against live guerrilla on 2026-08-24 (lane ledger-stamp-shift). Probe target was task-71af7d4c31f9ed5d, a row this lane filed: every step below is a REFUSAL, and a refused close writes nothing, so the row ended the session byte-identical (lifecycle open, 0/4 criteria met, no holder, description restored). No successful close was attempted on any row.

=== THE THREE HONESTY GATES (close.ex `overrides` map) ===

1. HOLDER — refuses {:not_holder, held}. Discharged ONLY by --set holder_override="<reason>". VERIFIED FIRING (exit 6): "this task's claim is held by \"gate-probe-a\", not by the worker you named, so closing it would record THEM ...". Recorded as close_override.holder (actor + held_by + reason + ts).

2. CRITERIA — refuses {:criteria_unmet, [0-based indices]}. Discharged ONLY by --set criteria_override="<reason>". VERIFIED FIRING (exit 2), full string: "acceptance criteria 0, 1, 2, 3 (0-BASED) are not met on the task AS STORED, and criteria flipped in this very close command do not count - that would be the closer grading its own homework. Stamp them as you prove them (bp task stamp <id> <worker> ...)". Recorded as close_override.criteria; the override NEVER flips the criteria - they stay met:false.

3. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT — refuses {:acknowledgement_unposted, issue}. Discharged by --set ack_override="<reason>" OR by the row's ack_gate criterion being stamped met. NOT VERIFIED BY FIRING - see the honesty note below.

NONE DISCHARGES ANOTHER, and this is now MEASURED, not read:
  * criteria_override against a non-holder close -> STILL not_holder (exit 6). PROVEN.
  * holder_override against unmet criteria -> STILL criteria_unmet (exit 2). PROVEN.
  * criteria_override against a stale epoch -> STILL fenced_off (exit 6). PROVEN.

=== ORDER OF CHECKS (close.ex ~378-395), and why it matters ===
check_fencing -> check_close_holder -> check_work_digest -> check_criteria_payload -> check_acknowledgement -> check_criteria_proven.
VERIFIED: a non-holder close on a row with four unmet criteria returns not_holder, not criteria_unmet - so holder genuinely precedes criteria.
The ack gate sits DELIBERATELY ahead of the criteria gate. The source records why, and it is the sharpest design note on the path: the acknowledgement criterion IS an acceptance criterion, so with the order reversed the caller hears "criteria_unmet: [0]" - a message that says nothing about a waiting reporter and points them at criteria_override, "the ONE override that must never discharge this."

=== THE NON-HONESTY REFUSALS ON THE SAME PATH (distinct, often confused) ===
  * fenced_off - epoch mismatch. VERIFIED FIRING (exit 6) after a pulse bumped the epoch 3->4 and a close used epoch 3.
  * doc_changed_since_claim - the brief moved under the claim; carries current_rev + changed_fields; discharged by --set observed_rev=<rev>. NOT VERIFIED (API 500s blocked the precondition twice; the brief never actually moved, so the close that followed refused on criteria instead - a contaminated run, reported as unverified rather than counted).
  * stale_claim, invalid_lifecycle, unknown_task, stale_rev - reachable but not probed.

=== ANSWER TO "ARE not_holder AND fenced_off THE SAME REFUSAL WEARING TWO NAMES?" ===
NO. Measured back to back on the same row in the same minute: a fresh epoch + wrong worker gives not_holder with a full explanatory sentence; a stale epoch + correct worker gives fenced_off. Both exit 6, but they are different gates with different messages and different remedies (holder_override vs re-claim). They are NOT the same refusal.

=== A REAL DEFECT FOUND WHILE PROBING - the fenced_off hint names a cause that did not happen ===
Stamping on a deliberately stale epoch returned, verbatim:
  bp: fenced_off
    hint: your claim epoch is stale (lease swept or a blocker/move fenced you) - re-claim under your worker id, then retry
NEITHER named cause occurred. The lease was live and nothing was blocked or moved: the epoch moved because MY OWN PULSE bumped it, seconds earlier. The hint omits the single most common cause and asserts two that are usually false. Source: internal/cli/errors.go:913. The same wrong pair is mirrored on origin/main in docs/contracts/roster-reading.md:117. PR #13894 corrected this in docs/setup/TASK-SYSTEM.md but the CLI string and roster-reading.md still carry it - the fix landed in one of three places.
Also inconsistent: on CLOSE the same refusal prints a bare "bp: fenced_off" with no hint at all; only the STAMP path carries the (wrong) hint.

=== WHY THE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT GATE IS NOT VERIFIED BY FIRING, AND WHAT IS ===
The gate fires only on a row where intake_born?(doc_id, content) is true - meaning doc_id == "gh-<N>" AND content.github.issue == N - which is unacknowledged (no criterion carrying ack_gate:true is met), on a done or cancelled close.
VERIFIED LIVE, the precondition: exactly three genuinely intake-born rows exist - gh-8463, gh-8461, gh-6290 - all lifecycle open, and ALL THREE carry ZERO acceptance criteria, hence zero ack_gate criteria, hence unacknowledged. That matches the module's own note that nine of eleven measured rows carried no criteria and "an empty list is exactly what let them read as proven."
NOT VERIFIED, the firing, and the reason is a refusal to take a risk rather than a limitation:
  (a) Probing a real intake row is unsafe HERE SPECIFICALLY BECAUSE those rows have zero criteria. The criteria gate runs AFTER the ack gate, so on a normal row it is a backstop - if my reading of the ack gate were wrong, criteria_unmet would still refuse and nothing would be written. With zero criteria there is NO backstop: the ack gate is the only thing between the probe and closing a real outsider's issue row.
  (b) Minting my own gh-<N> row is unsafe because the GitHub bridge is ACTIVE on guerrilla (bp github status -> health.active true, live conflicts, non-empty mirror queue). A GenServer pumps mutation_events into debounced outbound MirrorJobs, so a new gh-* row risks an outbound write to GitHub - a hard prohibition on this lane.
So the gate is characterised precisely but NOT run. Anyone completing it should mint the row on a server with the github plugin OFF, where the ack predicate still applies because close.ex calls Acknowledgement directly rather than through plugin dispatch.

=== A FOLKLORE TRAP THIS TURNED UP ===
"gh-* rows are protected by the acknowledgement gate" is FALSE for most of them. Of the seven gh-* rows in the published corpus, gh-1 through gh-6 are NOT intake-born: gh-1 carries github.issue 1580, so "gh-" <> "1580" != "gh-1" and intake_born? returns false. They are internal rows mirrored OUT to GitHub, not reporter issues taken IN. Only the drafts-perspective rows whose id and issue number agree (gh-8463, gh-8461, gh-6290) are subject to the gate. An audit that assumed the id prefix was sufficient would be wrong on four of seven.

=== LIFECYCLE ASYMMETRY, from source, worth knowing before it bites ===
The criteria gate EXEMPTS cancelled and blocked by name (abandoning acceptance criteria is what cancelling means). The acknowledgement gate exempts blocked but DELIBERATELY NOT cancelled, and the source states the reason: "we are not going to do this" is the single message an outsider most needs and is least likely to receive, so a cancel is the last place to hand out an exemption. NOT VERIFIED by firing (would require cancelling a real row; bp task create was returning DBConnection.ConnectionError throughout, so no disposable row could be minted).

=== DOCUMENTED VS FOLKLORE ===
DOCUMENTED: all three honesty gates and their overrides are named in the bp task close help text (plugins/tasks.ex:804), including "none of them discharges another". TASK-SYSTEM.md's troubleshooting table documents not_holder, criteria_unmet, fenced_off, doc_changed_since_claim, stale_claim, not_ready, blocked_by_unsatisfied_deps.
FOLKLORE (nowhere written down): the ORDER of the gates and why ack precedes criteria; that a pulse is the usual cause of fenced_off (and that the shipped hint says otherwise); that fenced_off prints a hint on stamp but not on close; that exit codes differ (criteria_unmet 2, not_holder 6, fenced_off 6, API failure 8); the cancelled-vs-blocked asymmetry between the two gates; and that a gh-* id does not imply intake-born.

=== CROSS-REFERENCE, and it sharpens the ack-gate risk above ===
An existing row already names the underlying hazard: `zero-criteria-is-a-legal-bypass-of-the-close-gate` - "Zero acceptance criteria is a LEGAL BYPASS of the close honesty gate, not just an audit blind spot - 27 open rows, 143 already spent it". That is exactly why the three intake-born rows could not be probed safely: a row with zero acceptance criteria passes the criteria gate VACUOUSLY, so on gh-8463 / gh-8461 / gh-6290 the acknowledgement gate is not merely first, it is the ONLY gate standing. This inventory did not discover that hazard; it independently hit it from the other direction and should be read alongside that row.

=== FILED WITH content.dedup_bypass, DELIBERATELY AND ON THE RECORD ===
bp task create refused twice with its own honesty gate - "the backlog scan failed (Postgrex.Error)" and then "the backlog scan did not finish inside its 5000ms budget. The create was REFUSED rather than filed unchecked - no duplicate check ran, so nothing here claims this task is new." That refusal is itself a fourth gate, on the CREATE path rather than the close path, and it fails CLOSED under load. Rather than retry-loop against a saturated server I bypassed it explicitly, having first run the duplicate check by hand: `bp search` over the close/honesty-gate vocabulary and a title scan of the open backlog returned no row inventorying these gates. So the bypass carries a manual check, not an unchecked filing.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The three honesty gates, their exact refusal atoms, their discharge keys, and the measured fact that none discharges another are recorded with the live refusal strings that proved it. Evidence: the run output.
The question 'are not_holder and fenced_off the same refusal wearing two names' is answered with a back-to-back measurement, not an inference. Evidence: both refusals from the same row minutes apart.
Every gate is either verified by firing, or explicitly recorded as NOT verified with the reason - no gate is reported as proven on a reading alone. Evidence: the verified/not-verified split.
A defect found while probing is filed rather than mentioned: the fenced_off hint names causes that did not happen. Evidence: the verbatim hint, the true cause, and the source location.
The probe leaves the ledger as it found it - no row closed, no criterion flipped, no brief left edited. Evidence: the post-probe read.

corpus.title: pr-task-gate reds correct PRs because it asks who is typing, not whether the change is task-backed

content.description:
THREE-PART LAW (charter .claude/workflows/bp-honest-gates-charter.md, D1): cause + population + ratchet. Here part three is the FIXTURE SET — the mutation-proof vehicle is the ratchet.

THE REAL ROOT TASK IS ALREADY FILED: pr-task-gate-contradicts-close-on-criteria (open, p1, unclaimed, github #4891). Concrete case: gr-p5r8-seal-predicate-freeze, 5/5 criteria met and legitimately closed, then PR #4848 failed the gate. Hit 3x on 2026-07-20 and resolved each time by hand. This slice is that fix; adopt its framing, do not re-derive it.

DO ORDER MATTERS — FIXTURES FIRST (charter D9). scripts/pr-task-gate.test.sh is currently 9/9 green, and three of four predicate mutations are caught. BUT deleting the gate's central lifecycle check entirely — `[ "$lifecycle" = "in_progress" ] || fail` at scripts/pr-task-gate.sh:91 — leaves the harness 9/9 GREEN. Cause: the only non-in_progress fixture is `doc openone open -` (test.sh:26) where `-` means claim:null, so "open task fails" is actually caught by the WORKER check at :92, never by the lifecycle check. The fixture set contains ZERO (non-in_progress lifecycle x worker present) cases and the two checks are indistinguishable on it.
Adding `doc donetask done fable-tob` and `doc canctask cancelled fable-tob` with two `check ... 1` lines gives an 11/11 baseline, and replaying that same mutation then fails with `FAIL done+worker fails want 1 got 0` / `FAIL cancelled+worker fails want 1 got 0`. WRITE THE FIXTURES AND SEE THEM CATCH THE MUTATION BEFORE YOU TOUCH THE PREDICATE. A builder given both at once writes the predicate first and reads a green harness as validation.

THE PREDICATE (charter D7). The invariant is "this change is task-backed", not "someone is actively typing right now".
  PASS when: (lifecycle == in_progress AND claim.worker present) OR (lifecycle == done AND claim.closed_by present).
  FAIL, definitively, when: no task reference; task 404; lifecycle == open; lifecycle == in_progress with no claim.worker; lifecycle == done with NO claim at all (never worked); cancelled.
  NEUTRAL (exit 2) stays exactly as it is: ledger unreachable, non-2xx, malformed JSON.
WHY closed_by AND NOT landed.prs: content.landed.{prs,files,capability_slugs} is the DESIGNED positive PR link (close.ex:290, union-merged :291-306, accepted over HTTP at tasks_controller.ex:459) — and it is DEAD DATA. 400 done tasks sampled from the live ledger: 0 with content.landed, 0 with landed.prs non-empty. The Go CLI structurally cannot send it: internal/apiclient/client_close_payload_test.go:103 pins the close body to exactly worker_id/observed_epoch/lifecycle_status (:123 adds only observed_rev). Gating on it today yields a gate that can never be green. claim.closed_by is populated on 375/400 and proves the task went through the claim/close engine rather than being hand-flipped through bp doc patch. Populating landed.prs is filed as wave-2 work.
WHY NOT blanket done==pass: that is the gate lying in the other direction. And a `done` task cannot be re-claimed to satisfy the old predicate either — the claimable allowlist is ~w(open blocked) at claim.ex:26 and queue.ex:35 — so the deadlock was genuinely unrecoverable.
THE 404 BRANCH STAYS DEFINITIVE (charter D8). It is decided by HTTP code at pr-task-gate.sh:58 BEFORE the body is ever parsed at :66, so no lifecycle/claim rule can reach it. It correctly caught an invented task id (`cloud-gui-remake-epic`) the same day. Keep the `nonexistent task fails (exit 1)` fixture green.

THE TRIGGER. .github/workflows/pr-task-gate.yml has NO `types:` filter — `on: pull_request:` carries only a comment — so it inherits opened/synchronize/reopened. A corrected PR body does not re-fire, and the verdict is STICKY; the documented workaround in the wild is closing and reopening the PR (observed twice in the run history, 4-9 minutes after the fail, both merging clean minutes later). Add `edited` so a body correction re-fires. This is mechanically isolated: the merge-base cutoff step (:52-64) has no `if:` and recomputes `enforced` fresh from base.sha on every trigger, and the hotfix lane (:66-75, auto-file keyed on PR number at :98-106) is idempotent — both work identically on `edited`.
SCOPE NOTE, argued not skipped: adding a `hotfix!` LABEL after open is a `labeled` event, not `edited`, so the hotfix lane keeps the same non-refire property. That is a real residue; name it in the PR body rather than silently widening scope.

DO NOT ABSORB task-1471170216ac6b54 — ITS MECHANISM IS REFUTED. It claims the TTL sweeper leaves lifecycle_status=in_progress with a nil worker. apply_reap/1 sets worker -> nil (ttl_sweeper.ex:256) and lifecycle_status -> "open" (:269) into the same new_content, written by ONE Repo.update_all (:284). `git log -S` puts both lines in the sweeper's FIRST commit (dc90f9071, 2026-05-27); only one commit has touched the file since. ttl_sweeper_test.exs:126-128 asserts the pair directly, 12/12 green. The live ledger has 9 in_progress tasks and 0 with a nil worker. The real source of that state is a hand-flip around the claim/close engine, which schema.ex:147-161 already warns about in its own comment. Its second defect (the work-digest close fence) is untested and may be independently real.

CALIBRATION, so you do not over-claim: of 19 pr-task-gate reruns traced over ~23h, 13 were the task being genuinely open/unclaimed at PR-open time (workflow discipline, not a gate defect — the `edited` change makes recovery cheap but does not make them pass), 4 were the hand-flip in_progress+no-worker state, 1 was a 404 race, and only 1 was the `done` case. The gate's honest green rate is 24/25 = 96% against a measured 80%; the entire gap is the contaminated predicate. This slice closes the gap; it does not claim to remove the retries.

DO NOT TOUCH anything outside scripts/pr-task-gate.sh, scripts/pr-task-gate.test.sh and .github/workflows/pr-task-gate.yml.

corpus.title: The publish seam still lets a pre-close draft write divergent criteria onto a done task — Content.Lifecycle.publish_after_gate/5 bypasses TerminalCriteriaFence (#17949's stated residue)

content.description: RESIDUE of task-3c3094aa8f5f3847 (cli PR #17949, Barkpark.Tasks.TerminalCriteriaFence), stated by its builder w8-publish-door 2026-09-12 and deliberately NOT closed there because content/lifecycle.ex was outside that row's granted fence. #17949 refuses a document-door write that changes acceptance_criteria on a task row that is and stays closed-terminal (done/cancelled), wired into Content.Writer's two task chains (do_create_document/6, do_upsert_document/6). Lifecycle's criteria_fence/2 is a REGRESSION fence (it walks the published row's proof-bearing criteria and refuses a draft that drops or unproves one); a published row with NO criteria, or a draft that ADDS an unmet entry beside met ones, regresses nothing and lands false-done. The rule is already written and public: TerminalCriteriaFence.changes_terminal_criteria?/2 (api/lib/barkpark/tasks/terminal_criteria_fence.ex) — the lifecycle seam should call it, not restate it. Natural shape per the builder: a terminal arm on gate_task_publish/2 + assert_no_criteria_regression!/3. Fence: api/lib/barkpark/content/lifecycle.ex (api lane) + api/test/barkpark/content/**. Witness row: task-2b7cbaf8265f6b4e (see #17949's module header).

corpus.title: A conditional acceptance criterion can go LIVE after its holder files it not-applicable, and nothing watches for it

content.description:
A criterion written as a CONDITIONAL ("If route X is taken: prove Y") can be honestly recorded as NOT APPLICABLE, and then have its condition become TRUE later — under a DIFFERENT row, after its holder has stopped watching. Nothing in the ledger re-evaluates it. The row sits at N-1 of N carrying a criterion everyone has filed as moot, and it reads as blocked-on-nothing.

MEASURED INCIDENT, 2026-08-24, start to finish inside 42 minutes:

  10:05:18Z  task-33e6c69d4640ee5b, criterion 3, holder `fix-mix-env-release` records an honest MISS:
             "Inline-annotation route deliberately NOT taken: main was red and the CI reconcile is the
              small, process-correct unblock... This criterion is therefore not applicable to the route
              taken and is left UNMET rather than stamped — a conditional criterion must not be collected
              by making its condition false."
             That reasoning is CORRECT. #13740 took the baseline-reconcile route.
  10:47:02Z  #13736 lands: "convert six line-pinned Traversal waivers to inline annotations". The inline
             route IS taken — under task-f44c1839cb28b0af, a DIFFERENT row, which has since closed done.
  ~18:00Z    An unrelated verification lane re-reads the row and finds criterion 3 unmet. Its condition had
             been true for seven hours. No event, no queue, no gate connected the two.

WHY THE HOLDER IS NOT AT FAULT, which is what makes this systemic rather than an incident. The miss note is
a model of honesty — it names the route taken, refuses to collect the criterion by making its condition
false, and says so on the record. The failure is that a conditional criterion has no watcher: `met` is a
one-way lock, `--miss` appends to `attempts[]`, and neither carries a re-evaluation trigger. The condition
lives in prose inside the criterion text, so nothing can evaluate it mechanically either.

BLAST RADIUS, not yet measured — that is criterion 1. The shape is "If <route/condition>: <proof>" in a
criterion body. A grep for a leading `If ` / `Once ` / `When ` / `Should ` in `acceptance_criteria[].criterion`
across the ledger bounds the population. Rows whose ONLY unmet criterion is a conditional one are the
suspect set: each is either genuinely blocked, or silently satisfiable, and today nothing distinguishes them.

WHY IT MATTERS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. (a) A row stalls at N-1 forever and its work looks unfinished when it is
done — the sobelow row sat closeable for seven hours. (b) The dangerous direction: a lane reads "not
applicable" and CLOSES the row on it, discharging a proof burden that has quietly become live. Closing on a
stale N/A is indistinguishable from closing on a satisfied criterion by anything the ledger records.

NOT A DUPLICATE of the criteria-gate rows. `close --set` un-setting `met`, and the criteria gate itself, are
about criteria being BYPASSED. This is about a criterion whose truth VALUE changes underneath an honest,
correctly-recorded miss. No gate is bypassed; the gate is evaluating a stale premise.

RELATED PRIOR ART, worth reading before designing anything: the standing rule "A criterion states a check,
not a fact" exists because a `met=true` went FALSE when a later decision superseded it. This is the same
decay running the other way — an UNMET conditional going satisfiable — which suggests the remedy is a
property of criteria in general, not a special case for conditionals.

REMEDY IS DELIBERATELY UNSPECIFIED. Options seen in the ledger already: a `--miss` that takes a re-check
trigger the way `stage --disposition parked` REQUIRES `--reopen-trigger`; a periodic sweep over rows whose
only unmet criteria carry conditional language; or a rule at authoring time that a conditional criterion
must name the observable that flips it. Decide on measurement, not taste — criterion 1 is the measurement.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: THE POPULATION IS COUNTED, not estimated: sweep acceptance_criteria[].criterion across the ledger for conditional openers (a leading If / Once / When / Should, case-insensitive) and report (a) how many rows carry at least one, (b) how many of THOSE are open with the conditional as their ONLY unmet criterion — the suspect set — and (c) how many of the suspect set have a condition that is TRUE on origin/main today. Paste the counts and the query used. If (c) is zero the row is still worth closing with that number on record; a measured zero is a result.

THE INCIDENT IS RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY, not copied from this brief: show from bp events (not from the criterion text) that task-33e6c69d4640ee5b criterion 3 was missed at 2026-08-24T10:05:18Z and that #13736 landed the inline route at ~10:47Z under task-f44c1839cb28b0af. Naming the two timestamps from the ledger itself is what proves nothing connected them.

A REMEDY IS CHOSEN ON THE MEASUREMENT AND THE REJECTED OPTIONS ARE NAMED. Whatever ships — a re-check trigger on --miss (mirroring how stage --disposition parked REFUSES without --reopen-trigger), a sweep, or an authoring rule — the row records what was NOT built and why, with the number from criterion 1 as the reason. If the population is small enough that no mechanism is worth it, say so explicitly and close: 'documented, not built' is a legitimate outcome here and must be stated rather than left implied.

IF A MECHANISM SHIPS, IT IS MUTATION-PROVED: plant a row whose conditional criterion is missed and whose condition is then made true, and show the mechanism SPEAKS (a red, a queue entry, a sweep hit) — with a control run on an untouched row showing it stays quiet. A mechanism that cannot be shown firing on a known positive is not a mechanism. Not applicable if criterion 3 concludes 'documented, not built' — in which case record THAT here rather than leaving it blank, since this row is itself about conditionals going stale.

corpus.title: Allow the non-flipping {:miss, note} attempt stamp on a DONE row - the sanctioned per-criterion instrument whose absence makes bulk closers paste one evidence blob across every criterion

content.description:
SPUN OUT OF task-c285e15a70e5bb59 (the duplicate-blob audit, closed 2026-08-24). That audit found a defect and named its cause; this row is the CURE. The convention filed alongside it is only the cheap mitigation.

THE PROBLEM, AS MEASURED. 108 published tasks carry 202 met=true criteria whose evidence is byte-identical to a sibling criterion's. A stratified hand-read (24 of 108, 8 per band, the 5+ band a full census) put the real rate at 12/24 strictly (15/24 counting borderline), extrapolating to roughly 43-57 tasks and 95-130 criteria -- NOT 202, which is a lead-count. The defect splits almost perfectly by CLOSER ROLE rather than by builder: bulk/packet closers (packet-closer-0823, cc-showcase, hg-close-packet, lead-mgseal, closed_by=None) were 12 real + 1 borderline and ZERO legitimate; single-row reconcilers (codex-task-quality-wave5, fable-hobby-lead, lead, worker-3, airdrop-spinner) were 9 legitimate and ZERO real.

THE CAUSE IS A MISSING INSTRUMENT, NOT CARELESSNESS -- and one row confesses it verbatim in its own evidence blob: '[lead reconcile: stamp failed on already-closed task, criteria corrected via mutate to reflect verified CI-green+merge]'. Barkpark.Tasks.Stamp gates on check_in_progress BEFORE check_holder, so any stamp against a sealed row returns {:not_in_progress, status} and writes nothing (re-proved live on ct-w1-tui-client: 'bp: not_in_progress:done', with a read-back confirming the row was untouched). A closer who has legitimately verified something about a done row therefore has NO sanctioned per-criterion write, and reaches for a raw /v1/data/mutate that pastes ONE string across every remaining criterion. The three closed_by=None rows are consistent with exactly that: a raw mutate leaves no claim attribution.

THE PROPOSAL. Permit the {:miss, note} ATTEMPT path -- and ONLY that path -- on a done (and cancelled) row. Concretely: relax Stamp.check_in_progress so it admits a terminal row when the built update is the attempt shape, while continuing to refuse {:met, _} on anything that is not in_progress.

WHY THIS ADDS NO FALSE-DONE SURFACE. The miss path CANNOT flip a lock, by construction rather than by convention. Internal.apply_entry_update's attempt clause does Map.put(entry, 'met', Map.get(entry, 'met') == true) -- it PINS met to its current stored value, normalising anything absent or malformed to false, precisely so the merge default of met->true is never inherited (the D8 lock-flipping footgun). Internal.flips_met_true?/1 returns false for any update carrying an 'attempt' key, so the D56 criterion_text_required guard does not even engage, and Stamp.build_update's miss clause requires a non-empty note. A miss appends %{note, ts, worker} to the criterion's attempts list, bounded to the 5 most recent. There is no reachable path by which an attempt-only stamp changes met, evidence, or any criterion text.

WHY THE SEAL ARGUMENT DOES NOT APPLY TO IT. Stamp's own comment justifies the in_progress gate as 'a done/cancelled task's ledger is sealed by close; stamping it would rewrite history behind the seal.' That reasoning is exactly right FOR THE MET PATH -- a met-flip after close rewrites the claim the close sealed. An attempt note rewrites NOTHING: it is append-only, it cannot alter the sealed verdict, and it is strictly more honest than the raw mutate that closers currently substitute for it. The seal protects the verdict; an attempt records an observation ABOUT the verdict.

WHAT TO DECIDE, NOT ASSUME. This row is a proposal, not a settled design. Open questions the implementer must answer rather than inherit: (a) AUTH -- a done row has a closed claim, so holder+epoch cannot be the check; is the right predicate the original closer, any workspace admin, or any authenticated agent, and does the answer differ for cancelled? (b) Should the attempts bound of 5 hold, or should post-close attempts have their own bound so a sweep cannot evict a builder's real mid-claim attempts? (c) Does close's work-digest fence need to know about post-close attempts (it should not -- attempts are not brief fields -- but assert it). (d) Does the task.criterion mutation event need a marker distinguishing a post-close attempt so boards do not render it as live progress?

RELATIONSHIP TO THE CONVENTION. The convention (receipt written ONCE at row level to close_reason/disposition_reason; unprovable criteria left met=false under close's existing --set criteria_override) is the CHEAP MITIGATION and needs no code -- it should land first and independently. It works by telling closers to stop trying to write per-criterion evidence at all. THIS row is the actual cure: it gives them the per-criterion instrument whose absence causes the substitution. Landing the convention does not make this row unnecessary; it makes it non-urgent.

EXPLICITLY REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, ratified by team-lead 2026-08-24: do NOT add a duplicate-evidence guard. A guard rejecting identical evidence strings would push the same closers into writing N slightly-varied strings -- strictly worse, because it would defeat the detector while leaving the criteria exactly as unproven. That is the same trap as raising a ratchet baseline to swallow a regression: the number goes green and the defect goes invisible.

URGENCY: LOW, but the underlying shape is LIVE. 31 of the 108 rows were created in 2026-08 and five confirmed rows were closed 2026-08-18 to 2026-08-22, the newest two days before the audit. The D56 criterion-text CAS does NOT block this shape, because writing the same TEXT to many criteria is entirely legal. The convention is what stops the bleeding; this row removes the reason it bleeds.

CODE ANCHORS: api/lib/barkpark/tasks/stamp.ex (check_in_progress, build_update, do_stamp_txn) and api/lib/barkpark/tasks/internal.ex (apply_criteria_update, apply_entry_update, flips_met_true?, merge_criteria).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A DECISION is recorded on the four open questions in the description BEFORE any code: (a) the auth predicate for a post-close attempt (original closer / workspace admin / any authenticated agent, and whether cancelled differs), (b) whether the 5-attempt bound is shared with mid-claim attempts or separate, (c) that close's work-digest fence is unaffected -- asserted, not assumed, and (d) whether the task.criterion event needs a post-close marker so boards do not render it as live progress. Evidence: the decisions with their rationale.

Stamp.check_in_progress admits a terminal row ONLY for the attempt shape: a {:miss, note} stamp on a done row succeeds and appends to the criterion's attempts list, while a {:met, _} on the same row still fails with {:not_in_progress, status}. Evidence: both outcomes proven by test, the refusal one included.

PROVEN UNABLE TO FLIP A LOCK, by test rather than by reading: a post-close miss on a criterion stored met=true leaves it met=true, and a post-close miss on one stored met=false leaves it met=false -- including the malformed/absent-met case that apply_entry_update normalises. A mutation that removes the met-pinning line must RED one of these. Evidence: the tests plus the mutation red.

The evidence field and every criterion text are byte-unchanged by a post-close attempt -- asserted directly, since evidence overwriting on the met path is exactly what makes the met path unsafe after close. Evidence: the assertion.

bp task stamp's --miss path accepts a done row end to end (CLI through controller through Stamp), and the CLI help states plainly that --miss works after close while --met does not. Evidence: a real run against a done row plus the help text.
MERGE-GATED (the lead closes this): PR merged to main with the required gates green on its head.

corpus.title: HANDOFF: the ready queue serves 28 unpublished orphan drafts — criterion 1 of tgw10-bl-drafts-in-ready-pool is discharged here, the fix belongs to truth-grip

content.description:
SCOPED OUT OF PDS WAVE 27 DELIBERATELY, AND THE REASON IS THE EPIC'S OWN LAW. tgw10-bl-drafts-in-ready-pool is an OPEN row at 0/5 on the TRUTH-GRIP epic. Building it under a PDS slice without claiming it is the false-done this epic exists to prevent.

WHAT PDS WAVE 27 MEASURED, which discharges that row's CRITERION 1 ('reproduced and its cause located in the ready query, paste the draft row ids and the query clause'):
  * `bp task ready --all` returns 28 `drafts.` rows, and ZERO of them has a published twin in the 3902-row published corpus. These are ORPHAN drafts — never published — being handed out as available work.
  * THE CAUSE IS AN OMISSION, NOT A BROKEN GATE: queue.ex's candidate filter (type == task, content.kind == task, lifecycle_status in claimable, QueueGate.executable_query) contains NO publication predicate. Barkpark.Content defines the seam (:published = documents without the drafts. prefix) and queue.ex never reaches for it. The twin-collapse axis is a CONDITIONAL SUPPRESSION that only fires when a distinct published twin EXISTS, so an orphan draft passes NOT EXISTS and is admitted. queue.ex's own comment says the quiet part: suppressed 'WHILE ITS PUBLISHED TWIN EXISTS IN SCOPE'.
  * MAGNITUDE: 336 draft task rows store-wide, 316 of them orphans. The 28 are the claimable slice.
  * tgw10's own filed figure (14 rows / 859-row pool, 2026-07-27) is now 28 / 1262 — do not quote its numbers.
  * ALSO DISCHARGED, UNBIDDEN: its criterion 4's duplicate doc_id is still live — drafts.stw1-basepath-redirect-fix exists under TWO uuids (3b0d293a-acb9-40d8-9326-3e948b17ab36 and c6cb6318-3dff-4257-82b3-a9786d7b0190), both draft, both cancelled, so absent from ready. That is a write-path uniqueness defect unrelated to the ready filter.

WHAT A PDS FIX WOULD NOT DISCHARGE, and why the row stays truth-grip's: its criterion 2 needs a RULING nobody has minted (the PDS charter is silent on queue admission of drafts); its criterion 3 asks about blocked-in-ready, which a publication predicate would only incidentally touch; its criterion 5 is a truth-grip lead act.

CONSEQUENCE FOR PDS THAT MUST BE STATED IN THE WAVE PAPER: the census reads the PUBLISHED perspective, so it structurally cannot see these rows. A PDS exit 0 certifies THE PUBLISHED ROUND and is silent about 28 rows a worker is being offered.

corpus.title: The criteria gate discounts flips in the close it is gating - built to stop false->true self-grading, and the reverse direction sails straight through

content.description:
MEASURED, NOT REASONED, 2026-08-24 (lane ledger-stamp-shift, during the close-path honesty-gate inventory task-fb2aafff916ca8a5). A disposable row was closed `done` carrying an UNMET acceptance criterion with NO `criteria_override` recorded - no actor, no reason, no attribution. The criteria honesty gate did not refuse. It warned.

THE EXACT SEQUENCE, reproducible on any row you own:
  1. create a row with one unmet criterion, claim it
  2. `bp task stamp <id> <worker> <epoch> --criterion 0 --criterion-text "<exact>" --met --evidence "..."`  -> criterion now stored met:true
  3. `bp task close <id> <worker> <epoch> done "..." --set 'criteria:=[{"index":0,"met":false}]'`
RESULT on task-085400fe55735eb7: close rc=0, lifecycle `done`, criterion stored `met: false`, evidence preserved. The server's ONLY response was:

  warning: acceptance_criteria: 0/1 met - closed done with unmet criteria (advisory, no gate; set met/evidence per criterion before closing)

An advisory. No 409, no override key demanded, nothing on `close_override`. THE SYSTEM KNOWS ENOUGH TO WARN AND NOT ENOUGH TO REQUIRE.

WHY IT WORKS - A GUARD THAT REASONS ABOUT ONE DIRECTION OF A BOOLEAN. `check_criteria_proven` measures unmet AS STORED, and its documented rule is that criteria flipped in this very close command do not count. That rule exists to stop a closer flipping a criterion false->true in the closing write and grading its own homework - a real and well-defended hole. But the rule is stated over the STORED state only, so the REVERSE direction sails straight through: the gate reads the pre-write snapshot (met:true, nothing unmet, pass), and the SAME write then flips it to false. The gate never sees the delta, only the before. A guard that reasons about one direction of a boolean is a guard against half a defect.

WHAT THIS ALSO RETRACTS. It was widely repeated today - by me, and onward by the lead to a dozen lanes - that "`met` is a one-way lock with no un-set on any path." THAT IS FALSE. The accurate statement is narrower: `bp task stamp` cannot un-set met (`Stamp.build_update` offers only `{:met, _}`, and the `{:miss, _}` attempt path PINS met to its stored value), but `bp task close --set criteria` routes through the same `Internal.apply_entry_update`, which does `met = Map.get(update, "met", true)` and writes whatever boolean it is handed. STAMP cannot un-set; CLOSE can.

WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY FROM `zero-criteria-is-a-legal-bypass-of-the-close-gate` (27 open rows, 143 already spent it) RATHER THAN FOLDED INTO IT. Same gate, DIFFERENT DOOR, and they close independently: the zero-criteria door is shut by requiring criteria at birth; this one is shut by making the gate measure the DELTA DIRECTION rather than only the stored state. Folding them means one fix gets credited for both and the other silently survives. Cite each other; do not merge.

SEVERITY, STATED HONESTLY. This is NOT a false-done in the usual direction - it leaves the criterion reading `met: false`, which is MORE honest than a fabricated met:true. The damage is to ATTRIBUTION: `criteria_override` exists precisely so that closing over unmet criteria records WHO decided it was done anyway and WHY, on the record, in `close_override.criteria`. This path produces the same outcome with none of that, so an auditor reading the row sees a done task with an unmet criterion and no explanation anywhere. It is an accountability hole rather than a correctness one - which is exactly the class this ledger's honesty gates exist to close.

CANDIDATE REMEDIES, for whoever takes it - not prescriptive:
  (a) make the criteria gate evaluate the POST-MERGE criteria state as well as the stored one, so a close that ENDS with an unmet criterion needs `criteria_override` regardless of which direction the write moved it;
  (b) or refuse a met TRUE->FALSE flip inside a close write specifically, the mirror of the existing false->true rule;
  (c) or promote the advisory to the 409 it already describes, since the warning text already names the exact condition the gate is supposed to enforce.
(a) is the general fix; (b) is the narrow mirror; (c) is the smallest diff and probably the honest interim.

METHOD NOTE, because this row's own evidence depends on it: every refusal string quoted in the inventory was re-derived from a run PROVABLY reaching the server and printed UNFILTERED. Two separate mechanisms fabricated a fake terse refusal earlier the same day - a missing `--yes` aborting client-side before any request is sent, and a probe helper that returned only the first line beginning with `bp:` and discarded the indented `hint:` line that followed. Both produce a convincing absence. Anything recorded as "gate X emits Y" needs both guards.


## CROSS-REFERENCE (2026-09-06): zero-criteria-is-a-legal-bypass-of-the-close-gate — the OTHER door, NOT folded in

The sibling row's real id is the literal slug `zero-criteria-is-a-legal-bypass-of-the-close-gate` (not a `task-<hex>` id), and its lifecycle is **`cancelled`** — closed by `lead-ledger` 2026-09-02 as REFUTED ON MAIN, because `check_close_artifact/5` already stands in the zero-criteria gap.
