corpus.title: Quota: demonstrate the count-then-compare over-admission in the suite, and file the fix sharpened with a costed menu

content.description:
Demonstrate the quota count-then-compare over-admission with a test that actually runs in the suite, and sharpen the filed task so a future wave inherits evidence instead of an argument. This slice ships NO FIX to `quota.ex`, and that refusal is the deliverable's whole point.

WHY NOT FIX IT — a category fact, not a difficulty, re-derived on origin/main 122fd0df81 and confirmed independently by three surveyors. `Barkpark.Tenancy.Quota.within_quota?/1` is `usage(id) < quota`, where `usage/1` is a live `Repo.aggregate(:count)` over `documents`. `BarkparkWeb.Plugs.RequireWithinQuota` (mounted at router.ex:273, :312, :667) calls `Quota.check(ws)` exactly ONCE per request and HALTS BEFORE the controller runs. The quota-relevant writes then open their OWN transactions in other modules — `Content.Mutations.apply_mutations/3` wraps the whole batch in one `Repo.transaction`, and `Media.upload/3` does a bare `Repo.insert` with no transaction at all. The check and the write are in different transactions, in different modules, at different points in the lifecycle. NO change confined to `quota.ex` can be atomic against a write that is not in scope of the check. A narrowed window there would be fail-open AND believed fixed, which is worse than the defect.

BUILD THIS.

(1) NEW FILE `api/test/barkpark/tenancy/quota_toctou_demonstration_test.exs`, `use Barkpark.DataCase, async: false`.

THE MODULEDOC IS PART OF THE DELIVERABLE. Its FIRST sentence must state that this file asserts the CURRENT, BROKEN behaviour and is a DEMONSTRATION, not a regression guard — and that when the invariant is pushed into the database these assertions MUST be inverted (`assert final > @cap` becomes `assert final == @cap`). A future reader who mistakes it for a guard will conclude the finding is fixed. Give every assertion a failure message that repeats the point.

(2) THE STAGED LEG IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE, because it needs no scheduler luck at all. Seed a workspace at `quota: 10` with 9 committed documents (headroom 1). Stage the interleaving explicitly: have all 8 callers execute `Quota.check/1` FIRST and observe `usage = 9 < quota = 10`, THEN have all 8 write. Assert 8 admitted and a final count of 17 — an overshoot of `fanout - headroom`. This is deterministic; it reproduces the plug's own semantics with the ordering made explicit rather than raced.

(3) A CONCURRENT LEG, to show the staged ordering arises naturally: a barrier-released `Task.async` fan-out under the ordinary SHARED sandbox. This WORKS under shared mode and the reason matters — the TOCTOU spans two STATEMENTS, so serializing them onto one connection still interleaves count/count/insert/insert. Measured 8 admitted / final 17 in 100% of rounds across 11 runs and four harness shapes. Do NOT reach for `Sandbox.unboxed_run`: it commits real rows that a killed run strands forever, and it buys nothing here.

(4) A SEQUENTIAL CONTROL, so the harness is not vacuous: the SAME code path driven by sequential callers admits exactly the headroom (1) and denies the rest (`%{admitted: 1, quota_exceeded: 7}`), final count exactly 10. Without this leg the demo cannot distinguish "the race is real" from "the gate is simply broken".

(5) THE BATCH-OVERSHOOT LEG — the strongest evidence in this slice, and it REFUTES the filed task's own bound. The overshoot is bounded by the CALLER-CHOSEN BATCH SIZE, not by the concurrency factor: `Content.Mutations.apply_mutations/3` matches `when is_list(mutations)` and hands the whole list to one `Repo.transaction`, and there is NO batch cap anywhere in `api/lib` (`git grep -E "max_mutations|too_many_mutations|@max_batch|length\(mutations\)" origin/main -- api/lib` finds only two telemetry `length()` tags and `pulse.ex`'s unrelated read-pagination `@max_batch 100`). Park a workspace at `cap - 1`, assert `Quota.check(ws) == :ok`, then create N documents in one batch, and assert the overshoot is `N - 1`. Single process, zero flakiness, and it SURVIVES any fix to the race — a fix that makes `within_quota?` atomic while still answering "room for one" before an unbounded batch is still fail-open. Keep N modest (25 is plenty); N=5000 blows the 15s Ecto transaction timeout, and an oversize batch then fails SAFE with a full rollback.

(6) PATCH THE FILED TASK `acpc-bl-quota-toctou` via bp (patch + re-publish) with FIVE corrections. Its current text is wrong or stale on four of them:
  - its stated filing reason ("the race is not deterministically provable by a single-process conn test") is OBSOLETE — the batch overshoot IS provable single-process, and a two-session psql reproduction runs in under a second. It is filed because the FIX LOCUS is out of fence and carries behaviour change, not because the defect is unprovable. Leaving the old reason standing invites a future wave to conclude the finding is soft.
  - its overshoot bound ("up to the concurrency factor") is REFUTED — see (5).
  - the media/documents question RESOLVES as PLUGIN-CONDITIONAL, and both prior readings were half right: `Media.upload/3` inserts only a `media_files` row, but it then calls `Plugins.Registry.run_after_media_upload/1`, which reaches `Plugins.Media.after_media_upload/1` -> `Assets.ensure_for_upload/1` -> `Content.create_document`, stamping the blob's `workspace_id`. Run-proven both ways: plugins discovered -> documents delta 1; media plugin excluded from the configured list -> delta 0. `BARKPARK_PLUGINS` unset is the documented production default and means discover-all, so the media quota gate is REAL on a stock install and decorative only under an explicit operator whitelist. A `documents`-side DB invariant would therefore fire inside a plugin callback whose failure is swallowed by `ResolverChain.safe_call/4` — a cost the menu must price.
  - SEVERITY is priority 2 with its trigger NAMED, not a bare number: zero live workspaces carry a cap (the only in-tree `set_quota/2` caller is the admin-gated `PlaygroundController`), so the gate is dark on a stock install — but `bpb-playground-rate-limit` intends anonymous exposure and the playground controller calls the cap "the abuse ceiling". Re-derive the priority the moment that ships.
  - and the fix would newly CONSTRAIN routes that are unmetered today: the flat `POST /v1/data/mutate/:dataset` (router.ex:1887) and `POST /v1/data/revision/:dataset/:id/restore` (router.ex:1880) both pipe `[:api, :require_token, :require_write, :idempotent]` with NO quota plug, and the tasks plugin, paperflow ingest and Studio LiveView write paths carry none either. That is a behaviour CHANGE, not just an atomicity fix, and it is the single biggest reason this exceeds a wave slice.

(7) ADD THE COSTED DESIGN MENU to that task, ranked, with option 4 REFUTED BY NAME:
  1. Statement-level trigger with transition tables + a `workspaces.documents_count` column + a `NOT VALID` CHECK. Measured to hold EXACTLY at cap under plain READ COMMITTED with no retry loop (the loser blocks on the workspaces row lock, then fails the check and rolls back). Cascade-delete cost 1.14x vs 4.9x for FOR EACH ROW. Costs to carry: it serializes every document write in a workspace on one row; an over-cap batch now rolls back ENTIRELY where today the plug admits the whole batch on one pre-check; the violation surfaces as a CHECK error on the `workspaces` table raised from inside a `documents` insert, so mapping it to the existing 402 needs a cross-table `check_constraint` on the document changeset or it is a 500.
  2. Per-workspace `pg_advisory_xact_lock` across check+write. In-tree prior art exists (`audit.ex:140`, `block_ops.ex`, `sessions.ex`), but it makes a three-lock protocol (quota -> task -> audit) with no documented acquisition order, and `crc32` and `hashtext` already share one bigint keyspace.
  3. SERIALIZABLE. Correct on the same-workspace case, but its SIRead predicate lock escalates to RELATION level at production size (measured at 5,942 rows) and FALSELY aborted two transactions working DISJOINT workspaces; there is zero 40001 retry infrastructure anywhere in `api/lib`.
  4. Conditional `INSERT ... WHERE (SELECT count) < limit` — **NOT A FIX**. Two psql sessions at cap 3 / count 2 running exactly that statement under READ COMMITTED BOTH returned `INSERT 0 1` and both committed; final count 4. Each writer evaluates its subquery against its own snapshot, and a read does not lock. List it explicitly as refuted so no future wave re-proposes it.

(8) DO NOT EDIT `api/lib/barkpark/tenancy/quota.ex`. Not one line. If you find yourself wanting to, that is the finding, not the fix.

HOST NOTE: prefix mix with `CC=/usr/bin/clang`. Use a unique `MIX_TEST_PARTITION`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: api/lib/barkpark/tenancy/quota.ex is UNCHANGED — `git diff origin/main -- api/lib/barkpark/tenancy/quota.ex` prints nothing; this slice files the finding, it does not narrow it

The new test file's moduledoc states in its FIRST sentence that it asserts the CURRENT BROKEN behaviour and is a demonstration rather than a regression guard, and names what must be inverted when a fix lands
The STAGED leg proves the over-admission deterministically: at cap 10 with 9 seeded documents, 8 callers each observe usage 9 < quota 10 and then all write, giving 8 admitted and a final count of 17
A barrier-released concurrent leg under the ordinary SHARED Ecto sandbox reproduces the same 8-admitted / 17-final result, showing the staged ordering arises naturally
A sequential CONTROL leg proves the harness is not vacuous: the same code path driven sequentially admits exactly the headroom (1) and denies the remaining 7, leaving the count at exactly the cap

A single-process batch leg proves the overshoot is bounded by the caller-chosen BATCH SIZE and not by concurrency: with usage parked at cap-1 and Quota.check returning :ok, one request creating N documents overshoots by N-1

The filed task acpc-bl-quota-toctou is patched and re-published with its obsolete filing reason corrected, its 'up to the concurrency factor' bound refuted, the plugin-conditional media/documents resolution recorded, the priority-2 trigger condition named, and the currently-unmetered write routes listed

The costed design menu is on that task, ranked, with the conditional INSERT option REFUTED BY NAME and carrying its two-session READ COMMITTED evidence (both sessions returned INSERT 0 1, final count 4 against a cap of 3)

Gate green from the builder's own worktree: `cd api && CC=/usr/bin/clang MIX_TEST_PARTITION=<unique> mix test test/barkpark/tenancy/quota_toctou_demonstration_test.exs test/barkpark_web/plugs/require_within_quota_test.exs` reports 0 failures
MERGE-GATED (lead closes): the PR is merged to main

corpus.title: Task tests set the Ecto sandbox to :shared from async:true cases — a measured 40P01 deadlock source

content.description:
MEASURED, not theorised. While building pds-w33-ledger-postread-core the four-file task gate hit 'Postgrex.Error ERROR 40P01 (deadlock_detected)' once in ~6 runs, raised out of Content.Writer.do_create_document in a test SETUP block, with one process waiting on AccessShareLock and another on AccessExclusiveLock. The receipt-honesty test reproduced it while it carried 'Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Repo, {:shared, self()})' and stopped reproducing entirely once that line was removed (every task verb runs its transaction and fires its broadcast in the CALLING process, so the checked-out connection is sufficient — no shared mode is needed).

The same line is still present in test/barkpark/tasks/stamp_test.exs and neighbours, several of which are ALSO 'use Barkpark.DataCase, async: true'. Flipping the sandbox to shared mode from an async case is the documented footgun: it hands one case's connection to every other process for the duration. This is a latent flaky-CI generator on the task suite, and a flake here reads as 'the ledger is broken' when it is not.

WORK: grep 'Sandbox.mode' across test/barkpark/tasks, and for each hit decide — drop it (the verb runs in-process, as receipt_honesty_test.exs now proves) or, where a genuinely spawned process needs the connection, use allowances instead. Do not simply mark files async:false; that hides the cause and costs suite time.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every Sandbox.mode({:shared,...}) call in test/barkpark/tasks is either removed or justified in a comment naming the process that needs the connection
The task suite runs 20 consecutive times with zero 40P01 deadlocks — quote the loop and its output

corpus.title: fix(cloud): the hostname claim doors race at READ COMMITTED, and the comment claiming a DB race backstop is false

content.description:
The hostname claim doors are check-then-write at READ COMMITTED with nothing serialising them, so two concurrent requests can both pass the guard and both commit — and the comment that claims a DB backstop exists is FALSE. Measured on origin/main c4508c4d7a, after PR #14458 made the application-level guard bidirectional.

THE FALSE COMMENT IS THE SHARPER HALF. registry.ex:6331-6333 states that "The DB-level uniqueness trigger ... is the race backstop between the check above and this write." That is not true. The trigger body (cloud/priv/repo/migrations/20260703110000_add_domain_cross_site_uniqueness.exs:45-48) is:

  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sites s WHERE s.id <> NEW.id AND d = ANY(s.domains))

A plpgsql EXISTS inside a BEFORE ROW trigger runs under the same READ COMMITTED snapshot rules as any other statement — it CANNOT see a concurrent uncommitted sites row. It NARROWS the window (its snapshot is taken later than the app check's) from milliseconds to microseconds; it does not close it. Only a UNIQUE INDEX, an EXCLUDE constraint, explicit locking, or SERIALIZABLE gives mutual exclusion.

A comment asserting a safety property the code does not have is worse than no comment: it tells the next reader not to check. Fixing the comment is mandatory in this row even if the lock is deferred.

THE THREE DOORS, all check-then-write, none locking:
  · add_site_domain/2   registry.ex:6310 — hostname_claimed? at :6324, Repo.update at :6338
  · create_site/2       registry.ex:5511 — first_claimed_domain at :5537, Repo.insert at :5539
  · set_custom_host/2   registry.ex:6494 — custom_host_taken? at :6501, Repo.update at :6505

All three ARE inside Repo.transaction, but only incidentally, via Accounts.audit/3 (accounts.ex:404) called at router.ex:7703 / :8463 / :4731. That does not help: BarkparkCloud.Repo sets no isolation level and runtime.exs:21 sets only pool_size, so this is stock READ COMMITTED; hostname_claimed?'s four legs are SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1 (registry.ex:6414, :6546, :6529, :6571) taking no row lock. The audit wrapper actually WIDENS the window, because the audit INSERT now sits between the write and the COMMIT.

COVERAGE WITH A DENOMINATOR. hostname_claimed?/2 (registry.ex:6399) has FOUR legs. The DB layer atomically enforces ONE (custom_host<->custom_host, via the real partial unique index barkparks_custom_host_unique_idx, 20260706210000_add_custom_host_to_barkparks.exs:14 — which is why set_custom_host can honestly rescue a unique_violation at :6505). It non-atomically enforces ONE (site<->site). It enforces ZERO of the other two. Across the surface cross-product — site/site, site/custom_host, site/url, custom_host/url, suffix — that is 1 of 5 pairs race-safe. registry.ex:6560-6563 already admits the custom_host/url hole in prose.

LIKELIHOOD, honestly: low. One of the two doors (POST /v1/barkparks/:id/domain) is require_primary_team_admin plus a DNS-ownership round-trip before the write (router.ex:4655, :4691), which makes the timing hard to hit accidentally. But it is STEERABLE — an attacker controlling both sides can widen the window by pointing DNS slowly. Real, rare, not exploitable-at-will.

THE REMEDY — Option D, and the alternatives were priced before choosing it.

  Add pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext("hostname:" <> norm)) as the FIRST statement inside
  hostname_claimed?/2 (registry.ex:6399), so ALL THREE callers inherit it and a fourth door
  cannot forget. Released at commit.

  Repo.query!("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext($1))", ["hostname:" <> norm])

WHY NOT THE OTHERS:
  (A) Extend the trigger to consult barkparks — cheap to deploy (CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION, no table scan) but NEARLY USELESS: it inherits the same non-atomicity. Worse, shipping it would RE-LICENSE the false comment. If ever done, the extension must sit INSIDE the FOREACH d IN ARRAY added LOOP (migration :44), never hoisted above the diff guard, or it puts a barkparks scan on all 10 sites-row writers.
  (B) EXCLUDE constraint — does not work; EXCLUDE is single-table and cannot span sites and barkparks. A GiST EXCLUDE on sites alone would fix 1 of 5 pairs but needs ACCESS EXCLUSIVE plus a full validating scan, and FAILS OUTRIGHT if prod already holds a duplicate — which is exactly the state the trigger migration was written to tolerate (:20-22). Highest-risk option on a live control plane.
  (C) Materialised hostname_claims table — the only structurally atomic option, closes all five pairs, and its backfill IS the census that task-<census-row> needs. But a two-phase deploy and a second source of truth. Revisit only if the namespace grows a fifth surface.

PRECEDENT — this is the repo's own pattern, not an invention. 20+ advisory-lock call sites in api/ (tasks/claim.ex:78, close.ex:335, compactor.ex:219, content/sessions.ex:68, audit.ex:174), and cloud/ already row-locks a check-then-write of identical shape: lock_team_for_quota/1 (registry.ex:305), whose comment — "so the count-then-insert below is serialized per team ... held until the enclosing transaction commits" — is this argument transposed.

WEAKNESS OF D, STATED: it is conventional, not structural. A fourth claim door that forgets the lock is unprotected. Placing it inside the shared predicate rather than at the three call sites is what mitigates that, and is why the predicate — not the callers — is the correct home.

BLAST RADIUS OF GETTING IT WRONG (this is why D beats A/B/C). If the backstop lives in the trigger or a constraint, EVERY writer of a sites row becomes a 500 candidate. There are 10 sites-row writers in registry.ex; only 3 touch domains (create_site :5539, add_site_domain :6336, remove_site_domain :6357). The other 7 (set_cf_binding :6146, set_site_env :6261, set_site_github :6862, clear_site_github :6918, update_site_settings :7966, set_site_current_deployment :7982, do_transition_deployment_with_site_update :8140) survive today ONLY because of the trigger's diff guard (added := NEW.domains EXCEPT OLD.domains, migration :33-44). The dangerous one is do_transition_deployment_with_site_update — it fires on every deploy settle, it is unattended, and only add_site_domain/2 has a rescue for Postgrex.Error (:6341). A too-strict trigger there does not 409, it 500s a deploy. An advisory lock adds no such surface.

ACCEPTANCE.
  1. hostname_claimed?/2 takes the advisory lock before its first SELECT; all three doors inherit it with no call-site change.
  2. The false "race backstop" comment at registry.ex:6331-6333 is corrected to say what the trigger actually does (narrows, does not close) and what now serialises the doors.
  3. A concurrency test: two processes racing the attach door and the custom_host door on the same hostname produce exactly one winner and one clean refusal, not two winners. If a true concurrency test is impractical in this suite, say so explicitly and assert the lock is TAKEN (the query is issued with the expected key) rather than pretending to prove serialisation.
  4. Mutation-proved: remove the lock and the concurrency test must red. If the test cannot be made deterministic, state that plainly rather than shipping a test that passes either way.
  5. No migration. No change to the trigger. No new lock on a live table.

FENCE: cloud/ only. Sequence AFTER the current CI freeze lifts.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: THE FALSE COMMENT IS CORRECTED — MANDATORY EVEN IF THE LOCK IS DEFERRED. cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/registry.ex (the sentence at ~6693 on today's head: 'is the race backstop between the check above and this write') no longer claims the DB uniqueness trigger closes the race. It says what the trigger actually does: a plpgsql EXISTS inside a BEFORE ROW trigger runs under the same READ COMMITTED snapshot rules and cannot see a concurrent uncommitted sites row, so it NARROWS the window from milliseconds to microseconds and does not close it. Verify: `git grep -n 'race backstop' cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/registry.ex` returns only corrected text.

ALL THREE DOORS ARE ADDRESSED TOGETHER OR THE RESIDUE IS NAMED. add_site_domain/2, create_site/2 and set_custom_host/2 are each check-then-write with no locking; the change either gives all three mutual exclusion (a UNIQUE INDEX, an EXCLUDE constraint, explicit row locking, or SERIALIZABLE — the row names these as the only mechanisms that suffice) or records which doors remain unserialised and why. Being inside Repo.transaction is not mutual exclusion and must not be cited as one.

THE RACE IS DEMONSTRATED, NOT ARGUED. A test drives two concurrent claims of the same hostname through one door and asserts exactly one succeeds. It is shown FAILING (both commit) before the fix — a sequential test cannot distinguish a locked door from an unlocked one and does not satisfy this.
MERGE-GATED (the lead closes this): PR merged to refs/remotes/origin/main with the four required contexts green; merge sha recorded.

corpus.title: An auto-stamped merge gate asserts a lead and a merge that nothing verified, and leaves no trace — so a fabricated close and an honest one are byte-identical

content.description:
HIGH-FLIP-RISK: the authority/reachability judgment. An independent second reviewer is owed before merge.

THIS IS THE WISH'S OWN SENTENCE — a guard that cannot tell an honest completion from a fabricated one — pointed at this epic's own ledger. Read charter D803 and Surface-fence ADD 1 first.

IN FENCE BY ADD 1 AND NOTHING ELSE. `api/lib/barkpark/tasks/close.ex`, its test, and the Go close-payload pin. One subject: an auto-stamped merge gate must leave a durable record naming what was ACTUALLY OBSERVED. Anything else in api/ or internal/ is out.

THE CHAIN, READ END TO END ON origin/main, WITH NO BREAK IN IT:
  1. tasks_controller.ex:484 is `|> Params.put_opt(:landed, params["landed"])` — a RAW, UNVALIDATED passthrough of a client body field. Every other opt on that pipeline gets a `Params.parse_*`; `landed` gets nothing. The route is the ordinary `:token_root` tier.
  2. close.ex:675 `autostamp_merge_gate/6` guards ONLY on `status == "done"` and `is_map(landed) and map_size(landed) > 0`. No lead check. No PR verification. No check that the PR belongs to this task.
  3. compose_merge_gate_evidence/4 (close.ex:728) writes `"auto: lead-closed on merge by <worker> (epoch N) - landed PR #N at <ts>"` ENTIRELY from caller-supplied bytes. Nothing contacts GitHub.
  4. unmet_after_autostamp/2 (close.ex:448) REJECTS every autostamped index, so check_criteria_proven/4 returns `{:ok, nil}` and compose_override_record(nil, nil, _) (:467) returns nil — NO close_override is minted at all. The deduction is silent by construction.
D797 recorded the live proof: a scratch worker paid a merge gate citing PR #11435, a different epic's PR it never touched, and the server auto-wrote 'lead-closed on merge'.

TWO SHAPES ARE EXPLICITLY REFUSED — DO NOT BUILD THEM:
  (a) AN AUTHORITY CHECK KEYED ON `worker_id` IS VACUOUS. close.ex:26-31 says so in the module's own words: 'NONE OF THIS IS AUTHORIZATION. worker_id arrives as a client-supplied body param ... a caller who wants to close someone else's task can simply claim to be them.' The attacker supplies the string. The only authenticated identity on the path is `caller_token_id` (controller :494).
  (b) A GITHUB ROUND-TRIP INSIDE THE CLOSE. It runs under `pg_advisory_xact_lock`; a network call there converts a fabrication bug into an availability bug. Verification belongs in `reconcile_merge_gate/3`, which is already async and webhook-driven.

BUILD PROVENANCE — the shape D679 already ruled is the right ceiling ('honesty-gate parity with close's content.close_override'):
  1. The evidence sentence stops asserting what nothing observed. corpus.title: The epic_assignment_runtime_attempts append-only guard refuses Ecto sandbox cleanup: 565 failures in every full local mix test run

content.description:
The append-only guard on epic_assignment_runtime_attempts refuses Ecto's sandbox cleanup, producing 565 failures in EVERY full local `mix test` run, on every agent that runs one.

MEASURED (full-suite run, 2026-09-07): 19,194 tests, 619 failures — 617 environmental, of which 565 are the single Postgres exception `epic_assignment_runtime_attempts is append-only (DELETE forbidden)` raised during Ecto sandbox cleanup, and 16 are `deadlock_detected` from seven concurrent suites on one shared test DB. Exactly 2 failures were the builder's own work.

MECHANISM — this section was WRONG in the first filing and is corrected here. Read it, not any earlier summary.

`barkpark_epic_ledger_immutable` is `CREATE OR REPLACE`d by SEVEN migrations: 20260715000100, 000300, 000400, 000500, 001100, 001200, 001300. LATEST WINS. The function actually installed is `guarded_immutability_function()` from `20260715001300_add_assignment_runtime_attempts.exs`, executed at line 66. An earlier filing named 20260715000300:73,84 — that is a real definition site, SUPERSEDED by four later ones. Containing the string is not running the code: on a function redefined seven times, grep-for-the-definition is a latest-wins race and grep does not tell you who won.

The DELETEs themselves live in `barkpark_teardown_cycle_ledger()` (20260719010000, ~lines 1300 and 1313).

THE LIVE EXEMPTION REQUIRES BOTH HALVES:

    teardown_workspace := current_setting('barkpark.cycle_teardown_workspace', true);
    IF TG_OP='DELETE' AND pg_trigger_depth() > 1 AND teardown_workspace <> '' THEN
      ... 'epic_assignment_runtime_attempts' -> row_workspace FROM epic_assignments ...
      IF row_workspace::text = teardown_workspace THEN RETURN OLD; END IF;
    END IF;

The designed exemption is "a CASCADE delete, inside a teardown that has ANNOUNCED which workspace it is tearing down." Ecto sandbox cleanup fails BOTH halves: it deletes at trigger depth 1, AND the GUC is unset.

THIS CHANGES THE REMEDY, NOT ONLY THE CITATION. Adding a depth exemption alone WOULD LEAVE IT RED, because the GUC condition stays false. Anyone who ships the one-line depth fix will see it stay red and someone re-files this next week.

THE OWNER'S REAL CHOICE IS BETWEEN:
  (a) Ecto sandbox cleanup SETS `barkpark.cycle_teardown_workspace` (and the guard's workspace match is made to hold for it), or
  (b) the test harness SHOULD NOT be deleting these rows at all — the append-only table is excluded from sandbox teardown by design.
Pick one deliberately and write the rejected alternative into this row.

Also corrected from the first filing: 20260715000300 does NOT ship two live variants — `cascade_aware` is in `def up` (line 32) and `strict` is in `def down` (line 36), so that file's DEPLOYED behaviour was always cascade-aware. And the escape hatch appears in EIGHT migrations, not six.

WHY CI IS GREEN AND YOUR BOX IS NOT — and why this is a LATENT TRAP, not a live breakage:
A `FOR EACH ROW` trigger fires once per row DELETED, so on an EMPTY table the DELETE matches nothing, the trigger never fires, and the setup passes SILENTLY. CI starts from a fresh database — verified: Elixir gate run 34124122245, `Test (Elixir 1.18.4 / OTP 27.0)`, SUCCESS, 4587 tests / 0 failures, with ZERO occurrences of this table's append-only message in a 3.6 MB log, against 41 append-only ERROR lines for OTHER tables and 29 chat-file mentions as a non-vacuity control. MAIN IS NOT BROKEN. On a shared box the fleet's epic-cycle work POPULATES the table; once it holds rows the trigger fires at depth 1 and every affected suite reds.

CONSEQUENCE: five test setups carry a hidden, unstated, unenforced precondition — "this table is empty". One leftover row reds them all with no code change. Any agent whose DB has run the epic-cycle suite cannot run the studio chat tests at all.

FENCE: api/priv/repo/migrations — outside every campaign lane's fence. No lane has touched it.

METHOD WARNING FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: the chain that produced the wrong citation started with a grep for the RENDERED message `is append-only (DELETE forbidden)`, which returns ZERO HITS. The source is a format string — `RAISE EXCEPTION '% is append-only (% forbidden)', TG_TABLE_NAME, TG_OP` — present in 8 files. A zero-result grep is not evidence of absence until the pattern has been tested against a known positive.

CORROBORATION FROM CI, 2026-09-07 (added after filing): the same trigger defect is now VISIBLE IN CI, not only on developer boxes. A recent Elixir gate run's log carries 21 `DBConnection.ConnectionError`, 11 `append-only (UPDATE forbidden)` and 9 `append-only (DELETE forbidden)` lines — AND THEY ARE CORRECTLY COUNTED AS ZERO FAILURES, because the suite passes while the trigger fires during sandbox teardown. That strengthens the filing in two ways: it refutes "this is only a contaminated local box", and it shows the noise is INVISIBLE TO THE PASS/FAIL SIGNAL, so nobody will notice it from a green run. The judgement to leave that noise alone rather than chase it as test failures was correct.

=== SECOND ADDENDUM, 2026-09-07 — THE CENTRAL MECHANISM ABOVE IS REFUTED. READ THIS, NOT THE ORIGINAL. ===

I filed this row saying "Ecto's sandbox cleanup deletes at trigger depth 1". THAT IS FALSE, and I
have verified the refutation myself on origin/main rather than relaying it.

(a) `DataCase.setup_sandbox` (api/test/support/data_case.ex:99,105) uses
    `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.start_owner!` / `stop_owner` — ROLLBACK, no DELETE. And
    `api/test/support` contains ZERO deletes of either guarded table. Ecto's sandbox is not the
    actor and never was.
    THE ACTUAL DELETES ARE FIVE HAND-WRITTEN `setup`-BLOCK PURGES in test files (studio chat +
    tenancy), whose own comments say they exist to clear `ON DELETE RESTRICT` children ahead of
    `Repo.delete_all(Session)`. So the remedy space is TEST-CODE-shaped, not Ecto-shaped.

(b) IT IS TEN ARMED STATEMENTS ACROSS TWO TABLES, NOT FIVE AGAINST ONE. Every one of the five setups
    deletes `chat_runtime_usage_receipts` on the line IMMEDIATELY ABOVE. That table's guard,
    `barkpark_runtime_usage_receipts_immutable` (20260715000900_add_runtime_usage_receipts.exs),
    has NO EXEMPTION PATH AT ALL: zero `pg_trigger_depth`, no GUC. CONTROL: 8 other migrations DO
    carry `pg_trigger_depth`, so the zero discriminates rather than merely finding nothing.
    CONSEQUENCE: any fix aimed only at `epic_assignment_runtime_attempts` repairs HALF of each of
    the five setups. The second table is dormant ONLY because it currently holds 0 rows; the day it
    holds one, the same tests red ONE LINE EARLIER.

(c) A GUC-ONLY FIX ALSO STAYS RED, not just a depth-only one — both halves of the exemption must be
    satisfied together. And the installed guard already carries a depth-only exemption for two
    SIBLING tables (`epic_benchmark_experiments` / `..._attempts`), so adding our table to that list
    LOOKS IDIOMATIC AND STILL LEAVES THE SETUP DELETES RED, because they run at depth 1. Probe:
    a direct DELETE reports `depth=1 guc=<UNSET>`; the same delete under a cascade reports `depth=2`.

A THIRD PATH THE ORIGINAL FILING DID NOT LIST: delete the PARENT `epic_assignments` row with the GUC
set — the attempts FK is CASCADE, so the child delete arrives at depth 2 WITH the GUC populated,
i.e. the designed exemption with NO guard change at all. It does nothing for
`chat_runtime_usage_receipts`.

=== THE RULING (main, 2026-09-07): TAKE THE ROOT CAUSE, NOT EITHER LISTED OPTION. ===

The five purges are a WORKAROUND FOR A LEAK, not a requirement. Their own comments say they clear
RESTRICT children ahead of `Repo.delete_all(Session)` — and that `delete_all` is only necessary
because something COMMITS `chat_sessions` outside its sandbox owner (a Recorder outliving the owner;
the shared test DB holds committed sessions that no rollback ever reclaimed).

FIX THE LEAK AND ALL TEN ARMED STATEMENTS BECOME UNNECESSARY — both tables, no migration, no guard
change, nothing prod-deploying, and the guards keep their full strength against a real direct DELETE.
Neither listed option achieves that: (a) is a prod-deploying migration that weakens two guards to
accommodate a defect, and (b) leaves the RESTRICT violation standing.

FALLBACK, if the leak proves expensive: scope the `Repo.delete_all(Session)` to the sessions the test
actually created, which removes the need for the RESTRICT purges without touching a guard.

c4's positive control still binds and is WIDENED: it must prove BOTH guards still refuse a real
direct DELETE — a fix that covers only the table with a hatch silently opens the one without.

=== THIRD ADDENDUM, 2026-09-07 — MY RULING'S NAMED MECHANISM WAS WRONG. THE RECORDER IS INNOCENT. ===
Written by main (team-lead), the ruling's author, after re-deriving the refutation independently.

MY SECOND ADDENDUM AND THE RULING IN IT SAY THE LEAK IS "a Recorder outliving its sandbox owner and
committing chat_sessions". THAT IS FALSE. Verified by me on origin/main, not relayed:

  - `api/lib/barkpark/studio_chat/recorder.ex` matches `create_session|Repo\.insert|%Session\{`
    ZERO times. POSITIVE CONTROL: two OTHER studio_chat files DO call `Repo.insert`
    (`runtime_telemetry.ex`, `runtime_usage.ex`) — so the zero DISCRIMINATES rather than merely
    finding nothing.
  - The structural argument is stronger than the grep: a process with no sandbox ownership record
    CANNOT commit through a sandboxed Repo at all — it raises OwnershipError. The Recorder story was
    never mechanically possible.

THE REAL ACTOR IS A TEST, and it commits BY DESIGN:
  `api/test/barkpark/studio_chat/runtime_usage_test.exs:1012` runs inside
  `Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.unboxed_run/2` — a real, UNSANDBOXED connection. Its own comment at
  :1081 says so verbatim: "`unboxed_run` COMMITS — that is the point." It needs two connections to
  genuinely block each other (55P03). Inside it, `CycleFleet.prepare_runtime_attempt/3 ->
  create_attempt_session/2` (`cycle_fleet.ex:4647`) mints a `chat_sessions` row, and teardown never
  reaches it because `chat_sessions` carries NO foreign keys at all (control: sibling tables carry
  8, 7 and 5).
  FINGERPRINT: all 86 committed rows carry provider "codex", mode "plan", empty cwd — the exact shape
  `create_attempt_session/2` writes and no other create site produces (the column default is
  'claude'). 85 of the 86 owner workspaces no longer exist.
  MUTATION-PROVEN BOTH WAYS on a clean private DB: origin/main's version of that file leaves exactly
  1 committed session (28 tests, 0 failures — INVISIBLE to pass/fail); the fixed version leaves 0.

HOW THE WRONG MECHANISM REACHED A RULING, recorded because the process failure is the transferable
part: it originated in an investigator's report. The lead re-derived that agent's OTHER claims — the
ten statements across two tables, `setup_sandbox` using `start_owner!`, the second guard's missing
hatch — each with controls, and did NOT re-derive this one. It relayed it; I adopted it into a
ruling; it was then stamped into c3's evidence. "A subagent's finding is evidence about the
subagent's SEARCH until the lead re-derives it" was honoured on four claims and skipped on the fifth,
and the fifth is the one that reached a ruling. THE TELL: it was the only claim in that report
phrased as an INFERENCE ("a Recorder outliving its owner") rather than as an OBSERVATION WITH A
COMMAND BEHIND IT.

THE RULING'S CONCLUSION SURVIVES INTACT AND IS UNCHANGED: take (b), fix the leak, not a migration.
Only the named mechanism was wrong.

AND MY SANCTIONED FALLBACK WOULD NOT HAVE WORKED AS WRITTEN. I wrote: "scope
`Repo.delete_all(Session)` to the sessions the test actually created." That INVERTS the purge's
purpose — at setup time these tests have created nothing, and the whole point is clearing rows they
did NOT create. Do not use it.

THE ACTUAL FIX IS BETTER THAN EITHER PATH I OFFERED (PR #16793, 100% test-side, edits no `lib/` file,
so it is not prod-deploying in any sense): all TEN purge statements are removed. The file already
knew about its residue and archived it, because the attempt row `ON DELETE RESTRICT`-pins the
session — that reasoning was right about the PIN and wrong about the ORDER. Running the purge AFTER
`Tenancy.delete_workspace/1` means the pin is already gone: teardown runs
`barkpark_prepare_workspace_cycle_teardown` and cascades `epic_assignments`, so the attempt leaves at
TRIGGER DEPTH 2 WITH THE GUC SET — through the guard's own designed exemption. No guard weakened, no
migration, both tables covered.

c3's STAMPED EVIDENCE STILL NAMES THE RECORDER and is the holder's to repair via
`bp task stamp --withdraw --note` (which keeps the original text and marks it superseded). That is
holder-only, so it is not mine. EVIDENCE IS PERMANENT AT CLOSE — this row is 5/6 and NOT yet closed,
so it is still repairable. It must be repaired BEFORE the close.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The mechanism is confirmed AT THE INSTALLED SITE, not a superseded one: barkpark_epic_ledger_immutable is CREATE OR REPLACEd by seven migrations and LATEST WINS, so the live body is guarded_immutability_function() from 20260715001300_add_assignment_runtime_attempts.exs line 66. Confirm which definition is actually installed (query the live function body, do not infer from grep) and quote it.

Both halves of the live exemption are shown to fail for Ecto sandbox cleanup: pg_trigger_depth() is 1 (not > 1) AND current_setting('barkpark.cycle_teardown_workspace', true) is unset. Demonstrated, not asserted — a depth-only fix leaves this red.

A full local `mix test` on a database that HAS rows in epic_assignment_runtime_attempts reproduces the append-only failures, and the same run on a freshly reset database does not. Both counts reported. This distinguishes the latent trap from a broken box.

The owner's choice is made deliberately between (a) sandbox cleanup sets barkpark.cycle_teardown_workspace and the workspace match is made to hold, and (b) the harness does not delete these rows at all. The chosen option AND the rejected one are written into this row with the reason.

A POSITIVE CONTROL ships with the fix, proving the guard STILL REFUSES a real direct DELETE in dev/prod after the change. A fix that silences the guard everywhere is worse than the tax it removes; without this control the change is not acceptable.

The five test setups carrying the unstated 'this table is empty' precondition are identified and each either states the precondition explicitly or no longer depends on it. Derive them by SHAPE, not by grepping a literal — a name-keyed grep cannot find a shape-keyed defect (a sibling sweep reported 6 and the honest count was 8).

corpus.title: How does a stale draft twin arise on today's server at all? — the deadlock it caused could not be rebuilt, and the CLASS is what the non-goal protects

content.description:
INSTANCE STALE, CLASS OPEN. Re-anchored 2026-09-08 on main's ruling, after lead-ledger-c5 could not reproduce the dead end this row was filed on.

WHAT THE ROW USED TO SAY IS PRESERVED BELOW AS THE INSTANCE. What changed is the question: it is no longer "fix the amend path" — c0's exact ask is already satisfied on today's server and is stamped with the run — it is "establish how a stale draft twin arises on today's server AT ALL": find a door that mints one, or establish that none does and say which change closed them.

THE NON-REPRODUCTION, WITH ITS THREE RECEIPTS. Driven 2026-09-08 by lead-ledger-c5 on scratch row task-3a8e1fa94a2e692f, created for the purpose and cancelled on the record — never a live row, because a probe whose failure mode corrupts the thing it measures gets its own sandbox.

 1. `bp doc patch` on a claimed, PUBLISHED task writes STRAIGHT THROUGH to the published row. Verb quoted, before/after quoted: BEFORE "CONTROL WORDING probe.", AFTER "AMENDED WORDING: ...". No publish was issued and the claim was never released — worker lead-ledger-c5, epoch 2, in_progress, unchanged across the amend.
 2. `bp doc get task drafts.<id>` returned rc=4 NOT FOUND both BEFORE and immediately AFTER every patch. THE BEFORE-ARM IS WHAT MAKES THE AFTER-ARM MEAN ANYTHING — an absence with no before-reading is not a measurement.
 3. TWO RECEIPTS THIS ROW RECORDS AS rc=5 BOTH RETURNED rc=0: patch-on-published, and `doc publish`.

Verified by READING THE PUBLISHED DOCUMENT BACK, not by trusting the patch receipt — which is exactly what this row's own non-vacuity criterion said not to trust. THE ROW'S OWN CRITERION CAUGHT THE ROW'S OWN PREMISE.

THAT IS A NON-REPRODUCTION, NOT A REFUTATION, AND THE ROW IS RE-ANCHORED RATHER THAN KILLED. An absence produced by following ONE documented sequence is evidence about THAT SEQUENCE, not about the world. The original twin came from an origin the reproduction could not recreate, and all three candidates remain live and are named rather than the flattering one being picked: a create whose publish leg failed; an older server behaviour since changed; or a path this row does not name. If patches no longer mint drafts the deadlock may already be foreclosed — but nobody has established how a twin arises today, and until someone does, the shape can reappear from a door nobody has looked at.

DO NOT CLOSE THIS ROW ON THAT NON-REPRODUCTION. Main's ruling, recorded here so a later lead cannot mistake a tidy negative for a finding. The absence criterion stays a MISS until a door is named or an absence is EARNED.

THE BINDING NON-GOAL IS UNTOUCHED AND WAS NOT TIDIED DURING THE RE-CUT: DO NOT WEAKEN THE PUBLISH CLAIM GUARD. A stale twin must still be unable to obliterate a live claim's state, and a fix that passes the amend criterion by loosening that arm does not satisfy this row. Its criterion is carried VERBATIM, not a syllable changed — a non-goal that gets tidied during a re-cut is how a guard quietly loses strength while the row still claims to protect it.

ORDERING IS PART OF THE SPEC: the COUNT criterion runs FIRST, before the door sweep. It is the cheapest criterion and the only one that can hand the next reader a live specimen instead of a reconstruction; a non-zero count changes the whole approach to the sweep. A cheap measurement placed after an expensive sweep gets done after the sweep, and by then it has bought nothing.

ONE MORE THING THIS ROW DEMONSTRATED ABOUT ITSELF: all four of its original criteria carried NO `merge_gate` declaration until lead-ledger-c5 set them to false. That makes it the FOURTH row in one night that was itself an instance of the undeclared-criterion population being documented beside it. A population that keeps reproducing itself on the very rows written about it is not an estimate; it is a demonstration.

--- THE ORIGINAL INSTANCE, AS FILED ---

A stale draft twin freezes a claimed row's acceptance criteria — every documented amend path is refused. The row recorded four refusals: a doc patch on the published id, a doc patch on the draft id, a publish of the twin, and an amend attempt via the task verbs, with the operator left with two prescribed cures of which one was impossible and the other did not work. Those receipts are kept because they are the evidence the shape once existed; they are NOT to be trusted as a description of today's server, and two of them have now been measured returning rc=0.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A criterion's WORDING can be amended on a claimed, published row that has a stale draft twin, without publishing that twin and without releasing the claim. Demonstrated end-to-end on a row deliberately put in this shape (published + live claim + a draft twin whose claim epoch differs), with the before/after criterion text and the verb quoted.

The publish guard's claim check is UNCHANGED in strength — a stale twin still cannot obliterate a live claim's state. Proved by a negative arm in the same run: attempting to publish a twin that lacks the published row's claim state is still REFUSED, with the refusal text quoted. A fix that passes criterion 0 by loosening this arm does not satisfy this row.

RUN THIS FIRST, BEFORE the door sweep and before any conclusion — it is the cheapest criterion here and the only one that can hand you a live specimen instead of a reconstruction. COUNT the shape on the live ledger: how many published `type:task` rows currently have a `drafts.<id>` sibling, over a stated denominator. A NON-ZERO count changes the whole approach to the criterion below — you stop sweeping candidate doors and start working backwards from a row that already has the shape. ZERO is a real answer and a dated one. Placed first on purpose: a cheap measurement placed after an expensive sweep gets done after the sweep, and by then it has bought nothing.

A door that MINTS a `drafts.<id>` twin on a PUBLISHED task row is either NAMED with a reproduction, or ruled ABSENT with the enumeration behind the ruling. Candidate doors to drive, not an exhaustive list: a `bp task create` whose publish leg fails after the draft write; the MCP bridge; Studio; a raw `POST /v1/data/mutate` on a task base; `bp doc patch` with an explicit `--perspective drafts`. A SINGLE NON-REPRODUCTION ON ONE PATH DOES NOT DISCHARGE THIS — that is the mistake this re-cut exists to record — and the finder must NAME WHICH PATHS THEY DROVE. An absence claim is only as good as the paths it swept, and it must list them.

If no door is found, the ABSENCE is EARNED rather than assumed: name the change that closed the last one (commit or PR, with a date), and state what would have to be true for a twin to appear again. If a door IS found, the original discoverability criterion comes back as written — 'the dead end is discoverable BEFORE it is hit: either the doc-patch refusal on the published id names the amend path that actually works, or a reader can enumerate rows in this shape; a doc-only sentence does not satisfy this' — because a reachable twin makes the refusal wording live again.

corpus.title: The attribution fence has no known author: find the write that added criterion 11, or ratify it as a charter decision

content.description:
Discovered while writing scripts/pds-crown-fence-arithmetic-2026-07-20.md (task pds-w10-fence-arithmetic), NOT taken this wave.

Criterion 11 of pds-w1-crown-proof — the SINGLE-RUN ATTRIBUTION FENCE — credits itself to 'the wave-9 ledger-fence slice, pds-w9-crown-ledger-fence'. That slice's own AC-4 evidence closes with 'array length 11 -> 11', i.e. it proves it added NO criterion. So some later, unrecorded whole-array patch added the fence.

Today the fence exists in the live task array and NOWHERE else: no charter decision (grep for 'attribution fence'/'MOSAIC' over .claude/workflows/bp-pds-charter.md returns only PDS-D179, which is a different question and explicitly must not be cited as 'mosaic forbidden'), no verdict file, and — until this wave — no ledger entry. bp doc patch is unfenced by claim or epoch and replaces the WHOLE array (PDS-D165), so the fence is one stale-copy patch away from silent deletion.

Wave 10 bought durability (the verbatim text now lives in scripts/pds-crown-ledger-2026-07-20.md) but NOT provenance. Remaining work:
1. Identify the actual write that added criterion 11 — task revs / audit log / the wave-9 build branches — and name the actor.
2. Ratify the fence as a numbered PDS charter decision so it has a durable home outside the array.
3. Either correct the stored credit line or record the mis-citation as permanent (correcting it costs another unfenced whole-array patch; wave 10 judged that not worth it for a credit line alone, and that judgement should be revisited by whoever holds the array next).

Not blocking the wave-10 climb: the fence's CONTENT is unaffected, only its authorship.

corpus.title: Pre-declare and commit the attribution-fence arithmetic, and make criterion 11 durable

content.description:
Two jobs, both PURELY documentary, both landing BEFORE the climb fires so the arithmetic can never be
litigated after the run when the incentive to read it loosely is highest.

JOB 1 — WRITE scripts/pds-crown-fence-arithmetic-2026-07-20.md, the pre-declared reading of the
crown's 12th criterion (the SINGLE-RUN ATTRIBUTION FENCE). With file:line evidence it must state:

 - Indices are ZERO-BASED (PDS-D149), so "criteria 0-10" is every criterion except the fence itself,
   criterion 10 INCLUDED. A live census over all 12 evidence fields shows only criterion 0 names a run
   id at all (20260720T032558Z-28651) — so all nine currently-met criteria need re-anchoring.
 - WAVE 9'S RUN ID CAN NEVER PAY CRITERIA 3 AND 4 (PDS-D194). Its transcript records rungs 3 and 4 as
   ABORT on cond_b at crown-transcript-w8.txt:322/:324. Criterion 3 needs a byte-scan with a FIRING
   control on the FULL bundle; criterion 4 needs the eight-webhook control to fire on it. Neither is
   producible from a run whose full export never happened. So criterion 6 must be RE-EARNED under a
   run that also greens 3 and 4 — the memory physics and the fence arithmetic agree.
 - THE FENCE'S TWO VERBS DISAGREE ABOUT CRITERION 10, resolved in advance: the requirement clause says
   CITE (satisfiable for a merge event) while option (a) says "re-prove criteria 0-10 from ONE serial
   climb" (no climb produces a merge, so option (a) is unsatisfiable for criterion 10 read literally).
   SAFE CONSTRUCTION satisfying both readings at no cost: criterion 10's evidence carries PR number +
   merge sha PLUS the climb run id, explicitly LABELLED as attribution rather than proof.
 - THE STAMP HAZARDS, both proven live: (a) --met REQUIRES --criterion-text matching the stored row
   byte-for-byte or it 409s, and criterion 6's stored text contains literal BACKTICKS that a naive
   double-quoted argument mangles into command substitution — fetch the text to a file and pass
   --criterion-text "$(cat f)". (b) evidence and criterion-text ride the URL QUERY STRING and die past
   roughly 9-11 KB combined as an opaque HTTP/2 stream reset that reads like a network blip; criteria
   5/6/9's own text already eats 846/2490/1098 bytes. Keep every evidence string TERSE — a run id plus
   a one-line transcript pointer, never a pasted block.
 - THE ORDER (PDS-D189/D195): lead claims the crown; re-stamps 0-9; merge; stamps 10; criterion 11 is
   DEFERRED, because the met-flip is the act that removes the last auto-close brake.

JOB 2 — REPAIR CRITERION 11'S DURABILITY (PDS-D197). Append to scripts/pds-crown-ledger-2026-07-20.md
criterion 11's VERBATIM stored text plus a provenance correction, and fix that file's own "eleven
acceptance criteria" header to twelve. Today the fence exists in NO charter decision, NO ledger entry
and NO verdict file, while that ledger declares itself the crown's durable recovery source and
describes an ELEVEN-entry array — so anyone repairing the crown from its own designated record
silently DELETES the fence, with no error on either side. Note the mis-citation honestly: the fence
credits pds-w9-crown-ledger-fence, whose own AC-4 evidence reads "array length 11 -> 11".

DO NOT stamp, patch or close pds-w1-crown-proof. This slice writes files only.

GATE: test -f scripts/pds-crown-fence-arithmetic-2026-07-20.md && grep -ci twelve scripts/pds-crown-ledger-2026-07-20.md && git diff --stat origin/main -- scripts/pds-pull-proof.sh

corpus.title: A draft twin was refreshed on a claimed row AFTER its stamps landed, carrying zero evidence — publishing it would have destroyed 5,287 bytes of proof

content.description:
MEASURED 2026-09-05 on task-bf3adebfec5833df, on the live guerrilla ledger, while closing that row. Filed with the writer UNNAMED because the measurement is complete and the unknown writer is the finding, not a reason to withhold it.

WHAT WAS THERE. A draft twin drafts.task-bf3adebfec5833df existed on a published, CLAIMED row. Its _createdAt was 2026-09-05T17:18:52Z and its _updatedAt 2026-09-05T18:07:08Z — a minute AFTER my stamps at ~17:51-18:06 landed on the published row.

The twin carried all four acceptance_criteria at met=false with ZERO bytes of evidence, and lifecycle_status "open". The published row at that moment carried met=[true,true,false,true] and 5,287 bytes of evidence across three criteria, lifecycle_status "in_progress".

So the twin was refreshed AFTER the stamps and did not contain them.

THE HAZARD. Publishing that twin would have destroyed every stamp on the row — three criteria of hand-written proof, replaced by empty strings, with met flipped back to false. There is no other copy: evidence is not versioned anywhere a reader reaches.

WHAT STOPPED IT was the patch door being fenced. Attempting `bp doc patch task task-bf3adebfec5833df` returned validation_failed with a refusal that named the fork precisely and offered discardDraft or publish as the two remedies. That refusal is well built. But a hazard surviving on ONE fence is not a safe hazard: the same twin is reachable by `bp doc publish`, which is a sanctioned verb, and nothing in that path is going to warn a caller that the twin is sixteen fields behind the row it would overwrite.

WHAT I RULED OUT BEFORE DISCARDING IT. I diffed the twin field-by-field against the published row before touching it, because it was not mine to delete and I did not create it deliberately. Content keys present in the twin and not the published row: only `title`, which lives at the top level on the published side, so not unique content. Every criterion carried zero-byte evidence. `twin carries any evidence at all? False`. It held nothing that was not already on the published row in a better state, so discarding it lost nothing — but that is a fact about THIS twin, not about the mechanism.

WHAT I CANNOT NAME is the writer. I did not call bp doc patch, publish, unpublish or restore-revision on that row before the twin appeared, and the timestamps bracket my claim and stamp calls. Somebody with the write-path context can determine whether claim, stamp, close or a Content.Mutations path mints or refreshes a draft twin on a published task, and whether that is intended. There is an existing test file api/test/barkpark/tasks/dedup_draft_debris_test.exs, which suggests draft debris on task rows is a known shape with prior work behind it.

PREVALENCE, MEASURED 2026-09-06 — the first hard number on how common these twins are, and it came out of an unrelated repair rather than a hunt.

While restoring 101 displaced stage notes across 74 task rows (task-d6f3e66b1b829e6e), every write was attempted through `bp doc patch` and its receipt read. TWO of the 74 rows were REFUSED by the draft-twin fence:

    tgw6-bl-primary-checkout-staged-grip-fork
      twin last touched 2026-08-24T18:56:23Z, twin disposition_reason 2,125 chars
      carries nothing the published row does not
    cch-w38-bl-inline-no-team-emitters-now-diverge-from-the-gates
      twin last touched 2026-08-23T07:08:51Z, twin disposition_reason 167 chars
      carries nothing the published row does not

So 2 of 74, about 2.7%, on a sample nobody selected for twinning — these rows were chosen because they had lost a stage note, which has no relationship to whether they carry a draft twin. That makes it a fair prevalence estimate rather than a hunted one, on a small sample.

TWO PROPERTIES WORTH MORE THAN THE RATE.

Both twins are WEEKS OLD — 2026-08-23 and 2026-08-24 — and both were last touched at a time nobody was editing those rows. The twin observed in the original filing was created and refreshed DURING a live session, minutes after stamps landed. So twins persist indefinitely once created; they are not a transient state that resolves itself.

Neither twin carries anything its published row does not. Combined with the original observation — a twin holding all four criteria at met=false with ZERO evidence while the published row held 5,287 bytes across three — the pattern is that a twin is a STALE SUBSET, never a divergent branch of work. That matters for the disposition: if it generalises, discarding is safe and publishing is the dangerous direction, which is the opposite of what "resolve the fork" suggests to a reader choosing between them.

I did NOT discard either twin. Reading is free; deleting content I have not been asked to delete, in order to complete an unrelated repair, is the original bug wearing a helpful expression. Both rows are recorded here and skipped in the restore, and their recovered notes are still owed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: NAME THE WRITER: identify which code path minted or refreshed drafts.task-bf3adebfec5833df on a published, claimed row, and whether that path runs on claim, stamp, close, or a shared Content mutation. Quote the function. "Could not reproduce" discharges this only with the reproduction attempt pasted, including which verbs were tried against a published claimed row.

MEASURE THE POPULATION: count published task rows that currently carry a draft twin whose acceptance_criteria hold strictly LESS evidence than the published row's. State the count and list the ids. A count of zero must be shown to be a real zero — paste the query and prove it can find a positive when one exists.

CLOSE THE PUBLISH DOOR or show it is already closed: publishing a draft twin whose criteria carry less evidence than the published row is refused, or is shown to be impossible today with the guard named. The patch door already refuses with a message naming the fork; the publish door is the one nobody has checked.

A regression test constructs the shape — a published row with stamped evidence plus a stale twin — and reds when the guard is removed. Asserting the guard in isolation does not discharge this; the test must build the divergence.

corpus.title: A met criterion cannot be un-stamped while its row stays open — charter D96 orders a reset no verb can perform

content.description:
A criterion can be stamped `met: true` and then NEVER un-stamped while the row stays open. Every write path is closed, and one of them is closed by a guard that is otherwise correct. A charter decision currently orders an action the tooling cannot perform.

THE LIVE CASE, which is how this was found. Charter D96 of the search-template epic instructs, verbatim: "the lead resets crit-2 to unmet and discharges it with a token-carrying `/v1/graph` probe under real concurrent load (or a post-#6284 route-concurrency fix), never a re-close on the stale flags." That instruction exists because a lifecycle transition does NOT reset met-flags: `stw10-backlog-flagship-health-pool` was reopened per D82 and carried its `met: true` flags across the reopen, so a p0 row reads `open` at 3/3 while its criteria are not discharged. The lead cannot carry out D96.

EVERY PATH, MEASURED 2026-08-21 (not inferred from the help text):

1. `bp task stamp --criterion N --met` — sets true. There is no inverse flag. `bp capabilities` contains zero occurrences of `unstamp`, `unmet`, `unset`, or `clear_criteria`.
2. `bp task stamp --criterion N --miss --note "…"` — appends to the criterion's `attempts` list and, by its own documented contract, "met never flips". Correct behaviour for recording a failed attempt; it cannot express "this was certified in error."
3. `bp doc patch task <id> --set 'acceptance_criteria:=[…]'` then `bp doc publish` — the patch LANDS on the draft correctly (verified via `bp doc get task drafts.<id> --perspective raw`: the draft held `met:false` with corrected evidence). The PUBLISH is then refused: `validation_failed` / "stale draft: publishing this draft would clear the `met: true` flag for acceptance criterion 1 … the published row holds that proof and this draft does not."
4. `bp task close --set 'criteria:=[…]'` — CAN write `met:false`, but only as part of closing the row. Using it here would mean closing a p0 row in order to say its work is not done, which is the opposite of the intent.

THE GUARD IN (3) IS RIGHT AND SHOULD NOT BE WEAKENED. Its reasoning is sound and worth preserving: "A stamp is written DIRECTLY to the published row and never rebases an open draft, so a draft minted before the stamp still carries the pre-stamp criteria." It exists so a long-lived draft cannot silently erase a stamp landed after the draft was minted — a real hazard on a board with concurrent writers. The defect is NOT that the guard fires; it is that there is no sanctioned verb to fall back to, so the guard's advice ("move the criterion through the sanctioned verbs") names a path that does not exist for this transition. A guard that blocks the wrong route while the right route is absent leaves the caller with only bad options.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE ROW. A stamp is the board's unit of proof, and today it is a ratchet that only turns one way while a row is open. Any criterion certified in error is permanent until someone closes the row — so the cheapest way to fix a false stamp becomes closing the task, which manufactures a false done to correct a false met. The stw10 case is exactly that shape: criterion index 2 was stamped on 2026-07-27 citing #6284, and the behaviour it certifies did not exist until d17beab24f (#9732) on 2026-08-06 — the tree on the stamp date held ZERO occurrences of `newestFailedStale`. A false stamp rescued ten days later by unrelated work is luck, and the board had no way to record that at the time.

WHAT TO BUILD — the smallest thing that closes the hole:

`bp task stamp --criterion N --unmet --reason "…"`, holder-only under the same epoch fence as `--met`, requiring `--criterion-text` verbatim exactly as `--met` does (the off-by-one guard must apply in both directions), refusing an empty reason, and emitting a `task.criterion` event so the un-stamp is auditable rather than silent. It must be REFUSED on a merge-gated criterion without the same `--merge-gated` lead override that `--met` requires, so the two directions stay symmetric. The reason belongs in the criterion's durable record, not in an ephemeral lease.

ACCEPTANCE MUST BE MUTATION-PROVEN: assert that an un-stamp with mismatched `--criterion-text` is REFUSED, then remove that check and watch the test go red. A happy-path test alone cannot distinguish this feature from one that flips whatever index it is handed.

INTERIM STATE OF stw10, so nobody mistakes it for discharged: the evidence strings on all three criteria have been corrected in place and criterion 1 now OPENS with `*** THIS FLAG IS WRONG AND CHARTER D96 ORDERS IT RESET. IT STANDS ONLY BECAUSE NO VERB CAN CLEAR IT. DO NOT SEAL THIS ROW ON IT. ***`. The discharge itself is tracked at `stw13-flagship-health-pool-underload-reseal`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An un-stamp with mismatched --criterion-text is REFUSED — mutation-proven: remove that check and watch the test go red; a happy-path test alone cannot distinguish this feature from one that flips whatever index it is handed.

corpus.title: A worker id is LANE-scoped, so two sessions of one lane write an indistinguishable ledger — and a claim can lapse because it never reached a held file

content.description:
Measured across the 2026-09-06/07 campaign in the cli lane, and adopted fleet-wide by main after three independent lanes hit it. TWO COUPLED DEFECTS, one identity and one bookkeeping.

(1) IDENTITY. Every lead session in a lane writes under the SAME worker id (the cli lane's is 'lead-cli'). There are ~122 lead sessions and 'idle' does not mean dead, so a predecessor that wakes on an inbox message writes claims, pulses, stamps and closes that are BYTE-INDISTINGUISHABLE from the live lead's. This is not a discipline problem that better instructions can fix: claim-health.sh and every other reader is STRUCTURALLY unable to separate them, because the discriminator was never written down. Main's own hidden-generation check was corrected twice in fifteen minutes for exactly this reason and landed on 'a generation label in a now-line is a CLAIM, not proof of authorship' -- which is the admission that the ledger records no author.

(2) BOOKKEEPING. A claim is protected only if its id is ALSO written into the lane's held file, which is what the pulse loop reads. These are two separate manual acts. Measured instance: task-f0e49432f1653c2f was claimed by lead-cli-11, never added to held.lead-cli-s8.txt, therefore never pulsed; the lease lapsed silently, a worker built PR #16660 against an unclaimed row, and the handover still described it as claimed. Nothing reported the gap -- it was found only because the successor re-read the live row instead of trusting the handover. Main reports this campaign has lost claims to lapsed leases three times; this is the first time the MECHANISM was identified rather than the symptom.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A DOC-ONLY ANSWER, A PER-LANE NAMING CONVENTION, OR AN AGENT INSTRUCTION DOES NOT SATISFY THIS CRITERION -- the discriminator must be a field the SERVER stores and a reader can query. Two ledger writes made under the same lane by two different sessions are distinguishable by reading the stored row alone, with no access to either session's notes. The negative arm is required: a value supplied only by the client, or one that a second session can trivially copy from a held file or a template, does NOT satisfy this -- that is precisely the failure mode that made a now-line's generation label unreliable evidence.

The separation is SHOWN TO DISCRIMINATE, not merely to exist: a reader (claim-health.sh or its successor) is run against TWO identities within ONE lane and attributes each write to the correct session, and is ALSO run against one identity twice and returns the same set both times. Both arms are required -- a reader that returns everything passes the first arm alone.

CLAIMING AND PROTECTING ARE ONE ACT. A claim that does not end up in the list the pulse loop reads is REPORTED at the moment it happens, not discovered later by a successor. Satisfied by a mechanism that performs both writes and reads the second one back, or by a check that reconciles held-file contents against the set of rows actually claimed by that worker id and names the difference in both directions. A convention written into a brief does not satisfy this: the measured failure (task-f0e49432f1653c2f) happened to a lead who had the convention in front of it.

MUTATION-PROVED AND NON-VACUOUS. Disarm the discriminator and the reader in criterion 1 must RED naming the collision, not pass quietly; disarm the reconciliation in criterion 2 and the held-file gap must go undetected in a test that then fails. A positive control shows each check can still fire on data it does not own -- a check that reads nothing passes everything.
MERGE-GATED (the lead closes this): the PR merges with all four required contexts green, read LIVE from .github/required-checks.json, and the merge sha is recorded here.

corpus.title: Movement 0: every open row on this epic names a divergence that is live TODAY — adjudicated by content, forwarded by membership, counted by a paginated walk

content.description:
MOVEMENT 0 — THIS ROW IS THE WAVE-7 CARRIER. It absorbs its own original ask (reproduce the Bands 1/3/6 census rows still at L4 confidence, whose embedded arithmetic is now stale a THIRD time: it asserts 91 children / 85 open, the roster read at Decide was 135 / 83 / 41 / 9 / 2) into the full-roster adjudication below. Filed here rather than as a new row because guerrilla's task CREATE verb was returning HTTP 500 at Decide (27.7s on a minimal 4-field payload) while PATCH answered in 0.49s — and this row's own subject IS census reproduction, so reusing it beats minting a duplicate.

ROUND 1. LEDGER ONLY — this slice touches NO repo files, opens NO PR, and needs NO worktree. HIGH-FLIP-RISK: closing a row by content that is actually still live is the exact fabrication this epic exists to cure. When a disposition below and the tree disagree, THE TREE WINS and you record the disagreement instead of forcing the close.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Wave 6 wrote a thirteen-row evidence-close list and never paid it. All thirteen are still `open`, so a wave that shipped five real fixes moved the open count by ZERO. The adjudication below is already DONE by two verifiers against origin/main; your job is the writes and the re-reads.

THE WRITE CONTRACT (charter D86 — obey it exactly, it was rehearsed on scratch rows):
- Use `bp task close <id> <worker> <epoch> <status> "<reason>"`, `bp task stage <id> <state> --note`, and `bp task move <id> <new_parent>`. These write the PUBLISHED doc directly.
- NEVER `bp doc patch` a disposition. It lands only in the draft; `bp task get` is published-first so a read-back shows nothing, AND it creates a draft twin that FREEZES the row's GitHub mirror (mirror_job.ex load_task/3 is draft-first).
- SIX rows carry a claim; a RELEASED claim still refuses a foreign close. Wrong epoch gives `fenced_off`, right epoch gives `not_holder:<w>`. Land it with `--set holder_override="wave 7 Movement 0 lead evidence-close over a released builder claim"`. The five released rows are held by `epic-builder-census-truth-pass-evidence-close-the-ver`; `gr-p5r5-successor-seal` carries an EXPIRED claim (previous_worker `lead-truthgrip`) and was NOT rehearsed — budget one retry.
- NEVER `bp doc delete` — it orphans the GitHub issue (proven: the issue stayed OPEN with no ledger row behind it). Cancel, never delete.
- RE-READ every row after writing. A printed rev is not persistence. Re-derive counts with a PAGINATED OFFSET-WALK: the query surface silently caps at limit=1000 with NO truncation flag, and a sibling epic's single-call lens under-counted by 48 rows while exiting 0.
- guerrilla degrades under load and 500s intermittently. Retry with backoff; never conclude a write failed without re-reading published state.

A. CLOSE BY CONTENT — 13 rows, each with the evidence to paste.
 1. gr-blk-oauth-head-mint — 26acc7a91 (#5378). `router.ex` refuse_head_on_side_effecting_gets answers 405+allow:GET; tests in router_oauth_test.exs and router_head_and_favicon_test.exs. AC3 (the other 55 GETs) is ruled OUT OF SCOPE BY DECISION in the fence's own comment and forwarded to cch-w2-head-sideeffect-fence, which is DONE.
 2. gr-blk-smoke-click-inert — 8c9c116c5 (#5379). smoke.mjs header "THE SHIM IS NOW CLICK-CAPABLE"; dispatchEvent + click() returning a fired count.
 3. gr-blk-revoke-harness-gap — 8c9c116c5 (#5379) + 0ed73651f (#5436). scenarios.mjs carries both session DELETEs with a 404 miss arm over a per-boot store; smoke asserts the list shrinks 4->3.
 4. gr-backlog-provider-reconnect — 2a6b673cc (#6538, wave 6's own slice). The false "no unique index, no 409" comment is gone; rotate-in-place is documented and implemented.
 5. gr-blk-ledger-close-bypass-audit — 515f14fdd (#5309) + a893c3821 (#5435). ensure_task_close_is_cas guards all four mutate clauses; mutate_controller_test.exs pins the refusal and the `source: :sync` exemption. DISCLOSE IN THE SAME BREATH: AC4 (record the 7 historical anomaly ids) is NOT satisfied by code — either write the ids or decline it explicitly.
 6. gr-backlog-e02-deploy-actor — charter :429-437 "RATIFY TRIGGER-ONLY", all eight grounds re-derived exactly (charter D87). Add the one missing sentence in the close evidence: a deleted actor's FK survives but preload(:actor_user) yields nil, so the join's only honest render is the `system` fallback Activity already shows.
 7. gr-blk-primary-checkout-reconcile — closed by STATE, not by a SHA. Re-run the check IMMEDIATELY before closing (the checkout is shared and volatile): expect 0 tracked modifications, ahead 0, and all four superset charters on origin/main. Close as "the recipe is a no-op and the tree is clean" — NEVER as "fixed by <sha>", and NEVER claim the 1095 lines were preserved (unknown). The 8 dangling commits are honest residue and are filed separately.
 8. cch-bl-overview-background-refresh-fails-silently — 576107987 (#6541). markRefreshStale() at app.js:5023 inside the `if (!full)` arm; refresh_failed a real dot state labelled "Not current". THE SHA WAS EARNED BY A DIFFERENT ROW (cch-bl-overview-subscription-band-stale) — name BOTH task ids in the close.
 9. cch-bl-close-fence-epoch-only — 448749cf1 (#6420). SUBTLE: check_fencing/2 is UNCHANGED (still epoch-only). It closes on criterion 2's SECOND arm — a separate holder gate check_close_holder/3 ("PDS-D288") refuses a foreign close and documents the legitimate allow-arms, with three committed {:error,{:not_holder,...}} assertions. Quote check_close_holder explicitly or a reviewer will read the close as fabricated.
10. task-04054d483ae95bd1 — 16453cf65 (#5044), paid by a SIBLING epic; all seven named modules are async:false and the hand-listed key set became a source-text scanner. The row's own body already carries an unread "PREMISE REFUTED" annotation. DISCLOSE: criterion 2 (5 consecutive random-seed suite runs) is NOT run-proven — close on 1+3 and say so, or spend the runs.
11. cch-bl-appcss-orphan-comment-live and 12. cch-bl-appcss-wound-owner and 13. task-1e2b96c8907edef0 (considering) — one wound, three rows. RE-MEASURE IMMEDIATELY BEFORE CLOSING (shared checkout): `git status --porcelain cloud/priv/static/app.css` empty, `git diff origin/main -- cloud/priv/static/app.css` 0 lines, delimiters balanced, `__css_check.mjs` 0 errors. Close as "NO LONGER REPRODUCES as of <timestamp> in <checkout>", NEVER as "fixed by <sha>".

B. THE 15th CLOSE, AND IT HAS AN ORDER CONSTRAINT.
gr-p5r5-successor-seal's work was EXECUTED by its `done` 15/15 child gr-p5r12-terminal-act; its own 13 criteria read 0/13 only because nobody stamped the parent (criterion 13 is in fact TRUE in the ledger). BUT it holds THREE OPEN children invisible to the seal predicate's clause (a), which reads direct children only: gr-bl-seal-predicate-provenance-gap, gr-bl-task-write-cap-breaks-briefs, gr-bl-reap-orphaned-preview-port-squatters. RE-PARENT THOSE THREE FIRST, then close gr-p5r5. Closing it first re-commits the self-orphan trap one level down. Send provenance-gap UP to this epic (it is a defect in seal-predicate.mjs, in fence); send task-write-cap and port-squatters to a real named owner per section E.

C. DO NOT CLOSE — three rows wave 6 listed that do not survive.
- gr-blk-cssom-parity-harden REPRODUCES: COUNT SKEW is still advisory (cssom-parity.mjs :649-657) with exit 0 at :705, and no CSS-nesting fixture exists. REWRITE it down to its one live gap instead: styleguide.html ships ~194 lines of inline CSS (lines 9-203) that the parity gate never certifies, and it IS served (router.ex Plug.Static allowlist). Its criterion-3 mutation anchors have also drifted (.modal-root 1029->1071, .wh-secret 3076->3150) — fix them or a future builder mutates the wrong rules and stamps a vacuous proof.
- gr-blk-console-refetch-storm CLOSES, but on 481d6f231 ALONE. Wave 6 cited two SHAs and 82eb84a37 is NOT an ancestor of origin/main (squashed away) — citing it writes a dangling SHA. `git log -S OVERVIEW_FULL` names 481d6f231 as the SOLE introducer. State the honest shape: 40->12 requests with tally [8,1,1,1,1], NOT "each of the five endpoints once", which is unachievable by design.
- gr-backlog-css-brace-detector does NOT close: AC2's E10 fixture does not exist.
