corpus.title: An 'open' row holding a claim is a deadlock — claim, stamp AND release all refuse it, and the board shows 23 such rows as TAKEN

content.description:
A task can sit `lifecycle: open` while still carrying a live claim, and in that state EVERY verb refuses it. Measured board-wide 2026-08-20: 23 such rows, claims 63h to 1,163h old (2.6 to 48 days), every one on a row that never reached `in_progress`.

THE DEADLOCK, all three refusals reproduced:
  bp task claim   -> not_ready               (someone holds it)
  bp task stamp   -> not_in_progress:open
  bp task release -> not_in_progress:open    (release REQUIRES in_progress)

And both write-arounds are guarded, correctly: `lifecycle_status` is reachable only through claim/close, so `bp doc patch --set lifecycle_status=in_progress` then publish returns `not found`; and `bp task stage`'s write set never includes `content.claim`, so staging cannot clear a holder either.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The board renders these rows as TAKEN. The next builder skips them. So the defect does not merely leave a stale field — it silently withdraws real ready work from the queue, and it does so on exactly the rows nobody is coming back to. Several of the 23 were held by `epic-builder-*` workers from waves that ended weeks ago, with `expired_at: null`, so the lease could never lapse on its own. That is quiet misdirection of the same family as a stale brief, and it hides work rather than mis-describing it.

THE ESCAPE EXISTS BUT IS UNDISCOVERABLE. It is one clause in the hint `claim` prints on refusal — "if YOU hold it, re-claim with your own worker id to renew the lease". Re-claiming with the STORED holder's exact worker id succeeds, bumps the epoch, and moves the row to `in_progress`, which is precisely what `release` requires:

  WK=$(bp task get <id> -o json | jq -r '.doc.claim.worker')
  E=$(bp task claim <id> "$WK" | grep -oE 'epoch=[0-9]+' | cut -d= -f2)
  bp task release <id> "$WK" "$E" --yes        # -> open, holder None

All 23 were freed this way; a re-sweep of 6,869 docs afterwards returns ZERO open rows holding a claim. But the recipe requires acting under the DEAD worker's id, so `released_by` records them rather than the actor — an attribution the ledger cannot distinguish from that worker having released it themselves.

WHAT TO FIX — pick one, deliberately:
  (A) Make `release` legal on an `open` row that holds a claim. Smallest change; the state is already anomalous, and refusing to let anyone clear it is the part that has no defender.
  (B) Make the anomalous state unreachable: a claim and `lifecycle: open` should not coexist. This needs a story for how the 23 got there — most plausibly a close/reopen path or a wave teardown that dropped `in_progress` without dropping the claim. Find that path, or (B) fixes the symptom's symptom.
  (C) Give every claim a real `expired_at`. All 23 had `expired_at: null`, so no sweeper could ever have reclaimed them. This is complementary to A/B rather than an alternative.

DO NOT ship a periodic janitor that force-clears old claims as the whole answer: that hides the state rather than making it unreachable, and a janitor that clears a claim a live agent still holds is a worse defect than the one it fixes.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The remedy is chosen from (A) make release legal on an open row holding a claim, (B) make the claim+open state unreachable, or (C) give every claim a real expired_at — and the choice is RECORDED with its reasoning. (C) is complementary to A/B, not an alternative to either. A periodic janitor that force-clears old claims is REFUSED as the whole answer: it hides the state instead of making it unreachable, and one that clears a claim a live agent holds is worse than the defect.

If (B) is chosen, the PATH BY WHICH the 23 rows reached claim+open is identified and named — most plausibly a close/reopen route or a wave teardown that dropped lifecycle_status without dropping content.claim. Without that path, (B) fixes a symptom of a symptom. If the path cannot be found, say so and fall back to (A).

A test FAILS on today's main and passes after the fix, constructed on a row genuinely in the anomalous state (lifecycle open AND content.claim.worker non-null), asserting that the chosen verb now succeeds. Asserting the guard in isolation does not discharge this — all three verbs already refuse correctly in their own terms; the defect is that TOGETHER they leave no exit.
MUTATION-PROVED: disarm the fix and confirm the new test reds. A test that still passes with the fix disarmed proves nothing.

The existing guards are PRESERVED, not loosened as collateral: bp doc patch must still refuse to set lifecycle_status directly, and bp task stage must still leave content.claim untouched. A fix that opens either door trades this deadlock for an unfenced write path.

A re-sweep of the live board reports ZERO rows with lifecycle=open AND claim.worker non-null, and the sweep command is recorded so anyone can re-run it. Baseline for comparison: 23 such rows on 2026-08-20, all freed manually by the lead via re-claim-then-release; a re-sweep of 6,869 docs immediately after returned 0.

The attribution gap is addressed or explicitly accepted on the record: the manual escape acts under the DEAD holder's worker id, so `released_by` names them rather than the actor, and the ledger cannot distinguish that from the worker having released it themselves. Either the fix removes the need to impersonate, or the reason for accepting it is stated.
MERGE-GATED (the LEAD closes this): the PR is merged, and the lead has independently re-run the board sweep and recorded the count rather than re-reading the builder's number.

corpus.title: Re-cut the vendored starter SDK tarballs: @barkpark/core and @barkpark/react have been STALE-SOURCE since 2026-09-11

content.description:
scripts/check-vendor-freshness.mjs reds STALE-SOURCE for BOTH vendored starter SDKs: @barkpark/core and @barkpark/react have been behind their source since the tarballs were cut on 2026-09-11. Every user who scaffolds from templates/search-starter or templates/astro-search-starter gets the old bytes.

This is the gate-and-remedy-in-different-trees case the workflow's own header documents: the check runs in search-template-gates.yml, the remedy (scripts/recut-vendor-tarballs.sh) writes templates/**, and the lane that owns the check is not the lane that owns the tree. GRANTED to studio by the orchestrator on 2026-09-13, explicitly including committing the .tgz files and templates/VENDOR-STAMP.json.

MEASURED BEFORE, in a clean worktree cut from origin/main dea298605:
  node scripts/check-vendor-freshness.mjs -> 2 freshness failure(s), both STALE-SOURCE.

The remedy is mechanical and self-verifying: the script builds js/packages/{core,react}, packs each with PNPM (never npm -- npm pack emits workspace:^ specifiers that are uninstallable outside the workspace and break npm ci in the templates), copies both tarballs into BOTH templates' vendor/ dirs, repins each template lockfile's two integrity values (a bare tarball swap leaves the old sha512 and npm ci then fails EINTEGRITY, or worse a warm cache reinstalls the OLD bytes), re-stamps templates/VENDOR-STAMP.json, and re-verifies.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER RUNS IT NEXT: the script needs the js workspace installed first (pnpm install in js/), or it dies at "sh: tsup: command not found" on its very first step. That is not a defect in the tree.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: node scripts/check-vendor-freshness.mjs exits 0 on the branch, reporting both @barkpark/core and @barkpark/react fresh across both templates, where it exited 1 with 2 STALE-SOURCE failures on origin/main.

The freshness check is proven still able to FAIL on this branch, not merely observed passing: mutating one stamped source digest in templates/VENDOR-STAMP.json reds it with a message NAMING the package, and restoring returns it to exit 0.
Both templates' package-lock.json integrity pins are repinned in the same commit as the tarball swap, so npm ci cannot fail EINTEGRITY or silently reinstall the old bytes from a warm cache.
PR merged to main (LEAD closes this criterion on merge).

corpus.title: /v1/me serves a confirmed flag and the console never reads it

content.description:
`GET /v1/me` serves `confirmed: not is_nil(user.confirmed_at)` and the router's own comment states the purpose: "email-verification adds `confirmed` so the SPA can nudge an unverified account". Grep the console SPA for `.confirmed` / `confirmed:` and the count is ZERO. The SPA never reads it.

So this is not a lie the console tells a user — it is a claim the SERVER's own comment makes about a capability that was never built. It belongs to the same family as the rest of this epic (an assertion nothing supports) but sits one layer over: the comment asserts a consumer that does not exist.

TWO HONEST DISPOSITIONS, and the row should pick one with evidence rather than assume:
(a) BUILD the nudge — an unverified account gets a surface that says so, three-valued over `meState()` like everything else wave 39 shipped, so a failed read never asserts "verified" or "unverified".

corpus.title: The binding ratchet cannot see a CLEAN waiver transfer — close it with Sobelow's own detector-to-function map

content.description:
FOUND AND PINNED by felix-w24-s4-annotation-binding-ratchet, filed rather than left implicit.

TWO NAMED BLIND SPOTS remain in the new --binding ratchet, both stated in the script header and both pinned by a selftest case asserted GREEN on purpose (`bind_transfer_blind_spot`), so the day either reds the limit has been closed and the case is what says so.

(1) CLEAN TRANSFER. An annotation displaced onto another def in a DIFFERENT function — well-formed, correctly indented, squarely bound — is indistinguishable from a deliberate waiver using source text alone. All four predicates pass it. Only the waived TYPE tells you which def the waiver was written for, and that needs the detector-to-function map.

(2) IMPORTED CALLS. MULTI-CLAUSE keys on qualified `Module.function(` tokens, so `send_resp/3` (via `import Plug.Conn`) is not a token and `XSS.SendResp` waivers on multi-clause controller actions are not clause-checked. api/lib carries ~10 XSS.SendResp annotations, so this is the largest uncovered family.

THE FIX FOR BOTH IS THE SAME AND IT ALREADY EXISTS IN THE REPO: `api/scripts/sobelow-baseline-staleness-check.sh --derive` GENERATES a detector-to-anchor-token table from the Sobelow detector modules in api/deps/sobelow (Parse.get_fun_vars_and_meta literal atoms plus the @..._funs atom lists) and embeds it between markers, with `--verify-tokens` re-deriving and diffing. Share that table with the binding ratchet and both blind spots close: a waived type maps to the tokens it can flag, so the checker can ask 'does the def this annotation is bound to actually contain a call this type could flag?' — which is exactly the clean-transfer question — and MULTI-CLAUSE stops needing the qualified-token proxy.

DO NOT hand-write a list of risky bare function names. That is the key-list shape this epic exists to remove (D5); derive it or do not do it.

NOTE: the two scripts are separate files today and the derived table lives in only one of them. Extracting it is the real work; the predicates themselves are small once the map is available.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The derived detector-to-token table is shared between sobelow-baseline-staleness-check.sh and the binding ratchet rather than transcribed twice, and --verify-tokens still re-derives it from api/deps/sobelow and diffs

The clean-transfer blind spot is closed: the bind_transfer_blind_spot selftest fixture — an annotation bound to a def that its waived type cannot flag, beside a sibling function the type CAN flag — flips from asserted-GREEN to asserted-RED, and the assertion names the predicate
MULTI-CLAUSE no longer depends on the qualified-token proxy: an XSS.SendResp waiver on a multi-clause controller action is clause-checked, proven by a fixture using an imported send_resp/3

The full binding run over api/lib is still GREEN and still BEAM-free at the point of merge — a map-driven predicate that reds on main would recreate the blind-gate failure mode this epic exists to remove

corpus.title: The live runner's CLEANUP UNVERIFIED points at an artifact dir instead of quoting what bp said

content.description: DISCOVERED WHILE BUILDING pds-w31-runner-cleanup-failclosed, NOT TAKEN THERE (file fence). hz_read() redirects bp's stdout AND stderr into the artifact file (>"$out" 2>&1). When the read fails, the artifact holds bp's actual sentence (e.g. 'rate limited (429)') but nothing prints it: read_failure_reason() can only say 'see the artifact dir $ART'. A human reading a CLEANUP UNVERIFIED line in a terminal therefore has to go find a /tmp directory to learn WHY the project could not be read, and the artifact dir is never cleaned up, so /tmp accumulates one pds-live-w30.<pid> per run. FIX: have read_failure_reason (or its callers) quote the first ~200 bytes of the failing artifact inline, the way preflight already does with 'bp said: %s'. SMALL, and it makes an honest refusal legible instead of merely correct.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A failed fence/cleanup/final read prints the first bytes of what bp actually said inline, not just a path to the artifact dir - proven by a --selftest row whose stub emits a distinctive sentence that appears in the runner output.
The artifact dir story is decided one way or the other (cleaned on success, or documented as deliberate residue) rather than silently accumulating one directory per run in /tmp.

corpus.title: CI renders a breakpoint the sweep actually derived — today its only rendered width is off the sweep's own axis

content.description:
UNBLOCKED 2026-09-07 (lead-gates-3, verified; routed as AVAILABLE WORK). ITS GATING SENTENCE IS SPENT — DO NOT RE-BLOCK ON IT.

This row opens "AFTER cch-w21-s1-members-roster-identity-and-remove MERGES. Wiring this against today's bytes reds on arrival, which is why it is round 2 and not round 1." THAT CONDITION IS NOW SATISFIED: cch-w21-s1-members-roster-identity-and-remove reads lifecycle_status=done with 10 of 10 acceptance criteria met. Read that row yourself before starting -- do not take this line on faith, it is a measurement with a timestamp like any other.

WHY THIS NOTE EXISTS AT ALL. The gate lifted and NOTHING announced it. The ledger has no back-link from a gating row to the rows it gates, so a dependency that clears leaves its dependants sitting with a stale "AFTER X MERGES" sentence at the top, and every subsequent reader re-blocks on that sentence and moves on. That is the mirror image of the discharged-elsewhere class: a ghost advertises work that no longer exists, and this advertises a blocker that no longer exists. It is the more expensive of the two, because a ghost costs one triage read while a silently-unblocked row costs every hour until somebody re-checks the dependency by hand.

WHAT IS NOT ASSERTED HERE. I verified the DEPENDENCY, not the premise. The finding itself -- console-harness.yml:291 running the sweep with no --re... breakpoint, so the only rendered width is off the sweep's own axis (D245) -- has NOT been re-derived against today's origin/main by me, and the row's own warning that "wiring this against today's bytes reds on arrival" was written about a tree that has since moved. Re-verify the finding before building; the gate being open is not the same as the defect still being there.

--- ORIGINAL TEXT BELOW ---

AFTER cch-w21-s1-members-roster-identity-and-remove MERGES. Wiring this against today's bytes reds on arrival, which is why it is round 2 and not round 1.

THE FINDING (D245, measured): `console-harness.yml:291` runs the sweep with NO `--render` — it exits 0 in 0.126s having measured ZERO pixels. The only rendered sweep in CI is `:438 --render --widths 901 --cell billing-trial`, and `WIDTHS.includes(901)` is FALSE: the sweep's derived boundary axis is [619,620,621,719,720,721,739,740,741,767,768,769,829,830,831,898,899,900]. So ZERO of the eighteen boundary widths this epic derived from app.css's own @media rules is ever rendered in CI.

THE FULL LEG IS CORRECTLY DECLINED AND YOU MUST NOT WIRE IT. `console-harness.yml:266-268` argues it by name ("MINUTES, not seconds ... deliberately not a CI step"), and the measurement STRENGTHENS that: the full render is 936 cells at 1.23s/cell = 19 minutes. The middle path is a BOUNDED second render step — `--widths` takes a comma list (parsed at :1371, unvalidated against the axis so off-axis widths pass) and `--cell` takes a comma list WITH a per-name refusal (selectNames/selectCells, :499-507/:1377), so a handful of cells costs seconds.

corpus.title: A stale claim map makes `not_ready` blame an owner who left six days ago, hiding a permanent blocker behind a temporary-sounding one

content.description:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 by lead-ledger-c5 on the live server. Filed on main's ruling. `not_ready_arm/2` in tasks_controller.ex is this lane's fence.

THE PAIRED REFUSALS ARE THE WHOLE ARGUMENT. Same verb, same session, same `cancelled` lifecycle. ONE difference: whether the stale claim map names me or someone else.

 A. probe row task-64a240372c57ecc0 — cancelled, claim map names ME:
      "lifecycle_status is \"cancelled\"; only [\"open\", \"blocked\"] is claimable.
       Reopen it with `bp task stage <id> open` first."
    CORRECT: names the permanent blocker and the only thing that changes it.

 B. cch-w58-bl-charter-and-cli-carry-three-unsupportable-sentences-about-the-merge-gate
    — cancelled, claim map names lead-instruments:
      "held by lead-instruments — nobody else can claim it. If that worker id is YOURS,
       re-claim with it VERBATIM to renew the lease."
    WRONG on three counts, in ascending order of harm.

THE CLAIM IN (B) IS NOT LIVE. content.claim.ts_iso = 2026-09-01T23:17:09Z, which is 8,966 minutes — 6.2 DAYS — against a 45-minute lease, with claim.now null. The lease expired six days ago and the map is residue. A claim.worker OUTLIVES its lease: `bp task stage <id> open` moves a row and leaves the claim map behind, so the presence of a worker id proves nothing about who holds anything.

WHAT IS WRONG, ascending:
 1. IT IS NOT HELD. Nobody holds that row.
 2. IT HIDES THE REAL BLOCKER. The row is `cancelled`, which no amount of waiting or asking lead-instruments will change. The message describes a transient social obstacle where a permanent structural one exists.
 3. ITS REMEDY WOULD FAIL TOO. "re-claim with it VERBATIM to renew the lease" is refused on a cancelled row regardless of who runs it — only [open, blocked] is claimable. SAME SIGNATURE AS THE stale_claim CASE: a refusal that names the wrong cause AND prescribes a remedy that cannot work. That is now twice in one file family.

AND THIS ONE TEACHES A WRONG SOCIAL MOVE, WHICH THE OTHERS DO NOT. The other wrong-cause refusals measured tonight cost the operator a wasted action. THIS ONE SENDS A LANE TO ASK ANOTHER LANE FOR A ROW NOBODY HOLDS — two lanes' time, no outcome, and the asker looks like they did not check first. That is what separates it from a wording nit.

THE MECHANISM. `not_ready_arm/2` is a `cond` and `held_by_other` is its FIRST arm — ahead of the queue gate and ahead of `claimable_statuses`. So any claim map, live or six days dead, masks every blocker below it. The arm is right for a genuinely held row; it is wrong as a first question, because it asks WHO rather than WHETHER.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, recorded because the finding nearly did not happen: this lane had earlier recorded "a stale claim.worker outlives the lease — the presence of a worker id proves nothing" as a note for whoever came next, then hit exactly that case and READ THE MESSAGE AS OWNERSHIP. It only checked because main asked it to apply its own finding. THE NOTE WAS WRITTEN AND STILL NOT APPLIED BY ITS AUTHOR.

AND IT MANUFACTURED A FALSE TAXONOMY ENTRY. On the strength of message (B) this lane reported a new failure class — "a criterion can be unpayable because of WHO HOLDS the row." That class does not exist here: nobody holds it, and the real cause is the terminal lifecycle, which was already a known class. A MISLEADING REFUSAL DID NOT JUST COST AN ACTION; IT PRODUCED A WRONG CATEGORY that was reported upward and had to be retracted.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `not_ready_arm/2` asks WHETHER before WHO: a terminal row reports its lifecycle blocker even when a claim map is present. Evidence: the paired refusals reproduced — a cancelled row with a FOREIGN claim map must return the same lifecycle-naming refusal that a cancelled row with the caller's own map already returns. That pair is the test; one arm alone does not show the ordering is the variable.

A claim past its lease is reported as RESIDUE, not as a holder. `held_by_other` must compare `claim.ts_iso` against the lease window before naming anyone. The measured case is 8,966 minutes against a 45-minute lease. Evidence: a refusal on a row with an expired claim map that does not say "held by".

THE MESSAGE NAMES BOTH FACTS, not just the corrected one — e.g. "a stale claim map from <worker>, lease expired <when>; the row is <status> and not claimable". A caller needs the PERMANENT blocker, not merely a corrected diagnosis of the transient one. A fix that stops saying "held by" and leaves the caller without the lifecycle reason has moved the confusion rather than removed it.

THE REMEDY SENTENCE IS TESTED, not just written: run whatever the refusal tells the caller to do, and show it succeeds. "re-claim with it VERBATIM to renew the lease" was measured FAILING on a cancelled row regardless of who runs it. A refusal that names the wrong cause AND prescribes an impossible remedy is the same signature as the stale_claim case in this file family, so this criterion is the one that stops it recurring: every prescription in a refusal is a claim, and must be executed before it ships.

THE POPULATION IS ENUMERATED: every arm of `not_ready_arm/2`, and every other refusal in this file that names a holder or a lease, is checked for the same ordering fault — does it ask WHO before WHETHER, and does it consult liveness before naming a person? Report which arms were checked and which were clean. A fix to the one reported arm leaves the file's other arms unexamined, and this defect was found by accident rather than by a sweep.

corpus.title: A press on an in-flight row falls through to whatever sits underneath it

content.description: FOUND while proving spd-w19-press-answer-hook on deployed guerrilla 051112568, NOT taken this wave. The shipped in-flight guard is .phx-click-loading { pointer-events: none; opacity: .6 } (root.html.heex). pointer-events:none does not swallow the press — it makes the row TRANSPARENT TO HIT-TESTING, so a second mouse press during the in-flight window is delivered to whatever element sits underneath. Measured: pressing #item-paper twice back-to-back, the second press arrived with ev.target having NO [phx-click] ancestor (recorded on=(none) refAtClick=null) — harmless there, because nothing beneath that row is bound. THE RISK IS THE GENERAL CASE: wherever an in-flight control overlaps a DIFFERENT phx-click element (stacked rows, a header action over a row, an overlay), an impatient second press can fire the WRONG server event, and neither LiveView nor the new press-answer hook can see it, because the press never reaches the intended element at all. Decide: keep pointer-events:none and accept the fall-through, or replace it with a guard that blocks activation without removing the element from hit-testing (never phx-disable-with, which D225 bans). Evidence: the wave-19 press-answer proof runs — the discard branch had to be driven by KEYBOARD activation because the mouse path cannot reach it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The fall-through is reproduced on a real overlap: two phx-click elements where the in-flight one covers the other, with the wrong event named in the frame trace (matched on type:click, never counted).

A decision is recorded — keep pointer-events:none, or replace it with a guard that blocks activation without leaving the element out of hit-testing — and the chosen shape is proven on the deployed build.

corpus.title: ?count=true is a shaping param the query ETag does not fence, so a counted request 304s from a countless validator

content.description:
FOUND BY: lane http-edge-etag while getting PR #14042 to mergeable. Sibling of
task-496f010fa8f4d9dc (the schema-edit axis). #14042 fences three shaping params
— fields, expand, resolve — via QueryController's @shaping_params. These are
two more inputs of the SAME shape that it does not fence, both on the branch
that still emits a validator (anonymous + unshaped).

## Axis 1 — ?count=true is a shaping param that is not in @shaping_params

QueryController.maybe_put_total/7 adds result.total to the body:

    defp maybe_put_total(inner, conn, %{"count" => "true"}, type, dataset, perspective, filter_map) do
      total = Content.count_documents(...)
      Map.put(inner, :total, total)
    end

It does not touch `rendered`. list_etag/3 folds ONLY `rendered`:

    parts = Enum.map(rendered, fn d -> "#{d["_id"]}:#{d["_rev"] || ""}" end)

So for an anonymous caller:

  GET /v1/data/query/<ds>/<type>              -> 200, ETag E, body WITHOUT total
  GET /v1/data/query/<ds>/<type>?count=true   -> 200, ETag E, body WITH total
  replay E against ?count=true                -> 304, empty body

That is byte-for-byte the same defect #14042 proved live on prod for ?fields=,
with `count` substituted for `fields`. The remedy is one word: add "count" to
@shaping_params. Direction is identical to the merged fix — it withdraws a
validator, it never grants one.

## Axis 2 — every EMPTY page of a type shares one validator

When `rendered == []`, `parts == []` and the payload degenerates to
"<dataset>|<type>|" — a constant per (dataset, type). But the body still echoes
the request:

    %{perspective: ..., documents: [], count: 0, limit: limit, offset: offset, hasMore: has_more}

so `?offset=900&limit=10` and `?offset=500&limit=50` (both past the end) return
DIFFERENT bodies under the SAME ETag, and each will 304 against the other's
validator. Narrow, but it is the same class and it is free to close by folding
limit/offset into the payload.

## Axis 3 (lower severity) — no Vary: Accept, though Accept changes the response

#14042 correctly adds Vary: Authorization. But QueryController.maybe_vendor_content_type/1
switches the response Content-Type on a request-header-derived assign:

    if conn.assigns[:barkpark_vendor_accept] do
      put_resp_content_type(conn, "application/vnd.barkpark+json", "utf-8")

set by BarkparkWeb.Plugs.AcceptBarkparkVendor from the Accept request header. Two
requests to the same URL differing only in Accept get different Content-Type and
the same ETag, with no Vary: Accept to tell a shared cache to key on it. Body is
unchanged; this is a representation-metadata variance, not a body leak, which is
why it is filed third.

## Why this is not just tidiness

Axis 1 is a NAMED failure mode with a reproducible transcript shape, identical to
the one #14042 shipped a fix and a mutation proof for. Leaving it open means the
suite in api/test/barkpark_web/integration/http_conditional_policy_test.exs
documents a rule ("shaped reads carry no validator") that the code enforces for
three of at least four shaping params.

## Protective test that must fail BEFORE the fix

Extend http_conditional_policy_test.exs's generated shaping table with
{"?count=true", "?count=true"} for the list route, plus an explicit
"a ?count=true request is not answered 304 from a countless validator" pin
mirroring the existing "and a shaped request is NOT answered 304 from an
unshaped validator". Keep the fixture-honesty control: assert the two bodies
actually differ (one has result.total, one does not), so the pin cannot pass
vacuously.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Axis 1: `count` is a member of QueryController @shaping_params, so an anonymous GET /v1/data/query/<ds>/<type>?count=true carries no validator and cannot 304 against the plain page's ETag; test in http_conditional_policy_test.exs; mutation: dropping count from @shaping_params reds it.

Axis 2: two EMPTY pages of the same (dataset, type) whose bodies differ (page shape: limit/offset/perspective or whatever the envelope echoes) no longer share one ETag — list_etag/3 folds the page shape; test; mutation: reverting to the rendered-only validator reds it. The body's `etag` field (the SDK's ifMatch write token) is untouched.
Axis 3: Vary on the list response names every request input that can change the bytes without changing the validator (Authorization and Accept); test; mutation reds.
PR merged to main with the integration dir green (lead closes); docs/api-v1.md stays within its byte budget.

corpus.title: Reconcile the 436 pre-close-snapshot draft twins of sealed task rows — dry-run first, two guards, two by-hand rows (main's OPTION A ruling on pds-w33)

content.description:
FILED BY lead-cli-3r2 on main's ruling (DECISIONS-FROM-MAIN 2026-09-03 22:20Z, OPTION A with two guards) out of pds-w33-bl-wrong-row-mutate-forks-published-tasks criterion 2. This row is the ONLY place the production ledger write may happen; pds-w33 records the ruling and closes without touching a row.

THE POPULATION, MEASURED LIVE (cli3-w12, guerrilla, dataset production, 2026-09-03 21:52Z; full lists and the rerun command in the pds-w33 c1 evidence): 9052 type:task docs = 8057 published + 995 drafts.*. 585 published rows have a drafts.<id> twin; 438 of those diverge on lifecycle_status (done->open 356, cancelled->open 38, in_progress->open 26, done->cancelled 17, open->cancelled 1). 436 of the 438 drafts are PRE-CLOSE SNAPSHOTS: the draft's _updatedAt is newer on 437/438 but its CONTENT is older — fewer met acceptance criteria on 322, no close_reason on 362 while the published row carries the close, claim at an earlier epoch or null. They are accidental forks of the draft-prefixing writer (Content.Writer.upsert_document always writes drafts.<id>; every canonical reader is published-first), left behind after the close path wrote the published row directly; the GitHub bridge collapses a draft only on a sync, and a sealed row is never synced again.

MAIN'S RULING (verbatim intent): the 436 are accidental forks, not a designed snapshot; discard them via THIS row, dry-run first with the dry-run output attached here. GUARD 1: discard only a draft whose published twin is SEALED (lifecycle_status done or cancelled) AND whose draft rev predates the close (draft _updatedAt < published close timestamp / the close's rev); anything newer than the close is a live edit and is LISTED, never discarded. GUARD 2: the prod write (--yes) happens only from this row, by the lead, after the dry-run count matches the census (436 plus or minus the rows closed since 21:52Z). Re-measure immediately before acting — 32 of the 438 forks were under 1 h old and heal on the bridge's next sync.

THE TWO BY-HAND ROWS (never in the bulk discard): (1) task-2b7cbaf8265f6b4e — published is done (claim epoch 77) with ZERO acceptance criteria while its draft holds 7 (6 met) and no close_reason; discarding the draft destroys the only copy of that criteria block — merge the criteria block into the published row by doc patch + publish, then discard. (2) cch-w37-bl-primary-team-gate-twins-are-one-gate — the published row is still OPEN (0/3) and the draft holds a cancel with a close_reason that never published; read the close_reason, and if it is a legitimate cancel publish it (that lands the cancel), otherwise discard it and say why.

WHY THIS IS NOT pds-w33's PR: #15851 makes the mutate envelope WARN on a fork (patch.forked_published / patch.stale_draft_base); it changes no data. Reconciling 436 rows is a mass write on the live ledger and needs the dry-run receipt on the record before anyone types --yes.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: DRY RUN FIRST: a script (committed under scripts/ or tooling/, read-only mode by default) re-measures the twin population on guerrilla and prints, per diverging id: published lifecycle_status + close timestamp/rev, draft rev + _updatedAt, met-criteria counts both sides, and the verdict DISCARD / LIST (newer-than-close) / BY-HAND. Its full output is attached to this row (evidence quotes the counts and the path to the attached file) BEFORE any write.

GUARD 1 IS IN THE CODE, NOT THE PROSE: the script discards only a draft whose published twin is sealed (done or cancelled) AND whose draft rev predates the close; a draft newer than the close is LISTED, never discarded. Proved by a test or a fixture run: one synthetic pair with a post-close draft is listed and NOT discarded, one pre-close pair is discarded.

GUARD 2: the write mode requires an explicit --yes AND the dry-run count within the tolerance main set (436 plus or minus rows closed since 2026-09-03 21:52Z); a count outside the tolerance REFUSES with the two numbers printed. The lead runs the write from this row; the run transcript (count, refusals, ids discarded) is attached as evidence.

THE TWO BY-HAND ROWS ARE HANDLED INDIVIDUALLY AND NAMED: task-2b7cbaf8265f6b4e (merge the draft's 7-criteria block into the published row, then discard) and cch-w37-bl-primary-team-gate-twins-are-one-gate (publish the draft's cancel if legitimate, else discard with the reason). Evidence shows the before/after read of each published row.

POST-SWEEP READ-BACK: the rerun command from pds-w33 c1 is run again after the write; the diverging count is quoted (expected: the LISTED rows only) and the published rows of three sampled discarded ids still serve their sealed status and their close_reason unchanged.

corpus.title: CI diet: the path-escape ratchet's SELFTEST is 114s of its 2m35s, and it runs on every PR

content.description:
Measured 2026-09-02: across 60 elixir.yml runs, 813 job-minutes, only 278 of them Test. The `path-escape` job ("Elixir path-escape ratchet") is the second-largest consumer at 171 min and it is the only one that runs on EVERY run, never skipped, including doc-only PRs where Test itself is skipped.

Step-level timings from four successful path-escape jobs on main show the cost is NOT the check:

  step 3  Harness (the ratchet must be able to fail)   114 s
  step 4  Every repo-root read is dispatched on         15-17 s
  steps 5-7  skip-disclosure + merge-authority           12 s total

The path lint takes 16 seconds. The 1980-line selftest harness that proves the lint CAN fail takes 114 seconds, and it runs on every pull request. That is ~84 job-minutes per 60 runs, about 10% of all elixir CI minutes, spent re-proving a property that changes only when the script itself changes.

The fix is placement, not deletion: condition ONLY the harness step on whether the diff touches scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh, scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.test.sh or .github/workflows/elixir.yml, plus always on push to main. The check keeps running unfiltered on every PR, the job keeps no job-level `if:` and no `continue-on-error:`, it stays in the Elixir gate aggregator's `needs`, and it gains no `needs: changes` (charter D26 forbids the dispatcher dependency). The condition must fail toward RUNNING: a skip only on a positive determination that none of the four paths changed.

In-tree precedent: scripts/required-checks.test.sh section 9 records that required-checks-drift.yml stopped running `--selftest` as a step of its own once another harness became its home.

This row exists because there was no correct row for CI-cost work. The builder searched `bp task ready --limit 1000` for path-escape / CI diet / selftest / job-minute / ci time and found only rows about WIDENING path-escape fixtures. PR #15572 was opened against task-9a08c27d897f38e6, which is the Format-pin DECISION row and does not describe this work; the trailer is being retargeted here.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: In .github/workflows/elixir.yml the path-escape job still carries NO job-level if:, NO continue-on-error:, and NO needs: — the condition lives on the harness step alone, and the check step Every repo-root read is dispatched on runs unconditionally on every pull request.

The harness step runs when the diff touches scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh, scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.test.sh or .github/workflows/elixir.yml, and on push to main; and it FAILS TOWARD RUNNING — an unresolvable base ref, a git error or empty diff output all run the harness rather than skipping it. Both directions observed, not asserted.

The sibling ratchets that read this YAML shape stay green: merge-authority-claim-check.test.sh (its B9 step-id assertion), gate-announces-skips.test.sh, cloud-path-escape-check.test.sh, console-path-escape-check.test.sh, and required-checks-verify.sh --selftest.

A before/after job-minute measurement on the same shape of PR: a doc-only PR where the harness is skipped shows the path-escape job dropping from roughly 2m35s to under 45s, measured from real step timestamps, not estimated.

corpus.title: DELETE /v1/auth/logout discards the revoke count and returns ok:true unconditionally - the PDS-D523 widening reached the source and one of two callers

content.description:
FILED BY silent-w12, triaging pds-bl-flash-redirect-success-class. That row's CODE half is now half-landed on origin/main: PDS-D523 widened the source and ONE of the two callers. This is the caller it missed.

WHO IS MISLED: every API client of DELETE /v1/auth/logout - the JS SDK, the bp CLI, an SSO front channel. WHAT THEY WRONGLY CONCLUDE: that the server session they asked to revoke is revoked.

WHAT LANDED. api/lib/barkpark/accounts.ex now returns the count:

  @spec revoke_user_session_token(binary()) :: {:ok, non_neg_integer()}
  def revoke_user_session_token(plaintext) when is_binary(plaintext) do
    ...
    {revoked, _} = from(t in UserSession, where: t.token_hash == ^hash and is_nil(t.revoked_at)) |> Repo.update_all(set: [revoked_at: now])
    {:ok, revoked}
  end

and session_controller.ex delete/2 (the Studio sign-out) READS it:

  {:ok, n} = Barkpark.Accounts.revoke_user_session_token(token)
  ... |> put_flash(:info, sign_out_flash(revoked)) ...
  defp sign_out_flash(0), do: "You were already signed out."
  defp sign_out_flash(_revoked), do: "Signed out."

WHAT DID NOT. api/lib/barkpark_web/controllers/auth_controller.ex, inside logout/2:

  token ->
    slo = saml_slo_url(token)
    audit_logout(token)
    Accounts.revoke_user_session_token(token)      # <- return DISCARDED
    slo
  end

  body = if slo_url, do: %{ok: true, slo_url: slo_url}, else: %{ok: true}
  conn |> clear_session() |> json(body)

The count is in hand at that call site and thrown away, and the very next statement emits an UNCONDITIONAL ok: true. Zero rows revoked - token already revoked, hash mismatch, a where clause that stopped selecting - reads to the client byte-identically to a successful revoke. The cookie is cleared either way, so this is never surfaced as an error; it is simply unfalsifiable from outside.

WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN THE STUDIO ONE it sits beside: the Studio path answers a human who can retry. This answers a PROGRAM, and it is the API contract's own success key.

SMALLEST CHANGE THAT MAKES THE FAILURE LOUD: bind the count and put it in the body - `{:ok, n} = Accounts.revoke_user_session_token(token)` and `%{ok: true, revoked: n}`. One line plus a key. It does not have to become an error (0 is idempotent, not a fault); it has to become READABLE, exactly as sign_out_flash/1 made the Studio path readable.

REPRODUCTION (no build): git show origin/main:api/lib/barkpark_web/controllers/auth_controller.ex | grep -n "revoke_user_session_token" -B 6 -A 8 - the discard and the literal %{ok: true} are within eight lines of each other. Compare against git show origin/main:api/lib/barkpark_web/controllers/session_controller.ex | grep -n "sign_out_flash" -B 14.

SCOPE NOTE, so this row is not over-read: this is the CODE half only. The LENS half of pds-bl-flash-redirect-success-class - teaching scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs to declare and count the flash+302 class - is STILL UNBUILT and stays on that row. report_blind_spots/1 on origin/main declares exactly three classes (json(conn,...), put_status(2xx), send_resp(conn,2xx)) plus the ecto.migrations note, and a grep for redirect or put_flash across that script returns zero.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: auth_controller.ex logout/2 binds the {:ok, n} from Accounts.revoke_user_session_token/1 and the JSON body carries the count (or an equivalent readable basis); the return is no longer discarded. Evidence quotes the diff.

A differential test proves the response DIFFERS between a live-session logout and a second logout of the same already-revoked token - it must not be possible for the two to be byte-identical. Evidence quotes the test and both bodies.
Idempotence is preserved: zero rows revoked is still a 200 with ok:true, never an error, and the SAML slo_url branch is unchanged. Evidence quotes the assertions.

The scope line holds: this row changes CODE only. The census lens work (declaring and counting the flash+302 class in scripts/pds-elixir-receipt-census.exs) is explicitly left on pds-bl-flash-redirect-success-class and is not claimed here.

corpus.title: Click-oracle round 2: the six constant-toast destructive DELETEs get wire coverage

content.description:
Follow-on to cch-w2-revoke-click-oracle, which made the smoke.mjs DOM shim click-capable and covered 2 of the 8 unfixtured destructive DELETEs. The remaining SIX are: /v1/auth/logout (app.js:1027), /v1/github/installation (:2295), /v1/barkparks/:id (:5430 and :5474), the webhook DELETE (:7381), /v1/sites/:id/github (:9991).

WHY THEY WERE LEFT OUT, honestly: unlike /v1/account/sessions, none of them interpolates a server value into its toast — they announce client-side CONSTANTS ('Instance removed', 'Webhook deleted'). So a generic 200 produces a message that is both indistinguishable from the real one and, in fact, honest. Their defect is NOT 'prod says 0'; it is 'nothing here would catch a regression'. That makes them a WIRE-assertion job (button wired for click + correct method and URL shape + a stateful list that actually shrinks where a list exists), never a text-assertion job. Do not fake a text observable to make them look like the sessions case.

Now unblocked: the shim can drive clicks, and route() takes an optional per-boot state bag (scenarios.mjs sessionsOf is the pattern to copy for a stateful fixture).

MIND THE SHIM'S DOCUMENTED BOUNDARY (smoke.mjs header): PARSED_TAGS is button|a ON PURPOSE. Widening it to containers hands app.js paths shaped like 'panel.querySelector(".fleet-body") || panel' (app.js:14321) a detached stub and reds six pre-existing scenarios. Covering a container-shaped control means building a real tree first — a separate, larger piece of work. And every new click check MUST assert a positive dispatch count, because an unparsable selector answers an empty list and a loop over nothing 'succeeds'.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Each of the six DELETEs is driven by a REAL click in a smoke scenario and asserted on the WIRE: the button dispatches >0 click handlers, and exactly one request with the right method and URL shape is logged. No text assertion is invented for a client-side constant toast.

Every new leg is proven able to fail by mutation, recorded with the mutation and its output — at minimum a click->mousedown dead-button mutation per control, which __app.test.mjs must be shown to miss.

Any leg whose success arm only refetches a list carries a STATEFUL fixture (the scenarios.mjs sessionsOf pattern), or is honestly reported as wire-only. A leg that stays green when its fixture is disabled is NOT shipped as covered.
PARSED_TAGS is not widened to container tags, or if it is, a real child/parent tree is built and all pre-existing scenarios stay green (the six #instance-tabpanel scenarios are the canary).
Gate green: node cloud/priv/static/__preview__/smoke.mjs && node cloud/priv/static/__app.test.mjs && node --check cloud/priv/static/app.js.

corpus.title: A team MEMBER can bind a site's GitHub auto-deploy and choose its webhook secret — only an ADMIN can unbind it

content.description:
A plain team MEMBER can create a GitHub binding on a team site that only an
ADMIN can remove. That asymmetry is incoherent regardless of which tier is
correct, and it is the headline: a permission model where the weaker principal
can create state the stronger one must clean up is broken on its own terms,
without needing to win the policy argument below.

## THE THREE DOORS, AND WHICH ONE IS OPEN

  cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/router.ex:8477  POST   /v1/sites/:id/github
      with_team_site(conn, fn conn, site -> ...)   <- :session default
      = Auth.require_user/2. Authenticated + team-scoped, NO ROLE CHECK.

  cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/router.ex:8550  POST   /v1/sites/:id/github/connect
      conn = Auth.require_team_admin(conn, [])

  cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/router.ex:8580  DELETE /v1/sites/:id/github
      conn = Auth.require_team_admin(conn, [])

The admin tier on `connect` is not incidental — the route's own comment states
the rule it is enforcing: "RBAC: registering a webhook is a capability action ->
team admin only (parity with the installation connect)". It is pinned by
cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/web/router_github_connect_test.exs:201, the test named
"member (not admin) -> 403".

`with_team_site/3` defaults to `:session`, which resolves to `Auth.require_user/2`
(cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/auth.ex). That plug assigns `:current_user` and
`:current_team` and checks NO role, so every member of the owning team passes.

## THE EXPLOIT PATH, IN THREE STEPS

1. POINT THE SITE AT A REPO THE MEMBER CONTROLS. `POST /v1/sites/:id/github`
   with `{"repo": "attacker/whatever", "branch": "main"}` writes `github_repo`
   and `github_branch` onto the team's site row. That is the site's build
   source: the same field `connect` writes at admin tier.

2. CHOOSE THE WEBHOOK SECRET, MINTING AN UNAUTHENTICATED DEPLOY TRIGGER.
   `webhook_secret` is CALLER-SUPPLIABLE on this route and is echoed back in the
   200 body. The member therefore knows the HMAC key for
   `POST /v1/webhooks/github/:site_id` (router.ex:8635) — a route with NO bearer
   auth by design, where the HMAC and the opaque site UUID are the only gates.
   They can now forge signed push deliveries at will and mint Deployments
   pinned to any `git_ref` they name.

3. THE BINDING SURVIVES THE MEMBER. Clearing it requires
   `DELETE /v1/sites/:id/github`, which is admin-gated. Step 1 also OVERWRITES
   an admin-established link and rotates its secret, so a member can silently
   break an integration an admin configured and cannot themselves undo it.

## BOTH READINGS, STATED HONESTLY

THE TIER MAY BE DELIBERATE. The router moduledoc's route table declares this
row `user`:

    POST /v1/sites/:id/github  user  link a GitHub repo + branch + webhook secret (manual)

and `cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/web/router_moduledoc_table_test.exs` re-derives
BOTH the table and the enforced tier from source and fails on any disagreement.
So `user` here is a recorded decision, not a forgotten fence. There is also a
coherent reason for the split: `connect` performs an OUTBOUND authenticated call
that spends the team's GitHub App installation credential (validates the repo
against the installation, registers the hook on GitHub); the manual route calls
GitHub not at all — the human pastes the secret themselves.

THE OUTCOME IS IDENTICAL THROUGH BOTH DOORS. That reason explains why `connect`
is admin-only; it does not explain why the manual route is member-open. What the
admin gate visibly protects — the team's production site building and serving
code the caller chose — is reached either way. The credential-spend argument
bounds what `connect` may do, not what the member may achieve.

## WHAT A FIX MUST CHANGE (two files, both of them, or neither)

  1. cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/router.ex:8477 — the gate itself.
  2. cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/router.ex route table (~line 199) — the
     declared tier for this row, plus whatever
     cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/web/router_moduledoc_table_test.exs requires to
     agree. Changing the gate WITHOUT the table reds that test; changing the
     table without the gate reds it too. It is deliberately a both-or-neither
     edit — that is what makes the current `user` tier a recorded decision.

NO TRIPWIRE TEST. A tripwire pins a boundary we are choosing not to cross; here
we are proposing to cross it, so pinning today's behaviour would make the fix
harder and read as endorsement of the tier.

## FALSIFIER

This row's premise is that the table still declares the route `user`. It is
falsified the moment that stops being true:

    grep -n 'POST    /v1/sites/:id/github  ' cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/router.ex

If that line no longer reads `user`, the tier has already been changed and this
row is stale — re-verify against the gate at router.ex:8477 before acting.

A second, independent falsifier for the behaviour itself: if
`with_team_site(conn, fn conn, site -> ...)` at router.ex:8477 has grown a role
check (or moved off the `:session` default), the hole is closed regardless of
what the table says.

## SCOPE / PROVENANCE

Found during the cloud/ control-plane defect sweep that produced PR #14368.
Adjudicated by the lead: FILE, DO NOT RE-TIER — the tier is machine-pinned as
deliberate and changing it silently overrides a recorded decision. On the owner
list for a policy call.

corpus.title: Eighteen curated validation messages break grammar once the per-field error reaches the user

content.description:
FILED BY WAVE 37 (charter D415). A copy debt that cch-w37-s1 EXPOSES rather than creates, and deliberately does not hold the client fix.

friendly() renders `field.replace(/_/g," ") + " " + msg`, which assumes `msg` is a PREDICATE. Ecto's messageless defaults ARE predicates and compose perfectly: "scope is invalid", "type is invalid", "name can't be blank", "team id does not exist", "slug should be at most 63 character(s)".

It is the CURATED messages that break, because half of them are full sentences rather than predicates. Of the 36 custom `message:`/`add_error` literals in cloud/lib, 18 compose and 18 grammar-break:
    key a team-scoped var with this key already exists
    slug a site with this slug already exists in this team
    user id user is already a member of this team
    credential a Cloudflare API token can't be blank
    event routes unknown channel: "pigeon"

These are UGLY, NOT WRONG — each still names the real cause, where the current string ("That didn't work — check your input.") names nothing. That is why wave 37 ruled them BETTER-but-clumsy and shipped slice 1 unnarrowed. The remedy is a server-side copy edit: rewrite each breaking literal as a predicate that composes after the humanized field name.

NOTE THE CLASSIFIER'S LIMIT: the 18/18 split came from a regex (/^(is|must|should|can't|has|does|had)\b/) applied to 36 literals that were all read by hand. Do not reuse the count as an oracle on a message set nobody rendered.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every curated message literal in cloud/lib is RENDERED through friendly()'s concatenation and classified by reading the resulting string, not by regex alone.
Each breaking literal is rewritten as a predicate that composes after the humanized field name; evidence quotes the before/after rendered strings.
The Cloud gate is green and no changeset behaviour changes — only message text.

corpus.title: The beat learns the two things the box already measures and throws away: the kernel's 15-minute load average, and its own 5xx rate

content.description:
TWO FIELDS, ONE THEME: the box already measures both of these and THROWS THEM AWAY. Neither needs a new probe, a new route, or a new syscall.

(1) `load15`. `cmd/barkpark-agent/main.go:317-332 loadProcProbe` does `os.ReadFile("/proc/loadavg")` then `strings.Fields`, then uses `fields[0]` ONLY -- `fields[1]` (load5) and `fields[2]` (load15) are already in memory and discarded. WHY THIS MATTERS (charter D67): `/v1/barkparks` serves exactly ONE beat -- `Registry.latest_health_payload_map/1` is a `DISTINCT ON (barkpark_id) ORDER BY inserted_at DESC` and `merge_pressure/2` folds that single row -- so the charter's original "2 of the last 3 beats" sustain is NOT COMPUTABLE by any consumer of the payload both surfaces read. load15 IS a sustained measurement, computed by the kernel as a 15-minute EWMA, delivered as ONE scalar. Live proof, 3 samples 60s apart over 4 SSH-reachable boxes: at 15:01:02Z guerrilla read load1 0.64x per core -- DARK on any single-beat fence -- while its load15 was 1.89x, 5.9x the busiest healthy box (jarl 0.32x/core). load5 is NOT sufficient (guerrilla read 1.50x in the same sample).

(2) `err_5xx_per_s`. `BarkparkWeb.RequestStats` is ALREADY a live 60s ETS ring, served at `GET /v1/instance/request-stats` (api router.ex:1616) and ALREADY polled every beat by `internal/agent/report.go` into `req_per_s` + `p95_ms`. Its handler is `handle_event([:phoenix,:endpoint,:stop], %{duration: duration}, _meta, %{table: table})` -- Phoenix hands it the conn (and therefore `conn.status`) as `_meta` and it DISCARDS it, inserting `{key, duration_ms}` with no status. WHY THIS MATTERS (charter D75): over 8 hours guerrilla served 6,472 distinct 500s, of which 6,472 -- 100.0% -- also emit `DBConnection.ConnectionError`; there are ZERO non-DB 500s. That is ~0.22 5xx/s sustained on a box `bp cloud status` calls healthy, and NOTHING today can say it. Repo-wide there is genuinely zero functional 5xx/error-rate symbol in Go or Elixir.

SCOPE, EXACTLY:
* `cmd/barkpark-agent/main.go` -- widen loadProcProbe (or add a sibling) to return load15; keep load1.
* `internal/agent/report.go` -- one `Load15 float64 \`json:"load15"\`` beside `Load1` at :82 using the SAME -1 sentinel convention, and one `Err5xxPerS float64 \`json:"err_5xx_per_s"\`` beside `ReqPerS` at :121, polled off the same request-stats envelope.
* `api/lib/barkpark_web/request_stats.ex` -- the ETS row becomes `{key, duration_ms, status}` and `compute/4` derives `err_5xx_per_s`. HONEST-METER LAW (D48, and this module already obeys it for p95): an EMPTY window is `nil`, NOT `0` -- a fabricated floor is a lie. Say so in the moduledoc, which already argues exactly this for p95_ms.
* the request-stats route/controller -- serve the new key.
* `cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/router.ex` -- ONLY the pressure region: one `load15:` and one `err_5xx_per_s:` key in `merge_pressure/2` (:8744-8770, the same one-line shape `cpu_cores` shipped through in #9826) and one `nil` each in `@unmetered_pressure` (:468-486).

FENCE: `dr-w5-s3` owns `router.ex`'s AGENT-ROUTE region (:1270-1350) plus `registry.ex`, `metrics.ex` and `telemetry.ex` this same round -- your router.ex hunks are ~7,400 lines away from its. Do NOT touch metrics.ex/telemetry.ex; the pressure block is what `bp cloud status` reads and that is this wave's surface. `dr-w5-s5` (round 2) owns `SpaceReport` in the SAME two agent files -- stay inside `HealthReport` and `loadProcProbe`.

THRESHOLD RE-DERIVATION IS PART OF THIS SLICE. The charter's 1.75x per core was fitted on a RECONSTRUCTED load15 series (an EWMA of the load1 series, alpha=exp(-60/900)); only 12 SSH spot readings are real load15. Once the field reports, re-derive the sweep on REAL `fields[2]` and either confirm 1.75x or say what it should be. The reconstruction OVERSTATES healthy load15 (jarl sims 0.99x against a live 0.32x), so the real margin should be wider, not narrower.

No required context asserts on the Go/agent half of this diff -- Cloud/Console/Elixir gates all report success by skipping. The blocking evidence for those files is a live beat read off the control plane, not a green PR.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `loadProcProbe` returns the 15-minute average from `/proc/loadavg` field index 2, and a unit test pins the parse against a REAL captured `/proc/loadavg` line (not a synthesized one) including the malformed/short-line failure path. Evidence: the test output plus the captured line.

`internal/agent/report.go` carries `Load15` beside `Load1` using the SAME -1 unmeasured sentinel, and `Err5xxPerS` beside `ReqPerS`; the existing report tests still pin that a missing probe yields the sentinel and never 0. Evidence: `CC=clang go test ./internal/agent/...` output.

`BarkparkWeb.RequestStats` keeps the response status on every sample and derives `err_5xx_per_s` over the same rolling window; an EMPTY window yields `nil`, never `0` (D48 honest-meters law, the same rule this module already applies to p95_ms). A test asserts the empty-window nil AND a mixed 2xx/5xx window's rate. Evidence: the passing test output.
The `/v1/instance/request-stats` route serves the new key and the agent polls it into the beat; a test covers the route shape. Evidence: the rendered JSON body with the key present.

`merge_pressure/2` folds `load15` and `err_5xx_per_s` through `measured_or_nil` (so the -1 sentinel and a missing key BOTH become nil, never 0), and `@unmetered_pressure` gains a `nil` for each so the block keeps its fixed shape on every write path. Evidence: the cloud test output plus the two quoted diffs.

THRESHOLD RE-DERIVED ON REAL DATA: once the field reports, a fresh window of REAL load15 per-core values is swept and the 1.75x fence is either confirmed FP-free against the healthy population or a corrected number is proposed with its firing/false-positive counts. Evidence: the sweep table with n per box and the window's start/end timestamps.

LIVE BEAT PROOF: a REAL beat persisted on the control plane for guerrilla carries a non-nil `load15` and a non-nil `err_5xx_per_s`, read back off `/v1/barkparks`, with the raw pressure block pasted. This is the blocking evidence for the agent half -- a merge is not evidence. corpus.title: SECURITY: item share link reads every paper in the workspace via LiveView re-mount

content.description:
EXPLOITABLE. An item share link bound to ONE paper reads EVERY paper in that workspace/project, including papers with no share configured at all.

REACHABILITY: unauthenticated holder of a leaked /s/<token> item link (kind=doc, ref_type=paper). No account, no membership, no other credential.

CHAIN (each step verified by direct read):
1. api/lib/barkpark_web/controllers/share_link_controller.ex:198-209 — /s/<tokenA> 302s to /w/<ws>/p/<proj>/papers/A?share=<tokenA>.
2. api/lib/barkpark_web/plugs/require_share_scope.ex:169-205 — maybe_grant_item_token/4 validates link.ref_id == path_params["slug"], then assigns share_public: true.
3. api/lib/barkpark_web/plugs/resolve_workspace.ex:68 — def call(%{assigns: %{share_public: true}} = conn, _opts), do: conn — the membership gate is skipped entirely.
4. api/lib/barkpark_web/router.ex:2438-2443 — live_session :scoped_paper_reader carries exactly ONE on_mount: {BarkparkWeb.PluginScopeSession, :scope}.
5. api/lib/barkpark_web/plugin_scope_session.ex:73-74 — that hook's own moduledoc says "Never halts — UI auth is the sibling BarkparkWeb.LiveAuth admin/ops on_mount hook". No LiveAuth hook is mounted on this live_session, and there is no global on_mount (api/lib/barkpark_web.ex:33-38).
6. api/lib/barkpark_web/plugin_scope_session.ex:51-55 — build/1 bakes scoped_workspace_id / scoped_project_id into the SIGNED LiveView session at dead render.
7. api/lib/barkpark_web/live/bulldocs_live.ex:64 — mount(%{"slug" => slug}) takes the slug from the CURRENT url; reader_scope(socket) (bulldocs_live.ex:1162) reads the session-carried workspace/project; fetch_paper/3 (bulldocs_live.ex:1178) calls Content.get_paper(slug, "production", scope). The item link is NEVER consulted again.

BulldocsLive defines no handle_params, so navigating to a sibling slug forces a full re-mount over the existing socket. The router pipeline — and therefore RequireShareScope — does not run on a WebSocket join. The attacker holds the signed LV session token from the page source and can join with any URL that matches this live_session.

The plain HTTP request GET /w/<ws>/p/<proj>/papers/B?share=<tokenA> is correctly DENIED. The socket is the only door, which is why the HTTP-level tests do not catch this.

PRIOR ART IN-TREE: the sibling LiveView already fixed this exact class. api/lib/barkpark_web/live_scope.ex:60-93 (arpss-lv-dataset-switch-reauth) re-derives the access grade on every scope-changing patch for :scoped_studio. The :scoped_paper_reader live_session never received the equivalent. The router comment at router.ex:2435 ("safe here because the reader never live-navigates across scopes") is the load-bearing assumption, and it reasons about SCOPES; an item link's contract is per-DOCUMENT, which that argument does not cover.

PROPOSED FIX: add an authorizing on_mount to live_session :scoped_paper_reader that re-runs the item-link / section-share decision against the mount params' slug, following the shape of LiveScope.reauthorize/3 at live_scope.ex:75-93. This requires threading the raw ?share= token into the LV session via PluginScopeSession.build/1 so it can be re-resolved on every mount — which also closes the sibling revocation gap (revoking a link today does not tear down an already-open reader socket).

SCOPE NOTE: a SECTION share (Sharing.shared?/4) legitimately grants the whole scope, so this affects the ITEM-link arm only. Do not narrow the section-share path while fixing this — that would break legitimate section-shared readers.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A regression test mounts BulldocsLive over a signed share session built for paper A and then requests paper B's slug; the mount is refused (halt or redirect), and the test FAILS on today's code. Test file path and the exact `mix test` command are recorded in the evidence.

The refusal is enforced by an on_mount hook on live_session :scoped_paper_reader (api/lib/barkpark_web/router.ex:2438-2443), NOT by a check inside BulldocsLive.mount/3 alone — so any LiveView later added to that live_session inherits it. The router diff showing the added on_mount is pasted.

The bound resource is read from the SIGNED LiveView session (built at api/lib/barkpark_web/plugin_scope_session.ex:51-55), not from mount params, so a re-mount cannot re-choose the slug. A test that mounts with a params slug different from the session slug asserts the session value wins.
Mutation proof: remove the new on_mount (or the session-bound slug check), confirm the regression test REDS naming the cross-paper read, restore, confirm green. Both run outputs pasted.

The sibling share kinds are exercised too: an item link of kind "doc" and a section share each get a test, and the evidence states explicitly which kinds are now confined and which are out of scope for this row, with the reason.

corpus.title: pds-record-parity.sh counts benign/genuine duplicates and never branches on them — the printed '18 genuine + 2 benign' is a literal, not a measurement

content.description:
GUARD-CANNOT-FAIL audit (git-only, read-only, 2026-08-23). scripts/pds-record-parity.sh's uniqueness leg classifies every duplicated PDS-D number against two baseline suppression lists.

THE DEFECT — a predicate computed and then never branched on. At :463 the loop declares `local num count lines n unexpected=0 benign=0 genuine=0`; :467 does `benign=$((benign + 1))` and :470 does `genuine=$((genuine + 1))`. Neither variable is READ anywhere in the file - git grep 'benign' and git grep 'genuine' over the script return only those assignments, the unrelated n_amb_benign counter (:523-533) and prose. The ruling is made on `unexpected` and `vanished` alone.

WHAT THAT COSTS. :455 prints 'baseline: PINNED for <charter> - 18 genuine + 2 benign, BY NUMBER.' as a hardcoded literal, standing beside two freshly computed counters that are thrown away. Nothing asserts the printed sentence still describes the lists. MEASURED on origin/main it happens to be true today: DUP_BASELINE_GENUINE (:251) holds 18 numbers and DUP_BASELINE_BENIGN (:254) holds 2 - so this is a latent drift, not a live lie. Add one number to either list and the script keeps printing 18/2 while counting 19/2, which is the 'printed a measured defect when nothing was measured' shape.

WHY THE EXISTING MIRROR ARM DOES NOT COVER IT. The STALE-BASELINE arm (:481-489) catches a baselined number that has VANISHED from the duplicate set. It does not catch a baseline that GREW, and it does not compare the counted classes to the sentence printed above them.

REFUSAL PATH: derive the printed numbers from the lists (word-count DUP_BASELINE_GENUINE / DUP_BASELINE_BENIGN) instead of typing them, and branch on the counters that are already being computed - if `genuine` + `benign` does not equal the number of baselined entries that actually fired, say so and fail, because that means a baselined number was classified by a different arm than the baseline claims. This is a small, self-contained change.

corpus.title: seal-run.sh advertises a --predicate flag that can never work and has zero test coverage

content.description:
scripts/seal-run.sh advertises `--predicate <path>` in its own usage block. It cannot work, and it cannot be made to work by the caller.

Refusal 4 does not compare the file you passed. It compares against a HARDCODED constant: PRED_REL="cloud/priv/static/__preview__/seal-predicate.mjs" (:63), used to compute WANT_BLOB from origin/main and compared against HAVE_BLOB = hash-object of $PREDICATE. $PREDICATE is the flag's value; PRED_REL is not. So any --predicate other than a byte-identical copy of origin/main's seal-predicate.mjs is a guaranteed exit 4 PRE-RUN - the program is never executed. Verified by run: rc=4, and the refusal text names the WRONG file in its remedy (it tells you to `git checkout origin/main -- cloud/priv/static/__preview__/seal-predicate.mjs`, which has nothing to do with the path you passed). That is a misleading remedy, not merely a refusal.

Three further independent binds, any one fatal: the interpreter is hardcoded (CMD=(node "$PREDICATE" --repo "$REPO")); an unsolicited --repo is injected that a non-node predicate would reject; and the token parser is the literal grep ^VERDICT-TOKEN: SEAL-PREDICATE, so any other program would have to impersonate a seal predicate to be parsed at all.

AND THE FLAG HAS ZERO TEST COVERAGE. scripts/seal-run.test.sh is 73 green mutation proofs and NOT ONE exercises --predicate: every fixture installs its stand-in by `cp "$FAKE" "$d/cloud/priv/static/__preview__/seal-predicate.mjs"`, i.e. it fakes the CANONICAL PATH. The one code path a re-point would use is unproven.

TWO HONEST OPTIONS: delete the flag (it is dead surface that reads as an escape hatch and cost a verifier real time this wave), or make it work - derive PRED_REL from the flag relative to $REPO, parameterise the interpreter and the token prefix. The second destabilises a 73-proof harness that is the only thing standing between this epic and wave 28's false verdict, so DELETION IS PREFERRED unless a second caller actually materialises.

RELATED AND ALREADY FIXED, so close it rather than planning around it: the open task dr-seal-run-harness-runs-in-no-ci is STALE - .github/workflows/shell-harnesses.yml:308-338 has a seal-run-guard job that runs the harness, with path filters at :97/:146.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: --predicate is either deleted from seal-run.sh (usage block included) or made genuinely functional with PRED_REL derived from the flag.
If kept, the harness gains at least one case exercising --predicate that FAILS when the derivation is reverted to the hardcoded constant.
If deleted, a run passing --predicate exits with a clear 'no such flag' rather than a misleading blob-drift refusal naming the wrong file.

corpus.title: The member self-scoped delivery read does not use the (team_id, inserted_at) index

content.description: cch-w31-s8 widened GET /v1/notifications/deliveries from admin-only to member-self-scoped, fencing the query with lower(recipient) = downcased caller email. MEASURED, and not free: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on a seeded 200k-row single team (50 recipients, ANALYZEd) shows the planner DECLINING notification_deliveries_team_id_inserted_at_index for the fenced query because lower(recipient) is unindexed. Member self-scoped: Bitmap Index Scan on notification_deliveries_team_id_index -> Bitmap Heap Scan (Rows Removed by Filter: 196000, Heap Blocks: exact=3637) -> top-N heapsort; 30.806 ms, shared hit=3798. Admin unfenced on the same team: Index Scan Backward using notification_deliveries_team_id_inserted_at_index -> Incremental Sort; 0.037 ms, shared hit=6. Roughly 630x the buffers. The team fence bounds it and 30 ms is an acceptable page today, but the member read scales with the TEAMS WHOLE LOG rather than the page size and notification_deliveries has NO retention policy. FIX: an index on (team_id, lower(recipient), inserted_at) so the fenced read walks the index in sort order and stops at the LIMIT. Deliberately NOT taken in s8: it is a migration, outside that slices declared file fence, and a migration mid-wave is collision-prone. PROOF OBLIGATION: re-run the same EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) after the migration and quote both plans - a green suite is not evidence here, the plan is. Anchors: maybe_delivery_recipient/2 in cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/notifications.ex; the numbers are recorded verbatim in the route comment above GET /v1/notifications/deliveries in cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/router.ex; the existing index is cloud/priv/repo/migrations/20260629120300_create_notification_deliveries.exs:32.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A migration adds an index covering (team_id, lower(recipient), inserted_at) on notification_deliveries. Evidence: the migration file and a successful mix ecto.migrate.

EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on the SAME 200k-row seeded shape shows the member self-scoped read using the new index instead of notification_deliveries_team_id_index, with buffers in the same order of magnitude as the admin read (baseline to beat: 30.806 ms / shared hit=3798 vs admin 0.037 ms / shared hit=6). Evidence: both EXPLAIN outputs, before and after.

The measurement paragraph in the route comment above GET /v1/notifications/deliveries is UPDATED to the new numbers, never deleted - it is the only place a reader learns this read was ever expensive. Evidence: the diff.

corpus.title: One PDS instrument finally runs under a required gate — with zero bytes of .github/

content.description:
THE FENCE GUARDS .github/, NOT CI. api/test/** is INSIDE the PDS fence and rides the already-required `Elixir gate` context (elixir.yml:646 `needs: [changes, mix-test, ...]`, fail-closed: a skipped mix-test greens ONLY when changes.outputs.test == 'false'). An ExUnit case that shells the residue lens's --selftest wires an instrument to a required gate with ZERO bytes of .github/.

CORRECTION THE BUILDER MUST CARRY: `Test (Elixir 1.18.1 / OTP 27.0)` is NOT the required context — it is an EXPLICIT entry in .github/required-checks.json's `exclusions` list, deliberately not requirable. Name `Elixir gate`.

Code.require_file — the repo's own prior art at api/test/barkpark/async_global_seam_guard_test.exs:24 — is UNUSABLE here: scripts/pds-status-only-residue.exs ends in System.halt(code) and would halt the whole ExUnit suite at the script's chosen exit code. Use System.cmd.

Costs measured: residue --selftest rc=0, 15/15 arms, 0.52-0.64s user CPU. The census --selftest is DISQUALIFIED (>210s, a 25-mutant harness that shells the real corpus) — cost, not fence.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An ExUnit case at api/test/barkpark/pds_residue_lens_test.exs, `async: false`, shells `elixir scripts/pds-status-only-residue.exs --selftest` via System.cmd with `cd:` the repo root, and asserts the exit code is 0. NOT Code.require_file — the script self-runs and ends in System.halt(code), which would halt the whole suite.
THE ASSERTION IS ON THE SELFTEST'S PROSE (`SELFTEST GREEN — exit 0`), never on an arm-count bucket — the arm count is the thing most likely to change for an innocent reason.

A FAIL-DEMO TEST PROVES THE GATE CAN RED: a one-token mutant of the lens exits 1 with `SELFTEST RED`. This is not optional. w36 R5 already proved that a gate on the OTHER script's --selftest would be 'the purest vacuous green available' (that census silently ignores unknown ARGV); the refutation does not transfer to the lens only because the lens has a real @known_flags allowlist that REFUSES unknown flags — and the fail-demo is what proves that difference rather than asserting it.

IT FAILS LOUD AND NEVER SKIPS: a missing script or a missing `elixir` binary makes the test FAIL with a named message, never `skip`. A skip-on-missing-binary would reproduce D26 — thirty green fixtures executed by nothing. Evidence: the fail-loud message, observed (running against a tree without the lens must print 'the gate is pointed at nothing').

scripts/pds-status-only-residue.exs is added to ELIXIR_TEST_ONLY_PATHS in scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh IN THE SAME PR, and the test names the script with a `"../../../scripts/..."` STRING LITERAL so the ratchet can resolve it. THIS IS LOAD-BEARING FOR CORRECTNESS, NOT PAPERWORK: the ratchet only sees `"../..."` literals, and the declaration is what makes a PR touching ONLY the instrument set changes.outputs.test=true — without it, mix-test is LEGITIMATELY skipped and the instrument's own guard never runs on the very PR that changes the instrument.

THE RATCHET LINE IS PROVEN LOAD-BEARING BY MUTATION: deleting it reds `bash scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh` with `::error:: UNCOVERED repo-root read: scripts/pds-status-only-residue.exs`, and restoring it greens. Both directions run.

THE SCOPE IS STATED HONESTLY IN THE PR BODY, in these terms: this moves 0 -> 1 of 19 executable pds-* instruments onto a required context, running on EVERY PR THAT COULD AFFECT IT — not on every PR (mix-test is path-gated and does not run on a docs-only or Go-only PR). Never claim 'the lens now runs in CI on every PR'.
ZERO BYTES of .github/ are touched. PDS-D607's policy fence is untouched; this crosses to CI without crossing it.

GATE: `cd api && CC=clang mix test test/barkpark/pds_residue_lens_test.exs` rc=0; `bash scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh` rc=0; `bash scripts/elixir-path-escape-check.sh --selftest` prints 113 passed / 0 failed; `cd api && mix format --check-formatted test/barkpark/pds_residue_lens_test.exs` rc=0. Capture every gate as `out=$(cmd 2>&1); rc=$?` — NEVER read `$?` through a pipe and never `cmd | tail && echo ok`; that trap fired live during this wave's own verification and published a false green. That exact trap fired during this wave's verification: `mix format --check-formatted <file> | tail -5` printed rc=0 on an UNFORMATTED file.

MERGE-GATED (the LEAD closes this): merged, AND the lead confirms from the first CI run that the case actually EXECUTED on the runner. The local measurement was Elixir 1.19.5 / OTP 28 while CI pins 1.18.1 / OTP 27, so 'bare `elixir` is on PATH in the mix-test job' is inferred (L2), not observed (L1), until that run exists.
