corpus.title: The orphan harnesses run in CI, and the one that is already red goes green first

content.description:
ORDER IS THE WHOLE SLICE: FIX THE RED FIRST, THEN WIRE. Wiring all sixteen blindly reds shell-harnesses.yml on the merge commit.

WHAT IS TRUE (charter D519, all re-derived against origin/main).

Of 32 shell harnesses on origin/main, exactly 16 are executed by a workflow and 16 are ORPHANS. A naive name-grep manufactures false orphans and you must not repeat it: `console-path-escape-check.test.sh` appears FOUR times in workflow files (console-harness.yml:673,1050,1062 and elixir.yml:253) and every one is a COMMENT; `cloud-path-escape-check.test.sh` and `elixir-path-escape-check.test.sh` are reachable via a wired parent's `--selftest` (cloud.yml:175, elixir.yml:241). Mention is not execution, and neither is absence-of-mention proof of orphanhood.

The 16 true orphans: seal-run.test.sh, cloud-path-escape-check.test.sh(*), elixir-path-escape-check.test.sh(*), console-path-escape-check.test.sh, pds-ledger-census_test.sh, pds-record-parity.test.sh, pds-scratch-target_test.sh, file-ci-failure-issue.test.sh, registration-sample.test.sh, install-cli.test.sh, fetch-prebuilt.test.sh, deploy/site-runtime-install_test.sh, tooling/task-obsession/reland_check.test.sh, scripts/barkpark-boot-selftest.sh, tooling/fleet/fleet-run-verdict-test.sh, scripts/audit-paper-readers-test.sh. (*) the two path-escape ones are reachable via --selftest; treat them as already covered and do NOT double-wire them.

NEITHER `scripts/seal-run.sh` NOR `scripts/seal-run.test.sh` appears in any of the 48 workflow files — the runner itself is uninvoked, not just its test.

15 of 16 pass against a clean `git archive origin/main`. ONE IS ALREADY RED: `scripts/registration-sample.test.sh` gives `pass 40  fail 3`, RC=1 on origin/main and `pass 43  fail 0` on `0e94b99fe^`. The break landed with 0e94b99fe (PR #11082, merged 2026-08-09T02:18:52Z), which added `internal/**` to CLOUD_PATHS at `scripts/cloud-path-escape-check.sh:219`. The harness's own control fixture writes `internal/tui/x.go` as a NEITHER-shape head; it now classifies CLOUD, so three `of which NEITHER` assertions (test lines 156, 181, 237) each read exactly one lower than expected. THE SAMPLER IS CORRECT — it faithfully reports the widened path set. The HARNESS's expectations are stale.

WHAT TO BUILD.

(1) FIX registration-sample.test.sh FIRST. The minimum fix is the three expected counts. The DURABLE fix, and the one to prefer if it is tractable: have the harness DERIVE the expected shape from the ratchet rather than hard-coding 3/2/0/2 — otherwise a future narrowing of CLOUD_PATHS inverts the fix and reds it again. If you take the minimum fix, say so in the PR body and state the inversion risk.

(2) WIRE THE ORPHANS into `.github/workflows/shell-harnesses.yml`, which is literally the file built for this class (its header: "Runs the repo's behavioral shell harnesses that no other CI lane executes"). It already carries five tenants, each with an explicit PER-FILE `paths:` entry on BOTH `pull_request` and `push: [main]` — D26 found that a `pr-task-gate.sh` edit did not even trigger it, so per-file paths are mandatory, never a directory glob. Template new jobs on the existing `release-scan-verdict` job, which already sets `fetch-depth: 0` for the same reason.

REQUIREMENTS THAT WILL BITE YOU IF MISSED:
  - `scripts/seal-run.test.sh` needs a FULL checkout (with only scripts/ present it drops to 63 passed / 2 FAILED: "the e2e fixture cannot be built (needs the real predicate and .github/workflows/cloud.yml)") and hard-requires `node` (:43 `command -v node || exit 2`). It does NOT need full git history — it builds its own shallow fixture from a `file://` clone. Default actions/checkout@v4 suffices; add a `command -v node` name-check step matching the file's existing precedent (python3 at :138-149, jq at :167-176).
  - `scripts/barkpark-boot-selftest.sh` is DIFFERENTIAL and needs one historical blob (0bff57e4f500e9c9fc99424fa2635ca9988be725:bin/barkpark). Without it it exits 2 forever — a gate that can only lose. Either give its job `fetch-depth: 0` (or the targeted `git fetch --depth=1 origin <sha>`), or leave it out of this slice and say so.
  - `timeout` is NOT on the macOS PATH; do not put it in any command a human may re-run locally.
  - No `continue-on-error` — shell-harnesses.yml bans it in prose.

HONEST LIMIT TO STATE IN THE PR BODY, not to hide: `shell-harnesses.yml` is NOT one of main's four required contexts (verified live: `Elixir gate`, `PR references an active task`, `Cloud gate`, `Console gate`; enforce_admins=true, strict=false). Wiring makes a harness RUN, not BLOCK. That is the right first step and must be sold as exactly that.

Prior art exists — `dr-seal-run-harness-runs-in-no-ci` is already filed for seal-run alone. Reference it; do not file a duplicate.

corpus.title: The :forbidden rung is a MEASURED deferral, not an oversight — a 403 box needs its own sentence, and refusing it without one is a UX regression

content.description:
MEASURED WAVE 60 (charter D715). cch-w60-s4 refuses an EXECUTE ask at a box whose update_unavailable_reason is 'identity_refused' and NOT at one whose reason is 'forbidden'. That is a doctrine call, and the measurement that makes it a call rather than a cost question is recorded here so nobody re-litigates it from scratch.

THE MEASUREMENT: both variants are free. The one-rung guard runs the shipped cloud suite at 3483 tests / 0 failures (byte-identical to the #11102-tip baseline). The two-rung variant ["identity_refused","forbidden"] runs 3490 tests / 1 failure, and the single failure is cch-w60-s4's OWN three-state discriminator correctly detecting the widening. Nothing in the shipped corpus objects either way.

THE DOCTRINE: a 401 means the box does not know our token at all, so the address may not be our box and an EXECUTE ask goes to a STRANGER — that is the leak the refusal exists to stop. A 403 means the box KNOWS the token and denies the principal: no stranger, no leak. And the box's own router (api/lib/barkpark_web/router.ex, the /v1/admin scope) puts GET /v1/admin/self-update, POST /v1/admin/self-update and POST /rollback in ONE [:api, :require_admin] pipeline, so a 403 on the READ is a structurally-guaranteed 403 on the WRITE — the trigger will fail anyway.

SO REFUSING ON :forbidden IS A UX NICETY, AND IT NEEDS ITS OWN SENTENCE: 'this box does not grant our token admin — re-provision it', not the identity-refused copy. Shipping it without that sentence trades a wasted request for a confusing one.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The measurement above is re-derived on the then-current main (one-rung vs two-rung whole-suite counts) rather than quoted from this row.
Either the guard widens to :forbidden WITH its own distinct console sentence and a re-provision affordance, or this row records the decision to keep one rung and states what a 403 box sees instead.
If widened: a test proves the two rungs produce DIFFERENT console copy, and reds if they collapse to one sentence.

corpus.title: The payload contract gets a bidirectional key-set guard that can lose in BOTH directions

content.description:
NOTE: this is the wave-10 row dr-w10-s4, RE-SPECIFIED by wave 11 rather than duplicated. Its original ask stands; what follows adds the two measured blind spots and the solved CI placement.

HIGH-FLIP-RISK: whether the extractor can SEE what it claims to census. Both of its measured blind spots are SILENT, and one of them bit the verifier who built the prototype within an hour.

WHY (charter D165). Keys are landing on one side of the wire and being dropped on the floor by the other, repeatedly and undetectably. Confirmed live on origin/main: cloud/ emits terminal_failure_rate ZERO times while internal/cli/cloud_deploy_census_cmd.go:398 branches on `census.TerminalFailureRate == nil`, so the human-facing `bp cloud deployments` headline is PERMANENTLY on its "this control plane sends no terminal-row rate" arm and no test can tell that from a genuinely older control plane. Three phantom Go fields (DeployCensus.Live, DeployCensus.TerminalFailureRate, DeployRate.Basis) decode keys nothing emits; at least 28 emitted keys across barkpark_json/site_json/deployment_json appear in no Go json tag at all, including failure_reason_raw — the whole point of the dr-w1-s2 honest pair, scrubbed and ANSI-stripped by the control plane and read by nobody.

WHAT TO BUILD. A bidirectional key-set census with a COMMITTED allowlist per direction, refusing rather than counting.
- Side A (emitted): the literal map keys of the Elixir serializers — barkpark_json/4 and its merge_* pipeline, deployment_json/1, @unmetered_pressure, DeployLedger.census/3 and rate/2. Prefer Code.string_to_quoted!/1 over regex: a naive regex over barkpark_json's base literal sees 35 keys where a transitive AST walk sees 57 — 39% blindness to the merge pipeline.
- Side B (decoded): the `json:"..."` struct tags in internal/cloudclient/.
- Two arms, both able to fail: UNREAD (emitted but in no Go tag) and PHANTOM (decoded but emitted by nobody).
- Each arm carries a committed allowlist file with a REASON PER ENTRY. Split it honestly into "ruled reconciled" vs "known open, tracked by <task id>" — do NOT bless the current divergence as reconciled. The three phantom census keys are "known open, the emitter is stranded in PR #10014".

TWO MEASURED BLIND SPOTS YOU MUST HANDLE, OR THE GUARD IS GREEN BY CONSTRUCTION:
(a) GUARDED CLAUSES ARE SILENTLY DROPPED. An AST collector matching {:def|:defp, _, [{name,_,args}|_]} misses every clause whose head is {:when, _, [{name,_,args}, guard]}. Measured: 40 keys collected instead of 57 — a 17-key silent loss with NO error and NO warning, and the 17 were every pressure vital, i.e. exactly the keys the census exists to check. Unwrap :when. Then add an ANTI-VACUITY FLOOR (a minimum emitted-key count, the same device CLOUD_ESCAPE_MIN already is for the path ratchet) so that a future Elixir syntax the walker does not match REDS instead of certifying a payload it cannot see.
(b) VARIABLE KEYS ARE STRUCTURALLY INVISIBLE. merge_job_status/4 does Map.merge(map, %{status_key => status, error_key => ...}) where the keys are function parameters. Four payload keys (provision_status, provision_error, deprovision_status, deprovision_error) can never be seen by a literal extractor and today surface as FALSE "decoded but never emitted". A Map.put/Map.merge whose key is not a literal atom must RED as "unresolvable key at <file>:<line>", never be silently dropped.
Also constrain SCOPE: a transitive walk that follows every local call over-collects (console, payload, status, steps, error leak in from helpers). Restrict to the entry function's map literal plus explicit puts/merges on the piped accumulator, or the allowlist becomes a junk drawer that hides a real divergence.

CI PLACEMENT (solved, and the ratchet ENFORCES it). scripts/cloud-path-escape-check.sh is the single source of truth for the path set cloud.yml dispatches on (it reads it via --print-set/--match; harness case 8 pins that). Place the census as an ExUnit test in cloud/test/ (the house pattern — four *_census_test.exs already live there) and ADD `internal/cloudclient/**` to CLOUD_PATHS (line ~105), so a Go-only edit to client.go still re-runs the census. Proven: --check stays rc=0 and --selftest goes 122 -> 123 passed, with the new assertion AUTO-DERIVED (harness case 6 loops over --print-set and probes every declared glob, so no test edit is needed). If you skip the declaration, the ratchet REDS by name — proven by planting a Cloud test that reads internal/cloudclient.

TWO COUPLED EDITS NOBODY MAY DISCOVER IN REVIEW:
1. CLOUD_ESCAPE_MIN (line ~144) must be raised in the SAME commit. The comparison is `-lt`, so forgetting it does NOT red — the floor silently decays from equal-to-population to one-below, which is the anti-neutered-scanner property degrading on the very PR that adds a guard. Set it to the measured count and update the census comment above it, which currently asserts "The measured population is 5".
2. PR #10014 (the lead's, do NOT re-cut it) adds `deploy/site-deploy-node.sh` to the SAME array for the same reason. Expect a trivial conflict and say so in the PR body: if #10014 lands first the floor is one higher than yours.

MUST NOT: widen any serializer or add any decoding field. This guard REPORTS, it does not repair — that is what keeps it honest and what keeps it out of slice S4's file.

GATE: bash scripts/cloud-path-escape-check.sh --check && bash scripts/cloud-path-escape-check.sh --selftest && cd cloud && CC=/usr/bin/clang MIX_ENV=test mix test test/barkpark_cloud/payload_key_set_census_test.exs
NOTE: the primary checkout is behind origin/main and does NOT contain scripts/cloud-path-escape-check.sh. Build in a FRESH worktree off origin/main.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The census reds on an EMITTED-but-unread key: inject a new literal key into an Elixir serializer and paste the failure naming that key by name
The census reds on a DECODED-but-unemitted key: inject a json tag into a cloudclient struct and paste the failure naming that key by name; then restore and show it green again

GUARDED-CLAUSE BLIND SPOT: the extractor collects keys from clauses whose head is a :when guard; prove it by quoting the emitted-key COUNT with and without the :when unwrap (expect ~40 vs ~57) and by asserting a pressure vital such as cpu_percent is present
ANTI-VACUITY FLOOR: a minimum emitted-key count exists and CAN LOSE — break the extractor (e.g. make the walker match nothing) and paste the floor refusal rather than a clean pass
UNRESOLVABLE KEYS RED RATHER THAN DROP: a Map.put/Map.merge with a non-literal key produces a named refusal citing file:line; prove it against merge_job_status/4 rather than a synthetic fixture

The committed allowlist splits ruled-reconciled from known-open with a REASON per entry, and the three phantom census keys (live, terminal_failure_rate, basis) are in the known-open half naming PR #10014 — quote the entries

internal/cloudclient/** is declared in CLOUD_PATHS and CLOUD_ESCAPE_MIN is raised in the SAME commit with its census comment updated; quote the diff of both and the new --check output showing the raised population

The ratchet DEMANDS the declaration: with the new Cloud test present but the path undeclared, scripts/cloud-path-escape-check.sh --check exits 1 naming BOTH the path and the reading file — paste that output, then the rc=0 output after declaring it
Gate green: bash scripts/cloud-path-escape-check.sh --check (rc 0) and --selftest (paste the passed/failed line, expect 0 failed) and the new ExUnit census file passes
git diff shows NO serializer widened and NO struct gained a decoding field — the guard reports, it does not repair

corpus.title: A long branch name stops 500ing the builder's own caption — deployments.detail becomes :text

content.description:
=== WAVE 35 RE-ANCHOR (charter D399) — READ THIS BEFORE THE BODY BELOW; WHERE THEY DISAGREE, THIS WINS ===

DISPATCHES NOW. Its blocker cch-w34-s2 is MERGED (#9739, and it is origin/main's tip c73bbc07c). The
sentence further down that says "AFTER cch-w34-s2 MERGES ... Do not dispatch beside it" is DISCHARGED —
leave it in place as provenance, do NOT self-block on it. This slice is ROUND 1.

*** THE LINE NUMBERS IN CRITERION 5 AND IN THE BODY ARE STALE, AND FOLLOWING THEM EDITS THE WRONG TEST. ***
#9739 -- the very merge this slice waits on -- shifted registry_test.exs by exactly +111.
  cited :1041 (the raise test)      -> ACTUAL :1152, test "cch-w33-s3: a caption ABOVE the column limit currently RAISES"
  cited :1020 (the round-trip test) -> ACTUAL :1131, test "cch-w33-s3: a caption at the column limit round-trips through the shared validator"
`mix test ...:1041 --trace` now runs [L#1033] "the ring drop DISCLOSES its cumulative count on the oldest
survivor", an unrelated console ring test. CITE THE TEST NAMES, not line numbers -- names cannot drift.

PRE-VERIFIED FOR YOU, so the lead's merge order is grounded rather than a gamble:
 - varchar(255)->text is METADATA-ONLY. On 27,000 rows, relfilenode is 2208300 BEFORE and 2208300 AFTER
   the ALTER (PostgreSQL 17.9). No table rewrite. You still owe your own run; it is no longer a bet.
 - THE BLAST RADIUS INSIDE registry_test.exs IS EXACTLY ONE TEST. Simulating the ALTER turns the file from
   94/0 into 94 tests / 1 failure, and the failure is only the raise test at :1152 ("Expected exception
   Postgrex.Error but nothing was raised"). The 255-round-trip sibling SURVIVES under :text.
 - The full migration chain applies cleanly at origin/main under MIX_ENV=test.

NEW OBLIGATION -- D251 IS NOT OVERRIDDEN. This repo has already fixed this exact 22001 class TWICE by
capping at the column: env_var.ex:103 (validate_length(:comment, max: 255), citing cch-w22-s3) and
deploy.ex:962 (short_detail/1 clamping to 255 for both terminal writers). Charter D251 rules the effective
cap is min(validate_length, column width, every downstream derivation). Widening to :text makes the shared
2 KB validator the real bound on a string the site page renders UNDER THE STATUS PILL -- the unbounded-
pill-text class this epic has already paid for three times. So: ship :text (the column stops lying about
what it stores) AND name and prove the RENDER bound. If no cap exists on that sub-line, FILE THE ROW
rather than shipping a 2,000-character pill. See criterion 10.

BUILD IN A WORKTREE CUT FROM origin/main with MIX_ENV=test on all three ecto tasks. The primary checkout is
~474 commits behind and does not contain these tests at all -- a verifier who ran it would have reported
the premise unreproducible.

=== ORIGINAL WAVE-34 BRIEF (line numbers stale where the note above corrects them) ===

AFTER cch-w34-s2 MERGES — this slice edits cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/registry.ex and cloud/test/barkpark_cloud/registry_test.exs, both of which s2 owns in round 1. Do not dispatch beside it.

WAVE 34, SLICE s5. ROUND 2. Build in a worktree at origin/main + s2's merge.

READ CHARTER D390 FIRST.

## The defect, run at the route

`deployments.detail` is `add :detail, :string` = **varchar(255)** (migration 20260703100000, line 14), but `set_deployment_detail/2` (registry.ex:6093) validates through the SHARED `validate_console_line/1` whose cap is **2 KB**. So a caption of 256..2,000 characters is neither refused NOR trimmed: it reaches `Repo.update/1` and raises `Postgrex.Error ERROR 22001 (string_data_right_truncation)`.

`POST /v1/builder/deployments/:id/detail` (router.ex:7343-7364) cases only on `{:ok,_} | {:error,:not_found} | {:error,:invalid}` and its `@doc` documents 200/404/422. Driven at the route: a 300-char caption logs `crash_envelope … status=500` and sends `{500, {"error":"server_error","request_id":…}}` — out of a function whose `@doc` promises telemetry that *"NEVER affects the build's outcome"*. A 200-char caption returns `{200, {"ok":true}}`.

## IT IS REACHABLE WITH ORDINARY PRODUCT DATA

`internal/builder/builder.go:129` sends `con.caption("Starting your build (%s)…", refOrNone(d.GitRef))` — **+23 characters over the ref**. And `git_ref` is itself varchar(255) with **no `validate_length`** anywhere in `Deployment.changeset/2`. So any branch/ref of **233..255 characters inserts successfully and then makes its OWN caption overflow.** Driven end to end: a 240-char `git_ref` persisted, its caption was 263 chars, the route answered 500, and `detail` stayed `nil`.

Blast radius, honestly: `internal/builder/console.go:134` swallows the non-2xx (stderr, return), so the BUILD does not fail. The harm is (a) an undocumented 500 logged at `:error` on a worker route, (b) a silently dropped caption, (c) `c.fails++` priming the shared narration counter. It **cannot on its own reach** the `maxConsoleFails = 3` latch — only `:129` interpolates, the other four captions are fixed short copy, and any subsequent successful console report resets `c.fails = 0`. **Do not claim this latches narration.**

## The fix: `:text`, NOT a 255-char cap

A detail-specific 255 cap would keep captions silently truncated — the exact "unknown collapsed into determinate" class this wave exists to kill. Instead:

    modify :detail, :text

`varchar(n) → text` is a **no-rewrite metadata-only change** in Postgres (no table rewrite since 9.1), so it is safe on a 27k-row table on an auto-deploying surface. Verify that on your own database and say so in the PR body — do not assert it from memory. Write a real `down/0`.

The existing 2 KB `validate_console_line/1` cap then becomes the real bound, and a 5,000-char caption truncates to 2,000 and STORES.

## THE PINNING TEST MUST FLIP IN THIS DIFF OR THE SUITE REDS

`registry_test.exs:1041` — *"cch-w33-s3: a caption ABOVE the column limit currently RAISES (see cch-deployment-detail-column-overflow)"* — deliberately CERTIFIES the defect. Its own comment says: *"WHEN THAT TASK LANDS: delete this test and assert the truncation instead."* Do exactly that. (It genuinely depends on the raise: mutating its input 5_000 → 200 reds it with *"Expected exception Postgrex.Error but nothing was raised"*.) Its sibling at :1020, pinning that 255 round-trips, stays.

Also remove the KNOWN DEFECT paragraph from `set_deployment_detail/2`'s `@doc` (registry.ex:6081-6086) — leaving prose that asserts a defect the code no longer has is this epic's own sin.

`router_builder_test.exs` covers the /detail route's 200 / latest-wins / blank-422 / unknown-404 / 401 arms and has **NO oversize case**. Add one: an oversize caption returns 200 (or a documented 4xx) and never a 500.

## Out of scope, filed separately

`git_ref` having no `validate_length` (a >255-char ref raises on INSERT) is the same class on a different route and is filed as its own row. Do not widen into it.

## Gate

    cd cloud && CC=clang MIX_TEST_PARTITION=_w34s5 mix test test/barkpark_cloud/registry_test.exs test/barkpark_cloud/web/router_builder_test.exs

Baseline at origin/main: registry_test 90 tests / 0 failures (the stale primary checkout reports 80/0 against a file that does not contain the pinning test at all — a vacuous green; always run in the worktree).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A migration changes deployments.detail from :string to :text with a working down/0, and the PR body states — verified against a real database, not asserted from memory — that varchar(n) -> text is a no-rewrite metadata-only change in Postgres. Evidence: the migration and the verification output.

The caption bound is now the SHARED 2 KB validator, not a detail-specific 255-char cap: a 5,000-char caption truncates to 2,000 and STORES rather than raising or being silently cut to 255. Evidence: a test.

POST /v1/builder/deployments/:id/detail no longer answers an undocumented 500 for an oversize caption — proved at the ROUTE, not at the context function. Evidence: a new router_builder_test arm and its output.
The reachability case is covered: a git_ref of 233..255 characters, whose builder caption is +23 characters, no longer 500s. Evidence: a test driving that exact shape.

The defect-pinning test at registry_test.exs:1041 is DELETED and replaced with a truncation assertion, as its own comment instructs; the 255-round-trip sibling at :1020 still passes. Evidence: the diff and the green run.
The KNOWN DEFECT paragraph is removed from set_deployment_detail/2's @doc, and the '@doc never affects the build's outcome' promise is now true. Evidence: the diff.
No change is made to git_ref validation or to anything under internal/ or deploy/ — the git_ref length gap is filed as its own row. Evidence: the diff's file list.

Gate green: `cd cloud && CC=clang MIX_TEST_PARTITION=_w34s5 mix test test/barkpark_cloud/registry_test.exs test/barkpark_cloud/web/router_builder_test.exs` reports 0 failures, run in a worktree at origin/main (the primary checkout is 466 commits behind and its green is vacuous). Evidence: the command and its tail.

WAVE-35 ADDITION (charter D399) — THE RENDER BOUND IS NAMED AND PROVED, so D251 is honoured rather than overridden. `detail` is the caption the site page renders UNDER THE STATUS PILL, and widening the column to :text makes the shared 2 KB validator the real bound. Either name the existing cap on that sub-line and prove it holds for a 2,000-character caption, or FILE a backlog row for the missing cap and say so in the PR body. Evidence: the rendered pill for a 2,000-char caption, plus the cap's location — or the filed row id.

WAVE-35 ADDITION (charter D399) — THE TWO TESTS ARE CITED BY NAME, NOT BY LINE. The brief's :1041/:1020 are stale by exactly +111 (shifted by #9739, this slice's own dependency) and :1041 now selects an unrelated console ring test. Evidence: quote the two test NAMES you edited, and paste `mix test` output proving the raise test is gone and the round-trip sibling still passes under :text.

corpus.title: A read-only share posture stops losing to caps.write — close the live write bypass, and collapse derive's three identical membership loads

content.description:
HIGH-FLIP-RISK: authorization/tenancy. An INDEPENDENT second reviewer is owed before merge (the lead dispatches it by hand).

THE DEFECT, PROVEN BY RUN THIS WAVE (PDS-D635). `Caps.write_capable?/2` (api/lib/barkpark_web/studio/caps.ex:284-289) tests `Map.get(caps, :write) == true` BEFORE `restricted?/1`, and `derive/1` (caps.ex:143-167) computes `write` from membership+grants ONLY -- it never reads `share_access`, `readonly_gate?`, `write_gate?` or `caller_context`. So a socket that is BOTH restricted AND has a write source short-circuits past the restriction, and the predicate's own docstring ("a RESTRICTED socket ... does not [pass]") is FALSE for all four restricted shapes.

REACHABLE THROUGH A REAL NON-ADMIN PATH. `LiveScope.authorize_read/4` offers the public-share arm BEFORE the grant arm (deliberately -- "grants only ADD access, never REMOVE it"), so a signed-in NON-MEMBER holding an ACTIVE WRITE GRANT who mounts a desk that is also `:docs`-shared read-only gets grade `:share_read`: `share_access: :read`, `readonly_gate?: true`, and NO `caller_context` and NO `write_gate?` -- so neither `Content.Scope.scope_to_grants/3`'s read-narrowing nor the per-event `Access.validate/3` write-narrowing is armed, while `derive/1` still returns `write: true`. A verifier's probe wrote persisted state through the REAL cid-targeted component event `inner-change` at `#paper-fb-<id>`: `stored = %{"amount" => "REACHED"}`, `flash = %{}`. The same intent through the EVENT route was HALTED with "This workspace is shared read-only" -- the two seams disagree about the same principal, op and socket. AND IT ESCALATES: a write grant naming ONE doc wrote a DIFFERENT paper on the same desk (`stored(other) = %{"amount" => "ESCALATED"}`, no flash), because `Access.admits_desk?/3` auto-satisfies the grant's own type/doc_id and defers narrowing to a mechanism this grade never arms.

THE FIX IS SURGICAL, NOT THE OBVIOUS REORDER. Flipping `restricted?/1` above `caps.write` wholesale would ALSO deny GRANT-graded sockets (write_gate? / caller_context), whose narrowing IS armed -- a real regression for legitimate grantees. Instead add a private `readonly_posture?/1` = `Map.get(assigns, :share_access) == :read or Map.get(assigns, :readonly_gate?) == true` and place a `readonly_posture?(assigns) -> false` branch ABOVE the `caps.write` branch in `write_capable?/2`'s cond. Leave the existing `restricted?/1` arm below untouched. `derive/1` stays an honest authority function -- do NOT zero its write arm; making derive lie about authority is the wrong shape.

ALSO IN THIS SLICE, SAME FILE, SAME FUNCTION (PDS-D634 -- they are ONE slice because the cost instrument's query-count assertions CHANGE when the collapse lands). A USER-principal `derive/1` issues exactly 4 Repo queries: three BYTE-IDENTICAL `Repo.one` membership loads (`:read`, `:write`, and `admin?/1`'s `:admin`, all reaching `Tenancy.Auth.membership/2`) plus ONE `Access.list_active_grants_for_grantee/1` `Repo.all` issued at caps.ex:152 BEFORE any member arm, so `or` short-circuiting cannot avoid the load. The autosave EVENT path derives TWICE (Caps.gate/3 then shared/paper.ex:99 write_denied?/1) = 8 uncached round-trips per debounced keystroke; at phx-debounce="500" that is 16/second/editing user. COLLAPSE the three identical membership loads to ONE load reused for all three actions -- this buys ZERO freshness loss (the grant Repo.all is the one that buys mid-session expiry truth and STAYS, unchanged and unconditional). Target: USER 4 -> 2 queries per derive, 8 -> 4 per event; API-TOKEN 2 -> 1 and 4 -> 2. Do NOT introduce a TTL memo across ops -- that trades the freshness derive/1's own moduledoc defends.

THE COST INSTRUMENT. Ship `api/test/barkpark_web/live/studio/pds_w43_caps_derive_cost_test.exs` with a PROCESS-SCOPED `[:barkpark,:repo,:query]` telemetry counter -- `:telemetry.attach/4` is NODE-global and an unscoped counter over-counted 800 as 806 on a verifier's first pass; filter on `self() == owner` (the handler runs in the querying process). ASSERT ONLY THE QUERY COUNTS (they are load-invariant: across three runs of the identical loop wall swung 2.47 -> 18.52 ms/op, a 7.5x spread, while the count did not move by one -- 8.000, 8.000, 8.000). PRINT the millisecond and wall figures, never assert them. Include an n=0 CONTROL row that must show zero queries. The instrument must carry, in its @moduledoc AND in its printed output, the blind-spot sentence from PDS-D633: ":erlang.statistics(:runtime) is a VM-GLOBAL sum of BEAM scheduler + async-thread CPU. It is accurate to <1% for pure in-BEAM work, blind to port children (2.58 s read as 6 ms), blind to I/O wait and to Postgres' own CPU, floored at 1 ms, and inflated by any concurrent process in the same VM (5.0x under 8 siblings)." A discipline stated only in prose is the defect clause 1 is about.

FILES: api/lib/barkpark_web/studio/caps.ex; api/test/barkpark_web/live/studio/pds_w43_caps_readonly_share_test.exs (new); api/test/barkpark_web/live/studio/pds_w43_caps_derive_cost_test.exs (new).

DO NOT record "the grant grade is safe" -- the pure `{:grant, ctx}` grade did NOT reproduce only because read-narrowing hid the target doc and the write was a no-op. That is INCONCLUSIVE; `pds-w42-bl-grant-graded-component-arm-unbuilt` stays open.

SUPERSEDES (lead closes on merge): pds-bl-w41-livescope-component-bypass-unrun (its criterion 1 is answered BYPASSED), pds-w42-bl-caps-derive-per-op-cost-unmeasured.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The bypass is reproduced BEFORE the fix: a test builds a signed-in NON-MEMBER with an ACTIVE WRITE GRANT on a :docs-shared desk, asserts the mounted socket carries share_access: :read, asserts Caps.derive/1 returns write: true, and asserts the pre-fix Caps.write_capable?/2 returned true -- evidence quotes the derive map and the assign values from the run.

AFTER the fix, the same socket is write-denied: Caps.write_capable?/2 returns false, and a REAL cid-targeted component event (inner-change on the composite paper block, routed via send(self(), {:paper_op, op})) leaves the stored block UNCHANGED and raises the deny flash -- evidence quotes stored-before and stored-after from the run, not the return value alone.
The doc-scoped ESCALATION is closed: a write grant naming ONE doc, on a share_read socket, no longer writes a DIFFERENT paper on the same desk -- evidence quotes stored(other) unchanged.

NON-REGRESSION, both controls, by run: the NEGATIVE control (identical setup, READ-only grant) is still refused with the store unchanged; the POSITIVE control (admin member, share_access nil) still writes. Evidence quotes both stored values.

GRANT GRADES ARE NOT DENIED BY THE FIX: a socket carrying write_gate? or a non-nil caller_context WITHOUT a read-only share posture still passes write_capable? when its caps grant write -- evidence quotes the predicate result for that shape, proving the fix did not become a blanket reorder.

MUTATION: moving the readonly_posture? branch back BELOW the caps.write branch makes the new test file RED -- evidence quotes the failing assertion and its left/right, proving the class descends from its substitution.

Caps.derive/1's membership loads are collapsed: pds_w43_caps_derive_cost_test.exs asserts a USER-principal derive issues exactly 2 Repo queries (was 4) and the autosave EVENT path exactly 4 (was 8), and an API-TOKEN derive exactly 1 (was 2) -- via a PROCESS-SCOPED [:barkpark,:repo,:query] counter, with an n=0 control row at zero queries. Evidence quotes the printed per-op rows.
The grant Repo.all is UNCHANGED and still unconditional -- freshness of mid-session grant expiry is not traded. Evidence names the line and states that no TTL memo was introduced.

The cost instrument carries PDS-D633's blind-spot sentence in BOTH its @moduledoc and its printed output, and asserts NO millisecond or wall figure (only query counts). Evidence quotes the printed sentence.

GATE GREEN, all four suites in one run: cd api && CC=clang mix test test/barkpark_web/live/studio/pds_w43_caps_readonly_share_test.exs test/barkpark_web/live/studio/pds_w43_caps_derive_cost_test.exs test/barkpark_web/live/studio/studio_live_caps_gate_test.exs test/barkpark_web/live/studio/pds_w41_caps_component_gate_test.exs -- evidence quotes the 'N tests, 0 failures' line and rc=0. Plus cd api && CC=clang mix format --check-formatted on both new files (capture rc as out=$(cmd 2>&1); rc=$? -- NEVER read $? through a pipe).
MERGE-GATED (the LEAD closes this): the PR is merged to main with the Elixir gate green, and an INDEPENDENT second reviewer has re-derived the authorization judgment.

corpus.title: The instance address on the front screen loses its TLD on a phone

content.description: FOUND AT W18 REVIEW BY DRIVING, and deliberately NOT papered over. cch-w18-s4 gave the preview fixtures the scheme the server really stores (registry/barkpark.ex provisioning_url/1 writes "https://" <> fqdn), which is fidelity, not a regression — but it EXPOSES a defect the bare-host fixture had been concealing for the whole epic: .instance-card-url is overflow:hidden / text-overflow:ellipsis / white-space:nowrap (app.css:3067-3070) and renders publicUrl(bp) as TEXT, so the real, production-shaped address ellipsises on the FRONT SCREEN at phone widths. DRIVEN AT REVIEW, Chrome 150.0.7871.187: 7 clipped cells over ?scen=overview-attention#overview and ?scen=mixed-fleet#overview at 320/360 — "https://production-5b2c1e.barkpark.cloud" reads 244/288 at 320 and 284/288 at 360; "https://reporting-5b2c1e.barkpark.cloud" 244/281 at 320; staging 244/266 and marketing 244/281 at 320. Clean from 390 up. On origin/main the same measurement is 0 clipped, because the fixture was shorter than production. WHY IT MATTERS TO A PERSON: what is cut is the END of the address — the TLD — so two boxes on different domains can render as the same visible string, and the ellipsis cue tells a person text is missing without telling them which. THE SWEEP CANNOT SEE THIS: its Q2 census counts text-overflow:ellipsis as an authored cue and skips the element, and no overflow-guard leg names this selector — the defect is invisible to every committed instrument, which is why it needs a leg, not just a rule. NOT a duplicate of cch-w16-bl-attention-pill-detail-truncated-front-screen (that one pays .status-pill-detail in the same card and is fixed).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: THE DEFECT REPRODUCES ON MERGED BYTES AT ITS NAMED CELLS: with `bp.url` carrying the scheme the server actually stores, `.instance-card-url` on the FRONT SCREEN reads clientWidth 244 of scrollWidth 288 for "https://production-5b2c1e.barkpark.cloud" at 320 and 284/288 at 360, and 244/281 for the Reporting card at 320 — 7 clipped cells across ?scen=overview-attention#overview and ?scen=mixed-fleet#overview, against 0 on origin/main's bare-host fixtures. Evidence: the per-scenario per-width table, both scenarios, with the address string quoted.

THE REMEDY IS CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY TASTE, AND THE ALTERNATIVES ARE PRICED: at least three candidates are driven cell-for-cell — (a) render the address without its scheme (`publicUrl` strips `https://` for DISPLAY while every href keeps it), (b) let the line wrap, (c) shrink the token. The PR records each candidate's clipped-cell count at 320/360/390 on both front-screen scenarios and states why the winner won. A candidate is not eliminated by argument.

A COMMITTED LEG MEASURES `.instance-card-url` AFTERWARDS AND CAN LOSE: overflow-guard's W18-overview-card-pill leg (or a sibling) asserts detail-style bounds on `.instance-card-url` across the same axis, and the mutation proof is DRIVEN — with the remedy commented out the leg exits 1 naming the 320 cell of each scenario; with it in place, exit 0 in one invocation. Evidence: both runs, verbatim.

NOTHING ELSE REGRESSED: __css_check exits 0, `node --test cloud/priv/static/__app.test.mjs` and `__preview__/breakpoint-sweep.test.mjs` pass, smoke renders all scenarios, and the full overflow-guard run is exit 0 with W15 still 90/90. If a cssom-heads.baseline move is involved it is taken from the D158 sentinel recipe on the merged tree, never by arithmetic.
MERGE-GATED (the lead closes this): the PR is merged to main and its SQUASH MERGE SHA is recorded here — never a branch SHA.

corpus.title: The provider connection says WHICH cloud account it points at

content.description:
WAVE 13 SLICE S5 - round 1, no dependencies. Wave Paper: cloud-console-hardening-wave-13-2026-07-31.

HIGH-FLIP-RISK: whether echoing a STORED, user-supplied subscription id is HONEST (it is an echo of input, not a server-confirmed identity), and whether the render path is genuinely reachable by a NON-ADMIN authenticated team member. Review must re-derive both independently, not re-read the builder's reasoning.

RE-SCOPED AT WAVE-13 DECIDE (charter D156). This row was filed by wave 6 as D78's honest residual and ruled "NOT cheap ... FILED, not built". That ruling rested on "the Provider schema has no account-identity column" - which is TRUE (registry/provider.ex carries only kind, label, encrypted_token, virtual credential, team_id) and NOT load-bearing for a TRANSIENT echo.

THE LIE. A person rotates a provider credential in one click and the console never says WHICH cloud account their team now points at. Today provider_json/1 (router.ex:8691-8709) emits exactly id, kind, label, team_id, inserted_at, updated_at; the rotate toast (app.js:2280-2282) says "Replaced the stored credential for Azure (label)"; the roster row (providerRosterHtml, app.js:2007-2029) shows kind + the person's own label + a relative timestamp. The tree's own comment at app.js:1995-1998 says outright there is NO health/verified field. Nothing in the DOM names the cloud account. Confirmed at the wire: driving #settings/providers and calling fetch('/v1/providers') returns 200 with {id,kind,label,team_id,inserted_at} and NO identity field.

WHY IT IS CHEAP FOR AZURE - THE FACT THAT SUPERSEDES D78's COST BASIS. build_provider_catalog("azure", provider) (router.ex:9093-9101) ALREADY opens with Registry.reveal_provider_token(provider) then Jason.decode, and the decoded map IS the four-field service principal INCLUDING subscription_id (@azure_fields is tenant_id/client_id/client_secret/subscription_id). That function is reached by GET /v1/providers/:kind/catalog (router.ex:3807) and GET /v1/providers/:kind/overview (:3815), BOTH gated `Auth.require_user(conn, [])` - any authenticated team member, no admin, no dark crown - and providers_overview already assembles a person-facing header `%{provider: %{kind:, label:}}` at :9035-9039 with the decrypted creds one call frame away. Zero new HTTP, zero new decrypt, zero migration. Driven at the seam: reveal_provider_token/1 -> Jason.decode -> creds["subscription_id"] returns the stored value.

WHAT IS REFUTED AND MUST NOT BE BUILT.
- "Azure.verify returns meta the router discards, so un-discarding it is a free server-confirmed fact" is FALSE, three ways. verify/1 (azure/client.ex:184-193) returns %{subscription_id: Map.get(creds, "subscription_id")} - THE VALUE THE PERSON TYPED - and binds the ARM response to `_decoded`, discarding it. That discarded body is `resourcegroups?api-version=...&$top=1`, a CAPPED LIST that is EMPTY for a fresh zero-resource-group subscription. And a resource-group NAME is not an account identity anyway: the recognisable value is the subscription displayName from GET /subscriptions/{id}, for which NO request builder exists (client.ex has exactly four: token_request, resource_groups_request, locations_request, vm_sizes_request). Do NOT add a fifth builder or a fifth HTTP call - that is priced separately as backlog.
- NO CONFIRM MODAL. D78 ruled that door closed for three measured reasons and it stays closed.
- NO MIGRATION, NO NEW COLUMN. This wave ships the TRANSIENT echo only.

WHAT TO BUILD.

1. SERVER: thread the stored subscription_id out of the already-decrypted blob in build_provider_catalog("azure", ...) into providers_overview's person-facing provider header (router.ex:9035-9039), as an explicit, provenance-carrying shape - e.g. `identity: %{label: "Subscription", value: sub, source: "stored"}`. When no identity is available for a kind, emit an EXPLICIT absence (e.g. `identity: nil` plus a stated reason), never omit the key silently.

2. CLIENT: render it on the providers page (app.js 2008-2300 region - providerRosterHtml :2008, providerConnectCardHtml :2084, renderProviderPage :2203) so the person sees WHICH account this connection points at, beside the "Verify & replace" form - i.e. BEFORE they commit a rotation - and after a rotate.

3. COPY MUST NOT OVERCLAIM. The stored subscription id is the value the person typed at connect time, proven reachable, NOT independently confirmed to belong to that credential. Say "the subscription you connected", never "verified account". A console that overclaims here becomes the exact lie class this epic exists to kill.

4. STATE THE HETZNER GAP OUT LOUD. hetzner_token_ok?/1 (router.ex:8967-8979) is `GET https://api.hetzner.cloud/v1/servers?per_page=1` matched on status class ALONE and returns a bare boolean; no call anywhere in the repo fetches a Hetzner account, project or organization identifier, and Hetzner Cloud tokens are project-scoped with no identity resource. Render an explicit, honest statement ("Hetzner does not report which project this token belongs to") - a console that says it cannot tell you has stopped lying. Cloudflare: verify_token keeps only %{status: ...}, but the STORED blob may already carry account_id / zone_id when the person supplied them (router.ex:8910-8919 cloudflare_credential_blob + maybe_put_field) - echo it when present, state the absence when not. Never a fabricated or inferred identity.

5. A TEST COVERS THE HONEST-ABSENCE PATH so an unknown identity renders as EXPLICITLY ABSENT rather than as a blank that looks known. Note the FakeClient's azure meta is a SUPERSET of the real one (it adds resource_count), so any shape widening must touch fake and real together or the tests diverge.

FILES: cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/router.ex (ONLY providers_overview ~:9035 and build_provider_catalog ~:9093 - a sibling slice owns merge_job_status ~:8461, the merge_provision_* serializers ~:8468/:8475 and deployment_json ~:10108-10134; stay out of them), cloud/priv/static/app.js (the providers page region 2008-2300 ONLY - siblings own :9214 and the rail above 13400), cloud/priv/static/__app.test.mjs, cloud/test/**.

GATE:
(cd cloud && CC=/usr/bin/clang mix format --check-formatted && CC=/usr/bin/clang mix test test/barkpark_cloud/azure_catalog_test.exs test/barkpark_cloud/web/router_providers_catalog_test.exs test/barkpark_cloud/registry_azure_credentials_test.exs) && node --check cloud/priv/static/app.js && node --test cloud/priv/static/__app.test.mjs && node cloud/priv/static/__preview__/smoke.mjs
The `cc` alias shadows the C compiler; CC=/usr/bin/clang is required. Nothing local runs the cloud formatter - run `cd cloud && mix format` before pushing.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Each supported provider either echoes an account identity the person can recognise before committing a rotation, or the UI states honestly that it cannot for that provider - screenshot or rendered markup pasted for azure AND for hetzner.

No fabricated or inferred identity is ever shown: the echoed value comes from the credential blob stored at connect time, and the copy says so ('the subscription you connected'), never 'verified account'.
The hetzner gap is recorded as a deliberate ruling and rendered as an explicit statement - hetzner_token_ok?/1 is quoted showing it matches on status class alone and returns a bare boolean.
A test covers the honest-absence path so an unknown identity renders as explicitly absent rather than as a blank that looks known.

Reachability is re-derived and named: GET /v1/providers/:kind/overview is shown gated Auth.require_user only, and the identity is read from the ALREADY-decrypted blob with no new HTTP call and no migration.
Gate green: cloud mix format --check-formatted, the three named ExUnit files, node --check app.js, node --test __app.test.mjs, node __preview__/smoke.mjs - counts pasted.
MERGE-GATED (LEAD CLOSES): the PR is merged to main with Cloud gate and Console gate green and the merge SHA recorded.

corpus.title: Cloud SPA ships 1.15 MB uncompressed on the sign-in critical path — Plug.Static has no gzip

content.description:
DISCOVERED BY cch-w10-oauth-exchange-code, not taken there (out of slice).

cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/router.ex:350-356 serves app.js (959,628 bytes) and app.css (198,954 bytes) through Plug.Static with NO gzip: option, and there are no .gz siblings on disk. Every cold console boot downloads ~1.15 MB uncompressed.

This is not merely a perf nicety — it is now a SECURITY-ADJACENT constant. The cch-w10 OAuth exchange code's 120s TTL was sized against exactly this page weight (IdP 302 -> cold SPA boot -> POST). A gzipped bundle would let that window shrink, which is strictly better for a credential that a response-header log can capture.

Fix shape: add gzip: true to the Plug.Static plug and emit .gz siblings at build/deploy time (Plug.Static only serves .gz files that already exist on disk — the option alone does nothing). Verify by measuring the served content-encoding, not by reading the config.

corpus.title: Sessions say where they came from - an origin column, six honest write sites, and nothing invented

content.description:
HIGH-FLIP-RISK: the judgment "each of the six write sites reports its OWN true origin" (charter D80). A wrong call here makes every test pass while five sites report one answer. An independent re-derivation is owed before merge.

THE GOAL. Account > Sessions shows a device and a real IP (wave 1 pinned that) but not WHERE the session came from. Add an `origin` column to user_tokens, populate it ONLY where the write site already holds the answer, render it ONLY when present, and backfill NOTHING. A partial provenance that never lies beats a complete one that invents.

THE SET IS CLOSED AT SIX, all funnelling through Accounts.create_user_session_token/2 (cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/accounts.ex, the ONLY code path that inserts a context:"session" row). Grep `Accounts.create_user_session_token` to re-anchor:
  router.ex - POST /v1/auth/login (password)
  router.ex - POST /v1/auth/two-factor-challenge (it also knows code-vs-recovery if you want finer)
  router.ex - GET /v1/auth/oauth/:provider/callback (`provider` is already bound in the same with-chain)
  router.ex - PUT /v1/account/password (the post-change re-mint)
  router.ex - defp register/4 (POST /v1/auth/register)
  device_auth.ex - consume_and_mint/1 (device link; it holds the whole %Request{} incl. client_name)
There is NO impersonation and NO magic-link path: `grep -rni 'impersonat|magic_link'` over cloud/lib returns zero.

THE ONE WAY THIS SHIPS DEAD, mutation-proven both directions. UserToken.changeset/2 has an explicit cast allowlist that does NOT include :origin. A slice that lands the migration + the schema field + the write-site attr but forgets the cast list runs 141 tests / 0 failures WHILE WRITING NULL ON EVERY ROW - cast/3 silently discards an unlisted key, with no Ecto warning and no compiler warning. Adding :origin to the cast gives 144/0 including an end-to-end probe; deleting it again reds that probe with `left: nil / right: "device_link"`. So your acceptance proof must be a ROUND TRIP through a real mint path, read back off the struct AND via raw SQL (Repo.query! "SELECT origin FROM user_tokens WHERE token_hash = $1") - the raw-SQL leg is the only assertion a struct default cannot satisfy.

DO NOT PUSH origin INTO session_opts/1 (charter D80). Five of the six sites share that helper, so widening it makes ONE helper answer for FIVE different origins - a complete provenance that invents, inside the wave that exists to remove invention. Append the keyword at each call site instead.

RENDER. session_json/2 in router.ex emits id, ip_address, user_agent, last_used_at, inserted_at, current. Add origin and emit it ALWAYS (null when unknown) so the client can distinguish "unknown" from "old client". In cloud/priv/static/app.js, sessionRowHtml appends to the existing .session-meta line only when x.origin is truthy - no new CSS class, so this stays off the css_check path. "approved 2d ago" uses the TOKEN's own inserted_at: the device request row carries no approval timestamp and is DELETED before the mint, so mint time is the only available clock and it is the token's own truth. Do NOT add an approved_at column to chase it.

MIGRATION. `alter table(:user_tokens) do add :origin, :string end` - nullable, no default, no backfill. In-tree precedent: 20260629120100_add_session_lifecycle_to_user_tokens.exs added seven columns under the stated rule "every new column is nullable/defaulted so pre-existing session rows are untouched". Blue/green-safe in ONE direction only: an OLD node against the NEW schema is fine, a NEW node against an UN-MIGRATED DB fails every UserToken select - so the migration lands before or with the deploy, never after. Say so in the PR body. Pick a timestamp later than any migration already on origin/main.

NO LEAK RISK, measured: pat_changeset/2 has its own separate cast list, pat_json/1 and session_json/2 are explicit-key maps, and UserToken has no @derive Jason.Encoder - so PAT rows can never receive or expose origin.

MECHANICAL NOTE: DeviceAuth.approve/2 returns bare :ok, not {:ok, _}. A builder pattern-matching {:ok, _} there gets a MatchError.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The migration is additive-nullable with no default and no backfill, and applies cleanly. Evidence: the migration file contents plus the `mix ecto.migrate` output line for it.

PROVEN BY ROUND TRIP, never by column existence: a test drives a REAL mint path end to end and reads origin back BOTH off the struct AND via a raw `Repo.query!` against the column. Evidence: the test output, plus mutation output showing that removing :origin from UserToken.changeset/2's cast list reds it with `left: nil`.
All six write sites stamp their own literal origin, appended AT THE CALL SITE - session_opts/1 is NOT widened. Evidence: the six diffs, plus a diff or grep showing session_opts/1 unchanged.
It never invents: calling create_user_session_token with no :origin opt leaves the column nil, and no existing row is backfilled. Evidence: a test asserting nil for the no-opt case.

session_json/2 emits origin ALWAYS (null when unknown) and the SPA session row renders it ONLY when present. Evidence: the serializer diff, the sessionRowHtml diff, and a test asserting the key is present-and-null for a session minted without an origin.

Gates green from a worktree cut off origin/main: `cd cloud && CC=clang mix test test/barkpark_cloud/web/router_sessions_test.exs test/barkpark_cloud/web/router_pat_test.exs test/barkpark_cloud/device_auth_test.exs test/barkpark_cloud/accounts_test.exs <new probe>` reports 0 failures; `node --check cloud/priv/static/app.js` and `node --test cloud/priv/static/__app.test.mjs` report 0 fail. Evidence: pasted output tails.
MERGE-GATED (the LEAD closes this, never the builder): the PR is merged to origin/main and the MERGE SHA is recorded here.

corpus.title: The VISIBLE measure — the inspector's default becomes bucket-aware via the D91 hybrid (root.html.heex sole owner, round 1)

content.description:
THIS IS THE WAVE'S HEADLINE. Epic criterion 1 is stamped met:true on 'viewport 900 = content 640px = 64.00ch', reproduced four times by two independent agents. That is an honest number about the box the LAYOUT holds. The reader at viewport 1024 sees 38.00ch with a 300px panel sitting on the text. Closing this gap is the wave.

READ THE CHARTER FIRST: .claude/workflows/bp-studio-space-priority-charter.md, decisions D91 and D92 (wave-6 amendment). READ IT VIA `git show origin/main:<path>` OR IN A FRESH WORKTREE — D69: the primary checkout is ~69 commits behind origin/main and returns confident empty greps. This epic has been burned six times by stale premises.

THE DEFECT (D87, reproduced this wave on a different document, digit-for-digit). The Document inspector is SERVER-DEFAULT OPEN — one unconditional `sidebar_open: true` in `sidebar_assigns/1`, with zero bucket, param or storage input anywhere — and at every bucket below `wide` it is out of flow (`@container content (max-width: 860px)` makes `.bp-doc-sidebar.is-open` `position: absolute; width: 300px; z-index: 5`) and OVERLAYS the reading column rather than docking beside it. Measured visible_content_px: viewport 1024 -> 380px, 900 -> 448px, 800 -> 398px, 764 -> 396px, 700 -> 332px, 640 -> 272px, 500 -> 176px. At 1440/1280 it DOCKS and costs nothing.

YOUR SHAPE IS ALREADY RULED — DO NOT RE-LITIGATE IT (D91). Both obvious shapes were built and driven against deployed guerrilla, and BOTH ARE REFUTED.
 (a) SERVER-SEEDED IS REFUSED. The static render's root element is bare `<html lang="en">`; `mount.ex` seeds `width_bucket: "wide"`; the true bucket arrives only in a post-connect handle_event. Measured cold-load marks at viewport 1024: firstAnimationFrame t=20.1ms, DOMContentLoaded t=79.5ms, phx-connected t=419.5ms. A server-seeded close cannot land before ~400ms of a 300px panel on the reading column, every document open. D12 refused this and now carries a number. No cookie exists that could give the server a first-byte width signal.
 (b) CSS-ONLY DEFAULT-CLOSED DOES NOT FLASH (first frame t=38.0ms already off-canvas, 0 of 400 frames ever visually open) BUT IT FAILS THIS TASK'S OWN CRITERION 2. Tested in its strongest honest form (translateX(calc(100% - 41px)), leaving the strip and its control on screen and clickable), three real clicks give: collapsed -> is-open w=300 aria-expanded="true" AND transform matrix(1,0,0,1,259,0), STILL OFF-CANVAS -> collapsed. The control toggles forever between 'collapsed strip' and 'open-but-CSS-hidden'; the inspector's contents can never be seen below wide, and aria-expanded="true" announces a panel the user cannot see — the exact class of a11y lie #4633 just landed to fix. Cause is structural: `sidebar_toggle_panel` is a bare `!` flip and CSS is stateless, so a rule suppressing `.is-open` suppresses the server default and the user's explicit open alike.

BUILD THE HYBRID. CSS paints the default-closed state at FIRST PAINT (that property comes ONLY from a rule in the cascade at first paint — the width bucket is already stamped pre-paint by the inline head script, D2, so `html:not([data-width-bucket="wide"])` is true at first paint). The rule YIELDS to an explicit user open via a DOM marker the server stamps — which the server knows WITHOUT knowing the viewport, so D12's flash never opens. The proven selector shape is:
    html:not([data-width-bucket="wide"]) .bp-doc-sidebar.is-open:not([data-user-opened]) { … }
Proven end to end in a browser: first frame t=26.8ms closed, 0/300 inspector-visible frames, no transitions; stamping the marker -> transform: none, inspector visible, reader column 720px -> 420px; removing it -> closed again.

THE FOUR FILES AND WHAT EACH OWES.
 - root.html.heex — the default-closed rule plus the `::after` scrim guard (the existing scrim is `pointer-events: none` on `.editor-with-preview:has(.bp-doc-sidebar.is-open)`; make sure it does not paint over a closed panel).
 - studio_live/components.ex — render the marker attribute on the `<aside class="bp-doc-sidebar">` root. NOTE its body and title are `:if={@panel_open}`, so 'collapsed' REMOVES them from the DOM — CSS-hidden is a different state and you must not conflate them.
 - shared/paper.ex — seed the 'user has not asked' flag beside `sidebar_open: true` in `sidebar_assigns/1`.
 - handlers/paper.ex — set it in `sidebar_toggle_panel`, currently a bare `assign(socket, sidebar_open: !socket.assigns[:sidebar_open])` documented 'Pure assign flip'.

HARD CONSTRAINT, LOAD-BEARING FOR EPIC CRITERION 2 (D92). Your rule is scoped `html:not([data-width-bucket="wide"])` and MAY NOT MOVE ONE PIXEL at viewport 1280 or 1440, where the inspector docks and costs nothing. A wide-bucket change here would also invalidate the floor slice's 676px input. Prove the wide rows are unmoved.

ONE THING THE PROOF DID NOT COVER, AND YOU OWE IT: the server half was SIMULATED by setting/removing the attribute from the console. Confirm that LiveView does not DROP the marker on a diff that re-renders the `<aside>` — cheap to check, unproven so far.

YOU ARE SOLE OWNER OF root.html.heex THIS ROUND (D16/D92). Do not touch `measure_parity_test.exs` (spd-s7-fenced, and it is the round-2 floor slice's file). Do not touch the floor rule, the `@container content (min-width: 720px)` gate, or `--paper-gutter` — that is spd-w5-measure-lever-moves, round 2.

BANNED: line numbers in any evidence (D60/D73 — navigate by selector/marker). Bare `640` (D70 — say `viewport 640` or `content 640`). Any ch figure without its face + font-size + derivation, and cross-face division (D83/D86 — that error manufactured a false criterion failure that sat in this charter as fact).

GATES — ALL FOUR, PASTE ALL FOUR OUTPUTS. Both colour gates have inverse blind spots and the Part E ratchet fails on SHRINK too (D53), so a tokenization that lowers the count reds until you lower the baseline in design/exemptions.json IN THE SAME DIFF.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The hybrid ships as ruled in D91: a first-paint CSS rule scoped html:not([data-width-bucket="wide"]) that yields to an explicit user-open DOM marker stamped by the server. Evidence quotes the shipped selector verbatim and names the four files touched.
The first-frame no-flash obligation is explicitly separated from this shipped settled-state repair and remains executable under one named successor.

The inspector remains REACHABLE at every width below wide — a real mouse click on the collapse control makes the panel CONTENTS visible (not merely is-open in the DOM), proven in the browser with the resulting transform/left/width pasted. This is the criterion CSS-only default-closed fails; if your build fails it too, report a MISS rather than flipping it.

visible_content_px is re-measured across the nine widths after the change and pasted as a table, each ch figure naming its face + font-size + derivation, no cross-face division (D83/D86). State plainly which widths now meet >=55ch visible and which do not.

WIDE IS UNMOVED (D92): viewport 1280 and 1440 rows are identical before and after — pane widths, .editor-panel width, content_px and visible_content_px — pasted side by side. A wide-bucket change here invalidates epic criterion 2 and the round-2 floor slice.

LiveView preserves the user-open marker across a diff that re-renders the <aside> — confirmed by an actual patch/re-render, not by reasoning. The wave-6 browser proof simulated the server half; this is the part it did not cover.

All four gates pass with output pasted: bash scripts/studio-literal-check.sh; node design/check.mjs; bash scripts/paper-editor-mirror-check.sh --write (then re-run without --write); CC=clang mix test test/barkpark_web/studio/ test/barkpark_web/live/studio/. Part E ratchet delta stated explicitly (it fails on SHRINK too, D53).

The ruling is written into the charter as the next free D-number, naming what it would have taken to decide the other way. A default chosen on taste and dressed as a measurement is a criterion failure, not a style note.

PR merged to main after the Elixir Test gate is green — LEAD closes this criterion (Format is advisory-red on main itself, D23; Sobelow reds are baseline drift, check main own run first; a red on sheets/engine_perf_test.exs is the mis-calibrated guard of D90).

corpus.title: Conflict rows discriminate by detail.source so co-occurring problems never collapse to one operator row

content.description: NAMED FAILURE (D17): four semantically-distinct problems reuse the frozen out_of_band_edit conflict kind, discriminated only by a detail.source string — human drift (NO source key), graphql (source=graphql), sub_issue_rejected (source=sub_issue_rejected), client_error (source=client_error). Conflicts.open_row/1 (conflicts.ex:92-103) and the partial unique index github_sync_conflicts_open_key (migration 20260707120000, lines 54-57) both key on exactly {repo,issue,kind} WHERE resolved_at IS NULL. So two co-occurring distinct problems on the SAME issue collapse to ONE operator row; one Resolve clears BOTH and the operator silently misses one (e.g. the sub-issue never gets linked and nobody knows). Merge-not-overwrite already shipped in wave 8 (refresh/2 Map.merge, conflicts.ex:125-131) so the payloads survive in the detail map — but the row still reads as ONE conflict with ONE source label. FIX (D17, no new kind — D14 is LAW): widen the dedup key to {repo,issue,kind,COALESCE(detail->>'source','')} in BOTH open_row/1 AND a NEW lockstep migration that DROPs and recreates the github_sync_conflicts_open_key partial unique index with the COALESCE(detail->>'source','') 4th component (keep the SAME index name so conflict.ex unique_constraint mapping still resolves). CRITICAL null-trap: Postgres treats NULL as DISTINCT in a unique index, so a bare detail->>'source' would break the five-human-edits=one-row invariant (conflicts_test.exs:48-57) because human-drift and detached records carry NO source key — you MUST use COALESCE(...,'') in BOTH the index expression AND open_row. Existing test conflicts_test.exs:101-126 currently asserts merge-collapse of a no-source record + a graphql record to ONE row (count==1) — that codifies the BUG; reverse it to expect 2 rows. BUILD IN AN ISOLATED WORKTREE off committed main; borrow main deps (symlink api/deps) + cp -a api/_build/test into the worktree (lockfree-worktree-gate) — never symlink _build. The mix test alias auto-runs ecto.migrate so the new migration applies to the test DB.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Fail-before protective test added: graphql + sub_issue_rejected recorded on the SAME {repo,issue} produce 2 DISTINCT open rows. It FAILS on current main (collapses to 1 via the {repo,issue,kind} key) and PASSES after the fix.

Conflicts.open_row/1 AND the partial unique index github_sync_conflicts_open_key are widened in lockstep to include COALESCE(detail->>source,empty) as a 4th discriminator, via a NEW migration that drops+recreates the index keeping the same name.

Null-source dedup preserved: five human-drift records with NO detail.source on one {repo,issue} still dedup to ONE open row (COALESCE empty-string guard); conflicts_test.exs:48-57 invariant still green.

The stale merge-collapse test (conflicts_test.exs:101-126) is reversed to expect 2 rows for a no-source record + a graphql record; no new conflict kind is added (conflict.ex @kinds unchanged, Health 3-kind bucketing untouched — D14 held).

corpus.title: Session-safe deferred relocation: two-phase pending queue, offload pending/run-pending, gated daily-tick re-check (a stop-gated asset is never a dead end)

content.description: ABSORBS nn-bl-auto-relocate-gates (b4). The ~/.claude case: you cannot relocate the config dir of the app you are running — today `offload apply` just errors on a stop-gate failure and the user must remember to retry. SEQUENCING: LAST slice of the wave — its files collide with nn-w2-cli-flag-trust (offload_cmd.go), nn-w2-playbook-generalize (offload.go), nn-w2-posture-data (schema.sql), nn-w2-daemon-leak-alerts (tick.go, config.go); branch from main only after those have merged. BUILD: (1) NEW table relocation_queue via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ONLY (D16 — never ALTER): id, queued_at, target_path, playbook_asset_id, dest_root, dest_volume_uuid, status ('queued'|'applied'|'blocked'|'cancelled'), blocked_reason, resolved_at, audit linkage. Store methods: Enqueue/ListPending/ResolveQueued (+tests). (2) Queueing: when Apply fails the stop-gate, offer explicit consent ('queue for when <gate> is not running? [y/N]' or a --defer flag — which must parse verb-first correctly per D22). Queued entries visible via `noo-noo offload pending`. (3) `noo-noo offload run-pending`: for each queued entry re-check EVERYTHING fresh — stop-gate (or path gate), volguard CheckDest, dest collision — then run the normal Apply; on failure mark blocked with reason, source untouched (Apply's existing restore law). (4) Daemon daily-tick re-check in RunTick (tick.go): behind a multi-gate cascade mirroring autoclean (config [offload] auto_apply_pending master switch DEFAULT OFF + risk_acknowledged_at timestamp required + per-tick budget of 1 + all fresh gate re-checks + two-phase queue-row update around the apply). TriggerPressure NEVER applies (test mirrors the errPressureTrigger law). Notification on success ('relocated X, freed YG internal'). Consent story: queueing itself requires explicit user action (prompt/--defer); daemon auto-apply additionally requires the config opt-in pair. Every state change lands in the queue row; the JSONL audit still gets its append entries on actual apply.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: relocation_queue exists via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS only; Enqueue/ListPending/ResolveQueued round-trip with two-phase status transitions (tests, incl. idempotent re-open).

run-pending re-checks stop-gate + volguard + collision fresh before applying; a still-blocked entry is marked blocked with reason and the source is untouched (test).

corpus.title: DeployRunner becomes observer+finalizer — spawn a surviving transient unit, re-attach on init

content.description: DeployRunner opens the engine as a BEAM Port.open child inside the slot's KillMode=control-group cgroup, so systemctl restart barkpark-slot@<slot> kills the build and wipes all run state (init/1 resets to empty maps). Make it an observer+finalizer of a surviving transient unit (D29/D31/D32/D33). (1) SPAWN: instead of Port.open({:spawn_executable,bash}), launch the whole engine as systemd-run --unit=bp-site-build-<slug>-<buildid> -p EnvironmentFile=<0600 build_env_file> -p MemoryMax=1500M -p CPUQuota=150% [--collect] bash deploy/site-deploy.sh — so the script runs in a SIBLING cgroup that survives the slot restart and keeps holding the per-slug flock (proven on guerrilla). Keep the spawn config-injectable (tests stub it); when systemd-run is absent (dev/macOS/CI) fall back to the current Port path so local tests still run. (2) ENV HYGIENE: write a per-run 0600 build_env_file (KEY=VALUE lines from the EXISTING child_env set-or-remove logic — reuse it, do not fork the allow-list) passed via -p EnvironmentFile=, NEVER --setenv/argv (proven leak via systemctl show). Set BARKPARK_SITE_STATUS_FILE / BARKPARK_SITE_LOG_FILE in the unit env pointing at the run's files. Unlink the build_env_file after the run finalizes. (3) MANIFEST: at spawn write a per-run manifest {slug, build_id, mode, runtime_target, unit_name, status_file, log_file, build_env_file, started_at} under a config-injectable run-state dir. (4) status(slug): reconstruct the render_run map from manifest+status_file+log_file — stage fold = first-seen ORDER, latest-status-wins, RAW engine tokens (do NOT pre-normalize; the CP maps ok->done). Never serve state :done before the fold is populated. Preserve build_id in the payload (slice stw6-build-id-match-404 depends on it). (5) init/1: scan the run-state dir; for each manifest run systemctl is-active <unit_name> — live => re-attach as :running, re-arm the deadline, repopulate single-flight (a same-slug re-trigger must 409, not flock-queue a second engine); terminal/absent => finalize as :done from the status file (exit_code, stages, failure_reason). Builds to the file contract slice stw6-engine-file-contract writes; the two agree on the BARKPARK_SITE_STATUS_FILE/LOG_FILE env names and the BPSTAGE grammar already in site-deploy-common.sh. This is .ex — WAITS for the Elixir Test gate; mix format every touched file.

corpus.title: Register the terminal run's prediction as a committed, frozen file — split from its checker

content.description:
CLAIM THIS TASK FIRST: `bp task claim spd-w13-prediction-registered <worker>`. pr-task-gate hard-fails a PR whose task is still `open`. Put `Task: spd-w13-prediction-registered` in the PR body.

Ship TWO NEW FILES and touch nothing else: `scripts/measurements/spd-round-trip-prediction-2026-07-21.json` (the FROZEN prediction) and `scripts/measurements/check-prediction.mjs` (the checker). Do NOT touch scripts/studio-desk-measure.mjs (slice B owns it) or any existing measurements JSON.

WHY A FILE AND NOT PROSE: no committed prediction file has ever existed in this repo — `git ls-files | grep -i predict` is empty. Every prior registration was prose in a task brief (D138) or a charter Decision (D150, D161). The nearest structural precedent is cloud/priv/static/__preview__/seal-predicate.mjs ("frozen BEFORE any builder flies, so its bar cannot be re-derived after seeing a result"), but it FUSES data and logic in one file. SPLIT them here: the prediction JSON is frozen at registration and never edited; the checker stays fixable, because it will have bugs (the prototype had a real misattribution bug within minutes of being written, and freezing them together forces a choice between shipping a known-buggy checker and breaking the freeze).

THE FORMAT (charter D189, all of it load-bearing):
- Rows keyed by the COMPOSITE `viewport_px|inspector_state|face`. Never an index. NOTE: rows key on `viewport_px`, NOT `width` — tooling written against `r.width` silently indexes nothing.
- Every predicted field carries a `basis`: `arithmetic` (fixed by the per-face 18px ch math — a miss is real font drift), `recomputed` (derived by the checker from raw fields), `ruling` (a covered column reports NULL not FALSE), `prior-observation` (a miss is same-build non-determinism). Without this every failure reads identically and the reader cannot tell drift from flake.
- The checker RECOMPUTES and NEVER reads a rows own verdict. This is the entire point: studio-desk-compare.mjs:216-218 copies applies_in_rows/passed_in_rows/vacuous straight out of the artefact without recompute, so it structurally cannot catch a row whose verdict field contradicts its own raw numbers. Prove your checker catches exactly that.
- BANNED_SCALAR hygiene: the prediction is REJECTED if it quotes applies_in_rows, passed_in_rows, vacuous, or artifact.row_count. Not theoretical — on a skipped run the guard reads `vacuous: true` with `applies_in_rows: 0`, so `passed_in_rows: 0` is a pass proving nothing.
- THREE exit states, not two: green / mismatch / UNEVALUATED, with distinct exit codes. A binary green/red forces "the run produced no evidence" to be recorded as a wrong prediction, which is a lie.
- Use `probe_px_per_ch`, NEVER `in_floor_px_per_ch` (unstable per row, carries empty-string values on some rows).

THE FIGURES ARE OBSERVED FACT, not assumption — read off the deployed round trips own before/after at 18px: native 10.0000 -> 55ch = 550.00px; georgia 11.0469 -> 607.58px; source-serif-4 9.1719 -> 504.45px. NO CROSS-FACE DIVISION ANYWHERE.

THE ROUND-TRIP SECTION: predict against reached-widths x 3 faces x 6 fields with `ran:true` and the reached count STATED — not a bare 27. A failing open leg `return`s out of runRoundTrip, so `cells` is 27 or nothing, and it can be nothing for a reachability reason unrelated to fidelity.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: scripts/measurements/spd-round-trip-prediction-2026-07-21.json exists, is committed, and keys every row by the composite viewport_px|inspector_state|face. Quote three keys.
Every predicted field carries a basis drawn from {arithmetic, recomputed, ruling, prior-observation}. Quote one field of each basis.
The per-face 18px figures are registered exactly: native 10.0000/550.00px, georgia 11.0469/607.58px, source-serif-4 9.1719/504.45px, with no cross-face division anywhere in the file.
MUTATION PROOF: changing ONE predicted value drives the checker RED with a non-zero exit. Quote the mutated field and the mismatch line.

ANTI-BLINDNESS PROOF: an artefact whose verdict field contradicts its own raw numbers (flip one row verdict, leave raw px untouched) is caught as SELF_INCONSISTENT — the class studio-desk-compare.mjs:216-218 copies verbatim. Quote the output.
HYGIENE PROOF: a prediction quoting applies_in_rows/passed_in_rows/vacuous is REJECTED by a banned-scalar rule. Quote the rejection.

THREE exit states are distinct and demonstrated: green, mismatch, and UNEVALUATED (a run whose round trip did not run is reported as unevaluated, never as pass or mismatch). Quote all three exit codes.
The prediction file quotes probe_px_per_ch and nowhere quotes in_floor_px_per_ch. Show the grep.
GATE: node --check on both new files exits 0, and the checker run against a real artefact prints its verdict. Quote the command and verdict line.
MERGE-GATED (the lead closes this): the PR is merged to origin/main, freezing the prediction BEFORE the terminal run fires.

corpus.title: The renderer digest cannot see a dependency bump that changes rendered bytes

content.description:
A KNOWN, ACCEPTED gap recorded at the moment it was decided rather than discovered later (production-truth charter D7).

pt-w1-renderer-source-digest derives the render version from a sha256 over the renderer's own source files. That catches every in-repo renderer edit automatically — the goal. It does NOT catch a transitive Hex dependency bump that changes rendered bytes without touching a covered file.

This is a STRICTLY SMALLER gap than what it replaced (a hand-typed integer catches nothing automatically), which is why it was accepted rather than solved. Filed so the limit is visible instead of being rediscovered as a mystery 422 later.

If it ever bites, the candidate remedies are to fold a lockfile hash of the render-relevant dependency subtree into the digest, or to add a CI check that re-renders a corpus sample when mix.lock changes. Neither is worth building before there is a single observed instance — do not pre-emptively widen the digest, since an over-broad digest re-renders the corpus on every unrelated lockfile change.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An observed instance exists of a dependency bump changing rendered bytes with no covered-file change — this task should NOT be built speculatively
If it occurs, the digest or a CI check covers the render-relevant dependency subtree without re-rendering the corpus on unrelated lockfile churn
The eventual proof includes a negative control where an unrelated lockfile change leaves the renderer version stable.
